# Cryptanalyst — Voynich Manuscript Investigation
# Facts about the text that survived methodological scrutiny.

## F642: Multi-Word Label Terminal Construction — a-Onset Dominant at LL; ot-Onset Dominant at LF (exp_580)
**Experiment:** exp_580 (2026-04-12)
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** In 222 multi-word VMS labels (from 1,087 total label lines), a-onset words are massively elevated at the final position (LL: E=3.55×, count=53). The bigram patterns [ok/ot/o/y/d]-onset → a-onset are 3–6× more common in labels than in body text (y→a: 5.70×, ok→a: 4.38×, d→a: 3.33×, o→a: 3.37×, ot→a: 3.24×). ot-onset is the primary LF class in labels (E=1.41×), different from body text where y leads. Body grammar findings hold weakly and in attenuated form: -am LL enrichment 1.31× (vs body 1.76×), y-onset LF enrichment 1.73× (vs body 3.03×). Onset self-succession 1.27× overall (vs body ss_mean ~1.47×). All directional findings have low statistical power (N=222 multi-word labels, 355 bigrams).
**Limitation:** N=222 multi-word labels is too small for significance testing. The a-onset terminal class includes diverse words (aiin, al, am, ar, etc.) that have not been further decomposed. The ot-onset LF finding could reflect zodiac/cosmo_large label section dominance.
**Commitment status:** Part of proposed commitment C010.
**Magnitude context:** The a-onset LL finding (E=3.55×) is comparable in magnitude to the body y-onset LF enrichment. Body grammar's -am LL and y-LF patterns hold directionally but at 57–75% of body magnitude.

## F641: Label Corpus Suffix Profile — edy/aiin Massively Depleted; dy/y/am Elevated; Dialect Boundary Blurred (exp_580)
**Experiment:** exp_580 (2026-04-12)
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** VMS label text (1,442 tokens) strongly depletes the major body-text suffix paradigms: edy (0.26×), aiin (0.35×), ey (0.60×), ain (0.33×). Labels elevate shorter suffixes: dy (1.88×), bare-y (1.83×), am (2.19×), al (1.49×). The B-dialect edy marker is near-absent even in B-folio labels (B-folio labels edy=0.168 vs B-folio body 0.241). A-folio labels have edy=0.109 vs A-folio body 0.069. The A/B dialect boundary is substantially blurred in labels. Vocabulary: 47% of label types appear in body vocab; 53% are label-exclusive (547 types); 61% of label tokens by count appear in body vocab.
**Limitation:** Folio $L= tag may not accurately reflect dialect in mixed-content folios. Suffix classes are heuristic categories.
**Commitment status:** Part of proposed commitment C010.
**Magnitude context:** edy depletion (0.26×) in labels is one of the largest differences from body text. Standard body-text dialect classifier (edy-rate ≥5% = B) misclassifies most B-folio labels as A-dialect.

## F640: Label Corpus Onset Profile — ok/ot/o Dominant; q-Bench Near-Absent (exp_580)
**Experiment:** exp_580 (2026-04-12)
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** VMS label text (1,442 tokens, 1,087 lines, 11 label section types) has a radically different onset profile from body text. ok (17.2%), ot (16.3%), and o (10.9%) together comprise 44.4% of label tokens vs 14.6% body. q-bench classes (qok+qot+qo+cth) total 1.3% of labels vs 13.5% body. ch (0.47×), sh (0.28×), l (0.19×), p (0.13×) are substantially depleted. ok (2.85×), ot (2.97×), o (3.55×), s (1.99×), y (1.73×) elevated. d roughly flat (1.14×). Pattern consistent across all label sections. Token mean length 5.52 vs body 5.12.
**Limitation:** @L0 section classification uses folio number ranges; @Ri/@Ro radial labels (345 tokens) are included as labels.
**Commitment status:** Part of proposed commitment C010.
**Magnitude context:** ok/ot/o elevation (2.85–3.55×) is as large as major body text positional enrichments. qok/qot/qo near-absence (0.09–0.13×) is striking given their prominence in body text MID grammar. Labels constitute a distinct lexical register.

## F639: B-Dialect Document-Order Heterogeneity — Section Composition is the Complete Driver (exp_579)
**Experiment:** exp_579 (2026-04-12)
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** The document-order metric gradient found in exp_576 (First half am_ll=5.825 vs Second half 7.147) is caused by the changing section composition across document order, not by scribal-hand transitions or genuine linguistic drift. B-dialect divides into four sections with distinct positional grammar profiles: B_herbal (am_ll=0.162, d_ll=0.177, low qok_lf), B_bio (am_ll=0.053 — lowest by far, high qok_lf=0.148, high s_lf=0.172), B_astro (intermediate), B_pharma (am_ll=0.192 — highest, low d_ll=0.066). The first half is 28% herbal + 65% bio (Hand 2 dominant); the second half is 77% pharma + 23% astro (Hand 3 dominant). A section-composition prediction model explains 97–107% of the half-shift for all 5 primary metrics (am_ll: 106.8%, y_lf: 106.6%, d_ll: 98.9%, s_lf: 101.4%, qok_lf: 96.1%). Scribal-hand effects cannot be isolated from section effects because hands and sections are near-perfectly co-linear in B-dialect (Hand 2 = herbal+bio+astro; Hand 3 = pharma+astro). Within B_astro, Hand 4 (rose foldout, 159 lines) shows anomalous grammar attributable to diagram-label content rather than scribal idiolect. The gradient is step-wise, not monotonic — Q2 shows a bio-dominated dip in am_ll/y_lf and peak in qok_lf, while Q3–Q4 show pharma-dominated elevated am_ll/y_lf and depleted qok_lf. Enrichment-factor metrics confirm: am_ll_enr range Q1–Q4 = 5.6–8.2× (Full=6.9×, exp_576 full=6.55×); y_lf_enr range = 2.5–4.4× (Full=3.2×, exp_576 full=3.18×).
**Limitation:** Section boundaries are approximate (assigned by folio range, not formal codicological section assignment). The within-B_astro comparison of H2 vs H3 is underpowered (H3 in astro = 61 lines) — scribal hand as an independent driver remains untested (not refuted). Section composition explains the half-level shift but leaves 1–27% unexplained at the quartile level (larger residuals in Q4 for qok_lf and y_lf).
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Proposed qualification to C003 written (proposed_c003_qualification.md).
**Magnitude context:** The section-level grammar differences are large: am_ll raw rate varies 3.7× across sections (bio 0.053 to pharma 0.192). These differences are consistent with the existing section LF taxonomy in working_position.md (F447) and are not new — exp_579 connects those section differences to the exp_576 parameter-stability finding. All B-dialect full-corpus averages in the grammar spec should be understood as section-weighted means over a heterogeneous corpus.

## F638: Architecture Parameter Stability — Parameters are NOT stable structural properties of B-dialect; VMS corpus has systematic document-order heterogeneity; architecture generalizes for balanced splits; stochastic floor = 3/19.
**Experiment:** exp_576 (2026-04-12)
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** Three 50/50 corpus splits (Odd/Even folios, First/Second document order, Random) with independent 1024-combo grid search on each half. (1) CORPUS HETEROGENEITY: First/Second halves have systematically different metric profiles — First: am_ll=5.825, y_lf=2.745; Second: am_ll=7.147, y_lf=3.889 (23% and 42% higher respectively). Odd/Even and Random halves are nearly identical. This gradient is consistent with section composition changes across the VMS manuscript. (2) PARAMETER STABILITY: Five parameters (beta_scale, r_mid, p_qokch) unstable across 2/3 splits. p_blind stable across all 3 splits (always finds 0.115). r_lf near-stable (|A-B|≤0.07 all splits). beta_scale shows extreme instability (best: 0.8–2.5 depending on split). Random split found IDENTICAL parameters in both halves (|A-B|=0 for all 5). (3) CROSS-VALIDATION: Odd/Even: 17→15 (acceptable, 2/19 degradation). First/Second: 17→8 CATASTROPHIC (heterogeneous targets incompatible). Random: 17→14 (identical parameters, 3/19 degradation is stochastic floor). (4) ARCHITECTURE GENERALIZATION: The architecture itself generalizes for balanced splits (Odd/Even 15/19, Random 14/19 cross-val). The 19/19 full-corpus calibration reflects good average-case calibration over a heterogeneous corpus. The First/Second failure (8/19) is NOT a parameter degeneracy issue — it is corpus heterogeneity making two halves structurally incompatible targets.
**Limitation:** Grid search N=3 fast pass → N=10 confirmation. Parameter instability may partly reflect flat/degenerate optimization landscapes (multiple parameter sets achieving similar pass counts) rather than true corpus structural differences. Random split's identical-parameter convergence is a single instantiation (SEED=576000); another random split might show different parameter sets.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The stochastic floor of 3/19 (from Random split with identical parameters) sets the minimum degradation attributable to model stochasticity alone. First/Second's 9/19 excess over this floor is the corpus heterogeneity effect. This finding does NOT undermine C003 (19/19 is real) or C004 (copy-buffer mechanisms always active) but does qualify them: the 19/19 is an average-case result over a heterogeneous corpus, not a universal fit to any B-dialect subsample.

## F637: Q007 Copy-Buffer Amplification Diagnosis (exp_578) — Q007 adj_rate failure present in BASELINE simulation (not clamping-driven); copy-buffer + self-succession is root cause; sh/ch adj_rate NOT amplified by vocabulary clamping.
**Experiment:** exp_578 (2026-04-12)
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** Four-condition simulation test (Baseline/Sparse_clamp/All7_clamp/Rich_only_clamp). Key result: The Q007 adj_rate failure exists in the BASELINE simulation BEFORE any vocabulary clamping. Baseline sim adj_rate vs VMS: sh=1.081% vs 0.764% (1.41×), ch=1.020% vs 0.659% (1.55×), d=0.861% vs 0.480% (1.79×). Baseline vocabulary is 7–14× richer than VMS (sh CP90=1303 vs 145), yet adj_rate is 41–79% ABOVE VMS. ROOT CAUSE: copy-buffer + same-onset self-succession (sh→sh=9.2%, ch→ch=15.0%, d→d=8.6%) causes systematic over-repetition regardless of vocabulary size. Under All7_clamp: qok adj_rate increases +0.464% and d +0.420%, but sh DECREASES -0.040% and ch DECREASES -0.192%. CONCLUSION: vocabulary clamping is NOT the primary driver of sh/ch Q007 failure. The failure is architectural: any copy-buffer mechanism with ≥8% same-onset self-succession will overproduce identical adjacent word pairs for that onset class. See state/q007_investigation.md.
**Limitation:** N=5 trials per condition (low statistical power for small adj_rate differences). sh/ch decreases under clamping are small (< 0.2%) and may not be statistically robust. The causal mechanism (copy-buffer + self-succession) is inferred from the data pattern, not directly isolated.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Revises exp_577's hypothesis that vocabulary restriction is the primary Q007 mechanism. The failure magnitude (sim 1.4-1.8× above VMS) is consistent across vocabulary sizes.

## F636: Q007 VMS adj_rate Onset Decomposition (exp_577) — VMS sh/ch/d adj_rate near-random from CP90 pools; s/t have ZERO identical adjacent pairs; qok dominates overall adj_rate.
**Experiment:** exp_577 (2026-04-12)
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** VMS B-dialect adj_rate=0.933% decomposed by onset class. qok adj_rate=2.681% (0.86× random expectation from CP90=32); qok contributes 36.8% of all identical pairs from 12.8% of tokens. sh adj_rate=0.764% (1.108× random expectation from CP90=145); d adj_rate=0.480% (0.701× random expectation from CP90=146) — both near random expectation, implying NO special anti-repetition mechanism for sh or d. ch adj_rate=0.659% (1.910× above random expectation from CP90=290) — elevated due to ch self-succession (15.0% ch→ch). s adj_rate=0.000% (zero identical adjacent pairs from 452 tokens); t adj_rate=0.000% (zero from 466 tokens) — structural anti-repetition confirmed for both line-opening classes, maintained at both global and MID-only levels. VMS achieves near-random adj_rate for sh/ch/d because it has no copy-buffer; self-succession rates do not amplify repetition without copy-buffer recycling.
**Limitation:** The "random expectation" comparison (1/CP90) is a simplified model assuming uniform word frequencies. Non-uniform frequencies (more concentrated words) would give higher expected adj_rate. CP90 serves as a conservative lower bound on this expectation.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** s and t are the only onset classes with structural adj_rate=0 confirmed. This is mechanistically explained by their positional constraint (line-opening → cannot appear consecutively within a line in the normal sense). The near-random (ratio≈1.0) sh/ch/d finding establishes the key diagnostic: VMS's adj_rate for self-successive onset classes is purely vocabulary-size dependent, while the simulation's adj_rate is amplified above this by the copy-buffer.

## F635: A terminal pairs catalog — CONFIRMS F611 [c-gallows@LL][d@LF] CONF (28 lines, E=2.10×). NEW: [d@LL][d@LF] CONF (E=1.57×/68) — d self-succession at LL→LF is the largest terminal pair enrichment in A by obs count. [c-gallows@LL][d@LF] word pairs: diverse (cthy→daiin tops at 3/28; no other pair >1). Pos1 of c-gallows terminal lines: qot dir(2.98×/3).
**Experiment:** exp_572 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a (360 d-LF lines): [c-gallows@LL][d@LF]=28 lines (7.8%); E=2.10×/28 CONF (F611 confirmed). Breakdown: cth@LL=14, ckh@LL=8, cph@LL=4, sch@LL=2. Top word pairs: cthy→daiin(3), all others unique (28 total pairs, 28 distinct first-elements almost). NEW: d@LL in d-LF lines: obs=68, exp=43.4, E=1.57× CONF. D self-succession at LL→LF (within-line) is a new terminal pattern. Ch@LL in d-LF lines: obs=91, exp=71.3, E=1.28× (sub-CONF). Pos1 of [c-gallows@LL][d@LF] lines (N=28): qot@pos1 dir(2.98×/3), d@pos1 DEPL(0.60×/3). Note: [qo@LL][ch@LF] obs=13/373 ch-LF lines; E=1.35× by overall baseline (vs F623's E=1.66×/12 by LL-position baseline — F623 stands, different baseline). Ch@LL remains sub-CONF in d-LF lines (1.28×/91).
**Limitation:** C-gallows@LL word pair diversity: no dominant pair beyond cthy→daiin (N=3). Total c-gallows pairs N=28 spread over ~28 distinct combinations. Pos1 signals: N=28 insufficient for CONF (qot 2.98×/3 is dir). [d@LL][d@LF] E=1.57×/68: well-powered (obs>>10), robust CONF. [qo@LL][ch@LF] baseline discrepancy: F623 used LL-position baseline (lower base rate for qo at LL → higher E); exp_572 used overall word freq. F623 CONF stands as correctly computed.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** [d@LL][d@LF] CONF (1.57×/68) is a previously undocumented pattern in A. Combined with d→d CL CONF (E=1.77×/101, F560), d shows self-continuation at BOTH within-line LL→LF positions AND across-line LF→LF (CL) positions. This makes d the most "self-continuing" onset class in A at multiple structural levels. The combined picture: A lines end in d preferentially when the penultimate word is also d (within-line self-chain), AND when the next line also ends in d (cross-line self-chain). A d-cluster structure: [d...d] within-line + [d-LF line][d-LF line] across lines.

## F634: B qot→ot→a chain NEGATIVE; qot→ot→ot CONF — The B qot→ot CONF (F632) and ot→a CONF (F629) do NOT combine to form an enriched triplet: qot→ot→a obs=1, exp_markov=2.47, E=0.40×. The two bigrams are independent/mutually exclusive in sequence. BUT: qot→ot→ot CONF (E=1.58×/11) — ot self-succession extends through the qot→ot pathway in B.
**Experiment:** exp_571 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** B all: qot→ot=45 bigrams; ot→a=32/582 (5.5%); qot→ot→a: obs=1, exp_markov=2.47, E=0.40×. A: obs=1, exp_markov=1.02, E=0.98×. B qot→ot→ot: obs=11, exp_markov=6.96, E=1.58× CONF. B ot→a→ol: obs=5, exp=3.15, E=1.59× (underpowered obs<10). No other chains reach CONF.
**Limitation:** qot→ot→a: obs=1 — cannot flag DEPL (need obs≥3). The Markov model E=0.40× is suggestive but statistically underpowered. qot→ot→ot: obs=11, E=1.58× — meets CONF threshold.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** B qot→ot→a NEGATIVE: the chain qot→ot does NOT preferentially route to a. The bigrams qot→ot CONF (F632) and ot→a CONF (F629) are independent — when qot leads into ot, the ot grammar shifts toward self-continuation (ot→ot, E=1.58× in this context) rather than branching to a. This is consistent with ot→ot being the strongest B bigram coupling (E=2.31×/90) — once in an ot sequence, the next word is more likely to be ot regardless of what preceded. The qot→ot→ot CONF (1.58×/11) confirms that ot self-succession continues through the qot→ot gateway.

## F633: B q-bench routing dichotomy — qok→r CONF (1.57×/30, confirms F620); qot→r CONF (1.97×/10, confirms F632); combined q-bench → r CONF (1.61×/45); non-q-bench → r=baseline (0.94×). BUT: qo→r sub-CONF (1.33×/5 — NOT CONF individually). Qo routes to ol CONF(1.70×/26)+o CONF(1.51×/12)+self CONF(1.84×/16) instead. B q-bench splits: [qok/qot] → r; [qo] → ol/o/self.
**Experiment:** exp_570 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** B all (qok sender=1426, qot sender=380, qo sender=281): qok→r CONF(1.57×/30); qot→r CONF(1.97×/10); qo→r sub-CONF(1.33×/5); combined q-bench→r CONF(1.61×/45); non-q-bench→r=0.94×. Qo outgoing: qo→ol CONF(1.70×/26, F614 confirmed); qo→qo CONF(1.84×/16, F614 confirmed); qo→o CONF(1.51×/12, F614 confirmed); qo→d DEPL(0.34×/7); qo→ot DEPL(0.69×/13); qo→qot DEPL(0.68×/12). Additional qok/qot avoidances confirmed: qok→y DEPL(0.26×/12); qok→t DEPL(0.33×/9); qok→a DEPL(0.56×/29); qot→qo DEPL(0.51×/6).
**Limitation:** qo→r: E=1.33×/5 — sub-CONF on both counts (E<1.5, obs<10). Not reported as CONF individually. Combined q-bench→r CONF is driven by qok (30/45) and qot (10/45), with qo providing only 5/45. qo→d DEPL: obs=7 (≥3, qualifies DEPL). qok→y DEPL (0.26×/12): E extreme but note qok is a q-bench class not expected to route to openers — consistent with systematic opener avoidance.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The B q-bench → r coupling (CONF for qok and qot individually) shows that the dominant B template classes route preferentially to the dominant B terminal class (r=2.80×/48, F588). The structural dichotomy (qo routes to ol/o/self, not r) parallels qo's distinct positional profile: qo has B LL DEPL (F613) and A LF DEPL (F613) — a different structural role from qok/qot. The qok/qot routing to r together with qok→r CONF (F620) and qot→r CONF (F632) suggests a B sub-grammar: lines with qok or qot in MID position tend to end with r-onset words. This is the first documented B routing rule linking a specific MID class subset to the strongest LF class.

## F632: qot bigrams — CROSS-DIALECTAL: qot→qot CONF (A:2.88×/18; B:1.82×/29) strong self-succession; qot→a DEPL both (A:0.47×/5; B:0.58×/8); qot→o DEPL A(0.43×/5). A-SPECIFIC: t→qot CONF(2.03×/11, confirms F576); o→qot DEPL(0.48×/5); a→qot DEPL(0.52×/5); ol→qot DEPL(0.35×/3). B-SPECIFIC: sh→qot CONF(1.97×/72, confirms F617); qot→ot CONF(1.77×/45, confirms F629); qot→r CONF(1.97×/10 NEW); qot→sh DEPL(0.67×/24); qot→ok DEPL(0.56×/14); d→qot DEPL(0.63×/18); ok→qot DEPL(0.55×/14). qot-LF pos1: A: qot dir(4.06×/7), sh dir(2.00×/7), y DEPL(0.63×/5). B: y DEPL(0.57×/3); no CONF pos1.
**Experiment:** exp_569 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A (sender=243, receiver=218): qot→qot CONF(2.88×/18); qot→o DEPL(0.43×/5); qot→a DEPL(0.47×/5); qot→ol DEPL(0.52×/5); t→qot CONF(2.03×/11, incoming); o→qot DEPL(0.48×/5); a→qot DEPL(0.52×/5); ol→qot DEPL(0.35×/3). B (sender=380, receiver=389): qot→ot CONF(1.77×/45); qot→qot CONF(1.82×/29); qot→r CONF(1.97×/10); qot→sh DEPL(0.67×/24); qot→ok DEPL(0.56×/14); qot→y DEPL(0.65×/8); qot→a DEPL(0.58×/8); qot→qo DEPL(0.51×/6); sh→qot CONF(1.97×/72, incoming); d→qot DEPL(0.63×/18); ok→qot DEPL(0.55×/14); a→qot DEPL(0.21×/3). qot-LF A (48 lines): qot@pos1 dir(4.06×/7), sh@pos1 dir(2.00×/7), y DEPL(0.63×/5). qot-LF B (46 lines): y DEPL(0.57×/3), d sub-CONF(1.47×/13), s sub-CONF(1.51×/9).
**Limitation:** qot→a DEPL A: obs=5 (minimum for DEPL). qot→o/ol DEPL A: obs=5/3 (minimum). A qot-LF pos1 dir signals (qot/sh): obs=7 (below CONF threshold of 10). B qot-LF pos1=s: E=1.51×/9 — sub-CONF (obs<10). B d@pos1 in qot-LF: E=1.47×/13 — sub-CONF (E<1.5×). B qot self-succession incoming: E=1.78×/29 vs C007 (not in C007 — qot was not tested in exp_164/174, no conflict).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Qot→r CONF B (1.97×/10) is a new finding: both q-bench template classes (qok and qot) route to r in B (qok→r E=1.95×/30, F620; qot→r E=1.97×/10). R is the strongest B LF class (2.80×/48, F588). The q-bench → r routing suggests B template classes preferentially route to the dominant B terminal class. Qot self-succession cross-dialectally (A:2.88-3.21×; B:1.82-1.86×) joins ot (2.3×) as strong self-succession classes. The B extensive DEPL cluster for qot outgoing (qot→sh/ok/y/a/qo DEPL) shows qot is highly selective in B — routes primarily to ot, r, self (qot), and ch (sub-CONF); avoids all others. A qot-LF pos1 dir (qot/sh at 4.06×/2.00× with obs=7 each): qot-terminal lines in A open with qot or sh disproportionately — suggesting a sequential formula [qot or sh opener][...][qot at LF] in A.

## F631: qot positional — A: pos1=1.40×/73 (sub-CONF; NOT CONF — CORRECTS prior 1.79×/59 CONF from F539); MID flat (0.92×); LL flat (0.89×); LF flat (0.91×). B: pos1=0.69×/37 DEPL (confirmed); MID flat (1.08×); LL flat (1.07×); LF sub-baseline (0.86×). Qot is a flat/neutral class in A; B MID class with pos1 DEPL (less extreme than ot 0.26× or ch 0.22×).
**Experiment:** exp_569 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A: total=11327; baseline=2.57%; pos1=73/2033=3.59% (E=1.40× — sub-CONF, below 1.5× threshold); MID=131/5554=2.36% (E=0.92×); LL=41/1870=2.19% (E=0.89×); LF=46/1870=2.46% (E=0.91×). B: total=10163; baseline=4.19%; pos1=37/1283=2.88% (E=0.69× DEPL); MID=286/5928=4.83% (E=1.08×); LL=57/1279=4.46% (E=1.07×); LF=46/1279=3.60% (E=0.86×). CORRECTION: prior F539 value A pos1=1.79×/59 was from pre-canonical methodology. Canonical result: 1.40×/73 — elevated but below CONF threshold (1.5×).
**Limitation:** A pos1=1.40×/73: well-powered (obs=73), E below CONF threshold (1.5×). NOT CONF — correction to F539. B pos1=0.69×/37: E=0.69× just below DEPL threshold (0.70×) — borderline DEPL. All other positions have E in 0.86-1.08× range — genuinely flat.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A qot pos1=1.40× is the largest non-CONF pos1 elevation among characterized classes. Compare: d(1.47× near-CONF in A from F554, now B CONF); ot(0.77×); ok(0.57×). Qot's A pos1=1.40× places it between pos1-flat and pos1-CONF — more "opener tendency" than ot/ok/ch, but not a confirmed opener class. The prior F539 value (1.79×/59 CONF) was an overestimate from the older corpus/methodology. The correction follows the same pattern as qok (1.47→0.87) and ot (1.29→0.77). B pos1=0.69×/37 DEPL — qot is less extreme than ot (0.26×) and ch (0.22×) in B; more comparable to ok (0.50×) and sh (0.70×). Qot's near-flat A profile and moderate B pos1 DEPL make it the most "neutral" of the characterized onset classes.

## F630: qot vocabulary — A: 291 tokens (2.57%); 69 types; qotchy(13.4%) CH-BODY DOMINANT — unique among characterized classes; diverse ch-bench+y+aiin. **Finding:** A herbal_a compound gallows: cth=2.68%; ckh=1.07%; cph=0.34%; sch=0.20% — total 4.29% of A words. B: cth=0.31%; ckh=0.09%; cph=0.07%; sch=0.18% — total 0.64% of B words (6.7× collective drop). Individual drops: cth=8.8×; ckh=12×; cph=4.9×; sch=1.1× (stable). Positional taxonomy: sch=opener (pos1 CONF A); cth=terminal (LF CONF A); ckh=MID (pos1 near-zero; LF DEPL); cph=MID/LL (pos1 near-zero; LL elevated). Vocabulary pattern: ALL 4 classes show A=y-body/lateral → B=edy shift (universal A→B compound-onset vocabulary transition). skh and sph = 0 tokens in both corpora (absent).
**Limitation:** B compound gallows too few for formal positional claims (cth=31; ckh=9; cph=7; sch=18). ckh pos1: obs=2 (not formally DEPL but directionally extreme). cph pos1: obs=1 (same caveat). Combined summary depends on consistent methodology across characterizations.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The compound gallows positional split (opener/terminal/MID/MID+LL for sch/cth/ckh/cph) demonstrates that the 4 compound gallows subclasses each occupy a distinct structural niche in A line grammar. This internal differentiation contradicts any hypothesis that all compound gallows are functionally equivalent. The A-specific prevalence (6.7× collective drop to B) suggests compound gallows are a feature of A-dialect word construction not present in B vocabulary. The exception (sch stable) suggests sch has a different origin or function from the other three.

## F606: sch bigrams — A sch→d dir (E=3.43×/6); sch→s (dir) (E=14.86×/3); B sch→d (dir) (E=4.79×/4); B ch→sch (dir) (E=2.66×/4). Sch→d elevated in both dialects; A d→sch (dir) (E=3.56×/3). Opener-to-terminal coupling: sch (pos1-opener) routes to d (LF-terminal) within the same line.
**Experiment:** exp_560 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a sch-sender (20 bigrams): sch→d dir (E=3.43×/6); sch→s (dir) (E=14.86×/3). sch→ch (E=1.28×/6 flat). Incoming (7 bigrams): d→sch (dir) (E=3.56×/3). B all: sch→d (dir) (E=4.79×/4); ch→sch (dir) (E=2.66×/4). sch→d routing is consistent in both dialects — sch at pos1 is followed by d somewhere in the line at ~3.4-4.8× baseline rate. All signals at (dir) or dir level due to sch's rarity (23 A tokens; 18 B tokens).
**Limitation:** sch→d A: obs=6, E=3.43× → dir (E≥2.0, obs≥5). sch→s: obs=3 only. d→sch A: obs=3. B: all signals (dir). LF-pos1 underpowered (N=2/1). No CONF bigram signals — sch is too rare for CONF.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Sch→d routing (opener→terminal) parallels s→sh CONF (F573) and p→qok CONF B (F596). Line openers route toward terminal classes in the same line — a structural principle extending across opener classes (sch, s, p). If sch→d is confirmed at higher N, it would be the third opener→terminal coupling documented.

## F605: sch positional — A pos1 CONF 11.54×/16 (HIGHEST pos1 E-value of any onset class); B pos1 dir 6.66×/9. Sch is the most pos1-concentrated onset class: 70% of A sch tokens at pos1. A LL (dir) 2.99×/4. Updated A opener E-value ranking: sch(11.54×) >> s(3.16×) ≈ p(2.99×) > y(2.78×) > t(2.27×).
**Experiment:** exp_560 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a sch positional: pos1=11.54×/16 CONF; LL=2.99×/4 (dir); LF=1.44×/2. B all: pos1=6.66×/9 dir. 16 of 23 A sch tokens at pos1 (70%). MID baseline extremely low (5/7333 = 0.07%). The E=11.54× is the highest pos1 enrichment E-value characterized — higher than p (2.99×), s (3.16×), y (2.78×), t (2.27×). Sch almost never appears at MID or LF positions. Cross-dialectal direction: both A and B show extreme pos1 enrichment.
**Limitation:** B pos1: obs=9 (one below CONF threshold). A LL (dir): obs=4, E=2.99× at threshold. LF: obs=2 — no formal claim. The high E value reflects sch's extreme concentration, not a large corpus.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Sch E=11.54× at pos1 reflects near-exclusive pos1 occupation (70% of tokens). Compare p: pos1 CONF both (2.99×/5.23×). Both sch and p are very rare (~0.20%) but almost exclusively openers. This extreme positional concentration may indicate a specific grammatical function — possibly line-initial markers or formulaic openers that appear only at sentence/line beginnings. The contrast with s (3.16× at much lower concentration level, many MID+LF appearances) is stark.

## F604: sch vocabulary — A: y-body (schey 17.4%, schol 13.0%, schy+schor 8.7% each); B: edy-dominant (schedy 38.9%, schdy 16.7%). A→B shift A=y/lateral → B=edy — universal compound-onset vocabulary shift. Frequency-stable (A=0.20%; B=0.18%) — contrast with cth's 8.6× frequency drop (F600).
**Experiment:** exp_560 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a: 23 sch tokens (0.20%); top: schey(4=17.4%), schol(3=13.0%), schy(2=8.7%), schor(2=8.7%). 16 unique forms all low-frequency. B all: 18 sch tokens (0.18%); schedy(7=38.9%), schdy(3=16.7%) — edy-dominant (56%). Sch is frequency-stable across dialects (0.20%/0.18%) unlike cth (2.68%/0.31%). The A→B vocabulary shift (y-body → edy) matches the universal pattern for compound-onset classes.
**Limitation:** N=23 (A) and N=18 (B) — very small samples. Vocabulary statistics unreliable at this N. All top-form percentages carry large uncertainty.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A→B compound-onset vocabulary shift (y/lateral → edy): confirmed for ch, sh, cth (F600), k (F578), t (F574), and now sch. This pattern appears universal across ALL compound-gallows and bench-compound classes. The consistency suggests a systematic B-dialect feature: B words ending in -edy are B-dialect equivalents of A words ending in -y or -ol/-or/-ey. The shift affects vocabulary but not necessarily grammatical role (sch is pos1-CONF in both dialects).

## F603: [cth→d] bigram position distribution — A herbal_a — The cth→d CONF coupling (F602, E=1.97×/37) is distributed across line positions: MID→MID+1=21 (57%), LL→LF=14 (38%), pos1→pos2=2 (5%). [cth@LL][d@LF] terminal formula: 14 lines (3.9% of d-LF lines), E=1.37× sub-CONF (need 1.5×). d-LF lines with any cth co-occurrence: E=1.29×/47 (sub-CONF). Inter-line coupling (cth-LF → d-LF successor): E=1.13×/17 (FLAT). Dominant cth→d pairs: cthol→daiin (6), cthy→daiin (6). H_new_FV RESOLVED NEGATIVE: the specific [cth@LL][d@LF] terminal formula is not confirmed — d↔cth is a distributed word-adjacency enrichment, not a terminal slot formula.
**Experiment:** exp_559 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a, 1961 multi-word lines; d-LF lines=360; cth-LF lines=88. d-LF lines with any cth (pre-LF): 47/360 (13.1%) vs baseline 10.1% → E=1.29× (sub-CONF). [cth@LL][d@LF] exact: 14/360 (3.9%) vs MID-baseline expectation 10.2 → E=1.37× (sub-CONF). [cth→d] bigrams by position: MID→MID+1=21, LL→LF=14, pos1→pos2=2. Dominant pairs: cthol→daiin(6), cthy→daiin(6). Cth-LF → d-LF inter-line: 17/82 (20.7%) vs baseline 18.4% → E=1.13× (flat). Formula lines [cth@LL][d@LF] pos1: qot (dir, E=5.92×/obs=3 — underpowered) — directionally consistent with F602's qo-class opener preference.
**Limitation:** [cth@LL][d@LF] formula: N=14 lines. Pos1 profile underpowered. E=1.37× for cth@LL-in-d-LF is not CONF (need ≥1.5×). The negative result is robust — the cth→d coupling (E=1.97×/37) is real (F602) but distributed across all line positions.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The d↔cth mutual coupling (F602) is a word-adjacency effect of strength E=1.97× in both directions. Compare: d→d self-coupling at LL (LL class distribution: d=18.9% of d-LF LL) is strong. The cth@LL in d-LF lines at 3.9% (E=1.37×) is below the ch@LL rate (25.3%) — ch is actually the dominant LL class before d-LF lines. This suggests d-LF lines are preceded more often by ch at LL than by cth. The [cth→d] coupling represents a tendency for these classes to appear together anywhere in a line, rather than a fixed formula.

## F589: r bigrams — l→r CONF B (E=3.30×/obs=17) CONFIRMED (exact replication of F586); l→r dir A (4.02×/5); r→l NOT elevated in B (0.79×/4) — l→r is DIRECTIONAL, not mutual (unlike o↔a). A r→a dir (3.26×/8); A r→ot dir (2.43×/6); B r→ol DEPL (0.66×/3); B r→ot DEPL (0.62×/4). B r-LF pos1: qok CONF (E=1.56×/obs=10) — qo-class opens r-terminal B lines at CONF.
**Experiment:** exp_554 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a (49 r-sender bigrams): r→a dir (E=3.26×/obs=8 — E≥2.0, obs≥5); r→ot dir (E=2.43×/obs=6); r→r (E=6.24×/obs=2 — too small). l→r cross-check: obs=5, exp=1.2, E=4.02× dir (consistent with F586). B all (88 r-sender bigrams): r→d near-CONF (E=1.62×/obs=7 — obs<10); r→a near-CONF (E=1.53×/obs=5); r→ol DEPL (0.66×/3); r→ot DEPL (0.62×/4). l→r cross-check CONF: obs=17, exp=5.2, E=3.30× (exact F586 replication). Reverse coupling: B r→l=0.79×/4 — NOT elevated, confirming l→r is directional only. B r-LF (N=48): qok@pos1 CONF (1.56×/10). A r-LF (N=16): s@pos1 (dir) (3.01×/4 — meets (dir) threshold).
**Limitation:** A herbal_a: only 65 r-tokens (0.57% of words) — underpowered. A r→a dir (3.26×/8) is the strongest A bigram signal but obs=8 (below CONF threshold of 10). B r-LF: N=48 is moderate; qok CONF borderline (1.56×/10). B r→d near-CONF: obs=7 at E=1.62× — below CONF threshold. The directional l→r coupling (r→l NOT elevated in B at 0.79×) is robust: obs=4 (above threshold for DEPL at obs≥3), E=0.79× (between 0.7 and 1.0 — not formally DEPL but clearly below baseline).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** l→r directional (not mutual) contrasts with o↔a mutual coupling (F566: both directions CONF). L sends to r at 3.3×; r does not return to l. This suggests l→r is a terminal sequence (l-word followed by the terminal r-word), not an exchange or rotation. Given r is the most LF-enriched class in B (F588: 2.80×/48), l→r CONF B may primarily be a [l-word][r-word at LF] pattern. B r-LF pos1=qok CONF (1.56×/10) means lines of structure [qok][...][l][r] are plausible candidates.

## F593: Complete B positional architecture — 3-layer structure: LAYER 1=pos1 OPENERS (p,s,y,t,d); LAYER 2=MID classes (ch,qok,qot,ok,ot,sh,k); LAYER 3=LF TERMINALS (r,l,ol,o,a). Openers (s,y,t) are LF-DEPL; terminals (r,l,ol,a) are pos1-DEPL. Cross-dialectal A/B LF inversion: A LF CONF = d+cth (completely different terminal layer from B). Y,qok,sh are LF-DEPL in BOTH dialects.
**Experiment:** exp_555 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** Complete B positional complementarity across all characterized onset classes. Layer 1 (OPENERS/pos1 CONF): p(5.23×/27), s(4.77×/165), y(3.54×/147), t(3.18×/78), d(2.64×/246). Layer 2 (MID — neither LF nor pos1 enriched): ch(pos1 0.25×/53 DEPL, LF 0.91×), qok(pos1 0.88×, LF 0.58×/112 DEPL), ok(pos1 0.54×/46 DEPL, LF 0.90×), ot(pos1 0.26×/22 DEPL, LF 1.14×), sh(pos1 0.65×/78 DEPL, LF 0.45×/54 DEPL), k(pos1 0.16×/4 DEPL, LF 1.18×). Layer 3 (TERMINALS/LF CONF): r(pos1 0.35×/6 DEPL, LF 2.80×/48), l(0.52×/41 DEPL, 1.85×/145), ol(0.63×/44 DEPL, 1.65×/115), o(1.00×/36 neutral, 1.58×/57), a(0.26×/12 DEPL, 1.52×/70). Cross-dialectal cross-class constants: y, qok, sh are LF-DEPL in BOTH dialects. A LF CONF (d: 1.53×/360; cth: 1.67×/88) vs B LF CONF (r+l+ol+o+a) = complete terminal-layer dialect inversion. O is the only B terminal with pos1-NEUTRAL (1.00×) — can appear at both LF and elsewhere; other B terminals are pos1-DEPL.
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A LF cth CONF (1.67×/88) is newly quantified here — consistent with A d→cth bigram CONF (F555) but is an independent positional claim not previously stated at CONF level. P-onset (Layer 1) is uncharacterized beyond this finding. O's Layer 3 membership is partial (pos1-neutral, not depleted).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The 3-layer architecture completes the structural characterization of B-dialect line grammar begun in exp_534 (qot/ot), exp_535 (ok), exp_537-540 (qok, sh, ch, d), and exp_541-554 (y, a, s, t, k, ol, l, r). The MID layer is structurally heterogeneous but positionally unified: template classes (qok/ok/ot/qot), bench classes (ch), lateral-bench (sh), and gallows (k) all share the property of neither opening nor terminating B lines at CONF rate.

CONF pos1-DEPL: ch(0.25×/53), k(0.16×/4), a(0.26×/12), ot(0.26×/22), l(0.52×/41), r(0.35×/6), sh(0.65×/78), ok(0.54×/46), qot(0.69×/37), ol(0.63×/44).

**Finding:** B all pos1 (1279 lines). Complete B pos1 CONF taxonomy. CONF openers: p(5.23×/27 — NEW, highest E), s(4.77×/165), y(3.54×/147), t(3.18×/78), d(2.64×/246). Dir opener: sch(3.97×/9). CONF pos1-DEPL: ch(0.25×/53), k(0.16×/4), a(0.26×/12), ot(0.26×/22), l(0.52×/41), r(0.35×/6), sh(0.65×/78), ok(0.54×/46), qot(0.69×/37), ol(0.63×/44). Its general B pos1 enrichment means p preferentially opens lines — it's not just a qok-LF or ol-LF opener but a general B line-opener. The high E-value (5.23×) with moderate obs (27) means p accounts for ~2.1% of B line openings but only ~0.4% of total B words — extreme positional concentration. Motivates H_new_FS: p-onset full characterization.

## F591: B LF word vocabulary — top B LF words: chedy(40=3.1%), oly(17=1.3%), dy(16=1.3%), lchedy(15=1.2%), dar(15=1.2%), daiin(13=1.0%), ol(12=0.9%), am(11=0.9%). **Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** B all LF word vocabulary from 1279 eligible lines. The single most common B LF word is 'chedy' (ch-onset, 40 obs) — ch is NOT B LF-enriched (0.91×) but has high overall frequency. ## F596: p bigrams — A: p→ol (dir) (E=3.81×/obs=4); p→sh dir (2.03×/5); underpowered for CONF. B: p→qok CONF (E=1.55×/obs=10); p→k (dir) (4.81×/4); p→ch DEPL (0.54×/4). P routes to qok at CONF in B after opening; avoids ch. P-LF pos1 underpowered (N=2-3 p-LF lines).

This contrasts with B d→sh CONF (F555) and s→sh CONF (F573) — each opener routes to different mid-line classes: p→qok; d/s→sh; t→ot. Compare: B d→sh CONF (the B-dominant opener d routes to sh at pos2); A qot→qot CONF (A opener qot routes to itself). Each opener appears to have a dialect-specific routing to a MID class.

## F602: cth bigrams — A: cth→d CONF (E=1.97×/obs=37 — NEW); d→cth CONF (1.97×/62, F555 confirmed); cth→cth CONF (2.46×/15); qok→cth DEPL (0.42×/10). BIDIRECTIONAL d↔cth MUTUAL COUPLING in A herbal_a at equal E-values (E=1.97× both directions). Cth-LF pos1 A: qot@pos1 dir (2.82×/9); qo@pos1 dir (2.97×/6) — qo-class opens cth-terminal lines, same as d-terminal lines (F556). B cth→ot dir (3.39×/6 — underpowered).
**Experiment:** exp_558 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a (215 cth-sender bigrams): cth→d CONF (E=1.97×/obs=37 — bidirectional with F555's d→cth CONF 1.97×/62); cth→cth CONF (2.46×/15 — strong self-succession); cth→cph (dir) (3.30×/3). Incoming: d→cth CONF (1.97×/62); cth self CONF (2.19×/15); k→cth (1.48×/14 near-CONF); qok→cth DEPL (0.42×/10). The d↔cth mutual coupling in A: d routes to cth (F555: 1.97×/62) AND cth routes back to d (1.97×/37) at the same E-value. Cth-LF pos1 (N=88 lines): qot@pos1 dir (2.82×/9); qo@pos1 dir (2.97×/6); o@pos1 (1.53×/9 near-CONF). Parallels d-LF pos1=qot CONF (F556): both terminal classes (cth, d) prefer qo-class openers, producing the structural pattern [qo/qot opener]...[cth/d at LF]. B all (24 bigrams — underpowered): cth→ot dir (3.39×/6).
**Limitation:** A cth→d CONF: obs=37 at E=1.97× — robust. K→cth: obs=14 at E=1.48× — near-CONF, below threshold. qok→cth DEPL (0.42×/10): strong DEPL — qok consistently avoids cth (qok is LF-DEPL; cth is LF-CONF; complementary). Cth-LF pos1: qot (2.82×/9) and qo (2.97×/6) are both dir (E≥2.0, obs≥5 for qot; but qo obs=6 — meets dir). Y@pos1 at cth-LF: E=0.76×/11 — NOT formally DEPL (E<0.70 threshold not met; E=0.76 is above threshold). Reported as sub-baseline directional only.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** D↔cth mutual coupling (E=1.97× both directions) is symmetric at the same E-value, unlike o↔a (asymmetric: o→a at 3.08-3.17× is stronger than a→o at 1.58-2.54×). Both d and cth are A terminal classes that mutually attract each other within lines AND both prefer qo-class openers at the line start. This suggests A lines containing both d and cth words are structured as [qo-opener]...[d or cth sequence]...[LF class], where d and cth appear in the second half of the line in either order.

## F601: cth positional — A: pos1 EXTREME DEPL (0.13×/7); MID FLAT (0.96×/143); LL elevated (1.35×/65); LF CONF (1.67×/88). Cth is a TERMINAL class in A — LL+LF enriched, pos1 absent. B underpowered (31 total tokens): pos1 and LF both ~1.79×/7 (dir only).
**Experiment:** exp_558 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A cth: pos1=0.13×/7 (DEPL — E<0.7, but obs=7 is borderline; very extreme depletion); MID=0.96×/143 (FLAT — near-baseline); LL=1.35×/65 (sub-CONF — below 1.5× but robustly above 1.0×); LF=1.67×/88 (CONF). The LL+LF joint enrichment (1.35× and 1.67×) means cth clusters in the final segment of A lines. Cth is uniquely placed at the end of lines — both LL and LF elevated, pos1 extremely depleted. B cth: pos1=1.79×/7 (dir); MID=0.72×; LL=0.78×; LF=1.79×/7 (dir). B shows directional LF enrichment consistent with A but underpowered.
**Limitation:** A pos1 obs=7 with E=0.13× — the obs=7 is above 3 (meets formal DEPL threshold: E<0.7, obs≥3). Strong DEPL confirmed. A LL obs=65 at E=1.35× — below CONF threshold (1.5×) but obs is high; directional enrichment at LL is robust. B: all claims directional only.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Cth's LL+LF enrichment (1.35×+1.67×) contrasts with d's pure LF dominance (d LL=1.06× baseline in A; LF=1.53× CONF). Cth appears earlier in the line's final segment than d. The pattern [cth at LL or MID][d at LF] is consistent with the cth→d CONF bigram (F602) — cth precedes d within lines.

## F600: cth vocabulary — A: y-body dominant (cthy 24.7%, cthol 14.5%, cthor 10.2%, cthey 9.5%); B: edy-body (cthedy 25.8%, cthdy 16.1%). A→B: A=y/lateral; B=edy-dominant. CRITICAL: cth is 2.68% of A words but only 0.31% of B words — an 8.6× frequency drop A→B. Cth is a major A class that nearly disappears in B.
**Experiment:** exp_558 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a cth (304 tokens, 2.68%): cthy=24.7%, cthol=14.5%, cthor=10.2%, cthey=9.5%; y-body + lateral forms ~59%. No edy-suffix forms in A. B all cth (31 tokens, 0.31%): cthedy=25.8%, cthey=19.4%, cthdy=16.1%; edy-forms ~42%. A→B frequency drop: 2.68%→0.31% = 8.6×. This is the most extreme cross-dialectal frequency change found for any onset class. Compare d: A=2.15%, B=0.92% (2.3× drop). Cth suppression in B is far greater than d's frequency change. The few B cth words that exist follow the edy-suffix convention. Cth vocabulary structure: [c+t+h][body] where body is y-suffix, lateral (ol, or), or ey in A; edy in B.
**Limitation:** B: 31 tokens is too small for robust vocabulary statistics. The 8.6× frequency drop is based on reliable corpus counts (A: 304/11255 words = 2.68%; B: 31/10159 words = 0.31%).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Cth's near-disappearance in B (0.31%) while being 2.68% of A is the most striking A/B class frequency asymmetry found. In terms of structural interpretation: if cth represents compound gallows words specific to the A herbal convention, then B's lack of cth reflects a fundamental difference in the word-formation rules between the two dialects. The B edy-compounds with cth prefix (cthedy) are present but rare — they may be loan forms from A or residual compound gallows usage.

## F599: Complete A/B cross-dialect positional comparison — A OPENERS (pos1 CONF): sch(3.91×/15 NEW), s(3.24×/163), y(2.81×/323), p(2.97×/15), t(2.28×/111); d near-CONF (1.47×/346). A TERMINALS (LF CONF): cth(1.67×/88), d(1.53×/360). B OPENERS: p(5.23×/27), s(4.77×/165), y(3.54×/147), t(3.18×/78), d(2.64×/246). B TERMINALS: r(2.80×/48), l(1.85×/145), ol(1.65×/115), o(1.58×/57), a(1.52×/70). D is the KEY DIALECT-CROSSING CLASS (A=terminal; B=opener). NEW: sch is A pos1 CONF (3.91×/15). Cross-dialectal constants: y,qok,sh LF-DEPL in both.
**Experiment:** exp_557 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** Complete cross-dialect comparison combining exp_555 (B) and exp_557 (A). A pos1 CONF openers: sch(3.91×/15 — NEW), s(3.24×/163), y(2.81×/323), p(2.97×/15), t(2.28×/111); d near-CONF (1.47×/346). A LF CONF: cth(1.67×/88), d(1.53×/360). B pos1 CONF openers: p(5.23×/27), s(4.77×/165), y(3.54×/147), t(3.18×/78), d(2.64×/246). B LF CONF: r(2.80×/48), l(1.85×/145), ol(1.65×/115), o(1.58×/57), a(1.52×/70). Cross-dialectal CONF openers (both): p, s, y, t. B-specific opener: d. A-specific openers: sch (dir in B). A-specific terminal: cth (pos1 DEPL 0.13× in A; no B LF CONF analog). B-specific terminals: r, l, ol, o, a (all sub-threshold in A LF). D undergoes the most dramatic role reversal of any onset class: A dominant LF (1.53×/360) vs B dominant pos1 (2.64×/246). Cth in A: purely terminal — almost never opens lines (0.13×/7 pos1) and appears at LF at CONF (1.67×/88). Sch: A pos1 CONF (3.91×/15, NEW) — not previously listed as CONF opener. Cross-dialectal constants: y LF-DEPL in both (A:0.63×; B:0.60×); qok LF-DEPL in both (A:0.57×; B:0.58×); sh LF-DEPL in both (A:0.55×; B:0.45×).
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. Sch obs=15 in A (borderline CONF). Cth in B: obs=7 at LF (dir only: 1.79×/7) — no B LF CONF claim for cth. D's "near-CONF" in A pos1: 1.47×/346 — strong signal (high N) but below 1.5× threshold; robustly below CONF but consistently above 1.0×. D may be approaching A-opener status in herbal_a but its dominant A role is clearly LF.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The A 3-layer architecture is less clean than B: d occupies both terminal and near-opener positions, making A a more "layered" structure than B's clean separation. B has 5 terminal classes vs A's 2 (cth, d). A LF is dominated by d+cth which together account for 22.8% of A LF words; B LF has 5 contributing classes accounting for 34% of B LF words more evenly distributed. B has a more distributed terminal vocabulary; A is more concentrated.

## F598: A LF word vocabulary — 'daiin' is the dominant A LF word (98=5.0% of all A LF lines). D-onset words (daiin+dy+dal+dam+dar+dain) = ~23% of A LF words (360 total). 'Cthy' tops cth-LF (27=1.4%). A a-LF: aiin(15) > am(12) — opposite of B where am(11) > aiin(8). Top single A LF word (daiin 5.0%) exceeds top B LF word (chedy 3.1%).
**Experiment:** exp_557 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a LF vocabulary (1961 lines). Top 6 A LF words: daiin(98=5.0%), dy(45=2.3%), cthy(27=1.4%), dal(24=1.2%), dam(22=1.1%), ol(22=1.1%). D-onset LF words together: daiin+dy+dal+dam+dar+dain = 229/1961 = 11.7% of A LF. Cth-LF: cthy(27) dominates (31% of cth-LF); cthey(9), cthol(6), cthor(6). A a-LF: aiin(15), am(12), al(10), ar(8) — aiin tops. Compare B a-LF: am(11), aiin(8), al(8), ar(7) — am tops. This aiin>am vs am>aiin reversal between A and B a-LF is a dialect-specific terminal particle difference. In A, aiin serves as the preferred terminal a-word; in B, am is preferred.
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56. The aiin vs am reversal between A and B a-LF: A aiin(15) vs am(12); B am(11) vs aiin(8) — small margins. Both are small obs counts but the direction reversal (aiin top in A; am top in B) is consistent and motivates further investigation.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** 'Daiin' at 5.0% of A LF is strikingly dominant — no single B LF word reaches this concentration (chedy=3.1% is top in B). Daiin's prevalence at A LF is consistent with d being the dominant A LF class (18.4% of A LF words) and daiin being the dominant d-onset word in A (F553: 32.3% of A d-tokens). The terminal role of daiin in A herbal_a is one of the most replicated structural patterns in this research program.

## F597: A LF full onset taxonomy — CONF LF-enriched: cth(1.67×/88), d(1.53×/360). CONF LF-depleted: y(0.63×/72), qok(0.57×/82), sh(0.55×/88), qo(0.53×/27). CTH pos1 EXTREME DEPL (0.13×/7) — exclusively terminal in A. A LF CONF = {d,cth}; B LF CONF = {r,l,ol,o,a} — complete terminal-layer dialect inversion (no overlap). Cross-dialectal LF-DEPL constants: y, qok, sh depleted in BOTH dialects.
**Experiment:** exp_557 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a complete LF onset distribution (1961 LF words). LF-CONF: cth=1.67×/88, d=1.53×/360. LF sub-enriched (directional but below CONF): f(1.72×/3), r(1.41×/16), a(1.35×/117), ol(1.24×/96). LF-DEPL: y=0.63×/72 CONF, p=0.59×/3 CONF (small obs), qok=0.57×/82 CONF, sh=0.55×/88 CONF, qo=0.53×/27 CONF. A pos1 CONF openers (new): sch=3.91×/15 CONF (NEW — previously uncategorized). Cth pos1=0.13×/7 — extreme terminal class that almost never opens lines. None of the 5 B LF-CONF classes (r,l,ol,o,a) reach CONF in A LF: r=1.41×/16; a=1.35×/117; ol=1.24×/96; l=1.16×/48; o=1.12×/105. Cross-dialectal LF-DEPL constants: y(A:0.63×/72; B:0.60×/25), qok(A:0.57×/82; B:0.58×/112), sh(A:0.55×/88; B:0.45×/54).
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A sub-enriched classes (r, a, ol, l, o all 1.12-1.41×) are directionally consistent with B CONF status but insufficient N for A CONF claim. The A LF CONF claim for d (360 obs) and cth (88 obs) are the most robust positional findings in the entire program. P LF obs=3 at E=0.59× — formally DEPL but borderline.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A has only 2 LF-CONF classes vs B's 5. This means A line endings are more concentrated (d+cth account for 22.8% of A LF) while B endings are more distributed (r+l+ol+o+a account for 34% of B LF). The A LF concentration in d (18.4%) and cth (4.5%) together represent line-terminal compounds: daiin, cthy, cthol — these are morphologically "short form + body" or "compound gallows + body" words. B terminals (lchedy, oly, ol, or, aiin/am) are morphologically simpler or edy-suffixed.

## F594: p vocabulary — A: diverse pch-compound forms (~60% ch-bench: pchodaiin, pchody, pchedar, etc.); B: pchedy dominant (34.1%) + pol (7.3%). A→B: A=diverse pch-bench (no edy); B=pchedy strongly dominant. P-onset is the lowest-frequency characterized class (A: 0.26%; B: 0.40%).
**Experiment:** exp_556 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a p (29 tokens): 20 unique types — near-complete diversity (0.69 type/token ratio). Ch-bench compounds (pch-) ~60%; also pol(2), paiin(2), pair. B all p (41 tokens): pchedy=34.1% strongly dominant; pol=7.3%; then 21 other types (mostly singleton). A→B shift: pch-bench (A) → pchedy (B) — the edy-suffix transformation. Pchedy is the single most concentrated word-type within any B onset class (34.1% vs lchedy=15.4%, kchedy=5.6%, tchedy=8.7%). P onset = [p][ch-bench body] in A; [p][ch-bench+edy] in B. The ch-bench compound structure persists from A to B but with edy-suffix added.
**Limitation:** 29-41 tokens is too small for robust vocabulary statistics. Many A forms are hapax legomena. B pchedy=14/41 is relatively robust.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Pchedy's 34.1% dominance within B p-onset suggests p is a highly specialized class with a canonical word form in B. Compare: bare 'ol' dominates A ol-class (33.8%, F581) — both p and ol have one form that is ~1/3 of the class. But pchedy is a ch-bench+edy compound, not a bare short form like 'ol'. The p class in B may represent a formulaic word used in specific contexts (possibly label or caption words given their concentration at pos1 = line openings).

## F590: B LF full onset taxonomy — CONF LF-enriched: r(2.80×/48), l(1.85×/145), ol(1.65×/115), o(1.58×/57), a(1.52×/70). CONF LF-depleted: y(0.60×/25), qok(0.58×/112), sh(0.45×/54), t(0.45×/11). The 5 LF-CONF classes are all lateral/vowel-initial. Cross-dialectal LF inversion: A LF CONF = d(1.53×/360)+cth(1.67×/88); B LF CONF = r+l+ol+o+a. Y,qok,sh LF-DEPL in BOTH dialects.
**Experiment:** exp_555 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** B all complete LF onset distribution (1279 LF words). LF-CONF: r=2.80×/48, l=1.85×/145, ol=1.65×/115, o=1.58×/57, a=1.52×/70. LF near-enriched: d=1.30×/121 (below CONF threshold), cth=1.79×/7 (below obs threshold). LF-DEPL: y=0.60×/25 CONF, qok=0.58×/112 CONF, sh=0.45×/54 CONF, t=0.45×/11 CONF. A herbal_a LF comparison: d=1.53×/360 CONF, cth=1.67×/88 CONF — no overlap with B LF-CONF classes. The 5 B LF-CONF classes (r,l,ol,o,a) share the property of short, vowel-heavy word forms at LF (raiin, lchedy, ol, or, aiin/am). Cross-dialectal constant: y(A: 0.63× DEPL; B: 0.60× DEPL), qok(A: 0.57× DEPL; B: 0.58× DEPL), sh(A: 0.55× DEPL; B: 0.45× DEPL) — all three LF-DEPL in both dialects at similar E-values.
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A LF cth CONF (1.67×/88) is quantified here for the first time — cross-verify against exp_543 (A d→cth bigram CONF, F555) which is a within-line not positional claim. The two are independent and compatible. D in B is near-enriched at LF (1.30×/121) — directional but below CONF threshold (1.5×). B LF-depletion of t (0.45×/11) is robust despite low obs (E well below 0.7 with obs=11).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The cross-dialectal A/B LF inversion is structurally fundamental: A closes lines with d-class (aiin-body: daiin) and compound-gallows (cth), while B closes with lateral/vowel-initial classes. This maps onto the A→B dialect vocabulary shift (edy-suffix in B; d→opener in B). The terminal word class change is consistent with the entire A→B structural reorganization documented across exp_534-555.

## F587: r vocabulary — A: aiin-body dominant (raiin 26.2%, rain 7.7%); lateral forms (rar, ral, ror, rol); ch-bench (rcheey, rchey). B: aiin-body (raiin 18.4%, rain 5.9%) + lateral forms (rol 7.4%, ror 4.4%) + edy-compounds (rchedy 4.4%, rshedy 3.7% ~8%). A→B: A=aiin-body dominant; B=aiin-body + edy-compounds (~8%). Low frequency class: A=0.57%, B=1.34% of words.
**Experiment:** exp_554 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a r (65 tokens): raiin=26.2%, rar=9.2%, ral=7.7%, rain=7.7%, rcheey=4.6%, ram=3.1%, ror=3.1%. Diverse vocabulary concentrated in aiin-body forms (raiin+rain ~34%) and lateral forms (rar, ral, ror, rol ~25%). B all r (136 tokens): raiin=18.4%, rol=7.4%, rain=5.9%, rchedy=4.4%, ror=4.4%, ral=4.4%, rshedy=3.7%, raraiin=2.2%. B has edy-compound forms (rchedy, rshedy, rsheedy ~10%) absent/rare in A. Bare 'r' (single letter) is excluded by len≥2 filter — shortest r words are 'ro', 'ry' (2-letter). Both dialects share aiin-body dominance (raiin is #1 form in both) and lateral forms. A→B shift: A=no edy-forms; B has ~10% edy-compounds with ch-bench+edy (rchedy) and sh-bench+edy (rshedy) patterns parallel to other onset classes.
**Limitation:** 65 A tokens is low — type diversity is limited (only 20 types). 'r' onset here captures all words starting with 'r' (no higher-priority prefix starts with r in ONSET_PRIORITY). raraiin (A: 3×; B: 3×) is a repeated lateral+aiin compound form.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** R vocabulary has notable shared forms across dialects: raiin (A: 26.2%, B: 18.4%) is the dominant r-onset word. This parallels a-onset where aiin, ar, al are stable across dialects (F569). Both a-onset and r-onset have aiin-body words as the dominant vocabulary items — both are "aiin-attracted" onset classes. Given the a→r and r→a directional bigrams (F589), the pair may be structurally related.

## F586: l bigrams — l→l CONF cross-dialectally (A: E=3.86×/obs=16; B: E=2.62×/obs=72); l→r CONF B (E=3.30×/obs=17 — strong new coupling); l→a CONF A (1.79×/17); l→ot CONF A (1.57×/15); l→sh DEPL B (0.64×/33). A l-LF pos1: qok CONF (E=2.90×/10) — lines ending in l in A herbal_a opened by qo-class. B l-LF pos1: ch CONF (1.66×/10) — ch opens l-LF B lines at CONF despite being most pos1-depleted class in B (0.25× general pos1 E). This is the first case of a pos1-avoider class having a specific LF-class pos1 association overcoming its general avoidance.
**Experiment:** exp_553 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a l (148 l-sender bigrams): l→l CONF (E=3.86×/obs=16); l→a CONF (1.79×/17); l→ot CONF (1.57×/15); l→r dir (4.02×/5); l→sh near-baseline. B all l (436 l-sender bigrams): l→l CONF (E=2.62×/obs=72); l→r CONF (3.30×/17); l→sh DEPL (0.64×/33). Cross-dialectal: l→l CONF both (strong self-succession). A-specific: l→a CONF, l→ot CONF. B-specific: l→r CONF (3.30×/17 — new strong coupling). A l-LF (N=48): qok@pos1 CONF (E=2.90×/10). B l-LF (N=145): ch@pos1 CONF (E=1.66×/10); ok sub-CONF (1.53×/8); sh DEPL (0.68×/6). The B l-LF pos1=ch CONF is paradoxical: ch is the most pos1-depleted class in B (F547: E=0.25×), yet specifically opens l-terminal lines at CONF. Demonstrates LF-class-specific pos1 grammar overriding general class avoidance.
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A l bigrams: smaller sender N (148) than B (436). l→r CONF B (obs=17 at E=3.30×) is well above threshold; A l→r dir (4.02×/5) is directional only (obs=5). B l-LF pos1=ch CONF: obs=10 at E=1.66× — borderline CONF but consistent direction (ch vs ok vs l-self all elevated together vs sh depleted).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** l→r CONF B (3.30×/17) is the strongest new onset-class coupling found in the l characterization. Paired with A l→r dir (4.02×/5), the l→r coupling may be cross-dialectal at the (dir) level at minimum. R-onset is uncharacterized — does r→l also CONF (mutual coupling analogous to o↔a)? And is r positionally enriched at LF (given l is strongly LF-enriched in B)?

## F585: l positional — A near-DEPL pos1 (0.73×/30); LF slightly elevated (1.16×). B pos1 DEPL (E=0.52×/obs=41); LF CONF (E=1.85×/obs=145) — one of the stronger LF enrichments characterized. L→l CONF cross-dialectally (A: 3.86×/16; B: 2.62×/72). L is a strongly LF-enriched class in B; pos1-depleted in both.
**Experiment:** exp_553 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a l: pos1=0.73×/30 (near-DEPL, below threshold); MID=1.01×; LL=1.11×; LF=1.16×. B all l: pos1=0.52×/41 (DEPL); MID=0.95×; LL=0.89×; LF=1.85×/145 (CONF). L is LF-enriched in B (1.85×/145 — strong), a pos1-avoider in B (0.52×), and near-pos1-avoider in A (0.73×). Compare: B ol LF CONF (1.65×/115, F582) — both ol and l are B LF-enriched at CONF. Updated LF-enriched classes: d(A), o(B), a(B), ol(B), l(B). B LF-CONF ranking (by E): l (1.85×/145) > ol (1.65×/115) > a (1.52×/70) > o (1.58×/57).
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A l LF: 1.16× is below CONF threshold (1.5×/10) — not formally confirmed in A. B l LF: 1.85×/145 — well above threshold, robust CONF.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** B l LF CONF (1.85×/145) is one of the highest LF enrichments characterized (compare B ol 1.65×, B a 1.52×, B o 1.58×). L-onset is the most LF-enriched B class by E-value. L also appears as a within-line bigram target: B s→ol/l coupling (F573), a→ol/l (F568) — consistent with l appearing frequently at terminal positions.

## F584: l vocabulary — A: mixed (lkaiin 6.7%, lor 5.0%, lchey 4.6%, lol 4.6%, lkain 3.4%; k-gallows+body forms prominent ~10%). B: lchedy dominant (15.4%), lchey 4.8%, lkeedy 4.8%, lshedy 4.7%, lkeey 3.7%; edy-compounds dominate. A→B shift: A=mixed/k-gallows+body; B=ch-bench+edy dominant (lchedy).

**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a l (208 tokens): lkaiin=6.7%, lor=5.0%, lchey=4.6%, lol=4.6%, lkain=3.4%, laiin=3.4%, lar=2.9%, lcheey=2.9%. Edy-compounds (lchedy, lkeedy, lshedy, lkedy) ~28% of B l. A→B shift: A=mixed (k-gallows+body + ch-bench + aiin); B=edy-dominant (lchedy is the single dominant form at 15.4%). The ch-bench structure persists as lchedy in B (vs lchey in A — edy suffix added).
**Limitation:** 'ol' onset has higher priority than 'l' — l-onset words exclude ol-initial forms. This means l-onset = words starting with 'l' but NOT 'ol'.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** lchedy in B at 15.4% is the dominant B l-form. Compare: lchey in A at 4.6% — A has lchey (no edy), B has lchedy (edy-suffix). The ch-bench affinity in l-onset parallels ch-bench affinity in k-onset (kchedy in B, kchy in A), suggesting a cross-class pattern of ch-bench compounds getting edy-suffixed in B.

## F583: ol bigrams — ol→ol CONF A (E=3.20×/obs=45 — strong self-succession); ol→o CONF cross-dialectally (A: 1.66×/24; B: 1.88×/21); ol→l CONF A (1.98×/15); B ol→k CONF (1.71×/16). B ol-LF: y DEPL (0.61×/8); d DEPL (0.63×/14) — main B openers (y, d) do NOT open ol-terminal B lines at above-baseline rate.
**Experiment:** exp_553 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a ol (375 ol-sender bigrams): ol→ol CONF (E=3.20×/obs=45); ol→o CONF (1.66×/24); ol→l CONF (1.98×/15); ol→k DEPL (0.64×/8). B all ol (440 ol-sender bigrams): ol→o CONF (1.88×/21); ol→k CONF (1.71×/16); ol→qok near-DEPL (0.74×/54). Cross-dialectal: ol→o CONF both (A: 1.66×; B: 1.88×) — ol is followed by o-onset at above-baseline rate in both dialects. A-specific: ol→ol CONF (strong; 3.20×/45), ol→l CONF (1.98×/15). B-specific: ol→k CONF (1.71×/16). A ol-LF (N=96): s@pos1 CONF (E=2.13×/17); p@pos1 dir (E=4.09×/3). B ol-LF (N=115): o@pos1 dir (2.16×/7); p@pos1 dir (2.06×/5); y DEPL (0.61×/8); d DEPL (0.63×/14).
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. ol→ol CONF A (3.20×/45) is robust. Cross-dialectal ol→o CONF: A 1.66×/24 and B 1.88×/21 — both above threshold. B ol-LF: y DEPL and d DEPL are at formal DEPL threshold (E<0.7, obs≥3) — the main B line-openers explicitly avoid ol-terminal lines in B.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** ol→ol A (3.20×/45) is one of the stronger self-succession signals (compare a→a CONF A: 3.15×/60; l→l CONF A: 3.86×/16). The ol self-succession in A may be part of "ol-run" phrases (multiple ol-onset words in succession). ol→o cross-dialectal parallels o↔a mutual coupling — ol-onset words precede o-onset at above-baseline rate, and o-onset precedes a-onset at above-baseline rate, suggesting an extended "o-region" cluster pattern: [ol-word][o-word][a-word] is a candidate sub-sequence.

## F582: ol positional — pos1 DEPL cross-dialectally (A: E=0.68×/obs=52; B: E=0.63×/obs=44). B LF CONF (E=1.65×/obs=115). A LF sub-CONF (E=1.25×). Ol is LF-enriched in B; pos1-depleted in both. A ol-LF pos1: s CONF (E=2.13×/17) — s opens ol-terminal A lines at CONF rate.

Pos1-depleted classes: a, k, ch (F579/F570/F547) now extended with ol (A: 0.68×; B: 0.63×) — all are below-baseline at pos1, though ol's E is less extreme than a (0.16×) or k (0.52×).
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A ol LF: 1.25× sub-CONF (below 1.5× threshold) — directional only in A. B ol LF: 1.65×/115 is above CONF threshold (robust).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** B ol LF (1.65×/115) is the third strongest B LF enrichment (after l: 1.85×/145 and o: 1.58×/57). Ol's pos1 depletion (0.63-0.68×) is moderate compared to the strong avoiders (a=0.16×, k=0.16-0.52×, ch=0.25-0.38×) but consistent across dialects.

## F579: k positional — pos1 STRONGLY DEPL cross-dialectally (A: E=0.52×/obs=32; B: E=0.16×/obs=4). K is a pos1-AVOIDER. MID slightly elevated both (1.13–1.15×). No CONF at any position. K joins the pos1-avoider cluster with a and ch.

## F577: A herbal_a t-LF pos1: o@pos1 dir (E=2.23×/obs=7); y DEPLETED (E=0.52×/obs=4) — y avoids opening t-terminal lines; o-onset opens them instead. Cross-LF-class exception to y's general pos1 enrichment.
**Experiment:** exp_551 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a t-LF (N=47 lines): o@pos1 dir (E=2.23×/obs=7 — meets dir threshold E≥2.0/obs≥5). y@pos1 DEPLETED (E=0.52×/obs=4). ch@pos1 sub-CONF (E=1.71×/6). All other opener classes near baseline. Y is the definitive line-opener (F558: pos1 CONF 2.78×) and opens many LF-class lines (ok-LF: F455; ot-LF: F456; o-LF: F564). But t-LF specifically reverses this: y is DEPLETED (0.52×) and o-onset is elevated (dir) instead. O-onset is the preferred opener for t-terminal A herbal_a lines. B all t-LF: N=11 (underpowered, no formal claims).
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B underpowered (N=11). o@pos1 dir: E=2.23×/obs=7 — meets dir threshold. y DEPL: E=0.52×/obs=4 — meets formal DEPL threshold (E<0.7, obs≥3). Both signals are borderline but consistent direction.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** y opens ok-LF at E=1.52×, ot-LF at E=1.80×, o-LF at E=1.50×. But for t-LF, y is at E=0.52×. This selectivity suggests that the line-opening role of y is LF-class-dependent — y specifically avoids t-LF lines. Since t is itself a line-opener (F575), there may be a structural incompatibility: lines that open with t also tend to end in t, but a different set of lines opens with o and ends in t.

## F576: t bigrams — A t→qot CONF (E=2.01×/obs=11); B t→ot CONF (E=1.55×/obs=21); ok DEPL both (A: 0.63×; B: 0.60×). T routes to dialect-specific template class after opening: A line-opener t-words are followed by qot; B line-opener t-words are followed by ot.

**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a (233 t-sender bigrams): t→qot CONF (E=2.01×/obs=11); t→ok DEPL (E=0.63×/obs=12); t→cph (dir) (E=3.05×/obs=3); t→ot sub-CONF (E=1.45×/17). T routes to the dominant template class in each dialect: A→qot; B→ot. Cross-dialectal: ok DEPL in both (0.60-0.63×). The dialect-specific routing (A: t→qot; B: t→ot) mirrors the broader A=qot/B=ot dialect difference in template class usage.
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A t→qot CONF (obs=11 at E=2.01×) is secure. B t→ot CONF (obs=21 at E=1.55×) is secure.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Within-line routing from an opener class to a template class (t→qot in A; t→ot in B) creates a specific opener→template bigram coupling. Compare: s→sh CONF (F573) — opener routes to MID class sh. T→qot/ot suggests opener routes to the within-line template sequence. This may represent a line-opening formula: [t-opener][qot/ot-word][...].

## F571: s vocabulary — A: mixed aiin-body (saiin 12.8%; sain 6.7%) and ar/al/or-body (sar 9.1%; sor 8.7%; sal 5.7%); sy=4.7% (gallows-body). **Experiment:** exp_550 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a s (298 tokens): saiin=12.8%, sar=9.1%, sor=8.7%, sain=6.7%, sal=5.7%, sy=4.7%, soiin=4.4%, sol=4.0%. Mixed vocabulary: aiin/ain group, ar/al/or group, and gallows+body (sy). B all s (276 tokens): saiin=22.5%, sain=12.7%, sol=8.7%, sar=7.2%, sal=4.7%, sor=4.7%; sol compounds prominent in B (solchedy, solshedy, solkeedy, solkeey). B s-onset: heavily aiin-dominated with s+ol compounds. A→B vocabulary shift in s-class: A=mixed; B=aiin+sol dominant. This parallels the overall dialect shift but is less extreme than d, y, sh which show near-total vocabulary inversions.
**Limitation:** Sol-compound forms in B may be related to the l-body compound structure; not clearly separable from 'ol' onset words.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** s-onset vocabulary diversity is moderate — top-3 words in A (saiin, sar, sor) account for 30.6%, leaving 69% spread across many rare forms. Compare: d (daiin=32.3% of d-tokens, F553 — more concentrated); y (top-3 account for ~15%). s is less concentrated than d but more than y.

## F570: a positional — pos1 STRONGLY DEPL cross-dialectally (A: E=0.16×/obs=14; B: E=0.26×/obs=12) — most extreme pos1 depletion of any characterized class. B all LF CONF (E=1.52×/obs=70). A a: LF=1.35× sub-CONF.
**Experiment:** exp_549 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a a: pos1=E=0.16×/obs=14 (14/1961 = 0.71% vs 4.41% baseline — EXTREME DEPL); MID=1.18×; LL=0.99×; LF=1.35× (obs=117, below E=1.5 CONF threshold). B all a: pos1=E=0.26×/obs=12 (DEPL); MID=1.00×; LL=1.18×; LF CONF (E=1.52×/obs=70). A a-onset is virtually absent at line-opening. B a = pos1-DEPL + LF-CONF. Positional hierarchy for pos1 depletion: A a (0.16×) << B a (0.26×) ≈ B ch (0.25×) < A ch (0.38×). Combined with y (pos1 CONF 2.78×/3.54×), the a/y positional opposition is the most extreme opener/avoider pair characterized. Also: a-LF pos1 has no CONF opener rule in either dialect (only weak (dir) signals a-self@pos1 E=4.79×/obs=4 and p@pos1 E=3.35×/obs=3 in A; (dir) p@pos1 in B) — paralleling ch-LF pos1 (F550, second major LF class with absent pos1 grammar).
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A a LF=1.35×/obs=117 is GENUINELY sub-CONF — not underpowered (obs=117 > threshold). The LF sub-CONF in A parallels o-onset A positional flatness (F562).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A a pos1=0.16× means a-onset words appear at line-opening at 1/6 the expected rate. Compare: B ch pos1=0.25× (F547), A ch pos1=0.38×. A a is uniquely extreme in pos1 avoidance. The a vs y opposition (0.16× vs 2.78× in A) represents the sharpest positional contrast documented across all characterized classes.

## F569: a vocabulary — DIALECT-STABLE: aiin (A: 24.6%; B: 26.2%), ar (A: 22.2%; B: 17.8%), al (A: 11.0%; B: 14.8%), ain (A: 5.6%; B: 6.6%). ar/al group ~35% both dialects; aiin/ain ~33-36% both dialects. No A→B vocabulary shift. Contrast with all other characterized classes which show major A/B vocabulary inversions.
**Experiment:** exp_549 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a a (499 tokens): aiin=24.6%, ar=22.2%, al=11.0%, ain=5.6%, am=3.2%; ar/al group=35.1%; aiin/ain/aiiin=33.1%; no edy-body. B all a (366 tokens): aiin=26.2%, ar=17.8%, al=14.8%, ain=6.6%, aiiin=3.6%, am=3.3%; aiin/ain group=36.3%; ar/al=34.7%; edy-body=1.1%. The top-4 words and their relative frequencies are nearly identical across dialects. A-onset is the most vocabulary-stable class among all characterized classes: d, y, sh, qot, ch all show major A/B vocabulary shifts; a does not. The tiny edy-body in B (1.1%) vs 0% in A is the only dialect difference.

**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Vocabulary stability of a-onset: ar/al group is 35.1% (A) vs 34.7% (B), nearly identical despite A/B dialect difference. This cross-dialectal stability makes a-onset vocabulary the most conservative characterized class — suggesting a-words (aiin, ar, al, ain) function as grammatical particles or function words that are preserved across dialectal variation.

## F568: a-onset bigram grammar CONF cross-dialectally — a→a CONF (A: E=3.15×/obs=60; B: E=4.01×/obs=44); a→ok CONF both (A/B: 1.60×/50 and 34); a→ol CONF A (1.95×/30); a→o CONF both (A: 1.58×/25; B: 2.54×/19); DEPL: a→d (A: 0.51×; B: 0.41×), a→qok (A: 0.42×; B: 0.18×); B-specific: a→y CONF (2.45×/15), a→k CONF (1.59×/10)
**Experiment:** exp_548 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a (381 a-sender bigrams): a→a CONF (E=3.15×/obs=60); a→ok CONF (E=1.60×/obs=50); a→ol CONF (E=1.95×/obs=30); a→o CONF (E=1.58×/obs=25); DEPL: a→d (0.51×/17), a→qok (0.42×/13). B all (295 a-sender bigrams): a→a CONF (E=4.01×/obs=44 — one of the strongest bigram signals found); a→ok CONF (E=1.60×/obs=34); a→ol near-CONF (E=1.89×/obs=29); a→o CONF (E=2.54×/obs=19); a→y CONF (E=2.45×/obs=15); a→k CONF (E=1.59×/obs=10); DEPL: a→qok (0.18×), a→d (0.41×), a→l (0.53×). Cross-dialectally conserved: a→a CONF (~3-4×), a→ok CONF (1.60× both), a→o CONF, DEPL of d and qok. B-specific: a→y CONF and a→k CONF. A-specific: a→ol CONF (B: 1.89× near-CONF). a-onset has one of the richest characterized bigram grammars, dominated by self-succession and ok/ol affinities while strongly avoiding d and q-class onsets.
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. a-onset includes a wide variety of words (aiin, ar, al, ain, etc.) — these bigram statistics pool across the whole a-class. a→a self-succession at 4.01× in B is among the highest E-values with large obs found in this project.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** a→a CONF (B: 4.01×/44) rivals qot→qot (A: 2.74×) and y→y (A: 1.88×/B: 3.18×) as one of the strongest self-succession signals. Compare: o→a at 3.08–3.17× (the reverse coupling, F563) — the o-a dyad has mutual strong affinity. a DEPL of d and qok cross-dialectally (0.42–0.51× and 0.18–0.42×) mirrors o DEPL of q-class: both o-class and a-class avoid template onsets as bigram targets.

## F567: o→a B-dialect-wide — all B sections show elevated o→a (B astro: E=5.23×/obs=5 dir; B herbal: E=2.92×/obs=4 (dir); B pharma: E=2.48×/obs=18 CONF). Not section-specific.
**Experiment:** exp_548 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** B herbal (162 lines): o→a E=2.92×/obs=4 ((dir)). B astro (544 lines): o→a E=5.23×/obs=5 (dir). B pharma (577 lines): o→a E=2.48×/obs=18 (CONF). All three B sections independently show elevated o→a — direction is consistent (E≥2.4× in all). B pharma provides CONF anchor. The o→a coupling is B-dialect-wide, not section-specific. Combined with F563 (CONF in A herbal_a) and F566 (mutual coupling), the o-a affinity is a fundamental cross-section, cross-dialect coupling.
**Limitation:** B herbal and B astro have insufficient obs for formal CONF. B cosmo not tested (too small). A herbal_a CONF (F563); A stars/cosmo underpowered.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** B astro shows the highest E (5.23×) with obs=5 — this is the dir threshold (E≥2.0, obs≥5). All B sections show at least (dir) level, suggesting the coupling is genuine and cross-sectional.

## F566: o↔a MUTUAL CONF coupling — both o→a CONF (F563: E≈3.1×) and a→o CONF (A: E=1.58×/obs=25; B: E=2.54×/obs=19). O→a is dominant direction (~2× stronger), but both directions exceed CONF threshold cross-dialectally.
**Experiment:** exp_548 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** o→a CONF cross-dialectally (F563: A 3.08×/67; B 3.17×/27). a→o CONF cross-dialectally (A: E=1.58×/obs=25; B: E=2.54×/obs=19). The o-a dyad forms a bidirectional affinity cluster within VMS lines. Coupling is directional (o→a is ~2× stronger than a→o) but both directions are CONF in both dialects. Coupling predominantly occurs at MID positions (F565: 61% A, 78% B) — within-line phrase pairs, not line-boundary.
**Limitation:** The coupling could reflect co-occurrence of specific word types (e.g., 'or' + 'aiin') rather than arbitrary o-class + a-class. See F565.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Mutual CONF bigram coupling between two classes is unusual. Compare: sh→ch and ch→sh are both DEPLETED (F328). d→a: in A herbal_a d→a has E=0.63× (DEPLETED) — so the d-class and a-class are mutually avoided as successors. The o-a mutual coupling is distinct: o and a specifically seek each other as successors.

## F565: o→a coupling is primarily [o-word][aiin] — 43% of A obs (29/67) and 30% of B obs (8/27) have 'aiin' as the specific target word. Secondary targets: 'ar' (A: 8; B: 3), 'al' (A: 6), 'aiiin' (A: 5). Coupling predominantly occurs at MID positions (A: 61%; B: 78%).
**Experiment:** exp_548 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a: 67 o→a pairs; aiin=29 (43%), ar=8 (12%), al=6 (9%), aiiin=5 (7%), ain=3 (4%). Positions: MID=41/67 (61%), LL=14/67 (21%), pos1=12/67 (18%). B all: 27 o→a pairs; aiin=8 (30%), ar=3 (11%), all others 1 each. Positions: MID=21/27 (78%), LL=5/27 (18%), pos1=1/27 (4%). The phrase pattern [o-word][aiin] is the dominant specific realization of the o→a coupling. 'aiin' is a common standalone VMS word (a-onset, classified by onset priority). The specific concentration on 'aiin' suggests this may be a grammatical construction: an o-word (often 'or', 'odaiin', etc.) followed by the word 'aiin' as a modifier, article, or inflectional particle.
**Limitation:** 'aiin' as both a standalone word AND as part of compound words (like 'daiin', 'okaiin', 'qotaiin') — these compound forms are classified under their first-onset class, not 'a'. The 'aiin' counted here is only the standalone free word 'aiin'.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** 29/67 obs concentrated in a single target word ('aiin') vs expected ~5 (at baseline) is a very strong concentration. The phrase '[o-onset word] aiin' appears ~6× more often than expected if target were random. This phrase-level specificity suggests o-word + aiin may be a formulaic or syntactic unit in VMS grammar.

## F564: o-LF pos1=y CONF cross-dialectally (A herbal_a: E=1.50×/obs=26; B all: E=1.53×/obs=10) — formally confirms F502/F503 at standard methodology; y is the only CONF pos1 class for o-LF in both dialects

This formally confirms F502 (o-LF pos1=y pooled A herbal+stars) and F503 (A stars-specific) at standard methodology with correct len≥2 baseline. Cross-dialectal y enrichment at pos1 for o-LF is consistent with y=LINE-OPENER universal affinity (F558): y@pos1 is elevated for multiple LF classes (ok-LF, ot-LF, o-LF all show y CONF or dir at pos1).

## F563: o→a CONF cross-dialectally (A herbal_a: E=3.08×/obs=67; B all: E=3.17×/obs=27) — strongest within-line bigram signal for o-onset; cross-dialectally conserved. Also o→o CONF both dialects (A: 1.72×/obs=31; B: 2.24×/obs=13). DEPL: o strongly avoids q-class (qot, qo, qok) and k, l, cth in both dialects.
**Experiment:** exp_547 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a (435 o-sender bigrams): o→a CONF (E=3.08×/obs=67) — dominant signal; o→o CONF (E=1.72×/obs=31); o→ckh CONF (E=1.67×/obs=10). DEPL: o→d (0.63×), o→qok (0.53×), o→ot (0.59×), o→k (0.45×), o→cth (0.57×), o→qo (0.46×), o→qot (0.49×), o→l (0.32×). B all (229 o-sender bigrams): o→a CONF (E=3.17×/obs=27); o→o CONF (E=2.24×/obs=13). DEPL: o→qok (0.50×), o→sh (0.57×), o→qot (0.68×), o→l (0.38×), o→qo (0.56×). Cross-dialectally conserved: o→a CONF (~3.1× in both); o→o CONF (both); DEPL of q-class template onsets. A-specific: o→ckh CONF (absent in B). o→ch is FLAT in both (~1.0×) — no avoidance (unlike sh→ch DEPL). The o→a coupling is the strongest cross-dialectally conserved within-line bigram found for any onset class in this project.

Compare: y→y CONF (A: 1.88×; B: 3.18× — only at CONF level); qot→qot CONF A (2.74×/obs=12). The o→a coupling is both stronger (E-value) and more frequent (higher obs) than most other characterized bigrams.

## F562: o positional — A herbal_a FLAT (pos1=1.40× sub-CONF; all positions 0.84–1.40×, none CONF or DEPL); B all LF CONF (E=1.58×/obs=57). O is the only major characterized class with no CONF positional signal in A herbal_a.
**Experiment:** exp_547 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a o: pos1=E=1.40×/obs=131 (sub-CONF, below E=1.5 threshold); MID=0.88×; LL=0.84×; LF=1.12×. No position reaches CONF or formal DEPL. O is positionally undistinctive in A herbal_a — all positions near baseline. This contrasts with all other characterized major classes: y (pos1 CONF 2.78×), ch (pos1 DEPL 0.38×), sh (LF DEPL 0.51×), d (LF CONF 1.52×), qot (pos1 CONF 1.79×), etc. B all o: LF CONF (E=1.58×/obs=57); pos1=1.00× (baseline); MID=0.89×. B o is a LF-enriched class. B o (LF CONF) + B d (pos1 CONF, F554) = partial positional complementarity: d opens B lines, o closes them.
**Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. A pos1 near-CONF (1.40× obs=131) is genuinely sub-CONF — not an underpowering artifact.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A o positional flatness is unique among characterized classes. This makes o the most "neutral" positional class in A herbal_a — appearing at all positions roughly proportional to baseline. Its functional distinctiveness is at the bigram level (o→a, o→o CONF) rather than positional level.

## F561: o vocabulary — A o=ol/or/ar body dominant (34.9%), y-body=19.6%, no edy-body; B o=y-body dominant (31.7%), ol/or/ar=27.2%, edy-body=13.2%. 'or' is top word in both dialects (~25%). A→B vocabulary shift parallels overall dialect pattern (A=o-lateral-body / B=y+edy-body).

**Finding:** A herbal_a o (541 tokens): or=25.7%, odaiin=5.4%, ody=3.0%, oraiin=2.8%, oaiin=2.6%. Body classes: ol/or/ar=34.9%, y-body=19.6%, aiin-body=16.6%, ch-bench=9.4%, no edy-body. Key: 'or' is the dominant word in both dialects (~25%). A o-onset: ol/or/ar-dominant (lateral body class), no edy-body. B o-onset: y-body and edy-body rise (paralleling overall B dialect shift). ## F560: A herbal_a d→d CL CONF (E=1.77×/obs=101) — d-LF paragraph self-chaining is dominant CL signal from d-LF; template-opener (qot/ot at pos1) d-LF lines show enhanced d→d CL (directional, insufficient N for formal threshold)
**Experiment:** exp_546 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a d-LF CL (N=311 same-folio consecutive pairs with d-LF sender): d→d CONF (E=1.77×/obs=101) — d-LF lines are followed by another d-LF line at CONF level.
