D self-succeeds at the paragraph/cross-line level: sequences of consecutive d-terminal lines occur at supra-baseline rate. Combined with F554 (d is dominant A LF class at 18.4%), this means d-terminal lines cluster into runs. Side finding: template-opener (qot or ot at pos1) d-LF lines show enhanced d→d CL — qot-opener d-LF: d→d E=2.45×/obs=9; ot-opener d-LF: d→d E=2.85×/obs=11 — both above the overall d→d rate of 1.77×. This is directional (N too small for formal CONF threshold) but consistent. H_new_FI NEGATIVE: qot-opener d-LF does NOT selectively enhance d→qot CL (E=4.26× but only obs=2 out of N=20). **Limitation:** A herbal_a only (n≤56). Template-opener subgroup analysis: N=20 (qot-opener) and N=21 (ot-opener) — too small for formal CONF threshold. The enhanced d→d CL for template openers is directional evidence only.

**Magnitude context:** d→d CL CONF (E=1.77×/obs=101) vs d→qot CL (E=1.37×/obs=10 here; F491 established CONF in original experiment). D is simultaneously: dominant A LF class (F554), CL self-successor (F560), and CL sender to qot (F491). The paragraph-level d-clustering is a structural property of A herbal_a text — not just a single-link coupling.

## F559: y within-line — y→y CONF cross-dialectally (A: E=1.88×/obs=40; B: E=3.18×/obs=20); y→ckh CONF A (E=1.73×/obs=13); y→k CONF B (E=1.68×/obs=11); y→ch BASELINE in both dialects

## F558: y positional — pos1 STRONGLY CONF in BOTH dialects (A: E=2.78×/obs=323; B: E=3.54×/obs=147); MID/LL/LF DEPLETED in both (~0.58-0.64×). Y is the definitive line-opener class.

**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a y: pos1=E=2.78×/obs=323 (CONF); MID=0.61× DEPL; LL=0.58× DEPL; LF=0.62× DEPL. B all y: pos1=E=3.54×/obs=147 (CONF); MID=0.64× DEPL; LL=0.58× DEPL; LF=0.60× DEPL. ALL other positions DEPLETED in both dialects. Y uniquely opens lines universally and avoids all other positions cross-dialectally. The y-class is the definitive VMS line-opener: 16.5% of A herbal_a line-starts are y-onset (vs 5.9% baseline); 11.5% of B line-starts are y (vs 3.2% baseline). Together with d (19.2% of B pos1), y and d account for 30.7% of all B line openings.

The cross-dialectal consistency (both A and B show CONF pos1 enrichment) makes y the most robustly characterized line-grammar class. Complete pos1/MID/LF depletion pattern: y occupies the line-opening slot with near-exclusive affinity.

## F557: y vocabulary — A y: gallows+body compounds (yk-, yt-, ych- dominant; no bare 'y'); B y: edy-body dominant (yteedy 6.4%, ykeedy 6.1%); highest type-token diversity of any characterized class (A: 274 types/671 tokens)

**Finding:** A herbal_a y (671 tokens, 274 types): top words ykeey(4.6%), ykaiin(3.7%), ykar(2.7%), ytaiin(2.4%), ychor(2.1%). Body classes: k-gallows+body (yk-), t-gallows+body (yt-), ch-bench+body (ych-). All compound forms, no bare 'y'. B all y (330 tokens, 140 types): yteedy(6.4%), ykeedy(6.1%), ytedy(3.9%), ykedy(3.3%); edy-body dominant. A→B vocabulary shift in y-class: A=gallows+complex-body; B=gallows+edy-body. Y maintains gallows onset affinity in both dialects while adopting B edy-body convention. Type-token ratio (A: 274/671 = 0.41) is the highest of any characterized class — y vocabulary is maximally diverse.
**Limitation:** Small body-class categories are approximate — 'other' captures overlapping forms.

## F556: A d-LF pos1: qot CONF (E=1.92×/obs=25) and ot CONF (E=1.72×/obs=24) — d-terminal A lines open with template classes; B d-LF pos1=qo dir (E=2.21×/obs=9)

**Date:** 2026-04-11

Combined with CL F491 (d-LF → qot-LF on next line), the paragraph structure is: Line_i=[qot/ot(pos1)...d(LF)] → Line_{i+1}=[...qot(LF)]. Template classes open d-terminal lines and appear at LF on subsequent lines. B all d-LF (N=121): pos1=qo dir (E=2.21×/obs=9, near-CONF) — B lines ending in d tend to open with qo-onset, consistent with B astro d→qo CL dir signal (F530). **Limitation:** A herbal_a n≤56; B all. B d-LF pos1=qo: obs=9, E=2.21× — dir threshold (obs≥5, E≥2.0×) met. Near-CONF.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A d-LF pos1=qot/ot CONF (E=1.72-1.92×, obs=24-25) — two template class CONF signals from same line. This nests with F491 (CL d→qot) to create a multi-line template structural pattern. The y-class is DEPLETED at pos1 in A d-LF (E=0.88×), consistent with the template/d coupling being the dominant opener structure.

## F554: A/B d positional INVERSION — A d: LF CONF (E=1.52×/obs=360); B d: pos1 CONF (E=2.64×/obs=246); MID-DEPLETED in BOTH (A: 0.73×; B: 0.67×). D is a structural edge class.

Cross-dialectal structural conserved property: MID-DEPLETED in both (A: 0.73×; B: 0.67×). D is a structural EDGE class — it appears at line boundaries and avoids interior positions universally.

**Magnitude context:** qok→qot E=2.22×/obs=12 (CONF) — directed (qot→qok sub-CONF 1.42×). SCOPE: A-herbal_a-SPECIFIC (exp_538: A stars=ZERO E=0.00×; A cosmo=DEPLETED E=0.53×). Does NOT form triplet chain: N=8 successor cases spread across 6 targets with no concentration (exp_538). The qok→qot coupling is a herbal-specific local pattern, not a general A-dialect rule.

## F541: qot/qok/ot share A=ch-mediated/B=edy-dominated vocabulary architecture; ok DIVERGES (aiin-dominated both dialects) — template class vocabulary taxonomy complete
**Experiment:** exp_537 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** qok vocabulary: A herbal_a (199 tokens, 57 types): qokchy dominant (17.6%), ch-mediated forms ~29%. B all (1929 tokens, 143 types): qokeedy+qokedy = 23.5%, qokain+qokaiin = 22.4%. Template class vocabulary taxonomy: {qot/qok/ot} = A:ch-mediated (29-36%) / B:edy-dominated (17-24%); ok = aiin-dominated in BOTH dialects (A: okaiin=12.3%; B: okaiin+okain=23.6%), ch-mediated ~12%. The vocabulary split is ok vs {qot, qok, ot}. qok LF-depleted cross-dialectally (A: 0.57×, B: 0.58×) is the structural positional signature of qok. All four template class vocabularies now characterized.
**Limitation:** B all pools all B-dialect sections. ok's aiin dominance is quantitative, not absolute — edy is still present (B ok edy+eedy=15.6%).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The vocabulary split (ok vs qot/qok/ot) aligns with the self-succession tier split (ok=A-only vs qot/ot=both-dialect, qok intermediate). ok is structurally the most divergent template class.

## F540: B ok-LF lines open with t-onset at CONF (E=1.95×/obs=16); A ok-LF pos1=s dir (E=2.22×/obs=5)

The B ok-LF → t CONF signal is new and unexpected: t-onset openers specifically co-occur with ok-terminal lines in B-dialect. ## F539: Template class positional hierarchy (A): qot(CONF)>qok(near-CONF)>ot(neutral)>ok(neutral) at pos1; qo-prefix confers line-opener tendency
**Experiment:** exp_536 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a pos1 enrichment for all four template classes: qot=E=1.79×/obs=59 (CONF, F533); qok=E=1.47×/obs=62 (near-CONF, just below threshold); ot=E=1.29×/obs=53 (sub-CONF); ok=E=1.10×/obs=53 (neutral). Gradient: qot > qok > ot > ok. qo-prefix confers line-opener tendency: both qot and qok are pos1-elevated (CONF or near-CONF) while non-prefixed ot and ok are neutral. LF: qok DEPLETED in both dialects (A: E=0.57×; B: E=0.58×) while others near-baseline. B-dialect: all four depleted at pos1 (ot=0.34×, ok=0.49×, qot=0.60×, qok=0.88×) — B excludes all template classes from pos1. The qok/ok spatial pair hypothesis (H589_archived) is CLOSED NEGATIVE: no discrete spatial pair, only a qo-prefix gradient.
**Limitation:** qok near-CONF (E=1.47×) is below the CONF threshold (E=1.5×) — the gradient is confirmed at threshold level only for qot. All based on A herbal_a n≤56 and B all.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The 4-class gradient (1.79→1.47→1.29→1.10×) is the first complete positional hierarchy for the template class group. qok's LF depletion in BOTH dialects (E=0.57-0.58×) is the only cross-dialectal consistent LF signal in the template group.

## F538: ot and qot share identical vocabulary architecture: A = ch-mediated dominant; B = edy+eedy dominant — template parallel
**Experiment:** exp_535 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** ot vocabulary (193 A tokens/59 types; 943 B tokens/161 types) parallels qot vocabulary quantitatively: A ch-mediated forms = ~30% (otchy+otchol+otchor+otchey+otcho) vs qot ~36.5%; B edy+eedy = 17.1% (vs qot 22.2%); aiin/ain bodies A=6.2%/B=17.9% vs qot A=5.2%/B=17.2%; al/ar/ol/or bodies A=15.5%/B=15.5% vs qot A=15%/B=16.4%. The A=ch-dominated/B=edy-dominated vocabulary structure is a general property of the qo-prefixed template class pair {qot, ot}. The proportions differ (qot has more ch-mediation in A, more edy in B) but the structural topology is identical.
**Limitation:** ot type count (59 A types, 161 B types) vs qot (44 A types, 82 B types) — ot is more lexically diverse. Both based on B all (all B-dialect sections pooled).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Quantitative parallel across four vocabulary categories. The template pair vocabulary architecture is the most complete cross-class structural parallel identified in this project.

## F537: ot→ot CONF cross-dialectally (A: E=1.79×/obs=11; B: E=2.12×/obs=124); A ot→qo dir (E=2.24×/obs=7); ot→ch DEPLETED both dialects

**Finding:** ot within-line bigrams: (1) ot→ot self-succession CONF in both dialects (A: E=1.79×/obs=11; B: E=2.12×/obs=124) — re-confirms F369 with current methodology. B ot self-succession stronger than B qot (2.12× vs 1.93×). (2) A ot→qo dir (E=2.24×/obs=7) — new within-line coupling, not seen for qot. (3) B ot→a near-CONF (E=1.43×/obs=64). (4) KEY: ot→ch DEPLETED within-line in BOTH dialects (A: E=0.77×/obs=30; B: E=0.85×/obs=129). This contrasts with qot→ch which is BASELINE (A: E=1.06×; B: E=1.20×, F535). ot→qot is baseline in B (E=0.95×/obs=29), despite qot→ot being CONF (F534) — asymmetric coupling. B ot also depletes qok and sh as successor classes.

**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** ot→ch DEPL (E=0.77-0.85×) vs qot→ch BASELINE (E=1.06-1.20×): this is the primary within-line structural distinction between the two template classes. ot→ot CONF in both dialects confirms F369 with modern methodology.

## F536: B-dialect ot-onset STRONGLY DEPLETED at pos1 (E=0.34×/obs=42); A ot NEUTRAL at pos1 (E=1.29×/obs=53, sub-CONF)

B ot is a MID/LL-biased class. The qot/ot template pair: A qot=LINE OPENER (pos1 CONF, F533); A ot=NEUTRAL (pos1 sub-CONF); B qot=pos1-depleted (E=0.60×); B ot=strongly pos1-depleted (E=0.34×). qot is the more positionally constrained (= "hotter") template class; ot is the neutral/background partner.

## F535: qot→ch within-line is BASELINE in both dialects (A: E=1.06×; B: E=1.20×); F490/F491 CL chain is INTER-LINE only
**Experiment:** exp_534 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** Within-line qot→ch succession is near-baseline in BOTH A herbal_a (E=1.06×/obs=39) and B all (E=1.20×/obs=102). The famous d→qot→ch cross-line chain (F490/F491, CONF) operates exclusively at the between-line (CL) level — it is a paragraph-structure phenomenon. Within a single line, after a qot-onset word, ch-onset is NOT specifically enriched. qot's within-line grammar is instead: (A) self-succession (qot→qot CONF, E=2.74×/obs=12), mild routing to y (E=1.59×) and t (E=1.73×); (B) qot→ot CONF (E=1.58×/obs=52), qot→qot CONF (E=1.93×/obs=33), qot→r CONF (E=1.78×/obs=12). The CL and within-line qot grammars are structurally distinct.
**Limitation:** A herbal_a (141 qot sender bigrams); B all (456 qot sender bigrams). B all pools all B-dialect sections.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** Within-line qot→ch: E=1.06× (A), E=1.20× (B) — baseline. CL qot→ch (F490): E=1.58×/obs=48 (CONF). The contrast is structural: CL vs within-line grammar are different mechanisms.

## F534: B-dialect qot is a MID class (pos1 DEPL E=0.60×); dominant vocabulary qotedy+qoteedy (22.2%); rich within-line grammar
**Experiment:** exp_534 (2026-04-11)

(2) Vocabulary: qotedy+qoteedy dominate (22.2% combined), followed by qotain+qotaiin (17.2%), qotal+qotar (16.4%). This is completely different from A-dialect where qotchy dominates (20.7%). **Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** pos1 DEPL E=0.60× (obs=39). qot→ot CONF E=1.58×/obs=52. The A/B positional inversion for qot (A: pos1 CONF vs B: pos1 DEPL) is the sharpest dialect contrast for this onset class.

## F533: A herbal_a qot-onset is a LINE-OPENING class (pos1 CONF, E=1.79×/obs=59); self-clustering grammar

## F532: A stars a-onset ABSENT at pos1 (E≈0.07×/obs=1); CONF at pos2 (14.8%) and pen (9.8%) — cross-class "non-opener" rule
**Experiment:** exp_533 (2026-04-11)
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A stars a-onset positional profile (136 lines): pos1=0.8% (1/130 — near-zero), pos2=14.8% (18/122), pen=9.8% (12/122), LF=11.0% (15/136). The pos1 near-zero is a cross-class rule: a-onset words virtually NEVER open A stars lines despite being 11% of LF. Within-section E: pos1 ≈ 0.07× vs equal-position null (STRONGLY DEPLETED); pos2 ≈ 1.35× (slightly elevated). Contrast: t-onset and s-onset are CONF at pos1 (F523, F524). A stars has a positional complementarity: t/s = line OPENERS (CONF pos1); a = line NON-OPENER (near-zero pos1). The cross-A herbal_a E values are large (pos2 E=20×, pen E=8×, CONF) but reflect A herbal_a's near-absence of a-onset words overall (LF=1.7%), not meaningful enrichment. The meaningful signal is the within-A-stars pos1 near-zero.
**Limitation:** A stars 136 lines total. Only 1 a-onset word at pos1 — robust zero, not noisy. The per-LF-class analysis shows ot-LF pos2=a (dir, F520) and sh-LF pen=a (dir, F519) are the class-specific contributors; the cross-class pattern is the pos1 near-zero.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** E≈0.07× at pos1 (STRONGLY DEPLETED); cross-A-herbal_a pos2 E=20.4×/obs=18 (CONF). The near-zero pos1 is the structural finding. t/s/a positional complementarity is a distinctive A stars grammar feature.

**Experiment:** exp_528 (2026-04-11)

**Magnitude context:** E=4.19× for the conditional signal is notably strong for a pen rule. This is the most detailed within-section line-grammar characterization achieved for any LF class, showing that even within one LF class (ot), there are at least two distinct paragraph formulas in A herbal_a.

## F455: A herbal_a ok-LF → y at pos1 (E=1.62×/N=12, Confirmed); Bidirectional ok/y Grammar Pair
**Experiment:** exp_480_a_herbal_ok_lf_and_pharma_qok
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** A herbal_a ok-LF lines (N=53): y at pos1 E=1.62×(obs=12/53 = 22.6% vs 14.0% baseline; confirmed N≥10, E≥1.5×). LF words: oky(11), okaiin(5), okol(3), okain(3), okal(2). d DEPLETED at pos1 (E=0.45×/N=4). Directional: ok self at pen (E=3.04×/N=7), s at pos1 (E=2.04×/N=5), ok at pos2 (E=2.50×/N=5). Combined with F438 (A ok→y CL: ok at LL → y at next LF, E=1.52×/N=16), this establishes a bidirectional ok/y grammar pair in A herbal_a: ok at LF → y at pos1 (within-line, this finding) AND ok at LL → y at next LF (cross-line, F438). The ok/y pair suggests these onset classes are functionally linked: ok closes lines that began with y, and y opens the next line after ok-terminal lines.
**Limitation:** ok-LF N=53 (adequate). y at pos1: 12/53 obs. Cross-line direction (F438) uses all A-dialect, not herbal_a-specific — the bidirectional claim requires noting that F438 was section-general while F455 is herbal_a-specific.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** E=1.62×(N=12) for y at pos1. The bidirectional ok/y pair is the first documented case of a within-line routing rule (LF→pos1) pairing with a cross-line rule (LL→next-LF) for the same onset class pair. It suggests ok and y are grammatically complementary in A herbal_a paragraph structure.

**Magnitude context:** E=1.75×(N=15) for ot at pen. The doublet structure [ot...ot] at pen+LF parallels the ch-self-succession at pos1 (F449) and l-self-succession at pen (F451, E=2.18×), suggesting B pharma has a general pattern of onset-class persistence at adjacent positions for its major LF classes. F460 extends F450 to B-dialect-wide (E=2.24×/N=25).

## F447: B-Dialect Section LF Grammar Taxonomy: B herbal t-LF(2.34×/N=38)+y-LF(1.52×/N=55); B astro q-bench triplet qok(1.78×)+qot(1.94×/N=29)+qo(1.60×/N=34); B pharma ok-LF(1.47×/N=44)+o-LF(1.53×/N=36); B cosmo t-LF(2.23×/N=16); Cross-Dialectal: Both A+B cosmo t-LF Elevated and qot-LF~0
**Experiment:** exp_467_b_section_lf_grammar

(a) **B herbal** (f1-72, B-dialect folios): t-LF E=2.34×(N=38), y-LF E=1.52×(N=55), ot-LF E=1.55×(N=9), p-LF E=1.53×(N=8); qok-LF DEPLETED 0.54×(N=17), ok-LF 0.50×(N=5), ch-LF 0.59×(N=7).
(b) **B astro** (f73-84): q-bench triplet: qok-LF E=1.78×(N=149) [F431 confirmed] + qot-LF E=1.94×(N=29) [NEW] + qo-LF E=1.60×(N=34) [NEW]; s-LF E=1.31×(N=128); y-LF DEPLETED 0.47×(N=45) — the strongest y-depletion in any section; t-LF 0.70×.
(c) **B pharma** (f103-116): ok-LF E=1.47×(N=44), o-LF E=1.53×(N=36), ch-LF E=1.30×(N=46); qok-LF DEPLETED 0.52×(N=49), t-LF 0.62×(N=30), qot-LF 0.42×(N=7).

The cosmo content (f85-102) is the only section where A and B dialects agree on a shared LF grammar marker (t-LF elevated). **B astro F431 extension**: qot and qo were not previously identified as B astro LF markers. F431 covered only qok. The q-bench triplet elevation makes B astro the only section with three same-class onsets (qok+qot+qo) all elevated at LF. **B herbal t-LF → pos2: ch elevated E=4.09×(N=7)** — directional B herbal formula routing (t-opened lines tend to have ch at pos2). l-LF is NOT a B pharma marker (E=0.82×/N=21 — near-baseline; F423 l-chain concentration is within-line, not LF-class).

**Magnitude context:** B herbal t-LF (2.34×) is the strongest new section LF marker found. B astro qot-LF (1.94×) is the second-strongest overall (after herbal t). The B section LF taxonomy shows three distinct "LF chemistry profiles" roughly corresponding to: (1) early herbal/cosmo: {t dominant}; (2) astro: {q-bench dominant}; (3) pharma: {ok/o dominant} — a progression through the manuscript that parallels content domains.

## F445: A-Dialect Cross-Line Grammar Is Section-Specific: herbal_a Concentrates s→qot (E=3.2×/N=5) and s→s (E=3.0×/N=4); ch→ch and ok→y Shared Across herbal_a+cosmo; A "Stars" Section Shows No Cross-Line Couplings; A Less Section-Differentiated Than B
**Experiment:** exp_464_a_cl_section_specificity
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** A-dialect cross-line onset couplings are section-specific (993 total A-dialect CL pairs; herbal_a N=673, cosmo N=234, stars N=86). Section taxonomy: (a) herbal_a-concentrated: s→qot CL E=3.2×(N=5, F443's F443 primary source), s→s CL E=3.0×(N=4), sh→d CL E=1.9×(N=8); (b) cross-section (herbal_a+cosmo): ch→ch CL: herbal_a=1.5×(N=22), cosmo=2.2×(N=6); ok→y CL: herbal_a=1.7×(N=11), cosmo=1.8×(N=5); (c) absent from stars (f57-72, N=86 CL pairs): all tested cross-line couplings at baseline or zero (ch→ch: 0 cases; ok→y: 0 cases; s→qot: 0 cases). Additional result: d→sh CL is WEAK in A (overall E=1.13×/N=24, herbal_a=1.3×) — in contrast to B's d→sh CL (E=1.78×/N=16, herbal+pharma-concentrated). New from matrix: A cth→sh CL E=1.9×(N=12) — previously unexamined cross-line coupling. A/B comparison: B's cross-line section grammar has three distinct domain specializations (astro: ch→qot; herbal: ok→y+d→sh; pharma: qok→s). A's is less differentiated: ch→ch and ok→y appear in BOTH major A sections (herbal_a and cosmo), while s→qot is herbal_a-specific. Both dialects show herbal-section elevation of ok→y CL (A herbal_a=1.7×, B herbal=2.1×).
**Limitation:** Section-specific cells in A have lower N than B findings. herbal_a s→qot N=5, s→s N=4 are borderline. Stars N=86 result (all-zero) is informative but cannot exclude weak effects (E≤1.3×) at that sample size. cosmo ch→ch N=6 is small. All section-specific E values are directional by standard thresholds except herbal_a ch→ch (N=22) and herbal_a ok→y (N=11).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The herbal_a vs cosmo distinction suggests that A s→qot CL (F443) is specifically a herbal_a paragraph-level transition, while A ch-self-succession persists across A sections. B has no analog for A s→qot CL (B s→qot ≈ baseline); the herbal_a concentration of this rule makes it a specifically A herbal cross-line grammar element.

## F444: B Cross-Line Grammar Is Section-Specific: Astro ch→qot CL (E=1.9×/N=6); Herbal ok→y (E=2.1×/N=10) + d→sh (E=2.3×/N=5); Pharma qok→s (E=1.7×/N=13); Cross-Line Section Grammar Parallels Within-Line Formula Taxonomy (F430)
**Experiment:** exp_462_cl_section_specificity
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** B-dialect cross-line coupling enrichments are section-differentiated. ch→qot CL (F442: overall E=1.55×/N=9): 6/9 cases from astro, E=1.9× in astro. ok→y CL (F438: overall E=1.64×/N=21): herbal E=2.1×(N=10) and astro E=2.1×(N=4); pharma near-baseline (1.0×/N=7). d→sh CL (F438: overall E=1.78×/N=16): herbal E=2.3×(N=5), pharma E=1.8×(N=4); astro 1.2×. qok→s CL (F438: overall E=1.52×/N=31): pharma E=1.7×(N=13), astro 1.2×(N=16 — composition-driven, not grammar-driven). sh→d CL (F438: overall E=1.57×/N=19): herbal E=2.1×(N=5), pharma E=1.6×(N=7). Section grammar cross-line taxonomy: (a) ASTRO: ch→qot CL; (b) HERBAL: ok→y CL + d→sh/sh→d CL; (c) PHARMA: qok→s CL; (d) herbal+pharma share: d→sh and sh→d. This maps onto within-line section grammar (F430): astro has qok-LF formula types (F431); herbal has d→ch→y and y→sh→ch formulas; pharma has l-LF and qok-formula types. The cross-line grammar section structure is a PARAGRAPH-LEVEL EXTENSION of the within-line section grammar: the same content domains (astro/herbal/pharma) that produce distinct within-line formula sequences also produce distinct paragraph-level line transitions.
**Limitation:** All section-specific E values are directional (herbal ok→y: N=10, highest for any single section finding; astro ch→qot: N=6; pharma qok→s: N=13). Some section-E values depend on section-specific LF baseline (d→qok astro: 20/26 cases from astro but E=1.4×, explained by astro's elevated qok-LF — composition effect rather than grammar). Bio and text sections have essentially no representation in any CL coupling (0 cases most), suggesting bio/text paragraphs don't follow the same cross-line grammar.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The section-specificity of cross-line grammar means that the F438/F442/F443 within-section E values can exceed the cross-section aggregate by up to 40% (herbal ok→y: 2.1× vs overall 1.64×). The section structure is a moderately important factor for cross-line grammar interpretation — the aggregate E values underestimate the strength of section-specific cross-line rules.

## F443: A/B s Cross-Line Secondary Target Inversion: A s at LL → qot CL (E=2.82×/N=6); B s at LL → qok CL (E=1.48×/N=6); Both Dialects s→s CL Stable (A=2.58×/B=2.15×); s+aiin-body Drives s Self-Succession in A (E=3.64×/N=5)
**Experiment:** exp_460_a_s_crossline
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** A-dialect s at LL generates two elevated cross-line targets: →qot (E=2.82×/N=6, confirmed from exp_459 directional) and →s self-succession (E=2.58×/N=8, F438 re-confirmed). Word diversity: 4 unique LL s-words, 5 unique LF qot-words, 5/6 unique pairs from 6 different folios (f8r/f14r/f15r/f47v/f49v/f87v) — class-level rule. B-dialect s at LL generates: →s (E=2.15×/N=10) and →qok (E=1.48×/N=6); B s→qot = 1.50×(N=1, essentially absent). A/B inversion in secondary target: A s→qot; B s→qok. The s→s self-succession (primary) is cross-dialectally stable. Body-class driver of A s→s: aiin-body (s+aiin: E=3.64×/N=5) — consistent with F441 principle (aiin-body drives cross-line self-succession). Body-class driver of A s→qot: y-body tentative (3/6 cases), directional only. Mechanism interpretation: A-dialect paragraph transitions from s-modal phase to qot-modal phase (consistent with A qot's high LL-enrichment in A dialect); B-dialect transitions from s-modal to qok-modal. Both dialects have s-persistence across lines. The complementary B finding: ch-LL → qot-LF (F442: E=1.56×); A s-LL → qot-LF suggests different paragraph-entry paths to qot onset by dialect.
**Limitation:** A s→qot N=6 is directional. The folio and word diversity (6 folios, 5/6 unique pairs) provides confidence that this is not a single-folio artifact. y-body as driver of s→qot is directional only (N=3). B s→qok N=6 is also directional. Neither the A s→qot nor B s→qok is large enough for formal enrichment statistics at standard thresholds.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A s→qot E=2.82× is comparable to A s→s (2.58×), suggesting qot-opening is roughly as likely as s-continuation after an A s-terminal line. This is a strong effect for N=6. The A/B inversion ({s,qot} vs {s,qok}) is the most specific A/B cross-line grammar difference identified for the s-onset class.

## F442: A/B ch Cross-Line Routing Inversion: B ch+edy at LL → qot CL (E=2.36×/N=7); A ch+edy at LL → ch CL (E=2.96×/N=13); B Overall ch→qot CL E=1.65×(N=9); A Overall ch→ch CL E=1.66×(N=28); Within-Line ch+edy Is Flat in B
**Experiment:** exp_458_ch_body_conditional
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** B ch+edy (chedy/cheey, first body char='e', N=142 at LL) at LL predicts qot onset at the next line's LF: E=2.36×(N=7). Within-line B ch+edy → all successors near-baseline (qok=1.17×, qot=1.05×, sh=1.03×, d=1.08× — no body-conditional preference within-line). Therefore B ch+edy→qot is a distinct cross-line rule with no within-line precedent. A ch+edy (N=52 at LL) at LL predicts ch onset at next LF: E=2.96×(N=13) — strengthening F441's finding (from 2.79×). A ch+edy→qot CL: E=0.00×(N=0) — completely absent. Overall: B ch at LL → qot CL E=1.65×(N=9), qok depleted (0.54×↓); A ch at LL → ch CL E=1.66×(N=28). This is the first documented case of a body-conditional cross-line rule with full A/B routing inversion for the same body class (ch+edy): B routes to qot, A routes to ch. Additional directional: B ch+aiin→d CL (E=1.88×/N=6); A ch+aiin→sh CL (E=3.73×/N=4) — consistent with H_new_U: aiin-body drives d (B) or sh (A) cross-line routing; B ch+d-body within-line → y (E=2.41×/N=5, directional).
**Limitation:** B ch+edy→qot: N=7 events is directional. The finding is corroborated by two independent analyses (exp_457: E=2.23×; exp_458: E=2.36×) and by the body-class specificity (edy-body not aiin-body drives qot). A ch+edy→ch: N=13 is adequate (F441 confirmed at stronger E). A ch+aiin→sh: N=4 is directional. B ch+d-body within-line → y: N=5 directional.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A/B routing inversion (B→qot vs A→ch) is a cross-dialectal discrimination marker at the cross-line body-conditional level — the third layer of grammar discrimination (after onset-class level and body-conditional within-line level). The B ch→qot cross-line association (E=1.65×) is weaker than the within-line formula-typed findings (E=2-4×) but is the first paragraph-level (LL→next-LF) body-conditional rule with full A/B inversion documented at N≥7. The A overall ch→ch CL (1.66×/N=28) is now the most robustly confirmed A cross-line self-succession rule.

## F441: Cross-Line Body-Conditional Couplings: F438 Rules Are Driven by Aiin-Body LL Words; B d+aiin→sh CL E=1.99×(N=14); B qok+aiin→s CL E=1.76×(N=17); B s+aiin→s CL E=2.60×(N=7); A ch+edy→ch CL E=2.79×(N=13); Within-Line vs Cross-Line Routing Differs
**Experiment:** exp_455_crossline_body_conditional
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** Body-conditional cross-line bigrams reveal that F438's cross-line couplings are specifically driven by the aiin-body (first body char='a': daiin/saiin/qokain-type words) LL subclass. B d+a-body → sh at next LF (E=1.99×/N=14 vs d→sh overall E=1.79×/N=16); B d+a-body → qok at next LF (E=1.68×/N=22); B qok+a-body → s at next LF (E=1.76×/N=17 vs qok→s overall E=1.51×/N=31); B s+a-body → s at next LF (E=2.60×/N=7 — drives F438's s→s cross-line self-succession). A ch+e-body (chedy/cheey) → ch at next LF (E=2.79×/N=13 — drives F438's A ch→ch cross-line, E=1.57×/N=28). General pattern: aiin-body LL words (d/s/qok+aiin) are cross-line bridge words routing to diverse subsequent-line LF classes; edy-body LL words (ch/qok+edy) drive same-class cross-line self-succession. Critical contrast: within-line (F439) qok+a-body → sh (E=1.73×), but cross-line (F441) qok+a-body → s (E=1.76×), NOT sh — the same body class has different grammatical routing depending on position context (MID within-line vs LL→LF cross-line).
**Limitation:** qok body N for cross-line: a-body N=68, e-body N=40. s+a-body N=19 (7 obs). All directional cases N<10 labeled as such. The negative (qok+a-body → sh NOT elevated cross-line) is based on moderate N (expected N=9.6, obs=17 for qok+a→s vs expected N for qok+a→sh would need separate tabulation). Within-vs-cross routing difference rests on comparing two different analytical frameworks (within-line MID bigrams vs cross-line LL→LF).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** B d+a-body→sh CL E=1.99× exceeds the onset-class-level B d→sh E=1.79× by 11%, showing the body-class analysis provides additional specificity. s+a-body→s (E=2.60×, N=7) is very high but small N. The A ch+e-body→ch finding (E=2.79×, N=13) is the clearest case where a body class specifically predicts a cross-line coupling: chedy/cheey words ending a line predict ch-onset words opening the next line at 2.79× above chance.

## F440: A/B Vocabulary Overlap is Frequency-Stratified: f≥20 Words 100%/82.6% Shared; Hapaxes 20.8%/13.8% Shared; l/r/p Near-B-Exclusive (Jaccard 0.024-0.082); B-Specific Vocabulary Edy-Class Dominated; All 64 High-Frequency A Words Appear in B
**Experiment:** exp_452_ab_vocab_overlap
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** A has 2,213 word types; B has 2,937; 796 shared (36.0% A, 27.1% B). Token coverage: A=74.9%, B=67.7% from shared-type words. Frequency-stratification: f≥20: A 100%/B 82.6% shared; f=2-4: A 56%/B 39%; hapax: A 20.8%/B 13.8%. All 64 A high-freq words (f≥20) appear in B; 21/121 B high-freq words absent from A (all edy-class: qokeedy/qokedy/otedy/qotedy). Onset class Jaccard: ok=0.249(highest), qok=0.244, sh=0.227, ch=0.212, y=0.202; l=0.082, r=0.053, p=0.024(lowest). l/r/p are near-B-exclusive classes (F423 pharma-l, F382 LL-r, B p-formula). cth is A-dominant: A=56 types/B=16 types; 62.5% of B-cth types appear in A (B uses a subset of A's cth vocabulary). B-exclusive high-freq vocabulary dominated by edy-suffix forms (qokeedy=248, qokedy=206, otedy=95). A-biased shared words: cthol(44:1), cthy(25:1), chor(6.58:1). Interpretation: A and B are dialectal variants of a common system sharing core vocabulary but diverging in: (a) suffix preferences for rare words (B: edy; A: ol/ch-midfix); (b) B-exclusive grammatical classes (l/r/p); (c) overall B has 33% more word types than A despite only 87% more tokens (B is less repetitive in rare-word production).
**Limitation:** Overlap is computed at the word-type level (exact string match), not at the morphological-stem level. Two cognate words with different suffixes (chol vs chedy) count as non-overlapping. This underestimates morphological relatedness. Folio-level noise (a folio miscategorized as A when it has mixed content) can inflate apparent A/B overlap slightly.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** 100% overlap of high-frequency words (f≥20) is very strong evidence against "completely separate systems" — if A and B were independent, we'd expect ~5-10% random overlap by chance given 2213/2937 types from a 5000-type pool. Observed 36%/27% overall overlap is 3-7× above chance. The frequency stratification (100% at high freq, 14-21% at hapax) mirrors the pattern in natural language dialectal variation where core vocabulary is shared and rare vocabulary diverges.

## F439: Body-Suffix Class Conditional Bigram Rules: B qok Aiin-Body → sh (E=1.73×/N=94), qok Edy-Body → qok Self-Succession (E=1.52×/N=165); Complete Within-Class Inversion (Same Onset, Opposite Successor Routing by Suffix Body); Also B ol/ok Body Splits; A e-Body → qo Rule (E=1.66-1.83×)
**Experiment:** exp_451_body_conditional_bigrams
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** H_new_M CONFIRMED. Body-conditional succession rules are a GENERAL feature of VMS grammar, not specific to sh→qok (F372). Strongest case — B qok onset class: words with 'a' as first body char (aiin-suffix: qokain/qokaiin/qokar/qokal, N_pred=435) have sh-successor rate 21.6% vs 7.4% for edy-body words → E=1.73× for sh; edy-body words (qokeedy/qokedy/qokeey, N_pred=608) have qok-successor rate 27.1% vs 5.3% for aiin-body → E=1.52×. Complete within-class inversion: qok+aiin-body → sh(↑), qok-self(↓); qok+edy-body → sh(↓), qok-self(↑). Also confirmed: B ol body-split (bare 'ol' → ch/k elevated, compound ol+c/s → qok elevated); B ok+e-body→l (E=1.63×/N=26) vs ok+a-body→l depleted (E=0.30×/N=5); B ch+'d'-body → ch/ok elevated; B ch+'o'-body → k elevated. A-dialect: e-body → qo elevated (sh+'e'→qo E=1.66×/N=13; ch+'e'→qo E=1.83×/N=10; ok+'e'→d+qok elevated). A's qo occupies the role B's qok has in e-body routing. Interpretation: VMS has a two-level succession grammar. Level 1: onset class (primary selector). Level 2: suffix body class (conditional router within onset class). The suffix body of a word influences the successor onset class, violating word-level independence from suffix structure.
**Limitation:** Body-char analysis uses first character after onset as proxy for suffix class. Some body chars may index multiple suffix types (e.g., 'c' could indicate ch-compound or ckhy-compound). A-dialect N values are small (N=10-15 for most findings). No control corpus comparison for generality of body-conditional rules.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The qok aiin/edy bifurcation (E=1.73× and 1.52× with N=94 and N=165) is larger than the onset-class-level qok self-succession finding (B qok self-succession MID E=1.16×, F380). Body-conditional routing has stronger E than the onset-class grammar for this case. This implies the SUFFIX CLASS carries grammatical information about word position in a sequence — a finding with implications for any mechanism model: pure positional slot models cannot generate body-conditional bigram rules (they place onset classes without body conditioning); copy-buffer models could generate this if the buffer retains word-level body class correlations.

## F438: Cross-Line Onset Grammar: Self-Succession Persists Across Lines (s→s A=2.57×/B=2.20×; ch→ch A=1.57×; y→y B=1.62×; ok→y A=1.52×/B=1.64×); Cross-Line/Within-Line Inversion Pattern (sh→d: CL=1.58×/pLL→LL=0.61× in B); B d→sh E=1.79×/l→sh E=1.63×/d→qok E=1.56×/qok→s E=1.51× Cross-Line Couplings
**Experiment:** exp_445_crossline_onset_matrix
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** Cross-line onset bigrams (LL of line N → LF of line N+1) reveal systematic grammar distinct from within-line grammar. Three rule classes: (1) Self-succession across lines: s→s (A=2.57×/N=8; B=2.20×/N=10), ch→ch (A=1.57×/N=28), y→y (B=1.62×/N=8), A qot→qot (3.10×/N=5). ok→y is cross-dialectally consistent (A=1.52×/N=16; B=1.64×/N=21) — ok at LL predicts y at next-line LF. (2) Cross-line inversion: onset pairs depleted within-line (pre_LL→LL) are enriched cross-line. B sh→d: CL=1.58×/N=19 vs within-line pLL→LL=0.61×. B d→qok: CL=1.56×/N=26 vs within=0.66×. A ol→d: CL=1.67×/N=8 vs within=0.27×. (3) B-specific structural couplings: d→sh (1.79×/N=16), l→sh (1.63×/N=19), qok→s (1.51×/N=31). B qok→s connects to B s-LF → sh-pos1 → qok formula chain (F326/F376): qok at LL ends the formula sequence, s starts the next line. A-specific: cth→sh (1.93×/N=12), o→s (2.21×/N=8). Notable depletions: B d→ol (E=0.19×/exp=5.1), B qok→ok (0.34×), B ch→ot (0.38×).
**Limitation:** Cross-line N counts are smaller than within-line (A=993 pairs, B=1495 pairs). Small-N results (N=3-4) reported but unreliable. Pre_LL→LL within-line comparison uses a different position pair; not a perfect within-vs-cross-line comparison. No folio-boundary control (some cross-line pairs may span different content sections).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** ok→y cross-line (A=1.52×/B=1.64×) is the first documented cross-line onset coupling with N>15 in both dialects. The cross-line inversion pattern (within-depleted → cross-enriched) has no prior documented parallel in this project. B d→sh cross-line (1.79×) is slightly stronger than B d→sh within-line bigram (~1.5× in F373). s→s cross-line (2.57×/2.20×) exceeds s self-succession values in any other context for A-dialect (s self-succession was not previously characterized as a leading rule). The B qok→s cross-line N=31 is the largest-N cross-line finding.

## F437: Onset Classes Have Differentiated Internal Structure (Exploratory): y-Onset Requires Midfix (A=12.9%/B=8.9% Zero-Midfix, Mean=1.98-2.05); B-qok/qot/ok/ot Skeleton Classes (75-83% Zero-Midfix); d-Onset Skeleton in A (73.7%); d+aiin=35%(A)/24%(B) Most Suffix-Concentrated; B-qok Structural Shift (83% vs A 54%) Explains F434 Vocabulary Divergence
**Experiment:** exp_438_stolfi_onset_structure
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** H492 ANSWERED (exploratory). A-dialect structural clusters: skeleton onsets (>70% zero-midfix): d(73.7%)/cth(73.6%); complex onset (lowest zero-midfix): y(12.9%, MeanMF=1.98), qo(39%)/sh(39%)/ch(42%)/o(42%). B-dialect skeleton onsets: qok(83.4%)/qot(77.6%)/ok(75.3%)/ot(75.2%)/d(72.5%); complex: y(8.9%, MeanMF=2.05)/l(36.5%)/o(42.8%). y-onset has near-universal midfix requirement in BOTH dialects — not independent of midfix (morphological constraint, not just frequency artifact). B-qok zero-midfix=83.4% vs A-qok=54.3% (29-point shift) explains F288/F434's qok midfix length divergence. d+aiin = highest suffix concentration: 35%(A)/24%(B). l-onset B: top suffix 'chedy'=14% (consistent with lchedy compound class; F423 l-pharma). Suffix entropy range: cth=3.10(low/restricted) → y=4.25(A)/4.17(B)(high/diverse). Onset class taxonomy: skeleton+aiin = d/qot(B); skeleton+edy = qok(B)/cth; complex+diverse = y.
**Limitation:** Exploratory analysis; no pre-registration; no control corpus comparison; suffix stripping calibration affects zero-midfix counts. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** y-onset's 12.9%/8.9% zero-midfix is the single most extreme structural property of any onset class — most onset classes have 40-85% zero-midfix, but y is at 8.9-12.9% (5-10× less skeleton-like). This means y-words are structurally equivalent to compound forms in other languages — they almost always carry additional characters between onset and suffix. This may explain why y-onset generates more word types per token (high type/token ratio in both dialects) and higher suffix entropy — it's not just a different onset character, it's a morphologically different template.

## F436: B-Dialect edy-Class Suffix Fraction by Onset Class: sh=45.8%(HIGHEST)/qok=40.4%/ch=36.1%/ok=30.5%/ot=28.5%/y=28.2%/ol=15.9%/s=4.9%/d=4.3%(LOWEST); Template Onsets (sh/qok/ch/ok/ot) Prefer edy-Class; Content Onsets (d/s) Anti-edy; Suffix Entropy NOT Correlated With Hapax Rate (Spearman<0.25 in Both Dialects)
**Experiment:** exp_437_suffix_entropy_hapax
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** H497 (negative) + H_new_B ANSWERED. H497: Spearman(SufH, hapax_rate)=0.071(A)/0.242(B) — no significant correlation in either dialect. Suffix diversity does NOT predict hapax rate; A shows moderate Spearman(SufH, type/token)=0.554 (more diverse suffix → more word types per token) but this collapses in B (rho=-0.035). H_new_B: B-qok edy fraction=40.4% is NOT unusual — sh=45.8% is higher and ch=36.1% is similar. Structural split: template/gallows-class onsets (sh/qok/ch/ok/ot) prefer edy-class suffixes at 28-46%; content/rare onsets (d/s) prefer aiin/ar-class at 4-5% edy. d-onset is most anti-edy (4.3%): d words predominantly end in -aiin/-in/-ar (daiin=dominant B word). sh being most edy-concentrated (45.8%) is consistent with sh's role as B-dialect template/interface class (F326: shedy drives sh→qok bigram). The template vs content onset split in suffix preference is a quantification of a qualitative pattern in the VMS literature.
**Limitation:** Spearman with N~15-18 onset classes; significance not formally tested. Suffix stripping calibration affects entropy values. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** d-anti-edy (4.3%) vs sh-edy (45.8%) is a 10.7× ratio in suffix class preferences between the two dominant onset classes. This is larger than any single formula enrichment documented (most formula E-values are 2-6×). The d/s anti-edy pattern connects to d-words (daiin/daim/dain/dar/dal) being "aiin-register" content words, while sh/qok/ch words (shedy/qokedy/chedy) are "edy-register" template words. The template/content onset split at the suffix level is consistent with the hypothesis that different onset classes mark different grammatical/functional categories.

## F435: Hapax Words (f=1) Are Structurally Abnormal vs Frequent Words (f≥5): Hapax Mean Midfix 6-8× Longer (A: 2.73 vs 0.43 chars; B: 2.79 vs 0.36), Mean Word Length 1.4-1.8 Chars Longer, No-Suffix Rate 20-22% vs 9-11%; Onset Distribution More Uniform (Higher Entropy); Positional Hapax Rate: LL > LF > MID in Both Dialects
**Experiment:** exp_435_hapax_structure
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** H495 ANSWERED. A-dialect: hapax N=1506/freq N=4901. Hapax mean len=6.33 vs freq=4.47 (+1.86 chars). Hapax midfix=2.73 vs freq=0.43 (6.3× ratio). B-dialect: hapax N=1894/freq N=10553. Hapax mean len=6.59 vs freq=4.96 (+1.63). Hapax midfix=2.79 vs freq=0.36 (7.8× ratio). Suffix: hapax 'no-suffix'=20-22% vs freq=9-11%. Frequent words dominated by aiin/ol/edy/eey suffix classes; hapaxes more evenly distributed. Onset distribution: hapax onset entropy A=3.96 bits vs freq=3.52; B=4.04 vs 3.69 — frequent words cluster in dominant onset classes (d=18.1%/ch=23% in A; qok=16.7%/ch=17.8% in B). Hapaxes sample onset classes more uniformly. Positional hapax rate: A=LL(27.3%)>LF(24.8%)>MID(16.2%); B=LL(22.2%)>LF(19.6%)>MID(10.7%). Interpretation: hapax word-length gradient is universal in natural language (Latin=1.79×, Italian=1.92×, both STRONGER than VMS per exp_436). VMS shows the pattern less strongly than natural language. The midfix-specific analysis (6-8× ratio) is VMS-specific: frequent VMS words have near-zero midfix (template skeleton) while hapax VMS words have substantial midfix — this decomposition is not directly applicable to inflectional Latin/Italian morphology. **Revised by exp_436:** the word-length gradient claim is not VMS-distinctive; the midfix layer claim remains VMS-specific.
**Limitation:** Midfix length depends on suffix stripping accuracy. 'Other' onset hapaxes may include transcription noise. Section distribution of hapaxes not analyzed. exp_436 confirms word-length gradient is universal; midfix claim not yet compared to control. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The 6-8× midfix length ratio is larger than any prior A/B dialect difference documented. Frequent words (mean midfix ~0.4 chars) are effectively onset+suffix concatenations with near-zero midfix, while hapax words (mean midfix ~2.75 chars) carry substantial mid-word material. If hapaxes are rare morphological productivities, this gradient suggests the productive system generates systematically longer words; if hapaxes are a separate register, the VMS has two structural vocabularies layered on each other.

## F434: A-qok vs B-qok Vocabulary Structural Divergence: A ch-midfix Forms = 13% of A qok Tokens (qokchy=8.2%/qokchol=3.0%/qokchor=1.7%); B Dominated by edy-Class Zero-Midfix Forms (qokeedy=12.9%/ain=11.8%/eey=11.3%/edy=10.8%/aiin=10.6% = 57.5% of B qok); A qok-'ol' Forms = 19.3% vs B = 1.7%; ch-Midfix Rate Ratio ≈ 5.4×
**Experiment:** exp_434_qok_dialect_structure
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** H498 ANSWERED. A-qok (N=462 tokens, 98 types): zero-midfix=49.4%, mean midfix=1.09 chars. ch-midfix forms: qokchy(38=8.2%)+qokchol(14=3.0%)+qokchor(8=1.7%) = 60 tokens = 13.0% of A qok corpus. qok-ol forms prominent: qokol(40=8.7%), qokal(20=4.3%), qokchol(14=3.0%), qokaly/qokeol additional = ol-terminal = 19.3% of A qok tokens. B-qok (N=1916 tokens, 142 types): zero-midfix=83.4%, mean midfix=0.37 chars. edy-class zero-midfix forms dominant: qokeedy(248=12.9%)+qokain(227=11.8%)+qokeey(216=11.3%)+qokedy(206=10.8%)+qokaiin(204=10.6%) = 1101/1916 = 57.5%. B ch-midfix (qokchdy=31+qokchy=15) = 46/1916 = 2.4% vs A=13%. A/B ch-midfix rate ratio ≈ 5.4×. Interpretation: A-qok structural divergence is vocabulary-level (3 moderately-frequent ch-midfix types in A vs few in B), not single-word outlier. A-qok suffix: ol-dominant (19.3%). B-qok suffix: eedy/ain/eey/edy/aiin = B edy-class pattern. A/B qok type/token ratios: A=0.21 vs B=0.074 — B vocabulary more concentrated.
**Limitation:** Suffix stripping calibration may affect midfix length values (A=1.09 vs F288's 1.34; direction consistent). PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** F288 documented A-qok MLen=1.34 vs B=0.52 without explaining the mechanism. This experiment identifies it: A's elevated midfix length is driven by ch-midfix qokchy/qokchol/qokchor being high-frequency in A (8-3% each) but rare in B (<2%). The ch-midfix forms embed a 'ch' character in the middle of a qok word — analogous to the p-formula opch embedding (F427) but at the word-type level rather than MID enrichment. The A qok-'ol' terminal dominance (19.3%) is also a new observation — A uses qok as an 'ol'-terminating class at high rate, which may connect to the bracket grammar (F413: qok-ch framing in A).

## F433: A/B daiin POSITIONAL INVERSION: A daiin=LL-Enriched(1.30×/N=87)/LF-Baseline(1.03×); B daiin=LF-Enriched(2.62×/N=86)/LL-Depleted(0.70×); B daiin LF Enrichment Section-Dependent: Pharma=3.57×/Bio=3.22×/Herbal=2.00×/Astro=1.60×(WEAKEST); Astro daiin LL=1.00×(Baseline, NOT Depleted)
**Experiment:** exp_431_daiin_position_section
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** H541 CONFIRMED + H546 ANSWERED. A-dialect: daiin LF=1.03×(near-baseline)/MID=0.91×/LL=1.30×(enriched, N=87/378). B-dialect: daiin LF=2.62×(N=86/258)/MID=0.77×/LL=0.70×(depleted). CLEAN A/B INVERSION. A d-onset LL=1.64×(consistent F385). B section breakdown: pharma=3.57×(N=45)/bio=3.22×(N=12)/herbal=2.00×(N=13)/astro=1.60×(N=16). ASTRO DISTINCT: daiin LF=1.60×(weakest) + LL=1.00×(baseline, NOT depleted, unlike pharma=0.32×). Mechanism: astro qok-LF dominance(E=1.91×, F431) competes with daiin at LF slot, suppressing daiin LF enrichment in astro. Pharma+bio drive the global B daiin LF enrichment (2.62×).
**Limitation:** Astro N=16/10 directional. Bio N=12 directional. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The A/B daiin inversion (A=LL/B=LF) is now the cleanest and most complete example of A/B positional grammar inversion documented for a specific word. Daiin is the most common specific word in VMS B (the word 'daiin' appears 258 times in B cont lines = 11.2/1000 words). The B section breakdown reveals that the pharma section is the primary driver of B's daiin-LF rule — pharma daiin LF=42.5% vs baseline 11.9% (E=3.57×). The astro section's weak daiin LF enrichment (E=1.60×) and absent LL depletion suggest astro has a qualitatively different daiin grammar, potentially reflecting that astro text is less "formula-like" in its daiin usage and more distributed, consistent with the section being dominated by qok-LF (F431) rather than d/daiin LF structure.

## F432: A-Dialect p-LF → opch MID Enrichment = 14.58×(N=3, DIRECTIONAL); Raw Rate 2.31% vs Background 0.16%; B Confirmation Reproduced (5.38×/N=40); Pattern Consistent With Cross-Dialectal p-Formula Self-Referential Structure
**Experiment:** exp_430_a_opch_check
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** H648 ANSWERED (directional). A-dialect: p-LF(N=35), opch MID=3/130=2.31%, non-p-LF background=8/5056=0.16%, E=14.58×. A opch vocab: opchey(2)/opchaldy(1). B-dialect reproduced: p-LF(N=224), opch=40/1484=2.70%, background=60/11969=0.50%, E=5.38×(consistent F427). **Limitation:** A N=3 completely directional. Higher A E-value (14.58×) inflated by lower A background, not necessarily stronger A signal. PASS with directional caveat.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** If the cross-dialectal interpretation holds, p-formula lines in both A and B dialects concentrate p-gallows-embedded opch compounds at MID at ~2.3-2.7% rate. This rate is 5-15× above each dialect's background, and the background difference (A=0.16% vs B=0.50%) reflects the general B/A vocabulary difference (B has more 'edy'-type compound words generally). The A-dialect p-formula line structure is already known to differ from B's in other respects (F404: A p→sh bracket vs B anti-bracket; F400: A p→sh pos1 routing). The cross-dialectal opch enrichment would suggest a deeper shared structure: the p-gallows character itself is embedded in MID content words in both dialect's p-formula lines, regardless of the dialect-specific routing rules.

## F431: B Astro Section (f75-f84) Has qok-LF Rate 1.91×(19.6% vs 5.6-5.9% in Other Sections); All 20 Astro Folios Contribute Uniformly; qok-LF pos1 Routing Near-Uniform Across Sections; Astro Formula-Type Concentration (F430) Explained by Elevated qok-LF Selection

**Finding:** H651 ANSWERED. B cont lines by section: astro qok-LF=147/750=19.6%(E=1.91×); herbal=16/277=5.8%(E=0.56×); bio=13/219=5.9%(E=0.58×); pharma=58/1038=5.6%(E=0.55×). MECHANISM: Astro formula-type concentration (F430: qok→sh→k/d→qok→ol/qok→ch→qo/qok→ch→ol in astro) is explained by elevated qok-LF rate, not section-specific routing grammar. Astro section systematically selects qok-class words as line-first words at 1.91× global rate.

The finding suggests the astro section content is systematically represented by qok-class onset words — a content domain → word-shape association. This is consistent with the astro section containing astronomical labels, zodiac notation, or similar structured text where template-class qok words are the dominant content-word type. Combined with F430's finding that d→qok→ol is astro-concentrated, the astro grammar appears to be: qok at LF (elevated) → qok/sh/ch at pos1 (near-uniform) → with formula-type routing preserved.

## F430: B Formula Types Cluster into Three Section-Specific Groups (ALL DIRECTIONAL, N=4-8 per type): Astro=qok-LF formula types(qok→sh→k/d→qok→ol/qok→ch→qo/qok→ch→ol, E=1.7-2.5×); Herbal=content-routing formula types(d→ch→y=5.0×/y→sh→ch=3.1×/p→sh→ok=2.8×); Pharma+Bio=y→o→ch(herbal=0×)

This is consistent with the "content class" interpretation: the section determines what content is being conveyed, and the content class drives which formula route is used. The astro section's qok-LF formula concentration is particularly striking ��� the astronomical/zodiac content (folios 73-84) may specifically use template-class (qok) opener grammar, while the herbal section uses content-routing formula types (y→sh, d→ch, p→sh). This would be consistent with the sections representing different content domains with section-specific language/grammar structures.

## F428: B t→ot MID Adjacency Is DISTRIBUTED Class-Level Sequential Pairing (E=2.15×/N=24); 18 Unique t-Words/15 Unique ot-Words; No Dominant Pair; 17% Same-Body Rate
**Experiment:** exp_426_t_ot_adjacency

**Finding:** H613b ANSWERED. B MID t→ot adjacency: E=2.15×/N=24 (consistent with F412=1.95×/N=22). Type diversity: 18/91 t-types and 15/146 ot-types appear in pairs; no pair occurs >2 times. Max pair: teey→oteey(N=2). Mechanism: CLASS-LEVEL sequential rule (t onset → ot onset), not compound construction. 17% same-body rate (4/24: teey→oteey, tar→otar, tedy→otedy) suggests mild body-templating but not dominant. ot-words following t are drawn from common ot vocabulary (oteey/otar/otedy are high-frequency ot-MID words generally).
**Limitation:** N=24 directional. Same-body rate (17%) uncertain at small N. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The t→ot class-level pairing (E=2.15×) adds to the inventory of B MID onset-coupling rules. It is weaker than the strongest coupling effects (l self-succession at pos1→pos2=3.03×, F423) but comparable to ot self-succession (E=2.19×, F422). The finding clarifies that the gallows t-onset word class has onset-level coupling to the template class ot in MID positions — a cross-class sequential rule distinct from self-succession. The mild body-templating (17% same-body) may reflect shared vocabulary structure between the t and ot onset classes (both use 'edy'/'eey'/'ar' body words), which is consistent with earlier findings that B has systematic body-class templating across onset classes.

## F427: B 'opch'-Compound Words Enriched 5.28×(N=39) at MID in p-LF Lines vs Non-p-LF Baseline(0.51%); o-Onset MID=1.98×; ch MID=0.60× Depleted; p-Gallows Self-Referential Structure in p-Formula Lines
**Experiment:** exp_425_opch_enrichment
**Date:** 2026-04-12
**Finding:** H640 CONFIRMED. B p-LF cont lines(N=219): opch-MID rate=2.70%(39/1445). Non-p-LF(N=2032): opch-MID rate=0.51%(60/11727). Enrichment=5.28×. Vocabulary: opchedy(13)/opchdy(7)/opchey(5) in p-LF MID. Broader o-onset MID: p-LF=6.64% vs non-p-LF=3.36%(E=1.98×). INTERPRETATION: p-gallows appears at LF AND embedded within MID body words ('op-'+ch body = 'opch'). p-formula lines have self-referential p-gallows structure: the gallows onset that defines the LF class also appears as an embedding within o-onset compound words at MID. The 'opch-edy' compound (most frequent: 35 total, 13 in p-LF MID) carries a p-element in a canonical o-class word position.

The combination of (1) p-LF at line first word, (2) sh/o at pos1, (3) opch-compounds in MID, and (4) o/qot/qo at LL creates a multi-scale p-gallows/o-class structure that spans the entire line. This is the first finding of WITHIN-WORD onset mirroring of the LF class in formula lines — the p-formula 'replicates' its LF gallows within MID compound words.

## F426: VMS B Confirmed Formula Type Inventory (10 Types, N≥5, E≥2.0, 'Other'-Filtered) — Formula-Typed = 2.6%(59/2265); CORRECTS F424: d→ch→l BELOW Threshold(E=1.57×, NOT a Formula Type); p→sh→qot BORDERLINE(E=1.78×, N=8); s→sh→qok CONFIRMED NON-FORMULA(E=1.26×/N=21)

FORMULA-TYPED FRACTION: 59/2265=2.6% (CONSISTENT WITH F416). **Magnitude context:** The 10-type inventory represents the definitive current characterization of VMS B formula grammar at the trigram level. The distribution of formula types by LF class: d=3 types(d→ot→ot/d→qok→ol/d→ch→y); qok=3 types(qok→sh→k/qok→ch→qo/qok→ch→ol); y=2 types(y→sh→ch/y→o→ch); l=1 type(l→ch→qok); p=1 type(p→sh→ok). d and qok are the most formula-active LF classes (3 types each), consistent with d being the most common B LF class (N=352 cont lines) and qok being a template/formula class (N=239, 4th rank). The p-formula (p→sh→qot confirmed in exp_392 at E=2.11×/N=8) is borderline in this analysis (E=1.78×) — reflecting that p→sh has only 56 occurrences and the qot routing is modest. The s-formula (s→sh→qok: E=1.26×/N=21, s→sh→l: E=1.87×/N=6) does NOT meet the formula-type threshold despite s being a formula LF class with clear routing (s→sh enriched at pos1). This suggests the s LF class routes broadly through sh (s→sh at pos1 is enriched) but once at sh, the pos2 routing is near-Markovian (qok is only mildly enriched at 1.26×). This is consistent with s being a "broad routing" formula class rather than a specific trigram formula type.

The 'or' dominance at pos1 in y→o lines suggests 'or' is a specific formula word for the pharma/bio y-grammar: a minimal o-class word functioning as a positional marker in the y→o→ch triple.

## F422: B Onset Self-Succession Survey — l=2.35×(N=102, HIGHEST); ot=2.19×(N=145); qo=2.14×; qot=2.16×; y=1.97×; s=0.33×(ANTI-SELF); p=0.61×(depleted); ot Run-Length Distribution GEOMETRIC (Not Super-Geometric Like A y-Chains); A/B: ot E_self B=2.19× > A=1.67×
**Experiment:** exp_419_ot_self_chain

**Finding:** H639 ANSWERED. All-position onset self-succession E = P(next=X|current=X)/P(X) in B cont lines. A comparison: ot=1.67×(lower than B)/y=1.39×(lower than B)/s=1.42×(HIGHER than B=0.33×)/t=0.35×(STRONGLY DEPLETED in A vs B=1.00×). B ot RUN-LENGTH: len=1: 943(88.7%); len=2: 96(9.0%); len=3: 23(2.2%); len=4: 1(0.1%). Expected under geometric with p_self=0.154: len=2=13.0%(observed 9.0%→FEWER doublets than expected), len=3=2.0%(observed 2.2%≈expected). CONCLUSION: ot self-succession is a bigram-level rule (E=2.19×), NOT super-geometric like A y-chains (F395). B has 23 ot-triples and 1 ot-quad. l onset (E=2.35×): NEW finding — l is most self-successive B onset class and previously uncharacterized. s anti-self-succession (E=0.33×) consistent with s routing through sh (formula LF class, not self-chain).

**Commitment status:** Not committed.

This combined with l→ch→qok=2.72×(N=5, F421) suggests l has a distinctive B grammar: both self-chaining AND specific formula routing to ch/qok. The l onset class in VMS corresponds to words like "lol", "laiin", "lchedy", "lkeey" — these are common body-class words. l self-succession in B may reflect a specific section/context where l-onset words cluster. The contrast between B s anti-self-succession (E=0.33×) and A s self-succession (E=1.42×) reflects the different grammatical role of s in each dialect: B s is a formula LF class routing through sh (not self-chaining); A s is a more neutral body-class word that self-chains at near-expected rates.

STRUCTURAL FORM: All corpora produce predominantly hetero-class trigrams; self-chain rare (VMS: d→ot→ot; Italian: m→a→m/s→e→s). **Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** VMS B having 10 formula types vs Latin's 4 at the same corpus size supports VMS's richer formula-typed grammar within its own onset-class framework. However, the mechanism (LF routing pos2 via pos1) is not VMS-specific. The key VMS distinction is: template-class onsets (qok/sh/ch/ot) are concentrated as pos1 in formula types, reflecting the B-dialect's template-class grammar rules (sh→qok bigram, qok/ch clustering). Natural language formula types reflect syntactic grammar (prepositional phrase patterns, verb-argument patterns). Both are real structured patterns; they differ in WHAT is structured (onset-class grammar vs syntactic grammar), not in WHETHER structure exists. New directional formula type discoveries: l→ch→qok(2.72×/N=5) is noteworthy as l is an uncommon LF class — suggests l-LF lines route through ch at pos1 to qok at pos2 with high specificity. d→ch→y(2.23×/N=5) suggests d-LF lines occasionally route through ch→y — interesting as y is a grammar-word class.

**Finding:** H630 ANSWERED. A cont lines with cth at pos1: N=75 (5.2% of 1456 A cont lines) vs B=2 (0.09% of 2322 B cont lines) — 37:1 asymmetry. LF DISTRIBUTION (N=75): d=1.61×(N=21)/qot=1.65×(N=6)/t=1.29×(N=7)/y=1.04×(N=11, BASELINE)/ch=0.85×/sh=0.90×/s=0.21×(DEPLETED)/qok=0.41×(DEPLETED)/o=0.55×. No single dominant LF class at E>2×. POS2 after cth-pos1 (N=65, len≥3): ch=1.34×(N=21,dominant)/qo=2.32×(N=5,elevated)/ot=1.90×(N=4,elevated)/ok=1.56×(N=7)/d=1.04×(baseline)/k=0.32×(DEPLETED). E_COND ANALYSIS: No (LF, cth, pos2) combination reaches E_cond≥2.0 at N≥3. Highest: d→cth→other=1.81×(N=2,dir)/y→cth→ch=1.69×(N=6). NEAR-MARKOVIAN throughout. COMPARISON: In A, cth IS formula-typed as a DESTINATION at pos2 (F406: o→sh→cth=4.33×/N=4; qot→ch→cth=2.60×/N=4). In A, cth at pos1 is NOT a formula class — cth is a body-class content word broadly distributed across positions (LF, pos1, pos2, MID all substantial). In B, cth appears only at MID (E=1.16×/F392) and is near-zero at LF/pos1/LL — B's cth grammar is MID-restricted.
**Limitation:** All E_cond below 2.0 — the ABSENCE of formula structure is the finding. qo=2.32×(N=5) and ot=1.90×(N=4) at pos2 are moderate and may reflect general A o-class body preference rather than cth-specific routing. B has only N=2 cth-pos1 lines — B comparison is confirmatory of the asymmetry only. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The finding confirms the cth positional asymmetry in A: cth is a formula DESTINATION (pos2 in F406) but not a formula SOURCE (pos1 here). This asymmetry — enriched as a destination by specific LF→pos1 pairs, but broadly non-constraining as a pos1 onset — distinguishes cth from onset classes like sh (which are both formula sources AND destinations in B). In A, cth fills the "content word" role: it appears at all positions without structural constraints, while specific grammar routes TO cth at pos2 (via o→sh or qot→ch). The d=1.61×/qot=1.65× modest enrichment among LF classes routing to cth-pos1 is consistent with d and qot being A's dominant LF classes that distribute across all pos1 classes. The s-depletion (0.21×) and qok-depletion (0.41×) at LF for cth-pos1 lines suggest that B-affiliated formula classes (s→sh, qok→sh routes) do not route to cth at pos1.

## F417: B p-Formula pos3 Grammar — ch-AVOIDANCE Extends to pos3(0.75×/N=32); qo ENRICHED at pos3(1.86×/N=14); pos2=sh→pos3=qo=2.55×(N=6,OVERRIDES sh→qok bigram); p→sh→qot→pos3 NEAR-MARKOVIAN(N=8,dir); o-class Enrichment Pan-Positional
**Experiment:** exp_413_b_p_pos3_grammar
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H623 ANSWERED. B p-LF cont lines ≥4 words (N=228). POS3 DISTRIBUTION: ch=0.75×(N=32,DEPLETED — global ch-avoidance continues); qo=1.86×(N=14,elevated); ot=1.39×(N=21); o=1.37×(N=11); qok=0.93×(near-baseline). POS2=sh→POS3(N=33): qo=2.55×(N=6,NEW); ot=2.06×(N=4); qok=0.66×(DEPLETED — general sh→qok bigram SUPPRESSED in p-lines); y=5.41×(N=3,dir); k=2.88×(N=2,dir). POS2=qot→POS3(N=17): near-Markovian (d=2.23×/N=3,dir; ch=1.08×). p→sh→qot→POS3(N=8,dir): ot=1.68×(N=2)/qok=1.68×(N=2)/ch=0.57×(depleted,N=1) — all directional. GLOBAL STRUCTURE: ch-avoidance confirmed at pos1(0.42×)/MID(0.69×)/LL(0.47×)/pos3(0.75×) — pan-positional ch-avoidance in p-formula lines. qo/o enrichment at pos3 consistent with MID/LL o-class enrichment (F409). The sh→qo routing at pos3 (given pos2=sh) overrides the unconditional B sh→qok bigram.
**Limitation:** p→sh→qot→pos3 N=8 lines total, 6 with ≥4 words — entirely directional. pos2=sh→pos3=y: E=5.41×(N=3) extreme but tiny N. pos2=qot→pos3: all N<5 except ch(N=4). PASS with directional caveats.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The extension of ch-avoidance to pos3 (now confirmed at pos1/pos3/MID/LL — four distinct positions) makes the p-formula ch-avoidance the most consistently documented cross-position signal in the VMS grammar: p-formula lines avoid ch regardless of position within the line. The suppression of the sh→qok bigram (from 1.97× unconditionally to 0.66× in p-formula pos2=sh→pos3 context) shows that formula-class context can override the general bigram structure. This is a key finding for the grammar model: formula-class LF rules have effects that propagate beyond the first 3 positions and can counter-act the baseline bigram structure. The specific routing p→sh→pos2=sh→qo(pos3) extends the o-class enrichment chain: the qo class is enriched at every position in p-formula lines (pos1 via o-class F409, MID via qo=1.50×/F409, LL via o=1.73×/F409, pos3 via qo=1.86×/this finding).

## F416: Formula-Typed Fraction Threshold Sensitivity — N≥5 Restores Signal: VMS B=2.6% > Shuffle=2.2% ≈ Latin=1.9%; N≥10 All Drop to 0% (VMS Corpus Too Small); Revised Summary: 2.6% Formula-Typed At N≥5; Specific Formula Types (y→sh→ch=2.53×/N=8, qok→sh→k=3.90×/N=5) Survive N≥5
**Experiment:** exp_412_formula_n10_threshold
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H637 ANSWERED. N-threshold sensitivity across VMS B(EVA)/VMS A(EVA)/Latin Caesar(first-letter)/Dante(first-letter)/VMS B shuffled: N≥3: VMS B=8.6%, shuffle=10.9%(bias confirmed). N≥5: VMS B=2.6%(N=59), shuffle=2.2%(N=50), Latin=1.9%(N=55), Dante=7.2%(large corpus). N≥10: VMS B=0.0%, shuffle=0.0%, Latin=0.0%, Dante=2.2%(6.5× larger corpus). N≥20: VMS B=0.0%. At N≥5: VMS B > shuffle AND Latin — genuine formula structure present at N=5-8 level. Top VMS B formula trigrams at N≥5: qok→sh→k=3.90×(N=5)/d→ot→ot=3.69×(N=5)/y→sh→ch=2.53×(N=8)/qok→ch→qo=2.35×(N=8). No VMS B trigram passes E≥2.0 at N≥10. REVISED F405 SUMMARY: "2.6% formula-typed at N≥5 (not 9.3% at N≥3)" is the appropriate characterization.
**Limitation:** Gap at N≥5 is small: VMS B=2.6% vs shuffle=2.2% (59 vs 50 lines). Dante N≥10 fraction (2.2%) reflects its 6.5× larger corpus, not denser formula structure. p→sh→qot did not appear in top-8 at N≥5 — borderline (N=8, just at threshold). PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The N≥5 result validates the formula structure at a methodologically clean threshold: the shuffled control drops BELOW real VMS (2.2% vs 2.6%), and natural language (Latin) is also below (1.9%). The formula structure is real but operates at 2.6% of lines, not 9.3%. The N≥10 floor reflects the maximum N of any formula trigram in VMS B: the strongest formula types are each observed only 5-8 times in 2276 lines. This is because each formula type is LF-class-specific (e.g., y→sh→ch requires y at LF AND sh at pos1, which together happen in ~51 y→sh B lines, of which only 8 route to ch). The VMS grammar has a few strong but low-frequency formula rules — not a high-N syntactic regularity like natural language. This distinguishes VMS from natural language in kind, not just in degree.

## F415: Formula-Typed Fraction (E_cond≥2.0, N≥3) Is NOT a Discrimination Metric — Shuffled VMS B=10.9% > Real VMS B=8.6%; Latin Caesar=10.8%, Italian Dante=11.3% Both Exceed VMS; Metric Biased by Bigram Strength; VMS First-Letter=4.2-5.1% < Natural Language=10.8-11.3%; Specific Formula Types Unaffected
**Experiment:** exp_411_reference_trigram_formula
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H631 ANSWERED (NEGATIVE + METHODOLOGICAL FLAG). Formula-typed fractions: VMS B EVA=8.6%(N=194/2265); VMS A EVA=7.9%(N=105/1327); VMS B first-letter=4.2%(N=95/2276); VMS A first-letter=5.1%(N=70/1360); Latin Caesar first-letter=10.8%(N=308/2854); Italian Dante first-letter=11.3%(N=1653/14635); VMS B shuffled-control EVA=10.9%(N=247/2265). CRITICAL: Shuffled control (10.9%) > real VMS B (8.6%). The metric is biased: strong bigrams in real VMS increase P(pos2|pos1) denominator, reducing E_cond values and formula-typed fraction. Shuffled data breaks bigrams, reducing denominators and inflating E_cond for small-N noise patterns. Under first-letter onset (same grain for all corpora): VMS B=4.2%, VMS A=5.1% substantially BELOW natural language (10.8-11.3%). This is consistent with VMS having stronger bigram structure than natural language (not weaker). The 9.3% formula-typed fraction (F405) is NOT evidence of distinctive grammar. F405's individual formula types (p→sh→qot, y→sh→ch) remain valid — they are large-N, high-E_cond, well-replicated findings. Only the fraction summary loses discriminatory value.
**Limitation:** Onset class granularity differs: EVA onset (20 classes) vs first-letter (26 classes). "Lines" defined differently: VMS manuscript lines vs Latin sentences vs Italian verse lines. N≥3 threshold too low for reliable E_cond estimation (shuffled baseline shows this). Latin Vulgate file was English translation (Douay-Rheims) — excluded. PASS with major methodological flag.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** This experiment reveals a structural limitation of the E_cond trigram formula methodology: it measures LF-conditional pos2 enrichment relative to the pos1-conditional baseline, but that baseline depends on bigram strength. In corpora with strong bigrams (VMS), the denominator P(pos2|pos1) is large, suppressing E_cond values and reducing formula-typed fraction. In corpora with weak bigrams (shuffled data, natural language at first-letter level), denominators are smaller, inflating E_cond. The formula-typed fraction is therefore a poor absolute comparison metric. The finding that VMS first-letter < natural language first-letter is consistent with VMS having stronger within-corpus bigram structure than natural language at the first-letter level — which is itself an interesting finding about VMS word-class bigram strength. The individual formula types remain the strongest findings from the grammar characterization phase (F396-F413): p→sh→qot, y→sh→ch, qok→sh→k, s→sh→l are all large-N, high-E_cond (>2×), cross-validated findings. The narrowing of F405's fraction claim does not affect these individual findings.

## F414: B Bracket Grammar Exists But Differs Structurally From A — B s qok-BRACKET(E=2.78×/N=6); B t sh-BRACKET(E=3.33×/N=4,dir); B d sh-bracket ABSENT(E=1.24×, vs A=3.78×); B y y-bracket ABSENT(vs A=5.21×); B p ch-CORRELATION(E=3.38×/N=4,dir,among-depleted-ch); A/B Bracket Inversion: A Uses sh as Line-Framing Onset; B Does Not
**Experiment:** exp_410_b_bracket_grammar
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H634 ANSWERED. B cont lines (len≥4, N=2211). Strongest B same-onset brackets (E vs independence): s→qok=2.78×(N=6)/t→sh=3.33×(N=4,dir)/qok→sh=2.97×(N=3,dir)/qok→ol=2.84×(N=4,dir)/p→ch=3.38×(N=4,dir). A/B CONTRAST: A d sh-bracket=3.78×(N=4) vs B d sh-bracket=1.24×(N=4,NEAR-BASELINE) — clear inversion; A y y-bracket=5.21×(N=3) vs B y y-bracket not detected; A p sh-bracket=2.06×(N=4,F404) vs B p sh-ANTI-bracket=0.44×(F404). B-specific: B s qok-bracket(E=2.78×,N=6) — not found in A. Shared: t sh-bracket (A=2.76×/dir vs B=3.33×/dir — both directional). B p ch-correlation (E=3.38×,N=4): among ch (a globally depleted onset in p-lines, 0.42×), when ch appears at pos1 it correlates with ch at LL — conditional correlation among rare events, not a true bracket enrichment. CONCLUSION: A bracket grammar uses sh as dominant line-framing onset across multiple LF classes; B does not use sh as line-framing onset.
**Limitation:** All B brackets N=3-6, all directional. Multiple testing: exploratory sweep. B p ch-correlation (N=4): among rare events only. B s qok-bracket (N=6): strongest B bracket, but small. PASS with strong directional caveat.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The A/B bracket distinction now has four confirmed differences: (1) A d sh-bracket absent in B (clearest: same N=4, E=3.78× vs 1.24×); (2) A y y-bracket absent in B (consistent with F401: A y-chains extend, B y-chains terminate); (3) A p sh-bracket vs B p sh-anti-bracket (F404); (4) B s qok-bracket B-specific. These four differences collectively define the A "sh-bracket grammar" (sh frames the content slot for the major A LF classes d/p and likely t) vs B's diverse weaker brackets. The B s qok-bracket (N=6) is the most solid B bracket finding and connects to B s→sh→qok formula type (F398): B s-LF lines both have a strong formula routing (s→sh→qok at pos2) AND show qok framing at line boundaries. This suggests qok is a B-specific "frame" onset class (also consistent with B qok being LF-enriched at 1.71× vs A=0.85×, F392).

## F413: A Bracket Grammar Is General — y-BRACKET(E=5.21×/N=3), d sh-BRACKET(E=3.78×/N=4), k ch-BRACKET(E=3.04×/N=4), p sh-BRACKET(E=2.06×/N=4,confirmed F404); A qot→d LL=1.91×(N=28/56,50%); sh-BRACKET Shared by d AND p LF Classes; All Directional
**Experiment:** exp_409_a_bracket_grammar
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H624 CONFIRMED (directional). A cont lines (len≥4, N=1182). Same-onset brackets (pos1=LL=X, E vs independence): LF=y pos1=LL=y: N=3/172, expected=0.6, E=5.21×(NEW); LF=d pos1=LL=sh: N=4/210, expected=1.1, E=3.78×(NEW); LF=k pos1=LL=ch: N=4/41, expected=1.3, E=3.04×(NEW); LF=p pos1=LL=sh: N=4/36, expected=1.9, E=2.06×(F404 confirmed); LF=t pos1=LL=sh: N=2/94, E=2.76×(dir,N=2); LF=ok pos1=LL=d: N=3/51, E=2.12×. Cross-class brackets: d→other→other=4.67×(N=3); y→o→ok=5.38×(N=3); ot→sh→ot=3.30×(N=3). A qot LL=d: N=28/56(50%) E=1.91×(no bracket — pos1=d only 1.38×). LF classes without bracket: s/sh/ch/qok/qo/o. The sh-bracket appears for BOTH d(E=3.78×) AND p(E=2.06×) — sh-bracket is shared, not p-specific.
**Limitation:** All bracket N=3-4 — entirely directional. Multiple-testing: exploratory sweep of 14 LF × ~20 onset classes. A qot LL=d is robust (N=28/56) and unidirectional (no pos1 correlation). PASS with strong directional caveat.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The A bracket grammar is a general structural feature of A line-grammar. The y-bracket (E=5.21×) connects to F395/F401 (A y super-geometric chains, y self-succession extends) — A y[LF] lines open AND close with y, framing the line with the same onset class. The d sh-bracket is particularly significant because d is the most common A LF class (N=210 cont lines). sh is near-baseline at pos1 for d lines, yet when sh appears at pos1 in a d-LF line, it also appears at LL at 3.78× the expected rate. This correlation pattern (not univariate enrichment, but joint enrichment) is the definition of a bracket rule. The consistency across p, d, k, y — four different LF classes with E=2-5× — suggests the A grammar encodes a LINE-LEVEL SYMMETRY RULE: whatever class opens the content slot (pos1) tends to close the content slot (LL). The strongest B counterexample is p anti-bracket=0.44× (F404): B explicitly does NOT bracket, while A broadly does. This is a fundamental A/B grammar distinction at the line level.

The mechanism implications: (a) if y-chains reflect a scribal practice of sequential y-words, that practice is section-specific; (b) if y-chains reflect a content category (plants, astronomical objects) that happens to produce y-class words in sequence, the bio section content may systematically produce more y-class items. Combined with F401 (A y grammar: self-chain + template-routing) and F395 (super-geometric A y chains), the y-onset class has a multi-level grammar: (1) y is LF-enriched (F392); (2) A y self-chains extend through multiple positions (F395/F401); (3) within A, bio/herbal sections have dramatically more y-chain occurrences than pharma/cosmo. The bio folio f67r2 (biological/human figure section) has BOTH a length-4 chain AND a length-3 chain — the highest y-chain density in any single A folio. This folio may be worth detailed examination for the scribal mechanism generating y-chains.
