POS2 GIVEN POS1: p→sh→qot=3.43×(N=8/52, confirms F396/398); p→sh→o=2.08×(N=4,new); p→ch→ot=3.77×(N=4/18, confirms F398). LINE LENGTH: mean=8.6 words vs B baseline=7.8 (p-lines longer; n=8-10 all E≥1.2×; n≤5 depleted). MID COMPOSITION (N=1053 tokens): ch=0.69×(DEPLETED — global ch-avoidance extends to MID); o=1.73×(enriched); qo=1.50×(enriched); qot=1.52×(enriched); ol=0.58×(depleted). LL (confirms F403 + adds): ch=0.47×(N=15); o=1.73×(N=25, TOP LL CLASS in p-lines); qot=1.53×(N=12); r=1.41×(N=11); l=0.66×(depleted). GLOBAL CH-AVOIDANCE: p-formula lines avoid ch at pos1(0.42×), pos2-after-sh(~0.18×,F396), MID-aggregate(0.69×), and LL(0.47×) — ch depleted across all positions in p-formula lines. GLOBAL O/QO ENRICHMENT: o enriched at pos1(2.24×), MID(1.73×), and LL(1.73×) — p-formula lines preferentially include o-class words throughout the line.
**Limitation:** p→o at pos1=2.24×(N=21) — adequate. ch MID depletion N=128 MID tokens in p-lines (adequate for 0.69×). p→ch→ot pos2: recomputed as 3.77×(N=4/18) vs F398's 5.28×(N=4/18) — the difference is that exp_398/exp_403 used conditional E (given pos1=ch in any line), while here the baseline is unconditional pos2 distribution. The 3.77× here vs 5.28× there reflect different baseline denominators. Both are correct; this result adds the unconditional-baseline perspective. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The global ch-avoidance in p-formula lines is now confirmed at four distinct positions (pos1, pos2 after sh, MID aggregate, LL). This is the most consistently negative cross-position pattern found for any (LF class, onset class) pair. Combined with F403 (cross-dialectal: A p also avoids ch at LL=0.45×), the p-ch avoidance appears to be a structural incompatibility between the p-formula class and the ch class throughout the entire line structure. The new finding that p-formula lines are LONGER (8.6 vs 7.8 words) is structurally significant: formula lines may require more MID words to complete their structure (more o/qo/qot body content). The o-class enrichment throughout (pos1=2.24×, MID=1.73×, LL=1.73×) suggests p-formula lines are "o-class lines" — the p LF-formula class is specifically associated with o-onset words at all non-formula positions. This connects to the broader picture: p-formula lines have: p[LF] → sh or o-class[pos1] → [o/qo/qot rich MID] → [o/qot/r LL], while avoiding ch and y throughout.

## F408: A vs B LF→pos1 Matrix — Four LF-Class Dominant pos1 Inversions: s(A→ch/B→sh), sh(A→ch/B→qok), ok(A→ch/B→qok), ot(A→ch/d, B→qok); A ch-at-pos1 Elevation Broadly Distributed (Most LF Classes A>B); B qok-at-pos1 from Template-Class LFs (ok/ot/qot→qok); B p→qok=0.00×(N=0/39) in A; s-LF and sh-LF Dominant pos1 Inversions
**Experiment:** exp_404_ab_lf_pos1_matrix
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H629 ANSWERED. A cont lines (N=1456), B cont lines (N=2322). DOMINANT POS1 INVERSIONS (4): (1) s-LF: A dominant=ch(31/89=35%) / B dominant=sh(63/264=24%) — INVERSION: B s-LF has formula routing (s→sh=B formula type F398), A s-LF routes to ch generically. (2) sh-LF: A dominant=ch(37/107=35%) / B dominant=qok(22/128=17%) — INVERSION: B sh→qok via global sh→qok bigram rule (F326=1.97×); A sh→ch→sh interleaving (F406=2.69×). (3) ok-LF: A dominant=ch(25/75=33%) / B dominant=qok(15/76=20%) — INVERSION: B template-class ok routes to qok; A routes to ch. (4) ot-LF: A dominant=ch/d(14/58=24%) / B dominant=qok(11/51=22%) — INVERSION: B ot-LF→qok template-class clustering; A ot-LF→ch. NON-INVERSIONS (both ch dominant): d/y/qok/p/t/o/qot LF classes. A ch-AT-pos1 ELEVATION SOURCE: broadly distributed — A ch routing higher from sh(A=1.23×, B=0.74×), ch(1.24×/0.84×), ok(1.18×/0.83×), s(1.23×/0.99×); B ch higher from d(0.91×/1.24×), t(0.66×/0.96×), o(1.00×/1.46×). B qok-AT-pos1 SOURCE: template-class clustering — B ok→qok=1.59×(N=15), B ot→qok dominant, B qot→qok=1.89×(N=11); p→qok=0.00×(N=0) in A (categorical — A p NEVER routes to qok at pos1). MECHANISM: A routes template-class LFs (ok/ot) to ch (cross-class transition); B keeps them in qok zone (intra-template clustering).
**Limitation:** All inversions have N≥39 per LF class (adequate for dominant pos1 claims). B p→qok=0/39 categorical. A qot→qok=3/72 — directional but consistent. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The four LF-class inversions (s/sh/ok/ot) directly explain the A/B pos1 distribution difference. The s-LF inversion is structurally the most significant: B has a formula type s→sh (F398: s→sh→l=2.06×) while A has no s→sh formula type — in A, s-LF lines open with ch generically. This means the B s formula type is not just a pos2 effect (F398) but already visible at pos1 (dominant pos1 = sh). The sh-LF inversion (A sh→ch vs B sh→qok) reflects B's sh→qok global bigram rule (F326: 1.97×) combined with A's sh↔ch interleaving (F406: 2.69×) — both dialects have sh-LF lines but they activate different bigram rules at pos1. The B template-class clustering (ok/ot/qot LF → qok at pos1) is a new structural property: template-class-opened lines in B tend to continue in template-class territory (qok) at pos1, while A routes them through ch. This extends F380 (qok/ot are MID-enriched) to the line-opening: in B, template-class LFs already "activate" qok at pos1, before the MID where qok normally dominates.

## F407: B pos3 Grammar — Formula Effects Decay by pos3; Unconditional pos2→pos3: sh→qo=2.16×(N=17)/qot→ot=2.25×(N=15)/l→l=2.16×(N=13)/y→y=3.41×(N=5); Onset Gradient pos1→pos3: sh 17%→10%↓/qok 12.5%→16.1%↑/ot 3.8%→6.6%↑; LF-Conditional Effects Not Detectable at pos3 Given N=4-8 per Formula Trigram
**Experiment:** exp_403_b_pos3_grammar
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H628 ANSWERED (partial). B cont lines ≥4 words (N=2211). ROBUST POS2→POS3 UNCONDITIONAL BIGRAMS: sh→qo=2.16×(N=17) — sh routes to qo at pos3, extending F403 (sh→qo LL=2.67×) to a global MID bigram rule; qot→ot=2.25×(N=15) — qot routes to ot at pos3 (template class pairing); l→l=2.16×(N=13) — l self-succession; y→y=3.41×(N=5) — y self-succession; t→ot=3.12×(N=7) — t routes to ot at pos3. FORMULA TRIGRAM pos3 (N=4-8 per formula, all directional): y→sh→ch[pos2]→pos3=dispersed (formula effect decays); p→sh→qot[pos2]→pos3=distributed (ot/qok mild 1.68×, N=2/8); s→sh→l[pos2]→pos3=qok=3.33×(N=3/6, directional); qok→ch→ol[pos2]→sh=4.39×(N=3/5, directional). LF-CONDITIONAL pos3 EFFECTS: not robustly detectable given small N. Grammar model: formula overlay (LF→pos2) + local bigram chain (pos2→pos3 unconditional). ONSET GRADIENT pos1/pos2/pos3: sh: 17.0%→10.8%→10.1% (LF-concentrated, decreases); qok: 12.5%→16.9%→16.1% (MID-concentrated); ot: 3.8%→5.9%→6.6% (MID-concentrated); ch: stable ~18-19%.
**Limitation:** Formula-conditional pos3 analyses all N=4-8 (highly directional). "Formula effects decay at pos3" is stated as "not detectable given N" rather than confirmed absence. Unconditional pos2→pos3 bigrams are the primary contribution (robust). PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The robust unconditional pos2→pos3 bigrams extend the global bigram grammar picture: sh→qo is now confirmed at pos2→pos3 as well as at LF→LL (F403); qot→ot pairing is a new template-class coupling; l self-succession (2.16×) adds to F326's l-level analysis. The sh gradient (pos1=17% → pos3=10%) quantifies the transition from LF-sensitive opening to Markovian MID — by position 3, sh's rate has converged to its MID steady-state (~10%). This is the "grammar relaxation" timeline: sh-opening lines transition to near-Markovian ch/qok/ok distribution by pos3. The formula overlay (9.3% of lines, formula at pos2) appears to be a 2-3 position effect; the global bigram grammar dominates from pos3 onward.

## F406: A Continuation Line Trigram Grammar — 7.6%(N=103/1360) Formula-Typed (vs B=9.3%); A pos1=ch=28.6%(vs B=19.0%); A pos1=qok=4.6%(vs B=12.3%); A Formula Types: sh→ch→sh=2.69×(N=8)/t→ch→sh=3.27×(N=5)/o→sh→cth=4.33×(N=4)/qok→ch→qok=3.10×(N=5); y→sh→ch NOT in A Formula List (A/B INVERSION CONFIRMED); B Formula Types y→sh→ch/p→sh→qot/qok→sh→k/s→sh→l ABSENT in A
**Experiment:** exp_402_a_trigram_inventory
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H627 ANSWERED. A continuation lines (N=1360, ≥3 words). Formula-typed (E_cond≥2.0, N≥3): N=103 (7.6%) vs B=9.3%. Near-Markovian: N=1257 (92.4%). Distinct formula trigrams: 27 (vs B=55). TOP FREQUENT TRIGRAMS (all near-Markovian): d→ch→ch(N=16, E=0.90×); d→ch→d(N=13, E=1.43×); s→ch→ch(N=13, E=1.43×); y→ch→ch(N=13, E=1.01×). First formula type at rank 9: sh→ch→sh(N=8, E=2.69×). POS1 DISTRIBUTION DIFFERENCE: A ch=28.6%(vs B=19.0%); A qok=4.6%(vs B=12.3%); A d=8.5%(vs B=3.0%); A cth=4.8%(vs B≈0%). A-SPECIFIC FORMULA TYPES: sh→ch→sh=2.69×(N=8, A sh↔ch interleaving from LF); t→ch→sh=3.27×(N=5, confirms F399 A t→ch→sh=3.28×); o→sh→cth=4.33×(N=4); qok→ch→qok=3.10×(N=5); qot→ch→cth=2.60×(N=4, A cth-routing). B FORMULA TYPES ABSENT IN A: y→sh→ch(B=2.88×/A≈0.62×,depleted), p→sh→qot(B=2.04×), qok→sh→k(B=4.16×), s→sh→l(B=2.06×). y→sh→ch A/B inversion DIRECTLY CONFIRMED in full trigram space.
**Limitation:** N=1360 A lines (60% of B). Many A formula trigrams N=3-4 (directional). Absent B formula types in A may be rare (N<3) rather than depleted — absence ≠ depletion for low-N cases. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The A/B trigram grammar comparison reveals two distinct pos1 composition systems: A is ch-pos1 dominated (28.6%) while B is more distributed (ch=19%, sh=17%, qok=12%). This means A's most common lines are d→ch, y→ch, s→ch (near-Markovian ch continuation), while B's most common lines are d→sh, s→sh (near-Markovian sh continuation). The formula-typed overlays are correspondingly different: A formula types involve ch→sh interleaving (sh→ch→sh, t→ch→sh) and A-specific cth class (o→sh→cth, qot→ch→cth), while B formula types involve sh→qot/k/l routing and sh→ch routing. The structural inversion (A y→sh→ch depleted, B y→sh→ch enriched) is now confirmed at the full trigram level: in the comprehensive trigram inventory, A's formula space simply does not contain y→sh→ch as a formula type. The A sh↔ch interleaving (F393: A sh→ch→sh=2.63×) now appears at the LF-conditional level: when sh is at LF in A, the ch at pos1, sh at pos2 pattern (2.69×) is formula-typed. This connects the MID-level interleaving (F393) to the line-opening structure: A sh-LF lines begin with a ch interleave before returning to sh at pos2.

## F405: B Continuation Line Trigram Grammar Is Predominantly Near-Markovian — 90.7% Near-Markovian (E_cond<2.0); 9.3%(N=211/2276) Formula-Typed; Top Trigrams: d→sh→qok(N=24, E=1.12×)/s→sh→qok(N=21, E=1.28×) NEAR-MARKOVIAN; All Five Prior Formula Types Confirmed; NEW: d→ot→ot=4.13×(N=5); qok→ch→qo=2.62×(N=8); l→ch→qok=2.96×(N=5); LF Primarily Controls pos2 Conditioning (Not pos1 Choice)
**Experiment:** exp_401_b_trigram_inventory
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H618 ANSWERED. B continuation lines (N=2276, ≥3 words). Formula-typed (E_cond≥2.0, N≥3): N=211 (9.3%). Near-Markovian: N=2065 (90.7%). Distinct formula trigrams: 55. TOP FREQUENT TRIGRAMS (all near-Markovian): d→sh→qok(N=24, E=1.12×); s→sh→qok(N=21, E=1.28×); d→ch→ch(N=15, E=1.04×); qok→ch→qok(N=15, E=1.61×). Formula-typed first appears at rank 10: y→sh→ch(N=8, E=2.88×), then p→sh→qot(N=8, E=2.04×), qok→ch→qo(N=8, E=2.62×). ALL PRIOR FORMULA TYPES CONFIRMED: y→sh→ch=2.88×(F398: 2.94×); p→sh→qot=2.04×(F396: 2.11×); qok→sh→k=4.16×(F398: 4.08×); s→sh→l=2.06×(F398: 2.06×); p→ch→ot=5.33×(F398: 5.28×). NEW FORMULA TYPES: d→ot→ot=4.13×(N=5) — d-LF with ot self-routing at pos1-pos2; qok→ch→qo=2.62×(N=8) — qok→ch body then qo; l→ch→qok=2.96×(N=5) — l-LF lines route ch→qok; d→qok→ol=2.51×(N=6). KEY STRUCTURAL RESULT: LF class primarily controls pos2 conditioning (not pos1 choice). p→sh at LF→pos1 is only 1.32× enriched (22.3% vs 16.9% baseline) — the formula effect is at pos2 (given p→sh, qot=2.04× at pos2). LF class is a "pos2-router" more than a "pos1-selector."
**Limitation:** Formula classification threshold E_cond≥2.0, N≥3 is arbitrary. At E_cond≥1.5, more lines qualify. The 9.3% is threshold-dependent. "Near-Markovian" does NOT mean random — global bigram enrichments (sh→qok=1.97×, F326) operate regardless of LF and are not captured by LF-conditional analysis. The 9.3% formula-typed fraction measures LF-conditional effects only. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Narrowed by:** exp_411 (F415) + exp_412 (F416). The 9.3% formula-typed fraction (at N≥3) is NOT distinctive relative to random (shuffled control=10.9%). At N≥5 (cleaner threshold), the fraction drops to 2.6% and VMS B slightly exceeds shuffled (2.2%) and Latin (1.9%), confirming genuine but low-frequency formula structure. The "9.3%" should be replaced by "2.6% at N≥5" in any characterization. The individual formula types (y→sh→ch, p→sh→qot, qok→sh→k) are unaffected — those specific trigrams at N=5-8 ARE the genuine signal.: within-line shuffled VMS B yields 10.9% formula-typed under the same E_cond≥2.0, N≥3 threshold. The metric is biased: stronger bigram structure in real VMS (vs shuffled) increases the E_cond denominator P(pos2|pos1), reducing formula-typed fraction. The individual formula TYPE findings (p→sh→qot, y→sh→ch, etc.) are unaffected — those specific trigrams are well-replicated with N=8-24. Only the "9.3% fraction is structurally distinctive" claim is narrowed. The summary characterization "90.7% near-Markovian" is redescribed as "90.7% have E_cond<2.0 at pos2 level" — this does NOT imply lack of structure (strong bigrams operate regardless of LF and are not captured by E_cond).
**Magnitude context:** The finding that 90.7% of B continuation lines are near-Markovian at the LF-conditional pos2 level is a structural constraint on any grammar model: the B line opening is not a "formula-first" grammar (where most lines follow LF-determined formulas) but rather a "bigram-chain grammar with formula overlays." The formula-typed 9.3% correspond to specific LF-class/pos1 combinations (y→sh, p→sh, qok→sh, s→sh, p→ch) that have been characterized in F396-F399. The NEW formula types (d→ot→ot=4.13×/N=5; l→ch→qok=2.96×/N=5) suggest that template-class onsets (ot, ok) can self-route even when d or l opens the line. The LF-as-pos2-router finding (p→sh is only 1.32× at LF→pos1 but 2.04× at pos2 given pos1=sh) resolves an apparent paradox: p is a "formula LF class" (LF-enriched 5.90×) but most p-LF lines do NOT specifically route to sh at pos1 (only 22% do, vs 17% baseline). The formula routing is post-pos1 (LF affects pos2 choice given pos1), not pre-pos1 (LF does not strongly determine pos1). This is consistent with the near-Markovian sh→qok bigram (1.97×) operating independently of LF: the sh→qok bigram operates regardless of whether LF=d/s/p/y/qok.

## F404: A p-Formula Lines Have sh-Bracket Structure — sh at pos1=1.66×(N=10/41) AND sh at LL=3.52×(N=7/41); sh-Bracket Enrichment=1.80×(N=3/40 vs 1.67 Expected); B p-Lines Are ANTI-Bracket=0.44×; A p Grammar: p[LF]→sh[pos1]→[MID]→sh[LL]
**Experiment:** exp_400_a_p_sh_bracket
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H622 PARTIAL SUPPORT. A continuation lines with p at LF (N=41). Marginals: p→sh at pos1=1.66×(N=10/41); p→sh at LL=3.52×(N=7/41). sh-bracket (sh at BOTH pos1 AND LL): 3 observed vs 1.67 expected under independence = 1.80× enrichment. B comparison: p→sh bracket=0.44× (depleted — B p lines have sh at pos1 but NOT at LL; LL routes to s/qo/k/o per F403). Three A bracket lines: f1/5 ("potoy shol...shoshy"), f3/11 ("pcheol shol sols sheol shey"), f42/16 ("pydaiin sheor shaiin tsh olchy sholy"). Cross-dialectal p-formula comparison: A p grammar = sh-bracketed line (sh as opening AND closing marker); B p grammar = sh-opened, s/qo/k/o-closed (anti-bracket). Both dialects share p→ch LL depletion (F403: A=0.45×/B=0.47×). The A sh-bracket is consistent with A sh pan-positional self-succession (F384/F400: A sh extends to 3-position chains) and A p→sh LL=3.52×(F403).
**Limitation:** N=3 bracket lines. 1.80× enrichment with N=3 is suggestive but not statistically robust as an isolated finding. The bracket enrichment depends on both marginals being independently established (pos1: N=10/41, LL: N=7/41 — both adequate). Independence assumption: pos1 and LL choices may not be independent given LF=p; if brackets come from a fixed template, the bracket mechanism is template-selection (strong) rather than two independent draws. B anti-bracket (0.44×) not independently tested — inferred from F396 (B p→sh at pos1) + F403 (B p→sh at LL depleted). PASS with N=3 caveat.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The A p-formula sh-bracket is a new line-grammar structure not previously documented. It extends the A/B dialect inversion pattern (F400: A sh-pos1 inverts B; F401: A/B y inversion) to the p-formula class specifically: A uses sh as a bracketing element (opening AND closing), while B uses sh only as an opener (pos1) and routes to other classes at LL. The sh-bracket in A is consistent with A sh's positional flexibility (F384: A sh LF/MID/LL all elevated) — in A, sh can appear at any position, so a p-formula that begins and ends with sh is natural. In B, sh is more position-restricted (F384: B sh LF+pos1 concentrated), making a sh-bracket structurally incompatible with B's line grammar. This finding connects to F403's A p→sh LL=3.52×(N=7/41) — that LL enrichment now has a structural interpretation: A p-lines that opened with sh tend to ALSO close with sh.

## F403: LF Class Has Direct LF→LL Associations — B p at LF → ch at LL=0.47×(N=15/222, STRONG); B sh→sh LL=2.07×/sh→qo LL=2.67×; B t→t LL=2.50×(N=7); B qok→s LL=2.16×; A p→sh LL=3.60×(N=7/41); A qot→d LL=1.79×(N=32/72); Cross-Dialectal: B/A p at LF Avoids ch at LL (0.47×/0.45×)
**Experiment:** exp_399_lf_ll_grammar
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H617 CONFIRMED. LF class has independent LF→LL associations not fully explained by pre_LL mediation. KEY B RESULTS: (1) p at LF → ch at LL=0.47×(N=15/222) — strongest LF→LL depletion; p-formula lines are ch-avoidant throughout (ch avoided at pos2: 0.18×, F396; and at LL: 0.47×). B p LL distribution: s=2.05×(N=8)/qo=1.89×(N=10)/k=1.74×(N=8)/o=1.70×(N=24). (2) sh at LF → sh LL=2.07×(N=11)/qo LL=2.67×(N=8) — sh self-routes and qo-routes at LL. (3) t → t LL=2.50×(N=7/205) — t self-routes across full line. (4) ot → ot LL=2.14×(N=8/50) — template class self-routes. (5) qok → s LL=2.16×(N=9/237). (6) qo → d LL=1.87×(N=11)/qok LL=1.77×(N=9). KEY A RESULTS: (1) p at LF → sh LL=3.60×(N=7/41) — A p lines specifically terminate with sh (A-specific). (2) p → ch LL=0.45×(N=3/41) — same p-ch avoidance as B. (3) qot → d LL=1.79×(N=32/72) — A qot LF-formula lines end with d (strong d-routing). (4) t → qo LL=3.57×(N=5/109). (5) s → s LL=2.06×(N=8/91). (6) y → o LL=1.82×(N=18/212). CROSS-DIALECTAL: B p/A p both avoid ch at LL (0.47×/0.45×) — INVARIANT p-ch depletion from pos2 to LL.
**Limitation:** B p→ch LL N=15/222 (adequate for 0.47×). B sh→qo LL N=8/126 (adequate). B t→t LL N=7/205 (adequate). B qok→s LL N=9/237 (adequate). A p→sh LL N=7/41 (adequate). A qot→d LL N=32/72 (robust). A s→s LL N=8/91 (adequate). Other directional claims N-labeled. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The B p→ch LL depletion (0.47×) is the most significant LF→LL finding: it extends the p-ch avoidance pattern discovered at pos2 (F396: p→sh→ch=0.18×) across the entire line to LL. This suggests p-formula lines are globally "ch-incompatible" — ch does not appear prominently at any position in p-opened lines. The self-routing pairs (B t→t/sh→sh/ot→ot at LL) suggest LF class has memory across the full line, not just at adjacent positions — the line "remembers" its opening class and terminates with the same or related class. The A p→sh LL rule (3.60×) and B p→s/qo/k LL rules show that while both dialects avoid ch at LL after p, they route to different classes: A terminates p-lines with sh (a response class); B terminates p-lines with s/qo/k/o (formula/template classes). This A/B divergence in p-LL routing (A p→sh LL vs B p→s/qo/k LL) is a new cross-dialectal distinction in line-terminal grammar.

**Limitation:** N=6 total raiin-pos1 lines — ALL findings directional. pos2=ch N=4/5 (most robust). LL=r N=2/6 (highly directional). The formula characterization is consistent across 6 lines but cannot be confirmed statistically at this N. PASS with highly-directional caveat.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The raiin formula connects F394 (B template classes at LF → raiin at pos1) to F383 (B ch→qok MID coupling) and F389 (B qot/qok→r pre_LL routing). The raiin-pos1 line is a "connector formula": template LF → r-onset bridge → ch/qok body. This is structurally similar to but distinct from the p→sh→qot gallows formula (F396) and y→sh→ch content formula (F398): the raiin formula uses an r-class word as the pos1 element (unusual, since r is LL-enriched/LF-depleted) and routes to ch→qok continuation. The r double-occurrence (raiin at pos1 + r-word at LL) in 2/6 lines is a new positional r pattern: r appears not just at LL via the qot/qok→r pre_LL rule (F382) but also at pos1 via the template-class-at-LF routing (F394). When both occur in the same line, the r class brackets the middle content.

## F401: A vs B y LF Trigram Grammar — STRUCTURAL INVERSION: A y→y→y=2.15×(N=3) EXTENDS vs B y→y→y≈0(TERMINATES); A y→sh→ok=2.47×(N=3) vs B y→sh→ch=2.94×(N=8); A y→ch NEAR-MARKOVIAN vs B y→ch→ok=1.87×; A y→d→ok=4.31×(N=3,dir); B y→l=1.49×(N=20,NEW); A y="self-chain+template-routing"; B y="response-routing+truncated-chain"
**Experiment:** exp_397_a_y_trigram
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H619 CONFIRMED. Full y trigram grammar characterized for A (N=212 y-LF) and B (N=261 y-LF). KEY INVERSIONS: (1) A y→y→y=2.15×(N=3/12) — self-chain EXTENDS to pos2; B y→y→y≈0(N=0/12) — chain TERMINATES at pos2. After (y,y), B routes to ch=1.45×(N=4)/d=2.00×(N=3) at pos2. (2) A y→sh→ok=2.47×(N=3)/ch=0.62×(depleted); B y→sh→ch=2.94×(N=8) — cross-dialectal pos2 inversion confirmed from F400. (3) A y→ch→pos2 NEAR-MARKOVIAN (ch=1.01×/d=1.24×/qok=1.77× — all mild); B y→ch→ok=1.87×(N=9)/ch=1.46×(N=13) — mild but directed. (4) A y→d→ok=4.31×(N=3/16, directional) — A y-d lines route to template class ok. (5) B y→l=1.49×(N=20/261) NEW — B y at LF routes to l at pos1 mildly; B y→l→ot=2.71×(N=4)/o=4.07×(N=2). (6) Cross-dialect both: y self-succession elevated (A=1.78×/B=2.13×); sh depleted (A=0.76×/B=0.57×). A-only: cth at pos1 after y (N=11, E=1.02×); B-only: r at pos1 after y (N=4, E=2.32×, dir). Summary: A y grammar = "self-chain + template continuation (ok)"; B y grammar = "response routing (sh→ch) + self-succession (terminates at pos2)."
**Limitation:** A y→y→y N=3/12 (directional; same as F393). B y→y→y=0/12 (adequate for "terminates"). A y→sh→ok N=3/24 (directional). A y→d→ok N=3/16 (directional). B y→l N=20 (adequate for 1.49×). B y→r N=4 (directional). Most other claims N≥5. All N-labeled. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The A/B y trigram grammar inversion is the clearest structural cross-dialectal distinction found in this phase of analysis. Both dialects have y as a LF formula class (F392), but the formula resolves differently: in A, y lines "stay in formula territory" (y→y self-chain extends, y→template continuation via ok); in B, y lines "open into response territory" (y→sh→ch=2.94×, y→ch→ok=1.87× — both response class continuations). The A y→d→ok pattern (y LF, d pos1, ok pos2) is a "formula-then-template" 3-gram specific to A — not seen in B (B y→d at pos1 has only N=10, near-baseline at pos2). The B y→y→y≈0 termination (B y-chain stops at pos2) directly connects to F395 (B has ZERO length-4 y-chains while A has 2) and F393 (A y→y→y=2.15×/B y→y→y=0.00×). The consistent cross-experiment picture: A y chains extend through multiple positions (F395: length-4 chains exist; F393: trigram extends; F401: pos2 y-successor enriched), while B y chains terminate after length 2 (pos1 only).

## F400: A Dialect sh-pos1 Grammar Inverts B — A y→sh→ch=0.62×(DEPLETED) vs B y→sh→ch=2.94×(ENRICHED); A sh-pos1 Baseline: sh DOMINANT (17.1%) vs B qok DOMINANT (27.1%); A sh→sh→sh Self-Chain=1.72×(N=5); A k→sh→qok=2.71×(N=4); A o→sh→cth=4.13×(N=4); A y→sh→ok=2.47×(N=3, NEW); B Five-Type sh-pos1 Taxonomy Does NOT Map to A

Both A and B have y as a LF-formula class (F392), both have sh as a pos1 response class, but they differ in pos2: A routes to ok (template class), B routes to ch (response class). This suggests the "content formula" line structure in A (y at LF) leads to template continuation at MID (ok at pos2), while in B it leads to response continuation (ch at pos2). The A sh self-chain extending to 3 positions (sh→sh→sh=1.72×) is new — combined with F384 (A sh pan-positional self-succession), A sh has the strongest sequential self-continuation of any A onset class across multiple positions. This is structurally similar to A y super-geometric chains (F395) but for sh.

## F399: B t LF→pos1 Is NEAR-BASELINE (ch=0.96×/sh=1.02×) — t Is NOT a Third Gallows Formula Type; A t→pos1: ch DEPLETED (0.66×/N=20), ot ELEVATED (2.77×/N=9), ol ELEVATED (2.20×/N=6); A t→ch→sh=3.28×(N=5) Interleaving; B t Trigram Grammar Near-Markovian; Gallows LF Class Taxonomy: p/f=STRONG FORMULA; t/k=WEAK/ABSENT FORMULA

Result: H609 REFUTED — t is not a third gallows formula type; F364's {k,t}→ch pattern is MID-specific and does not extend to LF→pos1. Gallows LF class taxonomy: STRONG-FORMULA {p(5.90×), f(1.69×B)} versus WEAK/ABSENT-FORMULA {t(1.02×), k(0.79×) in continuation lines}.
**Limitation:** B t→ch=0.96×(N=38) — robust for near-baseline. B t→sh=1.02×(N=35) — robust. B t→ch→k=3.75×(N=3) — directional. B t→ol→qot=3.43×(N=2) — directional. A t→ch=0.66×(N=20) — adequate for depletion characterization. A t→ot=2.77×(N=9) — adequate. A t→f=8.14×(N=3) — highly directional, reported as directional. A t→ch→sh=3.28×(N=5) — directional. All major claims N-labeled. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The t/k vs p/f distinction within the gallows class is now structurally clear: p→sh at pos1 is the strongest single LF→pos1 routing rule in B (5.90×), and p is the defining "gallows formula LF class" in B. f shows mild p-like enrichment (1.69× at LF in B). By contrast, t distributes to ch/sh approximately at baseline, and k is position-general in continuation lines (F397). The F364 {k,t}→ch rule is a MID-position rule that does not operate at the LF→pos1 step. This means the gallows class {p,t,f,k} has two structurally distinct sub-groups: (1) LF-formula gallows {p,f} — always open lines via pos1=sh routing; (2) LF-neutral gallows {t,k} — opener gallows present in folio-openers (F397: k opener LF=4.32×/3.88×) but not operating via a single pos1-directed rule in continuation lines. A t→ot elevated at pos1 (2.77×) is a new finding not previously documented — when A t opens a continuation line, it specifically avoids ch and routes to ot at pos1 (not template self-routing, but template-adjacent routing).

## F398: B sh-pos1 LF×pos2 Grammar — Four Types: Content-Formula (y→sh→ch=2.94×); Gallows-Formula (p→sh→qot=2.11×); Template-Class (qok→sh→k=4.08×/N=5); Formula-Terminal (s→sh→l=2.06×/N=6); Near-Markovian (d/t); s→sh→qot=0.00× (NEW categorical); p→ch→ot=5.28×(N=4/18)
**Experiment:** exp_394_b_sh_pos1_lf_pos2_matrix

**Finding:** H611 ANSWERED. Full B sh-pos1 LF×pos2 matrix (N=377 lines). NEW: s→sh→qot=0.00×(N=0/61) — extends F393's s→sh→d=0.00× to a dual depletion of {d, qot} at pos2 after s→sh. qok→sh→k: k-onset at pos2 is highly enriched when qok is at LF and sh at pos1 (4.08×/N=5). **Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The B sh-pos1 LF×pos2 grammar now has a five-type taxonomy. The most striking new result is qok→sh→k=4.08×: qok is a template-class onset (MID-enriched, F380) and k is a position-general onset in continuation lines (F397), yet when qok appears at LF and sh at pos1, k is strongly enriched at pos2. This pattern does not fit any previously characterized rule and suggests qok→sh is a "template-formula opener" with k as the specific continuation token. The s dual-depletion ({d,qot}=0.00× at pos2 after s→sh) confirms s formula-class avoidance of template-type onsets at pos2 — s lines open with a formula onset and continue with l/qok/ch (not template classes). The near-Markovian d→sh result (the most common sh-pos1 context, N=80) establishes that most B sh-pos1 lines are NOT formula-typed at pos2 — the formula effects are concentrated in the minority LF classes (y/p/s/qok). The B ch-pos1 grammar is less formula-typed than sh-pos1 (lower E magnitudes throughout), with the exception of p→ch→ot=5.28× which is the strongest single ch-pos1 effect found.

## F397: k-Onset Is a FOLIO-LEVEL Formula Class, Not a LINE-LEVEL Formula Class — k LF-Enriched in OPENER Lines (A=4.32×/B=3.88×) But POSITION-GENERAL in Continuation Lines (A=0.79×/B=0.66×); p/t Remain LF-Enriched in BOTH Line Types (p: A=3.60×/B=5.90×; t: A=2.48×/B=3.59×); k Continuation Distribution: A = flat; B = MID-DOMINANT (54%)
**Experiment:** exp_393_k_positional_census
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H606 ANSWERED. k positional profile in continuation lines: A=LF(0.79×/N=43)/pos1(1.22×)/MID(1.08×)/pre_LL(1.02×)/LL(0.81×) — near-baseline at all positions; B=LF(0.66×/N=34)/pos1(1.04×)/MID(1.07×/N=219)/pre_LL(1.11×)/LL(0.90×) — also near-baseline with slight MID lean. k total: A=314/3.7% of cont tokens; B=408/2.3%. Folio-opener k profile: A=LF(4.32×/N=16); B=LF(3.88×/N=8) — k IS LF-enriched at folio-first, matching p/t pattern. k LF enrichment drops 5.5-5.9× from opener to continuation lines, while p/t drop only 1.2-1.7×. Result: k is a folio-opener formula gallows class that loses LF affinity within continuation lines. p/t/f maintain LF formula status throughout all continuation lines. B continuation k is MID-dominant (54% of k tokens at MID; N=219/408) — consistent with F364 (k is ch-biased at MID/pre_LL in B).
**Limitation:** A k opener N=16 (adequate for 4.32×). B k opener N=8 (directional for 3.88×). A/B k continuation N=314/408 — robust for E values near baseline. f-onset N small (A=19 cont, B=9 LF cont) — directional only; consistent with prior F392. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** This resolves the k anomaly from F392 (k NOT LF-enriched in continuation lines unlike p/t/f). The distinction is structural: p/t/f operate as line-formula classes (they mark the beginning of every type of line — opener, continuation); k operates only as a folio-formula class (marks the beginning of a folio-first line, then disperses into position-general distribution within continuation lines). The mechanism explanation: folio-openers are "register-marked" by gallows classes including k; within-folio continuation lines follow a narrower rule where only {p,t,f} remain LF-concentrated. This is consistent with F345 (folio-first LF = 67-70% gallows {p/k/t/f}) combined with F388/F392 (continuation-line LF = p/t/f/s/y concentrated, k not). The B MID-dominance of k (54% MID in cont lines) is the strongest positional signal for continuation-line k and suggests k functions as a MID-content token in B, not a line-structural marker.

## F396: B p→sh Line Grammar — p→sh→qot=2.11×(N=8/51); p→sh→ch≈0(0.18×/N=1/51) CONFIRMED; p→sh→qok=0.58×(DEPLETED); Two B Gallows LF Grammar Types: Content-Formula (y→sh→ch=2.94×) vs Gallows-Formula (p→sh→qot=2.11×); p→sh LL Distribution Has No Single Dominant Class

The p→sh grammar specifically routes to qot at pos2 (not qok, not ch). Cross-LF-class comparison of pos2=ch rate when pos1=sh: p=0.02(0.18×) vs y=0.32(2.94×) — a 16× span for the same pos1 class. Two distinct B sh-pos1 grammar types: Type 1 = content-formula (y at LF → ch at pos2 after sh, 2.94×); Type 2 = gallows-formula (p at LF → qot at pos2 after sh, 2.11×). LL onset distribution for p→sh lines: distributed ("other"=15.7%; qok=9.8%; ch/k/d=7.8% each) — no single dominant LL-terminal formula. **Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** This finding completes the characterization of B gallows-class LF grammar at the trigram level. The two B gallows-formula types are not distinguishable from pos1 alone (both produce sh at pos1) but become distinguishable at pos2: y-LF lines continue into ch-routing, p-LF lines continue into qot-routing. This extends F393 (B p→sh→ch≈0 established) to a positive characterization (p→sh→qot=2.11×). The gallows-formula vs content-formula distinction is now structural: gallows-LF (p) opens a "qot-body" line grammar, while content-formula-LF (y) opens a "ch-body" line grammar, both mediated through the same pos1 class (sh). The LL distribution for p→sh lines is diffuse (no dominant LL formula), suggesting p→sh lines have greater line-terminal freedom than s/d formula lines which have concentrated LL routing (s→ol=2.98×, d→d=2.10×). The LF=p→pos1=sh→pos2=qot pattern connects to F394 (B template class → raiin → continuation) as a parallel formula-class→template-class pathway.

**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The B qok/qot → raiin formula at LF→pos1 is one of the clearest formula-level structures found: specific template-class LF words produce raiin at pos1 (which is primarily an LL word, F382, but appears here in pos1 context). This extends the template-class-at-LF → r-at-pos1 rule (F390) to word level: the rule is approximately qok-word → raiin → {ch/qok continuation}. The positional polymorphism of raiin (40% of pos1 r, 7% of LL r) suggests raiin is NOT position-assigned but rather a "content word" that can occupy different positions depending on the preceding onset class. B r vocabulary divergence (ram/ry at LL only; raiin at pos1 and LL) suggests partial positional vocabulary specialization within the r class.

## F393: LF→pos1→pos2 Trigram Structure — Grammar NOT Strictly Bigram-Markovian; B p→sh→ch≈0 (0.18×/N=1/51) — Strongest 3rd-Order Effect; B y→sh→ch=2.94×(N=8/25); A y→y→y=2.15×(N=3/12) — y Self-Chain Extends to 3 Positions; B y→y→y=0.00× (Chain Terminates After pos1); B (s,sh)→pos2=d=0 (Extends s-Formula d-Avoidance to pos2); Most Common B Paths Near-Markovian
**Experiment:** exp_389_lf_pos1_pos2_trigram
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H603 ANSWERED. Trigrams computed: A=1382, B=2225 (continuation lines ≥3 words). Key: (1) B p→sh→ch≈0: P(pos2=ch|(LF=p,pos1=sh))=0.02(N=1/51) vs baseline sh→ch=0.11 — 0.18× depletion, strongest LF-conditioning effect found. (2) B y→sh→ch=2.94×(N=8/25): y at LF enriches ch at pos2 after sh; p does the opposite. pos2 ch rate after sh spans 0.02(p)–0.32(y) — a 16× range for the same pos1 class. (3) A y→y→y: E=2.15×(N=3/12, directional) — y self-chain extends to 3 positions in A; (y,y)→ch=0.00 (ch excluded from pos2 after double-y). (4) B y→y→y=0.00×(N=0/12): B y-chain terminates after LF→pos1; after (y,y), B uses ch(0.33×/N=4) or d(0.25×/N=3) at pos2. (5) B (s,sh)→pos2=d=0.00×(N=0/61 vs baseline 0.03): s suppresses d at pos2 even when sh mediates, extending s-formula d-avoidance (F386 B s→d LF=0.29×) beyond direct bigram level. (6) A sh→ch→sh=2.63×(N=8/36): sh-ch-sh interleaving pattern. (7) Most common B paths (d,sh/N=80, d,ch/N=79, s,sh/N=61) are near-bigram-Markovian for most pos2 classes — LF conditioning confined to specific depletions (s,sh→d=0; specific classes near-zero for multiple LF classes).
**Limitation:** A y→y→y N=3/12 (directional). B y→sh→ch N=8/25 (adequate for 2.94×). B p→sh→ch N=1/51 (N=1 adequate for near-zero characterization of near-categorical depletion). B s→sh→d N=0/61 (adequate for 0.00× categorical). A sh→ch→sh N=8/36 (adequate for 2.63×). TVD values estimated from displayed data, not directly computed for all pairs. PASS with directional caveats.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The non-Markovian effects are concentrated in two patterns: (a) LF gallows/formula class modifies pos2 distribution when pos1 is a "response class" (sh/ch) — gallows p suppresses ch while formula-y enriches ch, both at pos2 after sh; (b) formula class self-chaining extends to pos2 (A y→y→y). The y-chain asymmetry between A (extends to 3+ positions) and B (terminates at pos1→pos2) is a new A/B structural distinction: A y-chains are longer. The strongest effect overall is that LF class (p vs y) causes a 16× difference in pos2=ch rate after pos1=sh — this is qualitatively beyond what bigram chaining would predict.

## F392: Cross-Dialectal LF-Enrichment Synthesis — Five Structural Classes: INVARIANT_LF+ {p,t,f,s,y}; INVARIANT_LF- {ch,ol,r}; A>B INVERSION {qot}; B>A CONTRAST {cth (A=0.13×/B=1.16×), d (A=1.15×/B=2.29×)}; Template Classes {ok,ot,qok} More LF-Depleted in B Than A; k Gallows EXCEPTION (A=0.80×/B=0.65× — Position-General Unlike p/t/f)
**Experiment:** exp_388_lf_enrichment_synthesis
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H604 ANSWERED. Full LF-enrichment table computed for all major onset classes in both dialects from continuation lines. Classification: (1) INVARIANT LF+ (both dialects E≥1.3): p(A=3.53×/B=5.85×); t(A=2.43×/B=3.58×); f(A=2.69×/B=1.67×[N=9,dir]); s(A=2.22×/B=4.73×); y(A=2.28×/B=3.52×) — gallows {p,t,f} and content formula {s,y} are cross-dialectally LF-enriched in CONTINUATION lines. (2) INVARIANT LF- (both E≤0.7): ch(A=0.39×/B=0.25×); ol(A=0.64×/B=0.58×); r(A=0.27×/B=0.30×). (3) A>B INVERSION: qot(A=1.65×/B=0.51×) — only confirmed inversion. (4) B>A CONTRAST (not inversion): cth(A=0.13×/B=1.16×, 8.9× ratio); d(A=1.15×/B=2.29×). (5) Template classes more LF-depleted in B: ot(A=0.91×/B=0.33×); ok(A=0.81×/B=0.49×); qok(A=1.09×/B=0.79×). (6) k anomaly: k(A=0.80×/B=0.65×) — NOT LF-enriched unlike p/t/f; k is position-general (distributed across positions) while p/t/f are LF-specific (p: 41/66=62% at LF in A; t: 109/255=43%). Additional finding: {p,t,f,s,y} are LF-enriched in continuation lines (not just folio-opener lines), confirming LF-grammar is a continuation-line property, not exclusively a register marker.
**Limitation:** f-onset N=9/9 (A/B LF=dir); cth A LF N=8/340 (near-categorical; E=0.13× is well-supported). All other major class claims from N≥25 (adequate to robust). Threshold choice (1.3/0.7) is analytical; actual E values reported. PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The cross-dialectal LF grammar has two invariant cores: LF-enriched gallows+content {p,t,f,s,y} and LF-depleted terminals {ch,ol,r}. The single true inversion is qot (A=1.65×/B=0.51×) — qot is A's LF-formula template class but B's MID class. The cth contrast (A=0.13×/B=1.16×) shows cth "migrates" from A LF-depletion to B LF-neutrality; combined with A cth=4.0%/B cth=0.3% (F388), cth is structurally A-specific and its positional grammar reflects A's grammar not B's. The k anomaly (k is NOT LF-enriched like p/t/f) establishes that gallows classes have internal LF heterogeneity: p/t/f are LF-concentrated, k is LF-general. This is consistent with F364 (k is sh-biased at LF→pos1 but ch-biased at MID, indicating k distributes across multiple positions). The overall pattern suggests A and B dialects share the same LF-grammar topology (same classes enriched/depleted) but differ in the magnitude of these enrichments and in the qot/cth/d inversion or contrast.

## F391: A-Dialect r-Onset Is LL-ENRICHED (2.95×) and MID-BASELINE (1.09×) but NOT LL-Exclusive; pos1 r=0 (Categorical in Continuation Lines); LF r=0.27× Depleted; 21 Tokens / 17 Types (81% Hapax) — A r Is Grammatically Marginal but Present at MID; No Dominant A r Word (raiin=19% Only)

A r's pos1 categorical absence (F390) is the sharpest positional constraint: r cannot occupy the second-word position in A. This distinguishes A's r from all other A onset classes: even LF-depleted classes (ch, sh) appear at pos1, but r=0 there. ## F390: Full LF→pos1 Bigram Matrix — LF-Formula Classes Do NOT Strongly Route to ch/sh; A Dialect pos1 r=0 (Categorical Absence); B y at LF AVOIDS sh (0.57×) and Routes to y(2.13×)/r(2.30×); B Template Classes at LF Route to r (qot→r=3.20×/N=6, qok→r=3.20×/N=12); Template Self-Routing Cross-Dialectal (qot→qot: A=3.0×, B=2.0×; qok→qok: A=2.17×, B=1.27×); A d/y at LF: ch/sh Near-Baseline; B d/s at LF: sh Mildly Elevated (1.40×/1.42×)
**Experiment:** exp_386_lf_pos1_matrix
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H600 ANSWERED. Full LF→pos1 bigram matrix computed for A (N=1478) and B (N=2271) continuation lines. KEY RESULT: A dialect pos1 r=0.0% categorical absence — r never appears at pos1 in A, extending A r-exclusion pattern to a full positional rule. LF-formula classes (d/s/y) do NOT strongly route to ch/sh at pos1: A d→ch=0.91×/sh=1.08×(near-baseline); A y→ch=0.83×/sh=0.76×(both below baseline); A s→ch=1.22×/sh=1.18×(mild). B ok at LF prefers template successors (d=2.13×, qok=1.56×, ok=1.61×, ot=1.76×, qot=1.66×) and avoids ch/sh (ch=0.82×, sh=0.70×). B d→s at LF=2.20×(N=6, directional). A y self-routing: y→y=1.78×(N=12); A qot→ch(1.40×)/qot→ot=0.00×/qot→ol=0.00×.
**Limitation:** A qot→qot N=6, A qok→qok N=9 (directional for 3.0×/2.17×; cross-validated by B self-routing pattern). B qot→r N=6, B qok→r N=12 (adequate for 3.20×). B y→y N=12 (adequate). A y→sh N=24/212 (adequate for 0.76× depletion). B y→sh N=25/261 (adequate for 0.57× depletion). All other main claims from N≥38 (adequate to robust). PASS.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The finding partially falsifies the working model: "LF-formula → ch/sh at pos1" is a B-only, mild effect for d/s (E≈1.40-1.42×), and y breaks it entirely. In A, the architecture does not exist at the onset-class level. The A pos1 r=0 categorical absence is the strongest new structural finding: r occupies LL (enriched, F382) but is completely excluded from pos1 in A. In B, r appears at pos1 baseline (0.7%), produced by template classes (qot/qok/r). The B template-class-at-LF → r-at-pos1 rule (qot/qok→r E=3.2×) is a new B-specific routing architecture. Combined with y→y self-routing and template self-routing, the full LF→pos1 picture is: pos1 is dominated by each onset class continuing itself (for template/self-succession classes) or by ch/sh as neutral successors to formula classes — not by directed LF-formula routing.

The generalized A pre_LL template→daiin rule now covers all four template classes (qot/qok/ok/ot) with E=1.48-2.31× — a near-universal line-ending grammar rule.

## F372: sh→qok Mechanism = 'she-' Body sh Subclass → qok-Class Uniform Successor; Q004 CLOSED; shedy/shey/sheody B Drivers (57.6% of sh→qok, over-represented); qok Distribution After sh ≈ Baseline; A sheody=3.52×, sheol=2.63×; shol/shor/shody Have LOW qok Rates (0.2-0.8×)

**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H579 CONFIRMED; H541 ANSWERED. A-dialect d-class LL E=2.08× (24.7% vs MID 11.9%). Decomposition: d-not-daiin LL=18.4% (E=2.35×); daiin LL=6.3% (E=1.55×). d-other is MORE LL-enriched than daiin itself — LL d-dominance is a d-CLASS property, not a daiin formula. Top d-LL words beyond daiin: dy(33,2.2%), dam(25,1.7%), dal(24,1.6%), dar(20,1.4%). B-dialect: d-other LL E=2.10× (8.1% vs MID 3.8%), daiin LL E=0.90× (NEUTRAL: 1.0% vs 1.1%) — confirms F341. B-dialect top LL d-words: dy/daiin/dal/dam/dar (same words as A, E=2.10× for d-other). Cross-dialect: {dy, dam, dal, dar} are LL-enriched in BOTH dialects; daiin is A-LL/B-LF (dialect inversion). Full A positional matrix: LF = p(6.40×)/f(4.57×)/s(4.20×)/t(3.63×)/y(2.63×)/qot(2.09×)/d(1.44×); LL = d(2.08×)/s(2.91×)/ol(1.37×)/ot(1.14×); ch depleted at LF(0.34×) and LL(0.75×). Full B LF = p(17.12×)/s(11.36×)/y(5.46×)/t(6.30×)/d(3.09×); B LL = d(1.84×)/ol(1.69×)/s(1.75×). d→d succession: A E=1.61× (19.2% vs 11.9%), B E=1.54× (7.6% vs 4.9%) — class-level sequential memory. Architecture: model d-CLASS LL affinity (not daiin-word formula); daiin's A-LL enrichment is d-class membership.
**Limitation:** MID_inner baseline requires n≥5 (lines of 2-4 words excluded from MID baseline, included in LL counts — this may slightly inflate LL/MID E for short-line LL words). A-dialect MID_inner N=2986 (robust); A LL N=1471 (robust). d-other LL specific counts: A N=271, B N=183 (adequate).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A-dialect d-class at LL = 24.7% (nearly 1 in 4 LL words is d-onset). d-other E=2.35× is the largest class-level LL enrichment found in this project for A-dialect (exceeding daiin E=1.55×). Cross-dialect confirmation: B d-other E=2.10× at LL despite B-dialect having different LF grammar entirely. d-class LL rule is the most architecturally robust finding in this session.

## F367: A-Dialect {aiin→ol} Shift Is Primarily qok-Onset Driven (herbal=0.85→pharma=6.60); qokaiin Near-Disappears in Pharma (8.04%→0.98%); ok Also Shifts (0.65→2.38 via okaiin Dropout); ch/sh Already ol-Biased in Herbal (2.94/2.96→3.3); Shift Mechanism = aiin-Word Dropout (Not ol-Word Emergence); d-Onset Non-Shifting CONFIRMED (0.16→0.32)
**Experiment:** exp_365_aiin_ol_shift
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H578 ANSWERED. A-dialect {aiin→ol} shift section-by-section word-level analysis. qok-onset: herbal ol/aiin=0.85 (balanced, qokaiin=8.04% of qok tokens N=23) → pharma ol/aiin=6.60 (qokaiin=0.98%, N=2; qokol herbal=6.64%→pharma=11.76%). This is the largest shift (+5.75 ratio change). ok-onset: herbal=0.65 (okaiin=31 tokens, okol=17) → pharma=2.38 (okaiin=5, okol=18) — shift via okaiin dropout. ch-onset: already ol-biased in herbal (ol/aiin=2.94: chol=184, chor=120, chaiin=31) → pharma=3.30 (chaiin=0 tokens, chol=42). sh-onset: herbal=2.96 → pharma=3.22 (shaiin/sheaiin/shain all absent in pharma). ot: herbal=1.50→pharma=1.25 (no shift). qot: herbal=1.71→pharma=1.00 (no shift). d-onset CONTROL: herbal=0.16 (daiin=326, d-ol=72), pharma=0.32 (daiin=101, d-ol=41) — stays strongly aiin-dominated. Mechanism: the shift is selective LEXICAL EXCLUSION — specific aiin-compound words (qokaiin, okaiin, chaiin, chain, shaiin, sheaiin) are near-absent from pharma section. ol-body words do NOT systematically increase; the ratio shift comes from aiin disappearance, not ol emergence.
**Limitation:** Text section shows N/A (insufficient A-dialect text-section data or parsing gap). qot pharma N=38 tokens (small sample). The "shift = aiin dropout" interpretation is based on ratio analysis; a prospective test would need to confirm the absolute absence of qokaiin in pharma is section-specific (not folio-count artifact).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** qok-onset shows the largest ratio swing (+5.75): the only onset class that goes from aiin-neutral in herbal to strongly ol-biased in pharma. ch/sh are already ol-biased in herbal (2.94-2.96) — the shift was already in place before pharma. d-onset is immune to the shift in both sections (daiin=1.3×-2.5× of d-ol words in both). This confirms F342 pharma=17.88× shift is concentrated in qok/ok, not ch/sh/d.

## F366: A-Dialect LL Is d-Onset Dominated (daiin=6.3%, top 6 words all d-onset); B-Dialect LL Distributed (chedy/ol/oly/am/qoky); A qot→daiin pre-LL E=2.52× (15.9%); B d→daiin pre-LL E=5.19× (N=7); B sh→qok-Onset LL; B qot→daiin=0 (Strong A/B Contrast); A ch→d-LL Pattern (daiin+dal+dy+dam=15.1%)
**Experiment:** exp_364_prell_ll_grammar

B-dialect top LL: chedy(40,1.8%), ol(33,1.5%), oly(31,1.4%), am(29,1.3%), qoky(27,1.2%), daiin(22,1.0%) — diverse onset classes. A pre-daiin: ch=33.3% (E=1.43×), qot=7.5% (E=2.52×, 7/44 qot pre-LL), ot=6.5% (E=1.38×), d=12.9% (E=0.80×, depleted), sh=7.5% (E=0.89×). B pre-daiin: d=31.8% (E=5.19×, N=7), ch=27.3% (E=1.68×). B qot→daiin pre-LL=0/111 (strong dialect contrast). B sh pre-LL → qok-onset LL (qoky/qokal/qokeedy/qokam/qokaiin all elevated). A qot words before daiin: qotchey(2), qotychor/qotchod/qotchor/qotal (each N=1) — diverse. A ch pre-LL→d-LL: daiin+dal+dy+dam=15.1% of ch pre-LL LL words (all d-onset). **Limitation:** B d→daiin pre-LL N=7 (directional). B sh→qok LL individual word counts N=3-6 (directional; consistent with overall sh→qok F336). A qot N=7 total pre-LL pairs (adequate for 15.9% rate claim at E=2.52×). A ch pre-LL N=344 (robust).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** B d→daiin E=5.19× at pre-LL is the largest pre-LL bigram E found; but based on N=7. A qot→daiin E=2.52× (N=7) and A ch→daiin E=1.43× (N=31) together explain 40.8% of A-dialect daiin at LL. The A-dialect LL layer is almost entirely d-onset — the most strongly biased onset at any positional slot found in this project.

## F365: No Folio-Opener LF+pos1 Word Pair Repeats in Either Dialect (Pure Onset-Class Grammar); A Opener pos1 sh-Dominated (shey=5,shor=4,sheol=3); B Opener LF p-Dominant (34%,edy-suffix); A Closer Top Word ycheor(3); A Closer pos1 ch-Diverse (chor/chol/cheor); B Closer LL Completely Hapax
**Experiment:** exp_363_opener_formula
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H565 ANSWERED. No folio-opener or folio-closer LF+pos1 word pair repeats in either dialect (N=1 for all pairs). A opener hapax=88%, B opener hapax=90% at LF. A pos1 most common words: shey(5,4.1%), shor(4,3.3%), sheol(3,2.5%) — sh-onset dominant consistent with gallows→sh rule. B opener top pos1: or(3,4.1%), ytedy(2), qokedy(2), shey(2) — diverse onset classes. B opener LF p-dominant (pchedar/pchedal/psheoky etc.); p=34% of B opener LF tokens. A folio-closer LF: ycheor(3,3.6%) = most repeated word; daiin(3) also. A closer pos1 ch-diverse: chor(4), chol(3), cheor(3), chear(2), chokal(2), cheol(2) — all different ch-body words. A closer LL: daiin(7,8.4%) dominant. B closer LF: ol(3,6.2%) most repeated. B closer LL: completely hapax (all count=1). Architecture: folio-opener/closer constraints are onset-class rules only — no word-level formula needed. A opener: gallows LF → sh-elevated pos1 (word-level sh vocab diverse). B opener: gallows LF → diverse pos1 (primarily o/sh/qok onset).
**Limitation:** B closer N=48 (some onset-class patterns at pos1/LL not robust). A opener N=121 (robust for LF onset profile). All major claims based on counts of 2-5 tokens — findings are directional for specific words but onset-class patterns are robust.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** 100% hapax at word-pair level (N=1 for all LF+pos1 pairs) is the most extreme hapax finding in this project. Contrast with continuation lines where daiin is 1.4-4.7% of tokens. The folio-register grammar is entirely encoded in onset-class rules, making it architecturally simple to implement.

## F364: A-Dialect Gallows Has Two Structural Sub-Classes ({p,f}→sh vs {k,t}→ch) at MID_inner; B-Dialect Split Collapses at MID (All Gallows ch-Biased); k Is sh-Biased at A LF→pos1 (Overriding Its ch-Bias) Due to Gallows→sh E=1.72×; A pre-LL k→ch E=10.00 (Most Extreme)
**Experiment:** exp_362_gallows_subclass
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H568 CONFIRMED WITH DIALECT SPLIT. A-dialect MID_inner: p→sh=30.8% (N=13), p ch/sh=0.50; k→sh=10.9% (N=119), k ch/sh=2.38; t→ch=26.2% (N=61), t ch/sh=2.29. Aggregate MID: pf ch/sh=0.50 (sh-biased), kt ch/sh=2.35 (ch-biased) — confirmed {p,f}→sh vs {k,t}→ch structural split at MID positions in A-dialect. B-dialect MID_inner: p→sh=3.9% (N=51), p ch/sh=4.00 — p is ch-biased in B MID; f→sh=0% (N=15). Aggregate B MID: pf ch/sh=5.50, kt ch/sh=2.06 — split COLLAPSES, all gallows ch-biased. B-dialect p→sh all-positions (F360: ch/sh=0.49) was entirely driven by LF→pos1. A-dialect LF→pos1: k→sh=38.1% (ch/sh=0.44) — k appears sh-biased at LF→pos1 because gallows→sh E=1.72× overwhelms k's MID ch-bias. A pre-LL→LL: k→ch=20.0% (ch/sh=10.00, N=50) = most extreme ch-dominance of any gallows onset at any position. Structural implication: A-dialect simulation should model p/f as sh-successor class and k/t as ch-successor class; B-dialect needs LF-position-specific p→sh rule only.
**Limitation:** A p-MID N=13 (directional); A f-MID N=4 (excluded from claims). Core A kt-MID N=119/61 (robust). B p-MID N=51 (adequate). A p LF→pos1 N=41 (adequate for direction).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The A-dialect pf vs kt ch/sh ratio at MID_inner (0.50 vs 2.35) is a 4.7× difference within the same "gallows" onset class. This is the largest within-class successor divergence found in this project. In B-dialect, the split is absent at MID — the gallows sub-class distinction is A-dialect-specific.

## F363: ok→ok Self-Succession Is CLASS-LEVEL Onset Memory (84-86% DIFFERENT ok Words); Continuation-Line E: A=1.93×, B=1.32×; No Dominant Word-Level Bigram; A-Dialect LL-Biased (15.5% vs MID 11.9% vs LF 6.8%); A okey→any_ok=35.3% (E=5.79×); B okedy/okar→any_ok≈16%
**Experiment:** exp_361_ok_succession

**Finding:** H570 ANSWERED. ok→ok self-succession is CLASS-LEVEL onset memory: only 14-16% of ok→ok pairs are SAME word; 84-86% are DIFFERENT ok-onset words. No dominant word-pair (top pairs N=2-5). Continuation-line ok→ok: A E=1.93× (51/436 vs 6.1% baseline), B E=1.32× (107/1097 vs 7.4% baseline). F326 discrepancy (B=1.96×) is explained by folio-opener/closer register contribution. A-dialect position gradient: LL=15.5%, MID=11.9%, LF=6.8% — ok-class memory strongest near line end. B-dialect no gradient (LF=11.8%, MID=9.7%, LL=9.1%). A okey→any_ok=35.3% (N=17, E=5.79×); B okedy→any_ok=16.1% (N=93, E=2.18×), okar→any_ok=15.8% (N=76, E=2.13×). Top ok-onset words: A=okol/okaiin/okeey/okeol/okal (each 6-7%); B=okaiin(12.5%), okain(9.5%), okeey(9.0%), okedy(8.1%), okeedy(7.6%). Architecture: ok-class onset memory is a genuine sequential rule requiring modeling, analogous to qok→qok in the copy-buffer architecture.

**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** ok→ok E=1.93× (A continuation) matches qok→qok (F326 B: 1.32×, A: 1.32×) and gallows→sh (1.22-1.72×). The 84-86% DIFFERENT-word rate is the clearest evidence for onset-class memory rather than word clustering.

## F362: ch→daiin Is a Cross-Dialect Sequential Rule (A: E=1.30×, B: E=1.45×), Strongest at pre-LL→LL (A: 1.69×, B: 2.02×); A-Dialect chol→daiin Dominant Word Pair (29%); B-Dialect chedy→daiin Dominant (26%); A qot→daiin E=2.50× pre-LL; B d→daiin E=5.57× pre-LL (N=7 directional)
**Experiment:** exp_360_ch_daiin_rule
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H571 CONFIRMED. ch→daiin is a cross-dialect onset-class bigram: A E=1.30× (N=85), B E=1.45× (N=39). Both dialects show strongest effect at pre-LL→LL: A E=1.69×, B E=2.02×. Effect also present at MID_inner (A: E=1.26×, B: E=1.75×) and LF→pos1 (A: E=1.33×). A-dialect: ch is dominant daiin predecessor by absolute count (30/87 pre-LL→LL daiin pairs, E=1.45×). A qot→daiin E=2.50× at pre-LL→LL (N=6); ot→daiin E=1.48×. sh→daiin E=0.94× (neutral), d→daiin E=0.79× (depleted) at A pre-LL→LL. B-dialect: d→daiin E=5.57× at pre-LL→LL (N=7, directional). A-dialect word-level: chol dominates ch→daiin (25/85=29%); chor second (8/85=9%). B-dialect: chedy→daiin (10/39=26%); chey, chckhy, cheey follow. **Limitation:** B d→daiin E=5.57× pre-LL based on N=7 (directional only). A qot→daiin N=6 (directional). Core A ch→daiin N=85 (robust). B ch→daiin N=39 (adequate). Overall ch→daiin effect is consistent across positions in A (1.08-1.69×); more concentrated at pre-LL in B.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** ch→daiin E=1.30-1.45× is moderate, comparable to other onset-class bigrams (gallows→sh E=1.22-1.72×, F359). At pre-LL→LL specifically, B E=2.02× is among the stronger sequential rules found. chol→daiin word-level pairing (25 tokens) is the most frequent specific word-level bigram identified in this project to date.

## F361: y→d Coupling from F326 (A: 1.37×, B: 1.49×) Is Near-Absent in Continuation Lines (A: 0.96×, B: 1.08×); F326 Coupling Likely Cross-Register Artifact; B y→daiin Weak (E=1.57×, N=9); ch-Onset Dominant Predecessor of A-Dialect daiin at pre-LL→LL (34.5%); ch→daiin New Rule
**Experiment:** exp_359_y_d_coupling
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H569 REFUTED. y→d coupling (F326: A 1.37×, B 1.49×) is near-absent in continuation lines: A E=0.96×, B E=1.08×. Architectural implication: y→d bigram rule is NOT needed in the simulation model. NEW: In A-dialect continuation lines, the word preceding daiin at LL is ch-onset in 34.5% of cases (30/87 pre-LL→LL daiin pairs). ch dominates pre-daiin position; y is minor (4.6%). **Commitment status:** Not committed.

## F360: Gallows→sh Bigram Is Multi-Position in A-Dialect (E=1.42-1.72×) but Positionally Specific in B-Dialect (LF→pos1 Only, E=1.22×); Pre-LL→LL Anti-sh After Gallows in A (E=0.28×); B Gallows→anti-ch Position-Specific (pos1/pre-LL, Not MID_inner); Gallows Class Internally Split: {p,f}→sh vs {k,t}→ch; B s-Onset Also sh-Inducing (19.1%)
**Experiment:** exp_358_gallows_mid_bigram
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H567 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED with dialect divergence. A-dialect: gallows→sh operates at LF→pos1 (E=1.72×), pos1→pos2 (E=1.46×), AND MID_inner (E=1.42×) — a multi-position rule. However, pre-LL→LL shows ANTI-sh after gallows (E=0.28×, 1.2% vs 4.3%). B-dialect: gallows→sh is POSITIONALLY SPECIFIC — strong at LF→pos1 (E=1.22×), REVERSES at pos1→pos2 (E=0.78×, N=92 directional), and neutral at MID_inner (E=1.00×). ALL_POSITIONS combined: A E=1.64×, B E=1.36×. Gallows→anti-ch in B: position-specific (LF→pos1 E=0.63×, pos1→pos2 E=0.62×, pre-LL→LL E=0.55×), absent in MID_inner (E=1.14×). A MID_inner: gallows→ch E=1.22× (slight ch elevation, contrasts with LF→pos1 E=0.59× anti-ch). Internal gallows split: {p,f} are sh-biased (A p→ch/sh=0.71, f→ch/sh=0.40; B p→ch/sh=0.49); {k,t} are ch-biased (A k→ch/sh=1.65, t=1.61; B k→ch/sh=2.31). A/B diverge on f: A f→sh=27.8% (sh-biased), B f→sh=5.6% (ch-biased). B s-onset→sh=19.1% (comparable to gallows class, above non-gallows baseline).
**Limitation:** B pos1→pos2 N_gall=92 (directional; reversal not definitive). A pre-LL→LL N_gall=82 (moderate). A f-onset N=18 all positions (directional). Core A MID_inner gallows E=1.42× based on N=197 (robust). B MID_inner E=1.00× N=413 (robust null).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A-dialect gallows→sh multi-position (E=1.42-1.72×) is the strongest multi-position onset-class bigram found to date (prior bigrams were single-position or class-level). B-dialect specificity to LF→pos1 suggests different mechanism from A-dialect. The {p,f}→sh vs {k,t}→ch internal split divides the previously unified gallows "class" into two distinct sub-classes with opposite successor tendencies.

## F359: Cross-Dialect Gallows→sh Onset-Class Bigram (A: E=1.72×, B: E=1.22×) and Gallows→anti-ch Bigram (A: E=0.59×, B: E=0.63×) in Continuation Lines; A k-Onset Strongest (k→sh=38.1%); Folio-Opener pos1 ch/sh Balance Explained by Gallows-LF → sh Rule; Gallows→sh Distinct from ch↔sh Avoidance (F328)
**Experiment:** exp_357_gallows_lf_pos1
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H566 CONFIRMED. Cross-dialect onset-class bigram rule: gallows-LF words (p/k/t/f) produce elevated sh at pos1 (A: 23.4% vs 13.6% non-gallows, E=1.72×; B: 19.6% vs 16.1%, E=1.22×) and depleted ch at pos1 (A: 17.4% vs 29.4%, E=0.59×; B: 13.2% vs 20.9%, E=0.63×). Per-onset: A k→sh=38.1% (N=42), A p→sh=24.4% (N=41); B p→sh=23.0% (N=222). Folio-opener pos1 sh=25.6% is EXPLAINED by gallows-LF→sh: opener is 74% gallows LF, which produces sh=23-29% at pos1; weighted prediction ≈22-25% sh. Opener gallows-LF→sh=29.2% vs cont gallows-LF→sh=23.4% — 5.8pp register-specific elevation exists but is minor. The gallows→sh rule is DISTINCT from ch↔sh avoidance (F328): gallows (p/k/t/f) produces sh; ch↔sh avoidance depletes ch→sh and sh→ch specifically. Both rules reduce ch-sh adjacency from different directions. This gallows→sh/anti-ch bigram was NOT captured in the 7×7 class-level bigram matrix (F326) because gallows were spread across multiple onset classes.
**Limitation:** Gallows→sh E values are smaller than top bigram signals (sh→qok=1.97×, qok→ch=1.2×). A-dialect gallows→sh moderately strong (E=1.72×); B-dialect weak (E=1.22×). Per-onset k→sh=38.1% claim based on N=42 (adequate). The 5.8pp folio-opener-specific elevation (29.2% vs 23.4%) is marginally significant (N=89); may be sampling variation.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A gallows→sh E=1.72× is comparable to sh→qok E=1.97× (F336) in magnitude. The gallows→anti-ch E=0.59× is comparable to ch↔sh avoidance E=0.56-0.57× (F328). These are moderately strong onset-class bigram effects. This is the first documented gallows-class-specific bigram rule.

## F358: Folio-Opener pos1 Cross-Dialect Grammar: t=0% at pos1 (Both Dialects); B-Dialect ALSO Excludes p and k (0/73 each); A Folio-Opener pos1 = ch+sh Balanced (25.6%+25.6%); B Folio-Opener pos1 = o/sh/qok/ch/d Diverse; Folio-Closer pos1 sh Depleted Cross-Dialectally (A: E=0.16×, B: E=0.49×); B sh "Migrates" from pos1 to LL (E=3.45×); Cross-Register ch/sh Ratio Gradient: opener<cont<closer in Both Dialects
**Experiment:** exp_356_register_pos1
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H563+H564 CONFIRMED. Folio-opener pos1: t=0/121 (A) and 0/73 (B) — universal cross-dialect t-exclusion at folio-opener pos1 (extends paragraph-level t-exclusion). B-dialect additionally excludes p (0/73) and k (0/73) from folio-opener pos1; only f=4.1% remains as allowed gallows at B pos1. A folio-opener pos1: ch=25.6%, sh=25.6% (perfectly balanced, ratio=1.00); contrast with continuation pos1 ratio=1.86. B folio-opener pos1: o=15.1%, sh=15.1%, qok=13.7%, ch=12.3%, d=11% — diverse. Folio-closer pos1 sh depletion is CROSS-DIALECTAL: A sh=2.4% (E=0.16×), B sh=4.7% (E=0.49×) vs continuation sh=15.0%/16.8%. B folio-closer: sh depleted at pos1 (4.7%) but enriched at LL (14.6%, E=3.45×) — sh "migrates" to LL. A folio-closer: sh depleted at pos1 AND near-baseline at LL (E≈1.0×). Cross-register ch/sh ratio at pos1: A=opener(1.00)→cont(1.86)→closer(15.50); B=opener(0.82)→cont(1.15)→closer(2.00) — monotonic increase in both dialects. Full 3-register 2-dialect pos1 table: ch from 12-25% at opener to 17-37% at closer; sh from 2-26% at opener to 2-8% at closer.
**Limitation:** B closer pos1 N=43 (adequate). B opener pos1 conditional analysis by LF onset N=2-11 per cell (directional). t/p/k=0% claims are null results — all robust (any observation would falsify). A opener N=121 (robust for 25.6%/25.6% balance claim).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** The ch/sh balance at A folio-opener pos1 (ratio=1.00) vs A folio-closer pos1 (ratio=15.50) spans a 15.5× range — the largest cross-register pos1 ratio contrast found in this project. Prior paragraph grammar (F345-type) established t=0% at paragraph pos=1; this confirms the same rule operates at folio level (independent confirmation across two position-classification systems).

## F357: A-Dialect Folio-Closer ch Elevation at pos1 Is General (E=1.34×, Not y-Specific); sh Strongly Depleted at pos1 (E=0.16×) = Anti-sh Constraint Extends to pos1; cth=0% at pos1; Folio-Closer Line Structure: {anti-gallows/anti-sh LF} → {ch×37%, sh×2%} → {ch×29%} → {d×29%/daiin×8% LL}
**Experiment:** exp_355_a_closer_y_ch_sequence
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H562 ANSWERED. The elevated ch at A-dialect folio-closer pos1 (37.3% vs 27.8% continuation, E=1.34×) is NOT y-onset-specific. ALL LF onset types show elevated ch at pos1 in folio-closer vs continuation: y-LF→ch(36.8% vs 23.2%), d-LF→ch(43.8% vs 25.4%), s-LF→ch(45.5%), o-LF→ch(60%), k-LF→ch(67%). Anti-sh at pos1: sh=2/83=2.4% (E=0.16×) vs continuation 15.0%. The same 0.16× depletion factor as folio-closer LF (F355). cth=0% at folio-closer pos1 (continuation=5.1%). General folio-closer line structure confirmed: {anti-gallows/anti-sh/anti-cth LF} → {ch=37%, sh=2%, cth=0% at pos1} → {ch/d body} → {d=29%, daiin=8.4% LL}. y→ch bigram in continuation = 0.86× (BELOW expectation); in folio-closer = 1.29× (slightly enriched, but ALL onset types enriched toward ch at pos1). B-dialect folio-closer structural comparison: B folio-closer MID=0% gallows (anti-gallows throughout); A folio-closer maintains ~4-6% gallows in MID. The sh-at-pos1 anti-pattern is new — not previously documented for folio-register structure.
**Limitation:** Conditional tables have small N for some LF onset types (o=5, k=3, t=2 in folio-closer). Core claims (aggregate pos1 distribution N=83; sh depletion N=2/83) directional but consistent across multiple independent checks. y-LF N=19 (adequate for 36.8% vs 23.2% comparison).
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** sh E=0.16× at folio-closer pos1 equals the sh depletion at folio-closer LF (F355: E=0.16×). This double-position anti-sh is stronger than any single-position sh depletion previously documented in the grammar-word analysis. ch→ch self-succession in continuation = 1.22× (F326 bigram matrix); folio-closer ch at pos1 (independent of LF onset) is 1.34× vs baseline — similar magnitude but unconditional on LF onset.

## F356: Both Folio-Opener and Folio-Closer Are Hapax-Dominated (80-90% Hapax Tokens vs 35-40% Continuation LF); B Folio-Closer LF Top Word = ol (3×); A Folio-Closer LF Top Word = ycheor (3×); B Folio-Closer LL = sh-Enriched (E=3.45×) With sh+ckhy Compound Class (No Formula Word); A Folio-Closer LL = daiin Dominant (8.4%); A Folio-Closer pos1 (Second Word) = ch Dominant (40%)
**Experiment:** exp_354_folio_closer_vocab
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H558+H560 ANSWERED. Both folio registers (opener and closer) are hapax-dominated: B folio-first LF=90.4% hapax tokens, folio-last LF=85.4%; A folio-first=87.6%, folio-last=80.7%; continuation LF=35-40%. No formula word dominates — onset-class constrained with diverse vocabulary. B folio-closer LF top word: ol(3/48=6.2%) — the bare terminal morpheme 'ol' appears as the most common folio-closing opener. B folio-closer formula class (l/ol/ot): 14/48=29.2% of folio-last LF tokens. Full B folio-closer LF vocabulary: ol(3), lchey(2), daiin(2), oteor(1), oteol(1), lol(1), olpchdy(1), lshee(1), olchar(1), otar(1). A folio-closer LF top words: ycheor(3/83=3.6%), daiin(3), chol(2), ykeey(2). A formula class (y/s/ch): 41/83=49.4%. B folio-closer LL: sh=14.6% (E=3.45×), ch=25.0% (E=1.73×), cth=E=5.91× (N=1); all 48 LL tokens unique (100% hapax at LL). Sh words: shckhdy, shckhar, shdy, shckhy — sh+ckhy compound class at LL. d-onset completely absent (E=0.00×). l-onset depleted at LL (E=0.22×) despite l enriched at LF — l appears at LF of folio-closer, not LL. A folio-closer LL: d dominant (28.9%), daiin=7/83=8.4% (most common individual word), ch=22.9% (E=1.41×). A folio-closer line positional structure: LF=y(23%)/d(19%), pos1=ch(40%!), pos2=ch(29%), LL=d(29%). A pos1 ch=40% is ~5.4× continuation LF ch-rate (7.4%) — strong y→ch onset bigram sequence within folio-closer line. B folio-closer: MID positions have 0% gallows — anti-gallows constraint tightens through line to 0% in internal positions.
**Limitation:** B folio-closer N=48 (small); individual word frequencies are directional. A folio-closer pos1 N=68 (adequate for 40% ch claim). All hapax-rate claims based on full token pools — robust.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** 40% ch at A folio-closer pos1 is substantially higher than the ~7.4% A-dialect ch-onset rate at continuation LF. No prior finding reports this y→ch within-line sequence. B folio-closer LL 100% hapax is a new observation.

## F355: A-Dialect Three-Register Grammar Is Section-Invariant (Parallel to B-Dialect F353): herbal=75% (E=6.05×), pharma=69.6% (E=3.83×) at Folio-First; Both With Short Folio-Last Lines (3.55/4.23 Words); A-Dialect Folio-Closer Formula = y/s/ch Onset (vs B = ol/l/ot); A p-Onset Absolute Exclusion (0/83) at Folio-Last Confirmed Cross-Section; Astro Anomalous (E=2.37× Last — Non-Prose Format)
**Experiment:** exp_353_a_dialect_section_three_register
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H557 CONFIRMED. A-dialect three-register grammar is section-invariant for herbal (N_first=88) and pharma (N_first=23): herbal folio-first=75% gallows (E=6.05×), folio-last=2.0% (E=0.16×), len_last=3.55 words vs cont=5.27; pharma folio-first=69.6% (E=3.83×), folio-last=9.1% (E=0.50×), len_last=4.23 vs cont=7.33. Astro anomalous (folio-last=22.2%, E=2.37×, N=9 — likely due to circular text format). Cross-dialect comparison reveals DIALECT-SPECIFIC folio-closer vocabulary despite shared anti-gallows structural constraint: A-dialect folio-closer LF = y(22.9%, E=1.60×)/s(13.3%, E=2.14×)/ch(13.3%, E=1.79×) enriched; B-dialect folio-closer LF = ot(E=4.09×)/l(E=3.94×)/ol(E=3.43×) enriched. A-dialect p-onset: 0/83=0.0% at folio-last LF across all sections (confirmed pan-A-dialect exclusion). A-dialect sh strongly depleted at folio-last LF (E=0.16×). A-herbal folio-first top words: pchor(3×), kooiin(2×), chor(2×), shol(2×), podaiin(2×) — hapax-dominated. A-herbal folio-last top words: ycheor(3×), daiin(2×) — y-onset formula confirmed. Full cross-dialect summary: both dialects share folio-opener gallows (74-75%) and folio-closer anti-gallows + short lines; the specific onset vocabulary at folio-closer differs by dialect (B uses line-terminal onset classes at folio-closer LF; A uses grammar-word classes y/s/ch).
**Limitation:** A astro N=9 (excluded from claims). A pharma N_first=23 (adequate). A cosmo N=1 (not used for claims). N_first ≠ N_last (88 vs 51 for herbal) because single-line folios assign to folio_first only.
**Commitment status:** Not committed.
**Magnitude context:** A-herbal folio-first gallows E=6.05× is stronger than A overall E=5.23× (F345) and B herbal E=2.67× (F353). The dialect-specific folio-closer vocabulary (A=y-onset vs B=ol/l/ot onset) is a new discriminant finding not previously characterized.

## F354: y-Onset Has Position-Specific B0 Subtype Distribution: Cont LF Uses yc- (29-34%), Cont MID Uses yk-/yt- (80-85%); B Folio-Last LF Uses yk- (83%, N=6 directional); A Folio-First LF Has Zero y-Onset (0/75=0%); Folio-Closer Anti-Gallows Applies to Onset Class Only (y+k Allowed Despite k-Body Gallows)
**Experiment:** exp_352_y_onset_structure
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H556 CONFIRMED. y-onset B0 distribution varies by position. B-dialect: cont-LF c=29.5%/k=23%/s=19.5%/t=22.2% (spread); cont-MID k=45.6%/t=37.2% (yk/yt dominant); folio-last LF k=83.3% (5/6 tokens = yk-: ykeod, ykeedal, ykaiin). B-dialect: only 1/73 folio-first LF is y-onset. Clarification: the folio-closer anti-gallows constraint (F351, F353) is ONSET-CLASS-specific — it excludes p/k/t/f as onset characters but allows y+gallows compound words (y-onset with k/t body). y-onset MID = yk-/yt- compounds (k+t=80-85%); continuation LF = yc-/ych- compounds (y+ch, 29-34%) — these are transition/formula markers at LF.
**Limitation:** B folio-last y-onset N=6 (directional, not statistically reliable for 83% claim). A folio-last y-onset N=19 (adequate). A folio-first y=0/75 is a robust null result.

## F351: Folio-Last Lines Are SHORT (B=4.81 Words, A=3.94 Words vs ~7-8 Continuation) and Have Cross-Dialectal Anti-Gallows LF (B: gallows E=0.60×, A: E=0.44×); A-Dialect p-Onset Completely Absent (0/83=0.0%); B Folio-Last LF: l/ol/ot-Onset Enriched (3.38-3.94×); Canonical am/l-Onset LL Formula Not Applied; Three-Register Line Grammar Confirmed

**Finding:** H551 CONFIRMED AND EXTENDED. Folio-last lines are structurally short (B: 4.81 words, N=48; A: 3.94, N=83; continuation ~7-8 words). B folio-last LL: sh=14.6% (E=3.45×), d=0.0% (E=0.00×); canonical am/l-onset formula absent (l-onset E=0.22×, am-suffix E=0.61×). ## F349: Folio-First LL Gallows Depletion Is Grammar-Driven (Not Length); B-Dialect Folio-First Lines Same Length as Continuation (7.67 vs 7.80 Words); l-Onset (dal/sal) Depleted at Folio-First LL (B: E=0.15×); s/sh/y Content Onsets Enriched (2.1–3.2×); A-Dialect daiin Depleted at Folio-First LL (E=0.63×) — Symmetric With LF Exclusion

The gallows signal is p-onset-class (gallows-bearing) not pch-compound specifically. B pd- E=4.84× based on N=3 only (directional). **Limitation:** A-dialect cont p-onset N=41 (small). B-dialect pd- claim N=3. H548 MID/LL positions are robust (N>400). Folio-first LL depletion could be explained by first-line length structure rather than grammar rule.

## F345: Folio-First LF Is Dominated by Gallows-Onset Words (p/k/t/f) in Both Dialects (~67–70%, E=3.3–5.2× vs Continuation LF); d/y/qok/s Onsets Are Cross-Dialectally Depleted (E≤0.20×); VMS Has a Two-Register LF Grammar: Folio-Opener Register (p/k Dominant) vs Continuation Register (d/qok/s/y Dominant)
**Experiment:** exp_343_folio_opener_formula
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** Follow-up to F344. B-dialect folio-first LF (N=46): 67.4% gallows-bearing (p/k/t/f), E=3.28× vs continuation (N=2316, 20.6%). A-dialect folio-first LF (N=75): 69.3% gallows-bearing, E=5.23× vs continuation (N=1554, 13.3%). Cross-dialect conserved enriched onsets: p (B=4.46×, A=14.15×), k (B=7.40×, A=4.60×). Cross-dialect conserved depletions: d (B=0.14×, A=0.08×), y (B=0.00×, A=0.00×), qok-class (B=0.00×, A=0.12×), s (B=0.19×, A=0.20×). Folio-first LF vocabulary is hapax-dominated (B: 39 types in 46 tokens, 85% hapax rate) — onset-class constrained but no dominant formula word. Contrast: continuation LF has daiin as canonical formula word (3.8%/5.1%). The two-register LF grammar: folio-openers require gallows-onset (p+ch/sh/k compound structures: pchedar, pchedy, tol, etc.); continuation lines use d/qok/s/y-onset formula words. A-dialect divergence: sh mildly enriched in A folio-first (E=1.32×) vs absent in B (0.00×); A p-onset enrichment even more extreme (14.15× vs B 4.46×). Both dialects: t-onset is mixed (B=0.97× baseline; A=2.43× enriched).
**Limitation:** B folio-first N=46 (small; excludes folio-first lines with <2 words). Individual onset enrichment estimates (e.g., f-onset E=11.19× from 2 tokens) are directional only. No statistical test computed for individual onset enrichments.

## F341: B-Dialect daiin Is LF-Enriched (E=2.57×); A-Dialect daiin Is LL-Enriched (E=1.37×) — Positional INVERSION; A-Dialect d-Onset Broadly LL-Enriched (dar=1.67×, dal=2.30×, dam=3.68×); B-Dialect dam=6.17× LL (Canonical am-Suffix Terminal Confirmed)

A-dialect daiin (N=443): LF=18.3% (E=1.05×), LL=23.9% (E=1.37×) — weakly LL-enriched content word. B-dialect d-onset: only terminal forms LL-enriched (dal=1.76×, dam=6.17×); daiin/dain are LF words. dam LL=6.17× (B) / 3.68× (A) — am suffix confirms canonical LL enrichment in both dialects. A-dialect: all d-onset words weakly LL-enriched — positional grammar is looser.
**Limitation:** All-position counts. B daiin N=264, A daiin N=443 (reliable). "Inversion" is relative (both dialects have all positions, different concentrations).

## F340: Universal A-Dialect Body Vocabulary Shift: ALL Template Onsets {ch,sh,qok,ok} Shift FROM {aiin,ain} TO {ol,or}; chor=8.98×, okor=8.82×, okol=6.96×, chaiin=6.18×; qokain=0.09×, okain=0.15× (Depleted); d-Onset Does NOT Shift (aiin-Dominant in Both Dialects)
**Experiment:** exp_338_ch_a_body_enrichment

Interpretation: B-dialect template onsets use AIIN-body vocabulary; A-dialect template onsets use OL/OR-body vocabulary. aiin body becomes more exclusive to d-onset in A-dialect. **Limitation:** All-position counts (LF+MID+LL); qok A_total=517 (A-dialect uses qok less, rate comparisons valid but rare forms uncertain).

## F339: All 'e'-Body Templates Are LL-DEPLETED (eey LL_enr=0.43×/0.35×, Most Depleted); 'am' Is Sole LL-Terminal (B=6.49×, A=3.52×); d+eey (deey) 100% LF in B (E=7.80×); A-Dialect 'aiin' LL-Enriched (1.225×) vs B-Dialect LL-Depleted (0.634×); 'eol'/'eor' Highest LF-Enriched e-Body (1.48-1.61×)

## F338: A-Dialect ch→sh Near-Baseline (E=0.954) Is NOT Power Artifact; Distinguishable from B-Dialect E=0.678 at 2.1-2.4σ; Min Detectable E=0.890 at 80% Power; A-Dialect ch↔sh Avoidance Genuinely Unidirectional (sh→ch Only)
**Experiment:** exp_336_ch_sh_power_analysis
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H529 CONFIRMED. A-dialect mixed-line expected ch→sh bigrams ≈ 58–76 (N=252 mixed lines, ch_rate=0.27, sh_rate=0.17). At these counts: (1) minimum detectable E at 80% power ≈ 0.890; (2) z-score between A-observed (E=0.954) and B-equivalent (E=0.678) = 2.10–2.40σ (above alpha=0.05 threshold of 1.645). A-dialect ch→sh E=0.954 cannot be explained by insufficient power — it reflects genuine absence of the ch→sh grammar rule in A-dialect. Full characterization: B-dialect bidirectional (ch→sh E=0.678×, sh→ch E=0.661×); A-dialect unidirectional (ch→sh E=0.954, sh→ch E=0.742×). The sh→ch direction is cross-dialect conserved (ancestral rule); B-dialect added the ch→sh direction or A-dialect lost it. Architectural implication: A-dialect extension requires sh→ch rule but NOT ch→sh.
**Limitation:** Expected bigram count is estimated (58–76), not directly measured from re-run of exp_326. Normal approximation to Poisson adequate for N≥30.

## F337: Body-Class Position Split Is Gradient-Dependent: B sh 'a'-Body EARLIER (z=−2.19, shar at 0.153); A ch 'a'-Body LATER (z=+2.04, chaiin/chal/cham late); B ot 'a'-Body LATER (z=+2.67, replicated from F331); No Universal 'a'=Late Rule
**Experiment:** exp_335_ch_sh_body_position
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H538 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED with reversal surprise. Significant results: (1) B-dialect sh: 'a'-body EARLIER than 'e'-body (z=−2.19, a_mean=0.282 vs e_mean=0.423, diff=−0.141); driven by shar(N=12, mean=0.153) as very-early-MID formula word. (2) A-dialect ch: 'a'-body LATER than 'e'-body (z=+2.04, a_mean=0.557 vs e_mean=0.474); driven by chaiin(0.578), chain(0.573), chal(0.721), cham(0.833) as late-content words. (3) B-dialect ot: 'a'-body LATER (z=+2.67, replicated from F331). Non-significant: qok/ok (both dialects, z<1.0); B-dialect ch (z=−0.54, N=74 small); A-dialect sh (z=+0.03). Pattern: 'a'-body position is onset-gradient-dependent — early-MID classes (sh) produce early-formula 'a'-body words; late-MID classes (ot) produce late-content 'a'-body words; middle classes (ch) show dialect-specific A-dialect late-content function. B-dialect shar is a dedicated early-MID formula word distinct from sh template class.
**Limitation:** B-dialect sh 'a'-body N=26 (shar=12 dominates). A-dialect ch 'a'-body N=96. s-onset excluded (N<5 for e-body).

## F336: sh→qok Is sh-Class-Specific (B=1.967×, A=1.741×); ch→qok Near-Baseline (B=1.147×, A=0.877×); No General "TEMPLATE→qok" Rule; ch vs sh Have Divergent Bigram Profiles; d→qok Depleted B=0.591× (Late→Early Anti-Gradient); A-Dialect ch→qok Below Baseline
**Experiment:** exp_334_ch_qok_bigram
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H539 REFUTED. sh→qok=1.967×/1.741× (cross-dialect elevated); ch→qok=1.147×/0.877× (baseline/depleted). ch→qok/sh→qok ratio: B=0.583×, A=0.504×. The sh→qok rule is sh-specific and requires a dedicated p_sh_qok parameter in the architecture — a general "TEMPLATE→qok" parameter does not exist. Pooled (ch+sh)→qok: B=1.454×/A=1.160× (driven entirely by sh). ch vs sh bigram divergence: sh→sh A=1.312× (elevated), ch→ch A=1.194× (mild), B both near-baseline. qok→ch=1.234× (B mild elevation); qok→sh=1.201× (B mild elevation) — coupling is roughly symmetric FROM qok but asymmetric TO qok (only sh elevates). d→qok=0.591× (B depleted, confirmed anti-gradient transition: late-MID→early-MID disfavored). A-dialect: ok→qok=1.676×, qok→ok=2.035×, ok→ok=1.959× (qok↔ok A-dialect substitution confirmed). ch↔sh avoidance confirmed: ch→sh=0.555-0.569×, sh→ch=0.555-0.727×.
**Limitation:** ch→qok=1.147× B (mild elevation, statistical significance not tested; N=331 obs vs 288.6 exp). A-dialect sample smaller.

## F335: Complete 7-Onset × 7-Body Doublet System Confirmed: ALL Onset Classes {qok,ok,ot,d,s,ch,sh} Produce Core Body Vocabulary {aiin,ain,ar,al,ol,or} in Both Dialects; ch/sh Are Template-Dominant (B: 5-6% 'a'-body; A: 21-28%); d Is Content-Dominant (64%); chol/chor Elevated in A-Dialect; 'eey' Achieves 7/7 Onset Coverage in A-Dialect
