## F333: Complete 5-Onset × 7-Body Doublet System Confirmed: qok/ok/ot/d/s ALL Produce Words for Body Inventory {aiin, ain, ar, al, ol, air, or} (5/5 Classes per Body, B and A); Onset Character Encodes Gradient Position, Not Body Access; 'a'-Body Fraction Varies (d=73%, ok=43%, qok=36%) but Body VOCABULARY Is Universal

## F332: MID Position Gradient Predicts Bigram Directionality at 68-73% Accuracy; Self-Succession Increases with Gradient Position (ot=1.89×, d=1.54×, ok=1.32× > ch/sh=0.94×); y Is Highest Self-Succession (2.49×) Despite Early Position; B-Dialect s→s = 0 (Zero Adjacent s-Onset Bigrams in MID)
**Experiment:** exp_330_bigram_directionality
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H534 CONFIRMED (moderate). B-dialect: 16/22 onset-class pairs gradient-consistent (73%); A-dialect: 19/28 (68%). Expected by chance: 50%. Cross-dialect: 14 pairs consistently gradient-consistent. Strongly forward-enriched pairs: sh→qok (E_fwd/E_bkwd = 1.64×), qok→s (1.83/2.00× B/A), sh→y (1.60× B). Strongly backward-depleted: d→qok (0.49×), d→y (0.59×). The gradient provides a partial ordering of onset classes by their MID position tendency; forward (early→late in gradient) transitions are enriched more often than backward. SELF-SUCCESSION gradient: y=2.49×/2.85× > ot=1.89×/2.05× > d=1.54× > ok=1.32× > qok=1.17× > ch/sh=0.94× > s=0.0× (B). LATE-MID classes (ot, d) cluster more strongly than early-MID (ch, sh). y is the exception: highest self-succession despite early-MID position (y→y formula-word clustering). B-DIALECT s→s = 0 (zero adjacent s-onset bigrams in MID, expected 1.1): B-dialect s-onset words strictly avoid adjacent succession in MID; A-dialect s→s = 0.887× (near baseline) — dialect-specific anomaly. ch↔sh mutual avoidance overrides gradient directionality (both directions depleted). Anti-gradient exceptions: ok→s (A), ok→ot (A) likely reflect A-dialect ok grammar differences.
**Limitation:** s-onset N small (137 B / 97 A); pairs with pos_diff < 0.03 are directionally ambiguous. All pairs counted equally (major and minor couplings same weight).

## F331: Onset-Class MID Position Gradient: sh(0.42) < y/ch/qok(0.48-0.49) < ok(0.50) < s/d(0.53-0.56) < ot(0.59); sh Early-MID, ot/d Late-MID; Gradient Consistent A and B; ok+'e'≈qok Position; ot+'a' Significantly Later Than ot+'e' (z=2.67σ)
**Experiment:** exp_329_ok_position_distribution

**Finding:** H532 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED (ot shows positional split, ok does not). Major BONUS finding: onset-class MID position gradient. Three functional tiers: (1) early-MID: sh (37.2% in 0.0-0.25 bin, front-loaded); (2) mid-MID: y/ch/qok/ok (uniform distribution, median≈0.50); (3) late-MID: d/ot (35-44% in 0.75-1.0 bin, back-loaded). ok+'e' (mean=0.493) nearly matches qok (0.491); ok+'a' (mean=0.510) intermediate between qok and d. ok sub-class split not significant (z=0.75). ot+'a' significantly later than ot+'e': z=2.67σ (B-dialect, 0.619 vs 0.558). sh earliest = consistent with sh→qok coupling (sh appears before qok in line sequence). ot latest = terminal MID class. Functional interpretation: MID span = opening formula (sh/y) + middle template (ch/qok/ok) + terminal content (d/ot/s). Gradient is a cross-dialect structural invariant.
**Limitation:** Normalized position uses within-line MID span; line length variation may blur gradient. Section-level confounds not controlled.

## F330: ok-Onset Is Compound Class with Two Sub-Classes: ok+'e'-Body (Template Forms, 43%) ≡ qok-'q' Substitutes + ok+'a'-Body (Aiin-Doublets, 43%) ≡ d-Onset Substitutes; ot-Onset Is Structurally Isomorphic; A-Dialect ok↔qok Coupling (E=2.03×/1.68×) Is Class-Level

**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H528 CONFIRMED. ok-onset B-dialect B0: 'e'=43.4%, 'a'=43.2%, 'c'=6.5%. Two-tier structure: (1) ok+'e'-body = template-copying forms (okeey=94, okedy=91, okeedy=74) structurally identical to qok+'e' words (qokeey=209, qokedy=225, qokeedy=252); (2) ok+'a'-body = aiin-paradigm doublets (okaiin=135, okain=102, okar=77, okal=67) structurally identical to d-onset (daiin=152, dain=50, dar=107, dal=67). ok = onset-substitution for both qok (template context) and d (aiin-body context). ot-ONSET ALSO BIMODAL (B-dialect B0: e=42.6%, a=36.3%): otedy(123), oteedy(74) = template; otaiin(91), otar(82), otain(68), otal(67) = aiin-doublets. ot and ok are structurally isomorphic. CROSS-DIALECT: A-dialect ok shifts 'a'-body (43.2%→24.3%) to 'o'-body (2.6%→17.6%): top A word = okol(32) vs B = okaiin(135); ok+'e' suffix shifts to -ol/-or (okeol A=31, okor A=15). A-DIALECT ok↔qok COUPLING: ok→qok E=1.676×, qok→ok E=2.035× (class-level, driven by ok+'e'-template words: okeey P(→qok)=17%, okey=29%); B-dialect: ok→qok=0.961× (near baseline), qok→ok=1.157×. ok Jaccard A/B = 0.216 (higher than other onset pairs, reflecting shared core vocabulary). Total ok types: B=151, A=91; CP90: 54 types for 90% coverage in BOTH dialects.
**Limitation:** ot A-dialect analysis not run. ok+'c'-body (6.5%) not analyzed as separate sub-class. A-dialect ok→qok coupling N=28 — moderate.

## F329: y→d Coupling Is Pure Class-Level Grammar Rule (E=1.37×/1.38× Cross-Dialect); Type/Token Ratio=1.00 (Every Bigram Unique Pair); Jaccard=1.9%; d-Words Following y Prefer Variant Forms (dar/dol) Over Default daiin

## F328: ch↔sh Mutual Avoidance Is Dual Mechanism (Line Segregation + Sequential Grammar); B-Dialect Within-Mixed-Line E=0.67 (Grammar Confirmed); A-Dialect Asymmetric: ch→sh Normalizes (E=0.954) but sh→ch Persists (E=0.742)
**Experiment:** exp_326_ch_sh_avoidance_mechanism
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H527 ANSWERED. Two-component decomposition of ch↔sh avoidance. **TEST 1 (Section analysis):** ch is dominant in ALL sections (B-dialect ch/(ch+sh): herbal=0.682, astro=0.523, bio=0.509, cosmo=0.599, pharma=0.766, stars_text=0.686). No section is sh-dominant. Section-level segregation does NOT explain the avoidance. **TEST 2 (Within-mixed-line):** B-dialect: 24.9% of lines are mixed (both ch and sh MID words present). Within mixed lines: ch→sh E=0.678×, sh→ch E=0.661× (average 0.67) — avoidance PERSISTS = GRAMMATICAL RULE confirmed. Global E=0.47 vs mixed-line E=0.67: the gap (0.47→0.67) = folio/line clustering component; residual (E=0.67 < 1.0) = sequential grammar component. Both mechanisms contribute; grammar is primary. A-dialect: ch→sh E=0.954 (normalizes in mixed lines, folio-level artifact only); sh→ch E=0.742 (persists — grammatical unidirectional rule). **Dialect divergence:** B-dialect = bidirectional grammatical avoidance; A-dialect = unidirectional sh→ch. **TEST 3 (Word ordering):** In B-dialect mixed lines, sh-before-ch arrangement is most common (48.7% vs 29.3% ch-before-sh, 22% interleaved). **TEST 4 (Folio specialization):** No B-dialect folio is sh-dominant (<30% ch); 15 folios are ch-dominant (>70%), primarily herbal/pharma/stars_text; bio section is consistently mixed (ratios 0.41-0.58). **Architectural implication:** Full recovery of global E=0.47 requires both sequential grammar rule (p_ch_sh parameter, recovers to E≈0.67) AND paragraph-level folio specialization (not in current 21-mechanism architecture).
**Limitation:** Mixed-line classification restricted to ≥3-word lines. A-dialect mixed-line sample (N=252) has lower power than B (N=581). The global vs mixed-line E decomposition assumes independence of components.

## F305: Vocabulary Clamping (H505) Reduces qok CP90 Ratio from 67× to 0.42-0.96× Depending on Lexicon Size; clamp_ALL_CP90 Achieves Near-VMS Ratios for All 7 Major Onset Classes (0.42-0.92×); Battery Unverified — Full Canonical Run Needed in exp_304

TARGET-AWARENESS NOTE: the clamping lexicon IS the VMS paradigm (directly encoded). The CP90 reproduction is not an independent prediction. ## F300: Text-Section qok/sh Paradigm Expansion (H502) Is Genuine Within-Folio Lexical Diversity, Not Register Mixing: Text Mean Per-Folio TTR = 0.350/0.588 vs Bio = 0.218/0.346 for qok/sh; ok/ot Show No TTR Difference (Paradigm Expansion in ok/ot Is Zipfian Accumulation)

## F299: Suffix Length Gradient (H491 beta=0.30) Improves B-Dialect MID Slope to 87% and Menzerath r to 45% of VMS Target While Maintaining 19/19 PASS; Architecture Now Has 16 Mechanisms
**Experiment:** exp_287_suffix_length_gradient
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H491 CONFIRMED — MAJOR IMPROVEMENT. Beta sweep: 0.00→menz_r=−0.049/slope=−0.031, 0.10→−0.072/−0.036, 0.20→−0.085/−0.044, 0.30→−0.111/−0.051 (all 19/19); 0.50→17/19 (edy_rate fails). All 19 metrics pass including fragile edy_rate=83.5%. Mechanism: at word_idx≥2, suffix weights biased by exp(−0.30×max(0, len(suf)−2)) — short suffixes (len≤2: am/ey/dy/ol/ar/al) boosted; aiin/eedy (len=4) penalized 0.73×; edy (len=3) penalized 0.86×. Later words in a line use shorter suffixes → steeper downward MID length slope → more negative Menzerath r. FRAGILE BOUNDARY: edy_rate=83.5% (above 80% floor); beta>0.30 pushes edy_rate below pass boundary. ARCHITECTURE: 16-mechanism B-dialect simulation. RESIDUAL GAP: menz_r 55% below VMS target; LF_wl=5.891 > MID_wl=5.246 (correct ordering) but the within-line gradient is now the dominant remaining gap.
**Limitation:** beta swept in fixed steps; finer grid around 0.30-0.40 not tested. Joint re-tuning with gamma/alpha not done. edy_rate fragility constrains further beta increase.

## F296: Three-Way Onset Class Vocabulary Characterization: (1) Template-Copying Classes (qok/ok/ot/ch/sh): MID-enriched, Low Hapax 4-12%, Closed Paradigm 18-43% of Types Cover 90% of Tokens; (2) Grammar-Word LF Classes (p/y/s/t): LF-enriched, High Hapax 27-62%, Larger Paradigm Needed 75-87% of Types; (3) Line-Terminal Classes (r/ol/o): LL-enriched, Moderate Hapax 16-44%; Suffix Entropy Positively Predicts Hapax in A (ρ=+0.682) But Not B (ρ=+0.098); B Has HIGHER Suffix Entropy in 18/20 Onset Classes but SMALLER Closed Paradigm
**Experiment:** exp_295_suffix_onset_paradigm
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H497 CONFIRMED (A-dialect), REFUTED (B-dialect). A-dialect Spearman(suf_H, hapax_r)=+0.682, B=+0.098 (N=18-20 onset classes). B has HIGHER suffix entropy than A in 18/20 onset classes (B range 3.131-3.920, A range 3.020-3.698) — OPPOSITE of the exp_294 qok standardization prediction. PARADOX RESOLVED: B uses more suffix types in balanced proportions (higher H_suf) but EXCLUSIVELY with ZeroMid templates → word-type concentration is extreme. Closed paradigm: B-qok 32/176 types for 90% coverage (18.2%), B-ok 33.8%, B-ot 39.0%, B-sh 43.3%. A equivalent: 57-68% of types needed. B-MID-enriched onset classes have lowest hapax: qok=4.0%, ok=9.4%, ot=11.2%, sh=11.7% vs LF-enriched classes: p=40.5%, t=30.6%, y=26.8%, o=30.1%. Template-copying classes = MID-enriched + low hapax + small closed paradigm. Grammar-word classes = LF-enriched + high hapax + larger paradigm. B standardizes at word-TYPE level (not suffix level); A retains more midfix diversity spreading tokens across more word types.
**Limitation:** Suffix entropy bounded by 22-entry SUFFIX_LIST; ~7-12% unrecognized suffixes compress entropy estimates uniformly.

## F285: Reducing LL Midfix Rate Worsens Menzerath r (Opposite of Prediction); LL_wl Excess Was Compensatory, Not Artifactual; VMS-Accurate LL_wl Gives menz_r=-0.043 (19% of Target)
**Experiment:** exp_285_ll_midfix_rate_sweep
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H489 NEGATIVE (opposite direction). SWEEP (p_ll_mf ∈ {0.00-0.486}, N=10): all 19/19 PASS. CRITICAL: higher p_ll_mf → more negative menz_r (not less). p_ll=0.00→menz_r=-0.039, LL_wl=4.939; p_ll=0.486→menz_r=-0.103, LL_wl=5.683. VMS target LL_wl=5.015 is between p_ll=0.00 (4.939, -0.076) and p_ll=0.10 (5.097, +0.082). FULL RUN (p_ll=0.00, N=30): 19/19 PASS. menz_r=-0.043 (VMS=-0.225, 19% of target). LL_wl=4.948 (VMS=5.015, -1.3%). MECHANISM: In the simulation, LL_wl > MID_wl makes short lines (fewer MID words, heavier LF/LL anchors) have higher mean_wl than long lines → negative r. When LL_wl < MID_wl (at p_ll=0.00, LL=4.94 < MID=5.43), short lines lose this anchor → weaker negative r. REVISED MENZ_R DECOMPOSITION: At VMS-accurate LL_wl (p_ll=0.00), menz_r=-0.043 (19% of VMS -0.225). At empirical LL_wl (p_ll=0.486), menz_r=-0.103 (48%) — the extra 0.060 was compensatory for insufficient MID slope, not genuine architectural match. The TRUE Menzerath r deficit (at correct LL_wl) is ~81% of VMS target. The primary driver is MID slope: -0.030 vs VMS -0.058 (50%). ARCHITECTURE DECISION: p_ll_mf=0.00 selected (LL_wl=-1.3% from VMS); menz_r=-0.043 is the honest simulation capability at current architecture. Path to Menzerath r: MID slope improvement (H490), not LL adjustment.
**Limitation:** Exact crossover p_ll≈0.05 (LL_wl≈5.015) not tested; N=10 sweep. LL midfix distribution may extract systematically longer midfixes than VMS LL words (which are dominated by short -am,-dy suffixes with minimal midfix), explaining why empirical rate (0.486) over-produces LL_wl.

LF_wl: 5.889 (VMS=5.732, 2.7% above — gap closed from 4.854). MID_wl: 5.428 (VMS=5.409, 0.9% above). LL_wl: 5.697 (VMS=5.015, 13.6% above — NEW CONCERN). Menzerath r gap (-0.108 vs -0.225) persists: investigating whether LL_wl reduction and additional gradient mechanisms can close it is H489.
**Limitation:** p_lf_mf=0.50 was selected as most negative menz_r among 19/19 values; result conditional on this calibration for menz_r diagnostic (not for 19/19 which holds at all values). ## F282: Word-Index-Conditioned MID Generation (gamma=0.30, alpha=0.15) Improves MID Slope 28× to 52% of Target While Maintaining 19/19; Menzerath r Remains Positive Due to MID-Midfix Interaction
**Experiment:** exp_282_word_index_conditioned_mid
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H483 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. MECHANISMS: (1) gamma=0.30 — length-biased buffer draw, preferring words near L_target(i)=5.40-0.053*i; (2) alpha=0.15 — onset bias toward short classes (d/s/y/k/t/l/r/p/f/o) at higher word_index. SWEEP RESULTS: all gammas 0.00-0.30 give 19/19 PASS; all alphas 0.00-0.15 give 19/19; alpha=0.20 gives 18/19 (edy_rate fails). BEST: gamma=0.30, alpha=0.15, N=30: 19/19 PASS. IMPROVEMENT: MID slope -0.001→-0.028 (28× improvement; 52% of VMS -0.053). MENZERATH: menz_r = +0.037 vs VMS -0.206 — cannot flip sign. FRAGILITY: d_ll=85.7%, edy_rate=86.8% (both approaching ±20% boundary). CRITICAL INTERACTION DISCOVERED: MID midfix (p_mf=0.20, exp_280) undid the Menzerath improvement from LF/LL midfixes (exp_270). Without MID midfix, B-dialect menz_r=-0.052 (VMS -0.206); with MID midfix, baseline menz_r=+0.097. The MID midfix increases MID word lengths → reduces LF/LL vs MID length contrast → reduces dilution effect of MID words in long lines → r flips positive. Word-index conditioning partially compensates (reduces late-MID mean) but cannot fully restore negative r. THREE-WAY INTERACTION: (1) LF/LL midfixes → r negative; (2) MID midfixes → r positive; (3) word-index conditioning → partial negative compensation. Net: r=+0.037. ARCHITECTURE: gamma=0.30 and alpha=0.15 accepted as 13th/14th mechanisms (improve MID slope without breaking battery). Menzerath r gap documented as structural — not resolvable by current mechanism combination.
**Limitation:** Menzerath r computed over all words (LF+MID+LL), not MID-only; the LF/LL anchors dominate in short lines and reduce sensitivity to MID-only gradient. gamma and alpha were swept independently — joint optimization might find better combination. N=10 sweep at fragile boundary (d_ll, edy_rate) — N=30 robustness of boundaries not tested.

## F281: Timm Modification Rate MP Cannot Be Reduced Below 0.90 Without Breaking 19-Metric Battery; Vocabulary Over-Production Is Structural (1.45–2.2× VMS at Any Viable MP)
**Experiment:** exp_281_timm_rate_sweep
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H485 NEGATIVE. SWEEP (N=10, p_mf=0.20): MP=0.50 → 18/19, types=4251 (TTR=0.276); MP=0.60 → 18/19, types=4834 (TTR=0.312); MP=0.70 → 18/19, types=5327 (TTR=0.348); MP=0.80 → 17/19, types=5890 (TTR=0.381); MP=0.90 → 19/19, types=6489 (TTR=0.417). FULL RUN (MP=0.90, N=30): 19/19 PASS (confirms exp_280 baseline). VOCABULARY SCALING: types scale monotonically with MP from 4251 (MP=0.50) to 6489 (MP=0.90). Even at minimum viable MP=0.50, types=4251 — still 1.45× VMS 2929. KEY IMPLICATION: the vocabulary over-production is STRUCTURAL to the Timm character-modification approach. Even a single-character substitution/insert/delete from a 16-char EVA alphabet generates enough combinatorial diversity to produce 1.5-2.2× more unique word forms than VMS. METRIC FRAGILITY AT LOW MP: qok_ll=85.7% (at MP=0.90) is already close to the 80% failure boundary; reducing MP to 0.50-0.70 pushes one metric below 80%. The Timm modification is necessary for maintaining LL onset enrichment metrics at VMS levels. ARCHITECTURE DECISION: MP=0.90 is a hard constraint. Vocabulary over-production (6442 vs VMS 2929 types) documented as residual structural gap not resolvable by parameter adjustment. Two structural explanations: (1) VMS copy mechanism preserves words more faithfully than character-level mutation (pure whole-word reuse without mutation); (2) VMS writers operated with a smaller effective word pool within semantic domains.
**Limitation:** Only MP ∈ {0.50, 0.60, 0.70, 0.80, 0.90} tested. MP values < 0.50 would generate even fewer types but likely fail even more metrics. The specific metric(s) failing at MP < 0.90 were not identified (N=10 sweep doesn't pinpoint failures). Most likely candidates from full-run proximity to bounds: qok_ll (85.7%), ch_ll (87.8%), ok_ll (93.4%).

"other" suffix masking midfix-containing words. ## F278: VMS Word Lengths Are Log-Normal and Narrower Than Latin; A-Dialect More Right-Skewed Than B-Dialect; VMS Lacks Both Very Short and Very Long Words
**Experiment:** exp_278_word_length_distribution
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H472 CONFIRMED (characterization). STATISTICS: A mean=5.260, std=1.918, skewness=1.417 (N=9,651). B mean=5.400, std=1.681, skewness=0.395 (N=18,649). Latin mean=5.604, std=2.822, skewness=0.584 (N=35,820). DISTRIBUTION SHAPE: VMS is concentrated at 4-8 chars (~80% of words). Latin has much higher variance — 28% at len 1-3 (function words) and 25% at len 9+ (polysyllabic content words); VMS has 12-14% at len 1-3 and only 3-5% at len 9+. VMS is NOT heavy-tailed like natural language word length distributions. LOG-NORMAL FIT: A log-normal(mu=1.597, sigma=0.358, median=4.94); B log-normal(mu=1.632, sigma=0.344, median=5.12). The log-normal profile (near-Gaussian in log-space) is consistent with the onset+suffix template generative model, which constrains word lengths to fixed ranges per onset class. DIALECT COMPARISON: B-dialect is more symmetric (skewness=0.395) and has larger fraction at 5-7 chars (B 64.2% vs A 54.5%). A-dialect is more right-skewed (skewness=1.417) with larger fraction of 11-15 char words (1.6% vs B 0.6%), likely reflecting A-dialect's longer compound onset prefixes and suffix diversity. MECHANISM: The narrow log-normal distribution is consistent with structured grammar — words emerge from constrained onset+suffix combinations with limited midfix variation, producing a fixed-range distribution. Natural language word length distributions (power law / Zipf) would require free morphological compounding, which VMS lacks.
**Limitation:** No formal goodness-of-fit test (chi-squared). Log-normal description is visual/qualitative. Latin corpus may include English text contamination (known issue from prior experiments — Cicero corpus). Skewness comparison is sensitive to the minimum word length threshold (len≥2 excluded true monosyllables).

FULL RUN (p=0.02, N=30): 19/19 PASS. sh→qok E_global=0.970 (VMS=1.905, Δ=-0.935). Baseline Δ=-0.966; improvement=+0.031 (3.2% of gap). All battery metrics within ±20%: ss_d=95.2%, ss_y=89.5%, qok_ch=95.6%, adj_rate=111.5%. DECISION: p_sh_qok=0.02 is technically viable (19/19 PASS) but the minimal E improvement (+0.031) does not justify adding a 13th mechanism. B-dialect architecture remains at 12 mechanisms. The sh→qok gap (Δ≈-0.935) is unmodeled by the copy-buffer Markov approach at any viable p value — consistent with exp_243's finding that full closure requires p≈0.42 (architectural limit). COMPARISON: A-dialect p_sh_qok=0.10 succeeded (exp_262) because A-dialect ss_d target=1.274 vs B-dialect ss_d target=1.585; B-dialect has less headroom.
**Limitation:** p=0.03 at N=10 may be noise (18/19 could become 19/19 at N=30). If confirmed at N=30, the improvement would be +0.033 E — still only 3.4% of gap and not worth the mechanism.

## F276: VMS MID Word Repetition Distances: A < B (Correct r_mid Direction); 2× Short-Distance Enrichment vs Shuffled; Simulation Over-Produces by 2–41× (Vocabulary Size Artifact)
**Experiment:** exp_276_word_repetition_distance
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H477 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. DIRECTIONALITY: VMS A-dialect MID median repetition distance=83 < B-dialect=96 (A mean=256 < B mean=427). Simulation (A r_mid=0.87; B r_mid=0.25) also A<B (A mean=109 < B mean=170). Correct direction in both VMS and simulation — consistent with buffer retention hypothesis. NON-RANDOM CLUSTERING: VMS exceeds shuffled baseline by ~2× at short distances. A frac≤5=0.107 vs shuffled=0.050 (2.1×); B frac≤5=0.084 vs shuffled=0.043 (2.0×). Non-random short-distance clustering confirms copy-buffer-style recycling in VMS. SIMULATION OVER-PRODUCTION: Sim-A median=2 (VMS-A=83; 41× too short); Sim-B median=41 (VMS-B=96; 2.3× too short). Frac≤5: Sim-A=0.695 (6.5× VMS-A), Sim-B=0.160 (1.9× VMS-B). Root cause: vocabulary size mismatch — simulation generates ~124 eligible types (A) and ~173 (B) vs VMS 214 (A) and 397 (B). Smaller vocabulary forces repetitions at shorter distances via pigeonhole effects. TOP WORDS (B-dialect): chedy (N=375, median=21), shedy (N=325, median=17), qokeedy (N=252, median=21). A-dialect: daiin (N=256, median=11), chol (N=209, median=15). CALIBRATION NOTE: A-dialect r_mid=0.87 creates tension — calibrated to ss_mean target, but produces unrealistically short repetition distances (median=2 vs VMS=83). Battery impact: none (not in 19-metric battery).
**Limitation:** Repetition distance mixes two effects: (1) true buffer recycling rate (r_mid), (2) vocabulary size (more types → longer distances). Simulation vocabulary is underspecified — onset×suffix combinations produce fewer unique types than VMS. Separating these effects requires holding vocabulary size constant. A-dialect extreme gap (41×) is partly r_mid=0.87 and partly small vocabulary; B-dialect moderate gap (2.3×) is primarily vocabulary size.

## F272: VMS B-Dialect Has Within-Line Word Length Gradient (MID slope=-0.053 chars/word-idx); A-Dialect Has No Gradient; Sim Essentially Flat; Onset Composition Shifts at High Word-Index
**Experiment:** exp_272_within_line_gradient
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H481 CONFIRMED. MID-ONLY GRADIENT (linlen≥8, excluding LF/LL): VMS-B slope=-0.053 chars/word-idx (r=-0.078, N=10373). VMS-A slope=+0.016 (r=+0.028, N=2627 — no gradient). Sim-B MID slope=-0.001 (essentially zero by construction). Sim-A MID slope=-0.005. STAIRCASE (VMS-B linlen 11+): idx0=5.59→idx1=5.18→idx2=5.28→...→idx10=4.57→idx11=4.35. Total drop from idx1 to idx11: -0.83 chars monotone. Simulation linlen 11+ flat: idx1-idx10 all 5.39-5.46. NORMALIZED QUINTILE: VMS-B 5.557→5.494→5.460→5.366→5.125 (monotone decline of 0.432 chars); Sim-B 5.643→5.415→5.420→5.417→5.491 (flat MID, last quintile UP due to LL midfix overshoot). ONSET COMPOSITION GRADIENT (VMS-B MID, linlen≥8): short-onset fraction (d/s/y/k/t/l/r/p/f/o) rises from 20.8% at idx1 to 32.7% at idx10 (57% relative increase). Sim-B flat at 23.3-24.0% across all indices. MECHANISTIC INTERPRETATION: short-onset (single-char) words are preferentially placed at high word-index positions in VMS B-dialect long lines; the buffer's uniform onset distribution cannot reproduce this. ARCHITECTURAL CONSEQUENCE: the B-dialect Menzerath magnitude gap (sim r=-0.055 vs VMS r=-0.206) is caused by the missing within-line gradient — simulation MID words are drawn position-agnostically, producing flat MID length regardless of word index.
**Limitation:** Small N at high word indices in linlen≥8 lines (N=329 at idx9, N=104 at idx10). Onset composition finding at idx10 may have noise. ## F271: Onset-Conditioned Midfix Does Not Improve B-Dialect Menzerath Over Position-Agnostic; B-LL Over-Correction Is Not Onset-Specific; Within-Line Word Length Gradient Is New Architectural Gap

**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H480 DISCONFIRMED. THREE-WAY COMPARISON (exp_268/exp_270/exp_271): A r=+0.078/−0.189/−0.183 (VMS=−0.190); B r=+0.097/−0.052/−0.055 (VMS=−0.206). The onset-conditioned midfix distribution correctly models VMS B-LL words WITH complex midfixes, but draws from this at rates that over-inflate short B-LL words. ROOT CAUSE OF B-DIALECT MENZERATH MAGNITUDE GAP: VMS B-dialect has within-line word length gradient — words at high word-index positions within long lines are shorter than words at low word-index. Position-agnostic MID buffer cannot reproduce this gradient; all MID words drawn from same distribution regardless of word index. PREFERRED IMPLEMENTATION: exp_270 position-agnostic midfix (simpler, same result). H481 generated (within-line gradient gap).
**Limitation:** B-dialect Menzerath magnitude gap (sim -0.055 vs VMS -0.206) is architectural, not calibration-related. The within-line word length gradient in VMS B-dialect requires a fundamentally different MID word generation approach (word-index-conditioned length or length-decreasing function over line position).

## F269: VMS Words Have Onset+Midfix+Suffix Structure; Mean Midfix Longer at LF/LL (1.7–2.3 chars) Than MID (1.4–1.8 chars); This Is the Root Cause of Simulation LF/LL Word Length Shortfall
**Experiment:** exp_269_lf_ll_word_length_gap
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H478 CONFIRMED (root cause). VMS words decompose as onset + midfix + suffix where midfix = characters between the onset prefix and the matched SUFFIX_PATTERN. MIDFIX LENGTHS: A-LF=2.290, A-MID=1.823, A-LL=2.309; B-LF=2.113, B-MID=1.409, B-LL=1.720. LF/LL positions have longer midfix than MID in both dialects. EMPTY MIDFIX FRACTION (words with zero midfix = pure onset+suffix): A-LF=26.3%, A-MID=34.1%, A-LL=30.6%; B-LF=33.6%, B-MID=45.3%, B-LL=35.9%. MID is MOST likely to be pure onset+suffix; LF/LL have more complex middle structures. TOP MIDFIXES: A-LF='ch','o','e','chy','che'; B-MID='e','ch','k','ed'. INDEPENDENT SAMPLING GAPS: even under perfect onset-suffix independence, expected word length underestimates actual by 0.73–1.07 (A) and 0.35–1.02 (B) — the midfix is the unmodeled component. SUFFIX DISTRIBUTIONS ALSO POSITION-SPECIFIC: B-LF has more edy(11.7%)/aiin(13.6%); B-LL has more am(13.3%)/dy(9.1%); B-MID has more edy(14.9%)/ey(13.4%). THREE COMPOUNDING FACTORS in simulation shortfall: (1) missing midfix (primary, larger at LF/LL); (2) suffix distribution mismatch (using global suffix in cipher_lf/cipher_ll); (3) 'other' suffix compensation (simulation uses literal 'other'=5 chars, actual VMS 'other' remaining ≈3.4 chars, partially offsetting shortfall). ONSET-CONDITIONED VARIATION: A-LL ch-onset mean=6.043 vs A-MID ch-onset=5.270 (+0.77!) — same onset, different lengths by position due to midfix/suffix positional grammar.
**Limitation:** Mean_midfix analysis includes 'other'-suffix words where midfix=full remaining (inflates mean). True midfix for non-'other' words is shorter (~0.4 chars for B-MID). Fix for simulation requires midfix sampling step — not yet implemented or tested.

## F268: Simulation Produces Positive Menzerath Correlation (+0.08 to +0.10) — Opposite of VMS (r≈-0.19 to -0.21); Root Cause: Simulation LF/LL Words Too Short by 0.6–0.9 Chars; MID Words Match Well
**Experiment:** exp_268_menzerath_simulation
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H473 DISCONFIRMED. SIMULATION r: A=+0.078±0.026 (0/30 negative), B=+0.097±0.021 (0/30 negative). VMS r: A=-0.189 (N=1675), B=-0.206 (N=2389). POSITION MEANS — A: VMS LF=5.447/MID=5.171/LL=5.403 vs Sim LF=4.708/MID=5.068/LL=4.775. B: VMS LF=5.732/MID=5.409/LL=5.015 vs Sim LF=4.857/MID=5.413/LL=4.947. The battery's word_len_mean calibrates global mean only — positional gap is undetected. This is a new structural gap not in the 19-metric battery.

## F267: VMS Exhibits Menzerath's Law (r≈-0.25 to -0.29); MID Words Shortest by Position; qot/qok Onset Words Longest; VMS Length Distribution Peaks at 5–6 Chars vs Latin's 2–3
**Experiment:** exp_267_word_length_position
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H471 CONFIRMED. MENZERATH'S LAW: A-dialect r(line_length, mean_word_length)=-0.249 (N=1687 lines); B-dialect r=-0.293 (N=2391 lines). Both negative — longer lines → shorter words on average. Bucket pattern confirms monotone decrease: lines of 2-3 words have mean≈5.8-6.1 chars; lines of 9-13 words have mean≈4.4-5.2 chars. WORD LENGTH BY POSITION: MID is shortest in both dialects (A-MID=5.268, B-MID=5.456). LF/LL rank reverses between dialects: A has LL longest (5.706 > LF 5.526 > MID 5.268); B has LF longest (5.821 > MID 5.456 > LL 5.275). WORD LENGTH BY WORD INDEX: Index-0 (LF words) longest (A=5.556, B=5.821); words at index 9+ shortest (A=4.687, B=4.909). ONSET CLASS → WORD LENGTH: Strong monotone association: other/o=4.6 chars; d=4.87; sh=5.2-5.5; ch=5.6-5.8; qok=6.28; qot=6.27-6.55. qot/qok ≈1.4× 'o'/'other'. Partially structural (longer onsets mechanically lengthen words). OVERALL MEANS: A=5.386 chars (N=10093), B=5.479 chars (N=19172) — very similar. LATIN COMPARISON: VMS peaks at 5-6 chars (43% A, 49% B); Latin peaks at 2-3 chars (38%); Latin mean=4.966 (VMS 9% longer). VMS has far fewer short words (2-3 chars: A=13.8%, B=12.0% vs Latin=38%). VMS distribution is distinctly non-Latin. ARCHITECTURE NOTE: Menzerath's Law likely emerges from existing copy-buffer architecture without explicit mechanism — buffer reuse preferentially recycles shorter (more frequent) words, which are shorter on longer lines. To be verified.
**Limitation:** Correlation r≈-0.25 to -0.29 is on low end of natural language range (typically -0.3 to -0.6). A/LL positional reversal vs B/LL unexplained — may reflect -am suffix confound. No simulation comparison run.

## F263: Position Stratification Shows MID Words Are Most Constrained at Both Onset and Suffix Zones; -am Suffix Increases LL Diversity
**Experiment:** exp_263_position_stratified_entropy
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H464 NEGATIVE (hypothesis direction wrong). ONSET ZONE (pos-0 entropy): MID has LOWEST entropy (A: 2.8353, B: 2.8804), not LF. LF has HIGHEST (A: 2.9777, B: 2.9793). MID pos-0 is dominated by ch/qo onset cycling from the copy buffer (A-MID: c=31.3%; B-MID: q=24.0%, o=23.5%) vs LF which is more diverse (A-LF: o=18.3%, y=15.5%, d=15.4%, s=15.4%). SUFFIX ZONE (last-1 entropy): MID also has LOWEST (A: 2.4343, B: 2.0800) due to y-suffix dominance (A-MID: y=38.1%; B-MID: y=49.2%). LL has elevated 'm' from -am suffix, which INCREASES diversity relative to y-dominated MID. B-LL last-1 entropy (2.3495) > B-MID (2.0800). -AM RATES: A: LF=0.43%, MID=1.00%, LL=8.18%; B: LF=0.05%, MID=0.32%, LL=12.64%. B-LL -am rate 39.5× B-MID. ARCHITECTURE VALIDATION: position stratification pattern is fully explained by copy-buffer mechanism — MID words recycled from buffer concentrate onset/suffix classes; LF/LL use dedicated generation mechanisms (cipher_lf/cipher_ll) with more diverse distributions. ONSET ENRICHMENT AT LF: y/s/t enrichment at LF is relative to baseline, not an absolute constraint below MID; ch/qo buffer dominance makes MID even more constrained.
**Limitation:** Folio-dialect classification simplified; 7K 'U' tokens excluded. Paragraph lines only. EVA character-level analysis; 'c','h' counted as separate characters.

## F262: A-Dialect p_sh_qok=0.10 Closes 53% of sh→qok MID Gap Without Battery Regression; A-Dialect Advances to 13 Mechanisms
**Experiment:** exp_262_a_dialect_sh_qok
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H461 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. p_sh_qok=0.10 achieves 19/19 PASS (N=30) in the A-dialect 13-mechanism architecture. sh→qok MID E2: Sim=1.345, VMS=1.741, Δ=-0.396 (53% of original gap -0.845 closed). SWEEP RESULTS (N=5): p=0.00: 19/19 Δ=-0.845; p=0.05: 18/19 Δ=-0.630; p=0.10: 19/19 Δ=-0.431; p=0.15: 17/19; p=0.20: 18/19. Slope: ~3.6 E2/unit p. CONTRAST WITH B-DIALECT: B-dialect same mechanism failed at p=0.05 N=30 (exp_243: ss_d regression). A-dialect succeeds at p=0.10 because A-dialect ss_d target (VMS=1.274) is lower than B-dialect (VMS=1.585), providing more headroom before d-onset self-succession is disrupted. FULL CLOSURE LIMIT: reaching VMS 1.741 from Sim 1.345 would require p≈0.22 (slope 3.6); p=0.15 and 0.20 fail N=5. Full closure not achievable without battery regression. UPDATED ARCHITECTURE: A-dialect 13 mechanisms (add p_sh_qok=0.10 to exp_258 12-mechanism baseline).
**Limitation:** sh→qok VMS count N=55 — sampling noise ±0.2 on E2. p=0.05 not tested at N=30; may also be viable. Finer grid (p ∈ {0.11, 0.12, 0.13}) not tested.

## F261: Unified Onset Persistence Rule Passes Battery But Degrades Structural Matches; Separate p_y_y + p_o_o Architecture Is Superior
**Experiment:** exp_261_unified_onset_persist
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H462 NEGATIVE. A single p_persist=0.10 applied to all onsets with MID rate below a threshold cannot replace separate p_y_y=0.10 and p_o_o=0.10 without degrading structural matches. RESULTS (unified thr=0.055, N=30): 19/19 PASS — but s→s=7.203 (VMS=0.887, 8.1×), l→l=18.272 (VMS=7.666, 2.4×). SEPARATE RULE RESULTS (N=30): 19/19 PASS — l→l=7.857 (VMS=7.666, +2.5% — MATCH), s→s=4.470 (VMS=0.887, 5× — less bad). DIAGNOSIS: threshold=0.055 captures 14 onsets including l (0.56% MID) and s (1.66% MID) in addition to y (5.22%) and o (5.10%). l-onset: buffer self-succession naturally achieves VMS l→l without explicit rule — unified persist rule amplifies 2.4× above VMS. s-onset: VMS shows DEPLETION (s→s=0.887 < 1.0 — anti-self-succession) — persist rule actively wrong direction. There is no threshold value that captures exactly y and o without also capturing l and s (gap between o=5.10% and ok=6.35% is the only separation point, but 14 other onsets with rates below o also get captured). KEY REFINEMENT TO ONSET-PERSISTENCE INSIGHT (F258): low onset frequency alone is insufficient criterion for applying a persist rule. The onset's VMS E2 target must also exceed what buffer dynamics naturally produce. l-onset: buffer already matches VMS l→l; no rule needed. s-onset: VMS shows depletion; persist rule wrong direction. A-DIALECT ARCHITECTURE UNCHANGED: 12 mechanisms with separate p_y_y=0.10 + p_o_o=0.10.
**Limitation:** Only threshold values 0.055–0.070 tested. No threshold captures exactly y and o without other low-frequency onsets. s→s over-production in BOTH conditions (VMS s→s=0.887 = anti-self-succession) is a pre-existing structural gap not addressed here.

## F260: VMS Character Bigram MI Is 2.3–2.7× Higher Than Latin; Top-PMI Bigrams Are Onset/Suffix Templates; B-Dialect More Constrained Than A
**Experiment:** exp_260_char_bigram_pmi
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H463 CONFIRMED. Within-word character bigram MI: A-dialect=1.815 bits, B-dialect=2.087 bits, Latin=0.781 bits (contaminated by English translation — upper bound for clean Latin). VMS MI is 2.3–2.7× Latin. B-dialect 0.27 bits more constrained than A-dialect. TOP PMI BIGRAMS (both dialects): `in`=4.1–4.3 (aiin suffix), `am`=3.7 (am suffix), `ch`=3.1–3.7 (ch onset), `sh`=2.7–3.4 (sh onset), `qo`=3.0–3.4 (qo prefix), `ai`=3.2–3.3 (aiin suffix), `ii`=2.8–3.0 (aiin suffix). DIALECT CONTRAST: `dy` more enriched in B (3.076 vs 2.343), `ed` more enriched in B (2.549 vs 1.230) — B-paradigm -edy/-eedy suffix confirmed at character level. `yd` more enriched in A (Δ=+2.71); `lk` more enriched in B (Δ=-2.12; olk- B-dominant onset class). AVOIDANCES: `oo` is most depleted in both (A=-4.815, B=-5.310); `yo`, `oy`, `de`, `yy` also strongly depleted. B-dialect suffix zone contains onset-class patterns (qo, ch, sh, ct, ck at high PMI) — morphologically complex compound B-forms. CHARACTER FREQUENCIES: B-dialect has 2× more 'e' (13.1% vs 7.0%; -edy/-eedy/-eey suffix); B has 2× more 'q' (4.1% vs 2.0%; qo- prefix dominance in B).
**Limitation:** Latin corpus contains English translation (Gutenberg bilingual edition) — 'wh', 'by', 'th' (English) inflate Latin PMI top-20. Latin MI value is an upper bound; VMS > Latin conclusion holds but exact ratio uncertain.

## F259: VMS Character Positional Entropy Is Structured (Not Random); B-Dialect Shows Peak-Suffix Profile; B-Paradigm Suffix Stereotypy Confirmed at Character Level
**Experiment:** exp_259_char_positional_entropy
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H449 CONFIRMED. Positional entropy h(c_i) by position: (1) ONSET CONSTRAINT: pos-0 entropy A=2.942 bits, B=2.996 bits — both ~1.06 bits below H_max=4.000 for 16 EVA chars; Latin pos-0=4.236 for 23 chars (near-uniform first letter). (2) A/B DIALECT CONTRAST: B-dialect entropy peaks at position 4 (3.455) then decreases monotonically to pos 11 (3.142) — genuine onset→peak→suffix profile resembling natural language morphology. A-dialect rises from pos 0 (2.942) through pos 10 (3.680) with only a weak suffix constraint — A-paradigm suffixes (-y, -ol, -or, -aiin) are diverse enough that positional constraint is spread. (3) SUFFIX ZONE: Last-1 char entropy: A=2.537, B=2.187. B-dialect last character 0.35 bits more constrained than A — because B-paradigm suffixes all end in -y (edy, eedy, eey), while A-paradigm endings are diverse. CHARACTER-LEVEL CONFIRMATION of A/B suffix paradigm asymmetry (F114-F119). (4) B-DIALECT MORE CONSTRAINED throughout positions 2–11 (B < A by 0.2–0.5 bits): B-dialect pos-2 character distribution shows e=27.6% dominance (B-suffix templates start with -e-), vs. A-dialect 15.5% at pos 2. (5) CONDITIONAL ENTROPY: VMS h(c_i|c_{i-1}) = 1.0–2.2 bits (A) / 1.0–2.0 bits (B) vs. Latin = 2.2–3.2 bits — VMS characters are ~1.0 bit more predictable given previous char than Latin characters, consistent with restricted 16-char alphabet and strong suffix bigram patterns. (6) NOT A HOAX (weak evidence): near-uniform entropy profile predicted by random generation NOT observed; structured positional constraint is present.
**Limitation:** EVA character-level analysis treats 'c','h' as separate (glyph-level tokenization would differ). Folio dialect classification simplified; ~7K 'U' tokens excluded. Long-word positions (pos 10-11) have N<300 — sampling noise possible.

## F258: A-Dialect p_o_o=0.10 Closes o→o MID Bigram Gap; A-Dialect Architecture Advances to 12 Mechanisms; 19/19 PASS
**Experiment:** exp_258_a_dialect_o_o_markov

**Finding:** H458 CONFIRMED. Sweep p_o_o ∈ {0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20}: p_o_o=0.10 is optimal (19/19, o→o Δ=+0.028); p_o_o=0.20 regresses to 18/19. Full battery at N=30, p_o_o=0.10: 19/19 PASS. o→o MID E2: Sim=2.848, VMS=2.801, Δ=+0.047 — MATCH. Baseline (p_o_o=0.00) 19/19 PASS at N=5 (confirms A-dialect filter_other fix produces clean 19-metric battery; VMS_REF am_mid_enr bug from earlier run corrected — correct value is corpus-computed ≈0.532). ARCHITECTURE NOTE: p_o_o calibrated to VMS target; result is conditional on this calibration. FINAL A-DIALECT ARCHITECTURE (12 mechanisms): exp_239 base + p_y_y=0.10 + p_o_o=0.10 + filter_other applied. The onset-persistence pattern (y→y and o→o both fixed at p=0.10, both onset rates ~4-5% MID) suggests a unified mechanism: buffer self-succession is insufficient for low-frequency onsets (~5% MID); both needed Markov rules at identical probability.

## F254: A-Dialect MID Bigrams — Most Pairs Match Architecture; o→o Genuine Gap (Sim=2.145 vs VMS=2.801); 'Other' Onset Bug Invalidates ot→ot; sh→qok Under-Produced (Not Yet Tested for Fixability)

A-dialect sh→qok: Δ=0.773 (below B-dialect architectural threshold at Δ=1.01) — a Markov rule may partially close the gap, but this is untested in exp_254.

## F253: p_ot_ot=0.10 — B-Dialect ot→ot Markov Rule; 19/19 PASS; Gap Reduced 56% (1.41→1.677 vs VMS=1.887); Architecture Updated to 13 Mechanisms [CORRECTED BY F256]
**Experiment:** exp_253_ot_ot_markov
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H447 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. Adding p_ot_ot to draw_buf (when prev_onset='ot', with prob p_ot_ot, seek ot-onset word from buffer): sweep at N=5 shows p_ot_ot=0.05→1.559, 0.10→1.677, 0.15→1.789, 0.20→1.875 (VMS=1.887). N=30: p_ot_ot=0.05 → 19/19 PASS, ot→ot=1.559; p_ot_ot=0.10 → 19/19 PASS, ot→ot=1.677; p_ot_ot=0.15 → 18/19 (FAIL: am_lf_enr=121.1%, 1.1% outside ±20%). DECISION: add p_ot_ot=0.10 to architecture. Gap: 1.41→1.677 (56% reduction, from 0.477 to 0.210). Full closure at p=0.15 would require accepting marginal am_lf_enr regression. CONTRAST WITH sh→qok: sh→qok failed because mechanism couldn't reach target at any viable p (architectural limit, Δ=1.01). ot→ot succeeds partially because Δ=0.477 is within mechanism range; am_lf_enr regression prevents full closure (parameter constraint, not architectural limit). MECHANISM: p_ot_ot biases buffer draws toward ot-onset words; at p=0.15, low -am rate of ot-onset words slightly reduces global_am_rate, inflating am_lf_enr = lf_am/global_am. At p=0.10, effect is small enough to stay within ±20%. ARCHITECTURE: B-dialect updated to 13 mechanisms — adds p_ot_ot=0.10 to exp_249 baseline. 19/19 PASS confirmed (N=30).
**Limitation:** ot→ot gap not fully closed (sim=1.677, VMS=1.887, 11% below target at p=0.10). Full closure at p=0.15 triggers marginal regression. The stars section (f103-117) dominates ot→ot (N=88/113) — the section-level mechanism that creates this grammar is not fully explained by corpus-wide buffer dynamics.

## F252: Section-Level Onset Grammar Variation — sh→qok and ot→ot Are Stars-Section Dominated; qok→ch More Uniform; ot→ot Is Grammatical (HHI=1.23×)
**Experiment:** exp_252_section_onset_grammar
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H451 CONFIRMED; H448 CONFIRMED. B-dialect MID-only E2 by section (folio ranges): sh→qok: stars=2.155(N=144), bio=1.832(N=165), herbal=1.534(N=14), astro=1.624(N=7), pharma=1.244(N=3), cosmo=1.041(N=6); total=1.967(N=339). qok→ch: bio=1.363(N=127), herbal=1.431(N=28), stars=1.234(N=180), astro=1.270(N=6), cosmo=1.047(N=9), pharma=0.760(N=6); total=1.234(N=356). ot→ot: stars=1.900(N=88, 78% of total), bio=1.354(N=12); total=1.887(N=113). SECTION TAXONOMY: stars section (f103-117, 45% of B corpus, astrological text) has strongest sh→qok and ot→ot grammar. qok→ch is more distributed. cosmo/pharma have near-random values but insufficient N. NOTE ON exp_244 LABELING: exp_244 called the stars section "cosmo" (matched by N=144 and E2≈2.15). ADDITIONAL: qok→qok section-specific — stars=1.358(N=138), bio=0.909(N=113, depleted!); the B-dialect qok→qok total=1.169 masks opposing section trends. y→y MID: stars=3.976(N=6), cosmo=1.938(N=6), bio=0; y→y MID is absent in bio/astro. ot→ot LEXICAL ANALYSIS (H448): HHI/null=1.23× (93 unique pairs from 113 total) — grammatical, matching sh→qok (1.29×) and qok→ch (1.39×). ot→ot is genuine grammar spread across vocabulary, not lexical co-clustering. Top-5 ot→ot pairs = 11.5% (same as qok→ch). INTERPRETATION: grammar intensity scales with line regularity/brevity (stars has shortest, most regular lines). Grammar rules are section-distributed, not manuscript-universal — qok→ch is the most section-universal B-dialect rule.
**Limitation:** cosmo and pharma have N=3-9 per pair — E2 unreliable (±0.7 1σ). Folio section boundaries are approximate. y→y too sparse for section-level claims. Bio qok→qok=0.909 is a single unexplained anomaly.

## F251: A-Dialect qok→qok MID E2=1.750 — NO GAP; Baseline Sim Already Produces 1.727 (1.3% Below VMS); p_qok_qok Causes Overshoot; Architecture Unchanged
**Experiment:** exp_251_a_dialect_qokqok
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H456 NEGATIVE (premise invalidated). The estimated baseline of ~1.3 for A-dialect qok→qok MID E2 in H456 was wrong. Actual N=30 baseline (exp_239 + p_y_y=0.10, no p_qok_qok): qok→qok MID E2=1.727 (VMS=1.750), a 1.3% gap — within sampling noise. Adding p_qok_qok at tested values causes overshoot: p_qok_qok=0.05 → 2.083 (+19%), 0.10 → 2.354 (+34%), 0.15 → 2.879 (+64%). Baseline N=30: 19/19 PASS. p_qok_qok=0.05 also gives 19/19 PASS (battery doesn't test qok→qok directly) but worsens structural match. DECISION: A-dialect architecture unchanged. MECHANISM: the copy buffer's natural window-memory self-succession mechanism produces the correct qok→qok enrichment without an explicit rule. qok is frequent enough (~15-20% MID) that buffer dynamics suffice; explicit rules are needed only when onset rate is too low for buffer self-succession (y at ~4% needed p_y_y=0.10). NEW INSIGHT: onset-specific Markov rules needed only when onset frequency is too low for buffer self-succession — explicit rule threshold is between y-onset (~4%) and qok-onset (~15-20%). CORRECTION TO F250: the A-dialect qok→qok=1.750 was described as "a genuine unmodeled structural gap" — this was wrong. The gap does not exist (sim already at 1.727). F250 taxonomy sentence ("qok→qok unmodeled") is superseded by this finding. Ancillary: A-dialect qok→ch baseline sim=1.133 (VMS=0.985, +15% overshoot) — a persistent feature from p_qokch=0.12 active in A-dialect; qok_ch battery metric passes (96.3%) but structural mismatch exists.
**Limitation:** Minimum tested p_qok_qok=0.05 gives 22% overshoot. Values below 0.05 might get closer to VMS, but the gap is only 0.023 (near-measurement-noise), so no rule is warranted regardless.

## F250: A-Dialect ch→qok MID E2=0.877 (DEPLETED) — Opposite of B-Dialect (1.147); qok↔ch Coupling Is B-Dialect Specific; A-Dialect qok→qok=1.750 Is Genuine Unmodeled Self-Succession
**Experiment:** exp_250_a_dialect_chqok
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H455 NEGATIVE. A-dialect VMS MID bigrams: ch→qok E2=0.877 (depleted below 1.0); qok→ch E2=0.985 (near 1.0); qok→qok E2=1.750 (much stronger than B's 1.169); y→y E2=2.853. B-dialect: ch→qok=1.147, qok→ch=1.234, qok→qok=1.169. DIALECT ASYMMETRY: qok↔ch bidirectional coupling is B-dialect specific. In A-dialect: no cross-class qok↔ch enrichment; instead, qok strongly self-succeeds (E2=1.750). Adding p_chqok=0.12 to A-dialect architecture passes 19/19 battery but worsens ch→qok structural match (0.930→1.354 vs VMS=0.877). DECISION: A-dialect architecture unchanged (p_chqok=0.00). New: A-dialect qok→qok=1.750 is a genuine gap not in battery or current model (B-dialect analogue was partially fixed by p_chqok; A-dialect needs a different approach, e.g., p_qok_qok Markov — H456 candidate). GRAMMAR TAXONOMY: B-dialect has cross-class onset coupling rules (qok↔ch at p=0.12 each). A-dialect has within-class self-succession rules (y→y at p=0.10, qok→qok unmodeled at E2=1.750). These suggest fundamentally different positional grammar structures between dialects.
**Limitation:** A-dialect only 1712 lines (vs B's 2411) — MID bigram counts smaller. qok→qok A-dialect 1.750 is a unitary number without simulation comparison (needs exp_250 sim verification).

## F248: exp_247 Simulation Bug — All Sim_2nd Values Invalid; ch→qok E2=1.147 (VMS) vs 0.989 (Sim) Is Real Gap; p_chqok≈0.08-0.10 Is Viable Architecture Extension
**Experiment:** exp_248_ch_qok_return
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H453 RESOLVED — exp_247 had a key-collision bug in simulation accumulation. Result: E3_pred was inflated 2-3× for affected trigrams, making Sim_2nd appear near zero. CORRECTED VALUES: qok→ch→qok Sim_2nd=1.367 (not 0.320). VMS 2nd_order=1.483 — gap is 0.116 (modest, ~1-2σ at N=69), not 1.16 (dramatic). VMS values in exp_247 are correct. LEXICAL: qok→ch→qok word triples are 67/69 unique (HHI/null=1.03×) — pure grammar not lexical co-clustering. ch→qok pairs: 331 total, 206 unique, HHI/null=2.72×, top-5=19.9% (chedy→qokXXX pairs drive modest concentration). SWEEP: p_chqok ∈ {0.00, 0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20}. p_chqok=0.10 matches ch→qok E2 (sim=1.194 vs VMS=1.147); improves qok→ch (1.196 vs VMS=1.234, up from 1.162); reduces qok→qok from 1.335 toward VMS=1.169 (to 1.191). Full 19-metric battery test needed (H454). ch→qok enrichment in VMS: what follows ch? ch→r (1.553), ch→t (1.482), ch→k (1.443), ch→l (1.375), ch→d (1.263), ch→qok (1.147) all enriched; ch→sh (0.569) strongly depleted. ch→ch=0.943 (self-succession depleted as in F246). ARCHITECTURE STATUS: ch→qok is a second unmodeled low-magnitude bigram rule (analogous to qok→ch but in return direction). Unlike sh→qok (Δ=1.01, architectural limit), ch→qok (Δ=0.158) is well within Markov mechanism range.
**Limitation:** Section distribution analysis inconclusive (folio-number format mismatch). qok→ch→qok second-order structure (VMS=1.483 vs Sim=1.367) is modest and may not be resolvable at N=69.

## F247: Onset Succession Trigrams — sh→qok→ch Is First-Order Sufficient (2nd_order=1.183); VMS Second-Order Grammar Modest; y→y→y and d→d→d Show Stronger Runs Than Sim
**Experiment:** exp_247_onset_trigrams
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**CORRECTION (exp_248):** All Sim_2nd values in exp_247 are INVALID due to key-collision bug in simulation accumulation (see F248). VMS values are unaffected. The corrected qok→ch→qok Sim_2nd=1.367 (not 0.320). H453 was generated on false premises. Corrected assessments below use VMS values only.
**Finding:** H452 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED. MID-only onset trigrams for VMS B-dialect (9247 trigrams). KEY RESULTS: (1) sh→qok→ch: VMS E3=2.853, E3_pred=2.413, 2nd_order=1.183 — consistent with independent first-order rules (N=70). (2) qok→ch→qok: VMS_2nd=1.483 (N=69). Corrected Sim_2nd=1.367 — modest gap (see F248). (3) Self-succession chains: y→y→y VMS_2nd=3.227, d→d→d VMS_2nd=1.970, ot→ot→ot VMS_2nd=1.298. Corrected Sim_2nd for y→y→y=1.363, d→d→d=1.307, ot→ot→ot=1.265 (from exp_247 — the self-succession trigrams did NOT share (x,y) prefix with other KEY_TRIGRAMS, so their Sim_2nd values are unaffected by the bug). y→y→y VMS_2nd (3.227) vs Sim_2nd (1.363): genuine second-order gap despite small N=2. d→d→d VMS_2nd (1.970) vs Sim_2nd (1.307): genuine second-order gap (N=5). ot→ot→ot VMS_2nd (1.298) vs Sim_2nd (1.265): no genuine gap. NOTE ON BUG SCOPE: self-succession trigrams (d→d→d, y→y→y, ot→ot→ot, sh→sh→qok, qok→sh→qok) have unique (x,y) prefixes in KEY_TRIGRAMS — not affected by the bug. The bug affects only: sh→qok→(ch, qok, ok) [3 sharing (sh,qok)] and qok→ch→(qok, sh) [2 sharing (qok,ch)]. For these, only VMS values should be trusted from exp_247. CONCLUSION: onset grammar is primarily first-order for chain composition; modest second-order structure for y→y→y and d→d→d self-succession runs.
**Limitation:** y→y→y (N=2) and d→d→d (N=5) very small counts — noisy second-order estimates. Sim_2nd for sh→qok→* and qok→ch→* trigrams must be taken from exp_248, not exp_247.

## F245: Copy Buffer Is Strongly Auto-Correlated — P(buf has X | prev=X) Is 2-4× Rate_mid(X); Sim OVER-Produces MID Self-Succession; exp_241 MISSED for ot→ot Was Measurement Artifact
**Experiment:** exp_245_self_succession_diagnostic
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H444 OVERTURNED (with caveat). Buffer composition analysis shows: when prev=X, P(buf has X) is 2-4× rate_mid(X) for all moderate onsets [qok: 1.54×, ot: 3.05×, ol: 3.00×, ok: 2.25×, y: 4.17×, l: 2.42×, d: 2.59×, o: 3.35×]. This autocorrelation comes from copy cascade: word generated from buffer is added back, enriching buffer for subsequent draws. Result: E_buf_theory (from actual buffer composition) EXCEEDS VMS E_mid for most onsets [ot: theory 2.195 vs VMS 1.887; ok: 1.756 vs VMS 1.322; y: 2.997 vs VMS 2.491; d: 1.988 vs VMS 1.540; o: 2.427 vs VMS 1.429]. The simulation OVER-produces MID self-succession, not under-produces it. The exp_241 MISSED classification for ot→ot (sim 1.287 vs VMS 1.886) was a measurement artifact: exp_241 used global bigrams with global onset rates; global rates mix LF/MID/LL compositions that differ between sim and VMS; cross-position pairs (27% of global pairs) dilute the MID-MID signal. Analytical verification: E_global_sim ≈ 0.73 × E_mid_sim(2.2) + 0.27 × 1.0 = 1.88, consistent with VMS E_global. The simple theory (E = 1 + p_stutter/rate) was wrong — it assumes stationary buffer. The true architecture gap is HIGH-MAGNITUDE CROSS-ONSET rules (sh→qok Δ=+0.97), not self-succession. NOTE: L→l may be a genuine gap (E_buf_theory=1.882 vs VMS 2.203). Direct verification pending (exp_246).
**Limitation:** Diagnostic uses simplified simulation (no Markov rules). Buffer composition may differ slightly from full exp_236 architecture. Comparison to exp_241 is analytical, not direct experimental verification.

## F244: sh→qok Enrichment (B: E_mid=1.967) Is a Genuine Grammatical Rule, Not Lexical Co-Clustering; Rule Is Section-Dependent (Cosmo: E=2.15, Astro: E=1.82, Herbal: E=1.62)
**Experiment:** exp_244_sh_qok_lexical
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** Q004 ANSWERED. HHI analysis of all 339 MID-only sh→qok pairs (B-dialect): HHI/null=1.29× (near-random pair distribution); top-5 specific (sh-word, qok-word) pairs cover only 18.6% of instances; enrichment persists after removing top-10 pairs (E drops from 1.962 to 1.418 — 27.7% reduction only). 205 unique word pairs from 81 distinct sh-words × 47 distinct qok-words. Conclusion: sh→qok is a grammatical onset-succession rule spread across the full sh and qok vocabulary — structurally identical to qok→ch (comparison: HHI/null=1.39×, top-5=11.5%). SECTION DEPENDENCE: cosmo E=2.146 (144 pairs), astro E=1.824 (165 pairs), herbal E=1.616 (21 pairs), bio E=1.120 (9 pairs). Both sh→qok and qok→ch are cosmo/astro-dominant — suggesting both are part of a richer sequential grammar active in those sections. ARCHITECTURE GAP: The copy-buffer Markov mechanism captures low-magnitude rules (qok→ch: Δ=0.27 above baseline) but cannot generate high-magnitude sh→qok enrichment (Δ=1.01 above baseline) without regression (exp_243). This is a fundamental limitation of the current architecture: it handles rare-onset succession rules (Markov boost to a scarce vocabulary class) but not common-onset rules (both onsets common, large structural bias required).
**Limitation:** Section classification uses rough folio-number ranges. The HHI residual (E=1.42 after top-10 removal) still exceeds baseline — the grammar is spread but not uniform.

## F241: H442 PARTIALLY ANSWERED — ONSET BIGRAM MODEL IS BATTERY-COMPLETE (19/19) BUT NOT FULL-BIGRAM-MATRIX-COMPLETE; TOP MISSED PAIRS: sh→qok (B, VMS 1.91×), p→sh (BOTH DIALECTS: B 2.06×, A 2.52×), s→sh (B 1.92×); p→sh IS CROSS-DIALECT CONSISTENT → CANDIDATE FOR THIRD MARKOV RULE

**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H442 PARTIALLY ANSWERED. Full onset bigram enrichment matrix computed for A and B dialects. (2) **Bigram completeness**: B-dialect: 27 CAPTURED / 71 OVERCAPTURED / 39 MISSED out of 137 significant pairs (|E-1|>20%). A-dialect: 25 CAPTURED / 65 OVERCAPTURED / 42 MISSED out of 134 significant pairs. (3) **Top missed cross-onset pairs**: (a) p→sh: B=2.055, A=2.522 — BOTH DIALECTS, similar magnitude → cross-dialect grammar rule candidate → generates H443. (b) sh→qok: B=1.905, Sim=0.969 — B-specific. (c) s→sh: B=1.915, Sim=1.032. The three remaining failures (am_lf_enr, am_mid_enr, word_len_mean) are structural and require architectural changes beyond parameter tuning. ss_mean margin is now the binding safety constraint for future additions.
**Magnitude context:** 15/18 is the 5th consecutive net +1 improvement since exp_226. Mode B architecture continues to absorb targeted mechanism corrections cleanly: onset-preservation (exp_219→+4), edy-fix (exp_226→+1), qok-ch Markov (exp_228→+1), stutter (exp_229→+1), LL onset fix (exp_231→+1). ## F228: qok→ch MARKOV TRANSITION FIXES qok_ch (77.5%→93.1% PASS) — 13/18 PASS — NEW PROGRAM BEST (+1 FROM exp_226); MECHANISM: SOFT BIGRAM TRANSITION (p_qokch=0.12); WHEN prev_onset=qok, DRAW NEXT WORD FROM ch-ONSET BUFFER WORDS; ss_mean IMPROVES TOWARD VMS (113.9%→109.6%); ALL 12 PRIOR PASSES MAINTAINED; 5 REMAINING FAILURES STRUCTURALLY UNCHANGED
**Experiment:** exp_228_qokch_markov
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H428 CONFIRMED. Single change from exp_226: soft Markov transition in copy-buffer MID selection. When prev_onset='qok', draw next word from ch-onset buffer words with probability p_qokch (fallback to uniform draw if no ch-onset words in buffer). Parameter sweep p_qokch∈{0.00,0.02,0.04,0.06,0.08,0.12} at N=10; best=0.12 (qok_ch=1.166, closest to VMS 1.267 in pass zone). Full run N=30 at p_qokch=0.12. (1) qok_ch FIXED: 0.982→1.180 (77.5%→93.1% PASS). Mechanism: qok→ch bigram explicitly produced by Markov bias; onset-preserving modification maintains ch-onset in output. (2) ss_mean IMPROVED: 1.326→1.276 (113.9%→109.6% PASS) — qok→ch bias reduces qok→qok self-succession; ss_mean moves toward VMS 1.164 without crossing lower bound. (3) ss_y IMPROVED: 1.598→1.643 (positive side effect). (4) ch_ll DECREASED: 1.062→0.992 — secondary effect: Markov adds more ch-onset MID words → global ch rate increases → LL ch less enriched relative to global → ch_ll decreases toward VMS 0.939 (still PASS at 105.7%). (5) All 12 prior passes maintained. (6) NET: 13/18 PASS — new program best (+1 from exp_226). (7) SWEEP DIAGNOSTIC: theoretical qok_ch prediction (slope≈5.5 per unit p_qokch) substantially overestimates actual (slope≈1.5). Root cause: Markov bias applies only to cp=0.55 fraction of MID words (not LF/LL); buffer ch-onset availability limits effectiveness; ch words re-entering buffer dilute enrichment over generations. Empirical sweep is necessary; analytical prediction is unreliable.
**Limitation:** (a) p_qokch=0.12 is target-calibrated to VMS qok_ch=1.267 — result is conditional on this choice. At p_qokch=0.00, qok_ch=0.986 (baseline). (b) qok_ch=1.180 (93.1% of VMS) — in pass zone but below VMS target. Higher p_qokch would push qok_ch higher. (c) N=30. (d) Theoretical slope underestimates actual required p_qokch.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key finding: bigram transition probabilities in VMS (qok→ch enrichment=1.267×) can be reproduced by a Markov copy-buffer bias. This is the first bigram-structure fix in the experimental program. The 13/18 ceiling: adj_rate (structural to onset+edy), qok_ll (p_blind ceiling), am_lf_enr/am_mid_enr (global am divergence), word_len_mean (generation model). These 5 require architectural changes beyond parameter tuning.
**Magnitude context:** This is the 4th consecutive +1 metric fix since exp_225: exp_225 (edy_rate partial), exp_226 (edy_rate+ss_y=+1 net), exp_228 (qok_ch=+1). The Mode B architecture continues to absorb new mechanisms cleanly: each fix is independent and non-interfering with previously fixed metrics. The sequential fix pattern validates the modular diagnosis approach (identify root cause → add targeted mechanism → verify no regression).

## F227: NO-CONNECTOR WORD GENERATION FIXES word_len_mean (122.9%→94.8% PASS) BUT REGRESSES edy_rate (96.4%→63.4% FAIL) DUE TO ARCHITECTURAL INCOMPATIBILITY; CONNECTOR PROVIDES MODIFIABLE MIDDLE REGION FOR edy WORDS; THESE REQUIREMENTS ARE MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE UNDER CURRENT ONSET+CONNECTOR+SUFFIX MODEL; NET 12/18 UNCHANGED
**Experiment:** exp_227_no_connector
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H427 NEGATIVE. Single change from exp_226: connector ('a','ai','o','oi','e','ei', avg 1.5 chars) removed from word generation; words generated as onset+suffix directly. N=30 simulations. (1) word_len_mean FIXED: 6.637→5.118 (122.9%→94.8% PASS). Reduction of 1.519 chars ≈ connector avg length (1.5 chars). Mechanistic consequence: shorter words without connector exactly match VMS 5.400 mean. (2) edy_rate REGRESSED: 0.187→0.123 (96.4%→63.4% FAIL). Mechanism: without connector, onset+edy words have no modifiable middle region (modifiable region = [onset_len : len(word) - edy_len]; when onset+edy=whole word, region is empty). Fresh-word fallback always triggered for edy buffer words → edy words systematically replaced by non-edy fresh words → edy_rate collapses. Example: "ch"+"edy"="chedy" (5 chars), onset=2, edy=3 → modifiable region [2:2] = empty → fresh fallback. In exp_226, "ch"+"ai"+"edy"="chaidy" (6 chars) → region [2:3] = 1 char → edy preserved. (3) ARCHITECTURAL INCOMPATIBILITY ESTABLISHED: word_len fix requires shorter words (remove connector); edy fix requires modifiable middle region (connector necessary); these are mutually exclusive for edy words of the form onset+edy. No connector length value simultaneously fixes both (min connector of 1 char → avg word_len≈6 → 111% of VMS 5.4 → still FAIL). (4) All 11 other previously passing metrics maintained within ±1% of exp_226. (5) NET: word_len_mean PASS (+1), edy_rate FAIL (−1), 12/18 unchanged.
**Limitation:** (a) The incompatibility is mechanistic and complete: no intermediate connector length resolves the trade-off — minimum 1-char connector still overshoots word_len. (b) edy_rate at 63.4% is more severe than the original exp_221 failure (72.2%), because more edy words lose their middle region without connector. (c) N=30. (d) The discrepancy between the pre-run diagnostic (predicted word_len≈8.00) and actual result (5.118) was due to the diagnostic sampling fresh words with suffix='other' (literal string); actual experiment includes Timm buffer equilibration that redistributes word lengths.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key diagnostic: the connector in the onset+connector+suffix generation model serves two roles — (a) cosmetic length contribution (avg 1.5 chars) and (b) structural provider of modifiable middle region for edy-ending words. These roles are coupled. Future attempts to fix word_len_mean must either (a) maintain a connector of length sufficient for edy preservation or (b) replace the generation model entirely (e.g., VMS-word-vocabulary sampling).
**Magnitude context:** This is the third metric-coupling incompatibility discovered in the program (after am_lf_enr/p_blind structural divergence in exp_222 and buffer-composition coupling in exp_225). The word_len/edy incompatibility is mechanistically tighter: it is a logical consequence of the generation model's structure, not a calibration trade-off. The 12/18 ceiling established by exp_226 now appears more constrained: fixing word_len requires architectural replacement, not parameter adjustment.

## F226: edy-SUFFIX PRESERVATION WITH FRESH-WORD FALLBACK ACHIEVES 12/18 PASS — NEW PROGRAM BEST (+1 FROM exp_221); edy_rate FIXED (72.2%→96.4% PASS); ss_y MAINTAINED (81.7% PASS); MECHANISM: FRESH RANDOM WORD WHEN NO MODIFIABLE MIDDLE REGION (66% OF VMS edy WORDS) PREVENTS BUFFER COMPOSITION SKEW; ALL 11 PRIOR PASSES MAINTAINED
**Experiment:** exp_226_edy_preservation_fresh_fallback
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H426 CONFIRMED. Single change from exp_225: when edy word has no modifiable middle region (onset+edy_len≥len(word)), generate fresh random word instead of returning unchanged. N=30 sims. (1) edy_rate FIXED: 0.140→0.187 (72.2%→96.4% PASS). Mechanism: edy-ending buffer words with middle region are modified with edy preserved; no-middle edy buffer words become fresh random words (edy≈19.4% global rate); combined output edy_rate≈96.4% of VMS. (2) ss_y MAINTAINED: 1.598 (81.7% PASS). Fresh-fallback avoids buffer composition skew (no enrichment of ch/sh/qok-onset edy words in buffer); buffer returns to global onset distribution; y-onset self-succession recovers from exp_225's 79.6% FAIL to 81.7% PASS. (3) adj_rate RESTORED: 0.003 (exp_221 level); fresh words are diverse, no exact copies. (4) All 11 previously passing metrics maintained. (5) NET: 12/18 PASS — new program best (+1 from exp_221's 11/18). (6) COMPLETE THREE-EXPERIMENT MECHANISM CHAIN: exp_222 diagnosed Timm erosion of edy endings → exp_225 confirmed fix (103.1% PASS) but introduced buffer skew → exp_226 eliminates skew with fresh fallback; mechanism fully characterized.
**Limitation:** (a) ss_y = 81.7% (recovered but slightly lower than exp_221's 83.5% — reduction from fresh-word substitution of edy words reduces y-onset in buffer slightly). (b) edy_rate = 96.4% (slightly below exp_225's 103.1% — fresh words contribute global edy rate, not guaranteed edy). (c) N=30.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key finding: 12/18 is new program best. The edy_rate fix mechanism is now fully established: protect edy suffix from modification + use fresh-word fallback for no-middle edy words. The 6 remaining failures (adj_rate, qok_ll, am_lf_enr, am_mid_enr, word_len_mean, qok_ch) require separate architectural mechanisms.
**Magnitude context:** The two-experiment edy fix (exp_225→exp_226) demonstrates that the onset-preserving approach generalizes: the same principle (protect a specific character region from modification) fixes a new metric (edy_rate) the same way onset protection fixed 4 metrics in exp_219. The exp_225→exp_226 iteration is methodologically significant: it shows that the side effect (buffer composition skew) was diagnosable and fixable without external calibration, using only mechanistic reasoning.

## F225: edy-SUFFIX-PRESERVING MODIFICATION FIXES edy_rate (72.2%→103.1% PASS) BUT MARGINALLY REGRESSES ss_y (83.5%→79.6% FAIL, 0.4pp BELOW 80% THRESHOLD) DUE TO BUFFER COMPOSITION COUPLING; NET 11/18 UNCHANGED; ROOT CAUSE: "UNCHANGED-COPY" FALLBACK FOR NO-MIDDLE edy WORDS (66% OF VMS edy WORDS) ENRICHES BUFFER WITH ch/sh/qok-ONSET edy WORDS, REDUCING y-ONSET CONCENTRATION
**Experiment:** exp_225_edy_suffix_preserving
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H425 PARTIALLY ANSWERED. Single change from exp_221 Mode B (cp=0.55, mp=0.90, p_blind=0.30): added edy-suffix protection to Timm modification. Modifiable region narrowed to [onset_len : len(word) - edy_suffix_len]; when empty, word returned unchanged. N=30 simulations. (1) edy_rate FIXED: 0.140→0.200 (72.2%→103.1% PASS). Mechanism confirmed: Timm modification was eroding 'edy' endings from copy buffer words. Protection prevents this erosion. Fresh words still draw from global suffix (edy≈19.4%). Combined output edy_rate ≈ VMS 19.4%. (2) ss_y REGRESSION: 1.632→1.556 (83.5%→79.6% FAIL — 0.4pp below 80% threshold). Mechanism: 66% of VMS edy-ending words have no modifiable middle region (onset+edy=whole word: chedy, shedy, qokedy). When selected from buffer, these are returned unchanged (exact copy). This enriches the buffer with edy words (predominantly ch/sh/qok-onset, NOT y-onset) → y-onset concentration in buffer decreases → ss_y decreases. (3) adj_rate increase: 0.003→0.005 (consistent: unchanged-copy fallback creates more exact consecutive edy pairs). (4) All other 10 previously passing metrics maintained within ±1% of exp_221 values. (5) NET: edy_rate PASS (+1), ss_y FAIL (-1), net 11/18 unchanged.
**Limitation:** (a) ss_y regression is 0.4pp below threshold — marginal, possibly within sampling noise. (b) The "unchanged-copy" fallback is one implementation choice; "fresh-word fallback" is an untested alternative that would not create buffer skew. (c) N=30 — same as exp_221; ss_y variance ≈ ±0.05-0.10 across experiments.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key finding: edy_rate fix mechanism is confirmed (Timm erosion was the root cause); but the "unchanged-copy" fallback for no-middle edy words introduces a buffer composition coupling that regresses ss_y. The fresh-word fallback alternative (H426) is the natural next test — if it fixes both metrics, we may achieve 12/18.
**Magnitude context:** edy_rate +30.9pp improvement (103.1% - 72.2%) is the largest single-experiment edy_rate improvement in the program. The mechanism is clean: edy words can no longer be modified into non-edy words. The ss_y coupling is a novel diagnostic: buffer composition skew from the unchanged-copy fallback. This reveals that the buffer's onset composition matters for ss_y — edy words and y-onset words are not co-occurring (VMS edy words are predominantly ch/sh/qok-onset), so enriching the buffer with edy words depletes y-onset ss_y.

## F224: MODE B ARCHITECTURE SPECIFICITY CONFIRMED (H408): EACH ARCHITECTURAL FEATURE IS NECESSARY; Mode B=11/18 > Alt B=10/18 > Alt A=9/18 >> Alt C=6/18; BLIND -am LL RULE PROVIDES am_ll/d_ll (+2 PASSES vs Alt A); VMS LF ONSET DISTRIBUTION PROVIDES y_lf/d_lf/s_lf/ss_d/ss_y (+5 PASSES vs Alt C); 5 UNIVERSAL FAILURES (adj_rate, am_lf_enr, edy_rate, word_len_mean, qok_ch) APPEAR IN ALL 4 ARCHITECTURES
**Experiment:** exp_224_parameter_count_control
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H408 ANSWERED — Architecture matters. Four architectures tested (N=20 each, cp=0.55, mp=0.90 fixed): Mode B baseline (11/18), Alt A — no LL rule (9/18), Alt B — uniform suffix LL at p_am=0.25 (10/18), Alt C — uniform LF onset (6/18). All share onset-preserving Timm modification + VMS MID onset for MID. (1) FEATURE 1 — Blind -am LL rule (p_blind=0.30): Alt A (no LL rule) loses exactly the metrics driven by this feature: am_ll=1.238 (18.9% FAIL; without LL -am rule, global am≈2% → LL am≈2% → ratio≈1.0×) and d_ll=0.816 (59.9% FAIL; d_boost in ll_onsets is part of the blind -am mechanism, absent in Alt A). am_lf_enr REVERSAL in Alt A: jumps to 1083.9% because Timm buffer erosion lowers MID am below global suffix am → global am drops below global suffix → LF (using global suffix) appears enriched relative to eroded global; mechanism runs OPPOSITE to Mode B direction. The blind -am LL rule provides exactly 2 unique passes: am_ll and d_ll; it is architecturally necessary. (2) FEATURE 2 — VMS LF onset distribution (p_lf=1.0): Alt C (uniform LF) loses 5 passes — all LF-onset-driven metrics: y_lf=1.295 (39.0% FAIL), d_lf=0.962 (43.5% FAIL), s_lf=1.798 (38.8% FAIL), ss_d=1.605 (124.3% FAIL — VMS LF d enrichment moderates global d rate; without it, d-onset words less concentrated at LF), ss_y=2.555 (130.7% FAIL — uniform LF changes y global rate distribution). VMS LF onset distribution is architecturally necessary (+5 passes). (3) FEATURE 3 — -am as the specific LL suffix mechanism vs uniform suffix bias (Alt B): Alt B (p_am=0.25 uniform suffix) loses d_ll (60.1% FAIL) because it lacks the d_boost present in Mode B's ll_onsets; LL onset draws from VMS MID distribution (d=4.87%) rather than d-boosted ll_onsets (d=14.79%). am_ll capped at 91.0% at best p_am — cannot reach VMS 6.550 at any tested p_am because Alt B mechanism lacks onset-structure component. The blind -am rule with d_boost simultaneously achieves am_ll AND d_ll through a single mechanism. (4) STRUCTURAL FAILURE — qok_ll: ALL architectures fail (122-175%). Mode B=122.6% is the best; Alt A/Alt B reach 173-175% because without -am LL rule's non-qok-word production, qok_ll is less constrained. Structural ceiling confirmed: qok_ll cannot reach VMS 0.595× under any tested architecture. (5) UNIVERSAL FAILURES (ALL 4 architectures): adj_rate≈0.003 (structural to onset-preserving modification), am_lf_enr distorted (different mechanisms in each: Mode B global am elevated; Alt A Timm erosion reversal; Alt B/C similar distortions), edy_rate≈72% (Timm buffer erosion universal), word_len_mean≈122% (generation model mismatch universal), qok_ch≈75-77% (no bigram Markov model universal).
**Limitation:** (a) Alt B sweep only to p_am=0.25; higher p_am might reach am_ll target but would further inflate am_lf_enr. (b) N=20 per architecture (lower precision than N=30 in exp_221). (c) Tested alternatives not exhaustive — other alternative architectures exist (Markov LL suffix model, context-sensitive LF mapping). Conclusion is that THESE alternatives are insufficient, not that all alternatives are. (d) Alt B sweep used N=10 per p_am value for parameter selection.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key findings: (a) Mode B's 11/18 pass count requires its specific architectural combination — removing or replacing any core component reduces pass count; (b) the losses are mechanistically traceable (not noise): am_ll/d_ll trace to LL rule removal; y_lf/d_lf/s_lf/ss_d/ss_y trace to uniform LF onset; (c) Mode B's 11/18 is therefore both corpus-stable (exp_223) AND architecture-specific — it is capturing something structurally particular about VMS B-dialect that alternative parameterizations cannot; (d) 5 universal failures establish the architectural class's boundary — they require mechanisms beyond the current copy-buffer + position-aware class.
**Magnitude context:** Alt C's loss of 5 passes (11→6) by removing VMS LF onset structure is the single most powerful architectural feature demonstrated in this program. VMS LF onset structure (y/d/s enriched at LF) is not a calibration artifact — any architecture without it loses 5/18 passes. Combined with exp_223's corpus stability, this means Mode B is capturing genuine VMS LF onset structure in a way that is robust to corpus variation and irreducible by parameter count alone.

## F222: VMS POSITIONAL SUFFIX DISTRIBUTIONS REVEAL ROOT-CAUSE STRUCTURAL TENSION IN p_blind MECHANISM: GLOBAL am RATE DIVERGENCE; am_ll REGRESSES TO 121.7% FAIL (7.968); am_lf_enr AND am_mid_enr OVERCORRECT IN CORRECT DIRECTION (0.051/0.061 vs VMS 0.122/0.195); edy_rate IMMOVABLE BY SUFFIX CHANGES; NET: 10/18 PASS (REGRESSION FROM 11/18)
**Experiment:** exp_222_positional_suffix_dist
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H423 PARTIALLY ANSWERED. Architecture: Mode B (cp=0.55, mp=0.90, p_blind=0.30) + VMS LF/MID/LL suffix distributions for respective positions. (1) VMS LL suffix (am=13.31%) for non-blind LL fraction double-counts -am at LL: blind fraction forces 100% am, then non-blind draws from 13.31% am suffix → LL am rate=39.32% vs 31.42% with global suffix → am_ll=7.97 (121.7% FAIL, was 6.258 PASS). (2) ROOT CAUSE — global am rate divergence: p_blind=0.30 mechanism generates global am rate≈5.5% (2.7× VMS global am rate=2.03%) because LL am rate (31-39%) is much higher than VMS LL am rate (13.31%). For any fixed LF/MID am rate X, am_lf_enr = X/5.5%, while VMS computes X/2.03%. The denominator mismatch distorts all positional am enrichment ratios. (3) am_lf_enr and am_mid_enr moved in correct direction but overcorrected: VMS LF am=0.25% → am_lf_enr = 0.25%/5% = 0.051 (too depleted; VMS=0.122); VMS MID am=0.40% → am_mid_enr = 0.061 (too depleted; VMS=0.195). The target LF am rate for correct am_lf_enr would be 0.122×5.0%=0.61% — between VMS LF (0.25%) and VMS global (2.03%). (4) edy_rate immovable: 0.139 vs 0.140 in exp_221, even though VMS MID suffix has edy=21.24% vs global 19.40%. Timm buffer erosion dominates: ~50% of MID words are modified copies with eroded edy endings; fresh word suffix rate has negligible impact on global edy rate at cp=0.55. (5) All previously-passing metrics maintained except am_ll. Net: 10/18 PASS (−1 from exp_221).
**Limitation:** (a) Only tested full positional suffix replacement; blend between VMS LF suffix and global may better approximate the 0.61% target LF am rate, but blend fraction has no principled motivation. (b) edy suffix protection (analogous to onset preservation) is untested — could prevent Timm erosion of edy endings without changing suffix distribution. (c) The global am rate divergence is specific to the p_blind=0.30 mechanism; a different am_ll mechanism that keeps global am rate at ~2% would allow correct positional am enrichment ratios.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key findings: (a) the p_blind mechanism produces global am rate≈5.5% (not VMS's 2.03%), creating a structural divergence that makes all positional am enrichment ratios incorrect when computed against the inflated global denominator; this is a diagnostic constraint on the architecture class, not just a calibration problem; (b) edy_rate cannot be improved by suffix distribution changes — requires a modification policy change (e.g., edy-suffix-preserving modification, analogous to onset preservation); (c) the 11/18 result from exp_221 remains the program best.
**Magnitude context:** The global am rate divergence (5.5% vs 2.03%) is the key architectural diagnostic from this experiment. It explains why am_lf_enr and am_mid_enr have been persistently miscalibrated: the denominator used to compute positional enrichment ratios is wrong in the simulation. The VMS achieves am_ll=6.55 by having LL naturally at 13.31% and global at 2.03%. Our model achieves am_ll≈6.26 by having LL at 31% and global at 5.5% — structurally different even if the ratio is similar.

## F220: VMS MID ONSET DISTRIBUTION FOR MID WORDS FIXES y_lf AND s_lf (H421 CONFIRMED); BEST RESULT: 9/18 PASS AT MODE B cp=0.6, mp=0.9 (onset-preserving + VMS MID onset for MID); y_lf 82.5%→103.9% PASS, s_lf 72.6%→108.5% PASS; 14 VIABLE cp/mp COMBINATIONS EXIST UNDER ONSET-PRESERVING REGIME; ss_mean=1.403 IS 95.8% OF VMS OFFICIAL 1.465 (NEAR-PASS) BUT 120.6% OF VMS CORPUS 1.164 (MARGINALLY FAIL)

(2) H420 ANSWERED: 14 viable cp/mp combinations exist in Mode B (ss_mean within ±20% of VMS corpus 1.164 AND adj_rate≤0.009). Viable range: cp=0.30-0.60 (multiple mp values). (4) ss_mean reference ambiguity: VMS corpus ss_mean=1.164 (same ZL3b parser) vs VMS official target=1.465; sim ss_mean=1.403 passes vs official (95.8%) but fails vs corpus (120.6%). This ambiguity affects whether the architecture should be considered as achieving ss_mean PASS. The y_lf/s_lf fixes are exact: the mechanism (global y inflation from LF override) was predicted, the fix (VMS MID onset for MID) was specified before running, and the result confirms the prediction. This is the clearest example of mechanistic hypothesis-prediction-confirmation in the project's discrimination phase.
