## F219: ONSET-PRESERVING TIMM MODIFICATION CONFIRMS EROSION DIAGNOSIS AND ACHIEVES 8/18 PASS (FROM 4/17); qok_lf FLIPS FROM WRONG-DIRECTION (186%) TO CORRECT-DIRECTION PASS (106%); ch_ll/ok_ll CORRECTED TO NEAR-NEUTRAL (PASS); ss_mean INFLATED TO 160% — cp/mp RECALIBRATION NEEDED UNDER ONSET-PRESERVING REGIME; MID ONSET RATES CONFIRMED RESTORED: ch=15.38%≈VMS 15.48%, qok=12.91%≈VMS 12.80%
**Experiment:** exp_219_onset_preserving_copy
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H419 CONFIRMED. Single architectural change: Timm modifications restricted to suffix positions only (onset prefix never modified). All other parameters identical to exp_218 (p_blind=0.33, p_lf=1.0 VMS LF dist, cp=0.76, mp=0.9). Results at p_blind=0.33: 8/18 PASS (from 4/17 in exp_218). (1) CONFIRMED IMPROVEMENTS from erosion fix: qok_lf 186%→106% PASS (wrong-direction eliminated — MID qok restored to 12.91%≈VMS global 12.80%; LF qok=9.95% now correctly depleted vs restored global); ch_ll 183%→117% PASS; ok_ll 155%→105% PASS; y_lf 75.7%→82.5% PASS; am_mid_enr 127%→99% PASS. (2) DIAGNOSTIC CONFIRMS MECHANISM: sim MID ch=15.38% (VMS global=15.48%); MID qok=12.91% (VMS global=12.80%); MID ok=7.18% (VMS global=6.87%) — all restored from erosion levels seen in exp_217/218. (3) CRITICAL SIDE EFFECT: ss_mean=1.863 (160% of VMS corpus 1.164) at cp=0.76, mp=0.9. With onset preservation, every modified copy has the same onset as its source → full onset self-succession per copy → inflated ss_mean AND ss_y (92%→127% regression). cp=0.76, mp=0.9 were calibrated for all-character Timm erosion; need recalibration for onset-preserving regime. (4) y_lf remaining gap (82.5%): sim global y≈4.1% > VMS global 3.39% because LF override draws y=11.28% while MID uses VMS GLOBAL y=3.39% (VMS MID y is actually 2.21%). Fix: use VMS MID onset distribution for MID onset_weights. (5) qok_ll still FAIL (122%): at p_blind=0.33, (1-p_blind)×qok_global ≈ 0.67 is the minimum achievable qok_ll → can't reach VMS 0.595× at this p_blind without overshooting am_ll.
**Limitation:** (a) cp/mp not re-swept; ss_mean of 1.863 is with exp_185 calibration parameters, which are invalid for onset-preserving regime. (b) y_lf 82.5% is borderline PASS (within ±20%), may fall to FAIL with minor parameter changes. (c) qok_ll 122% improvement is structural to the p_blind mechanism (minimum qok_ll ≈ 1-p_blind at p_blind=0.33). (d) Onset-preserving "delete" edge case: if only 1 suffix char, does a replace instead — rare but slightly affects word length distribution.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key findings: (a) Timm erosion hypothesis MECHANICALLY CONFIRMED: restricting modification to suffix restores MID onset rates to VMS global calibration and fixes all predicted positional enrichment failures; (b) qok_lf direction correction (wrong-direction → correct-direction PASS) is the strongest single confirmation — was the most striking failure in exp_217/218, now resolved by the single architectural change; (c) the onset-preserving architecture, once cp/mp is recalibrated for ss_mean, is the best architecture candidate to date — 8/18 pass at unoptimized cp/mp vs 4/17 in exp_218; (d) two specific remaining failures are mechanistically identified: ss_mean (calibration) and y_lf/s_lf/qok_ll (VMS MID onset distribution for MID words).
**Magnitude context:** qok_lf flipping from 186% wrong-direction to 106% correct-direction PASS with a single architectural change (one line of code restricting modification to suffix) is the clearest mechanistic confirmation in the experimental program. The direction of the failure mode (enriched when VMS is depleted) was caused by a specific mechanism (Timm erosion depresses global qok → LF qok appears enriched) and was corrected by fixing exactly that mechanism (onset preservation restores global qok → LF qok is correctly depleted). The causal chain is mechanistically verified.

## F218: VMS-CALIBRATED ONSET/SUFFIX DISTRIBUTIONS (H412+H413) ACHIEVE 4/17 PASS — SAME AS exp_217; d_lf IMPROVES (40.6%→91.2% PASS); y_lf REGRESSES (106.2%→75.7% FAIL) DUE TO GLOBAL y INFLATION; TIMM COPY BUFFER EROSION IS UNIVERSAL FAILURE MODE FOR ALL POSITIONAL ENRICHMENT METRICS — UNFIXABLE BY DISTRIBUTION CALIBRATION ALONE
**Experiment:** exp_218_vms_calibrated_distributions
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H412+H413 ANSWERED. Replacing exp_211's approximate ONSET_WEIGHTS and LL_ONSETS with VMS B-calibrated distributions (H412), and replacing y-only LF override with multi-onset VMS B LF distribution (H413), achieved 4/17 pass at p_blind=0.33, d_boost=14.05%, p_lf=1.0. (1) d_lf: 40.6%→91.2% PASS — H413's clear success: using VMS B LF distribution (d=14.81%) correctly places d at LF. (2) ss_y: 66.2%→92.3% PASS — improvement from VMS-calibrated onset weights. (3) y_lf: 106.2%→75.7% FAIL — REGRESSION. Root cause: VMS B LF distribution draws y=11.28% at LF; simulation uses VMS GLOBAL y=3.39% for MID onset_weights, but VMS MID y is actually ~2.35% (depleted because LF draws heavily from y). Using VMS LF distribution inflates global simulation y from 3.39% to ~4.28%, reducing the enrichment denominator. Expected y_lf_sim = 11.28%/4.28% = 2.63 ≈ observed 2.515. Fix requires using VMS MID onset distribution (not VMS global) for MID words. (4) qok_lf: 186% wrong direction (VMS 0.778× depleted). Timm erosion reduces MID qok below onset_weights; even VMS LF qok=9.95% appears enriched vs Timm-depleted global. (5) ch_ll/ok_ll/qok_ll: modest improvement from VMS LL distribution (196%→183%, 204%→155%, 310%→207%) but still large failures; root cause is Timm erosion depleting MID onset rates below LL rates, creating false enrichment at LL. (6) STRUCTURAL DIAGNOSIS: Timm character modifications (replace/insert/delete) erode multi-character onset prefixes (qok=3 chars, ch=2 chars, sh=2 chars) from MID copy buffer. This (a) depresses global onset rates for common multi-char onsets, (b) makes LF/LL onset rates (which bypass the buffer) appear enriched relative to Timm-depleted global average, (c) creates wrong-direction or exaggerated enrichments at LF/LL for ALL onset-class positional enrichment metrics. Fixing requires onset-preserving Timm modifications (e.g., modify only suffix positions, never onset positions).
**Limitation:** (a) p_blind=0.33 optimization at N=10 has variance; d_ll=91.2% is slightly below VMS 100%. (b) Timm erosion analysis is mechanistic reasoning, not directly measured — direct measurement of onset distributions at MID vs LF vs LL positions in simulation output would confirm. (c) p_lf=1.0 (maximally target-aware) ensures LF onset distribution matches VMS but does not guarantee correct enrichment ratios due to global rate shifts.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key findings: (a) Timm copy buffer erosion corrupts ALL positional enrichment metrics that normalize by global onset rate — this is a structural property of the architecture class, not a calibration artifact; (b) Even with maximal VMS calibration (all distributions derived from VMS B corpus), the architecture achieves 4/17 pass — establishing a hard ceiling for this architecture class; (c) y_lf can only be correctly reproduced if VMS MID y rate (~2.35%) is used for MID onset_weights rather than VMS GLOBAL y rate (3.39%); (d) The onset-preserving modification constraint (never erode onset positions in copy buffer) is the necessary architectural change to unblock the remaining positional enrichment metrics.
**Magnitude context:** 4/17 pass with maximal VMS calibration (vs 4/18 in exp_217 with exp_211 parameters) establishes that the exp_211 architecture class has reached a discrimination ceiling from distribution calibration alone. The remaining failures cannot be closed by further parameter tuning within this architecture. This is the strongest negative result for the Timm-copy-buffer class of architectures in the experimental program — it rules out distribution miscalibration as the source of failures and points to the copy mechanism itself.

## F217: exp_211 ARCHITECTURE FAILS 12/13 UNCALIBRATED VMS STRUCTURAL METRICS; SYSTEMATIC FAILURES: (1) LF OVERRIDE IS y-ONLY — d_lf=40.6%VMS, s_lf=13.1%VMS, severely underproduced; (2) LL_ONSETS ARCHITECTURE ENRICHES ch(196%)/ok(204%)/qok(310%) WHILE VMS HAS ALL THREE NEAR-NEUTRAL AT LL; (3) TIMM EROSION CAUSES WRONG-DIRECTION qok_lf (sim=1.309× ENRICHED vs VMS=0.778× DEPLETED); (4) WORD LENGTH OVERPRODUCTION (+33%); ONLY PASSING UNCALIBRATED METRIC: am_mid_enr (101.6%); CALIBRATION TARGET DISCREPANCY CONFIRMED: official ss_mean=1.465 vs corpus ss_mean=1.164

**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H410 ANSWERED (NEGATIVE). exp_211 best config (p_blind=0.40, d_am=0.16, p_lf_blind=0.22, cp=0.76, mp=0.9) tested against 13 uncalibrated VMS B-dialect structural metrics. ## F216: A-DIALECT PRIMARY METRICS ESTABLISHED: am_ll=3.499 (51% OF B_corpus 6.550), d_ll=1.655 (122% OF B), y_lf=2.184 (62% OF B), ss_mean=1.579 (136% OF B_corpus 1.164); adj_rate=0.00933 IS DIALECT-UNIVERSAL (A=B TO 4 DECIMAL PLACES); d-ONSET DOMINATES A LL (24.3%); A CIPHER CALIBRATION REQUIRES DISTINCT PARAMETER SETTINGS FROM B
**Experiment:** exp_216_a_dialect_primary_metrics
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H407 CONFIRMED WITH LARGE DIVERGENCES. (1) am_ll: A=3.499 vs B_corpus=6.550 — ratio 0.534. Both dialects have nearly identical -am base rates (A: 1.98%, B: 2.03%), so the divergence comes entirely from LL composition: A lines end in -am words at 6.93% vs B at 13.31%. d-onset dominates A LL (24.3%, 1.655× enrichment) — d is the A-dialect LL marker, while ch dominates B LL (14.5%). (2) y_lf: A=2.184 vs B_corpus=3.324. A y-onset base rate is nearly 2× B (6.26% vs 3.39%), yet LF enrichment is weaker — y-onset words are more uniformly distributed across A line positions than B. (3) d_ll: A=1.655 vs B_corpus=1.362 (A 22% higher) — A has stronger d-onset LL enrichment because d is the A dominant onset class (14.68% base vs B 6.70%). (4) ss_mean: A=1.579 vs B_corpus=1.164 (A 36% higher). A qok=1.697×/ok=1.806×/ch=1.235× vs B qok=1.191×/ok=1.330×/ch=0.970×. Note: B_corpus ss_mean=1.164 differs from B_target=1.465 (79.4%), likely due to different corpus slice for target derivation; A vs B comparison uses same parser so the differential is valid. (5) adj_rate: A=0.00933 = B=0.00933 — IDENTICAL TO 4 DECIMAL PLACES. Exact adjacent word repetition rate is dialect-universal. This is the strongest evidence of a shared underlying encoding process. (6) Cipher calibration implication: Architecture calibrated to B targets (am_ll=6.811, y_lf=3.506) would NOT reproduce A-dialect. A-dialect requires substantially different LL mapping (weaker -am weighting, stronger d-onset weighting) and LF mapping (weaker y-enrichment). Top A LF: d(16.2%)/y(13.7%)/t(7.9%)/ch(7.7%)/sh(7.1%). Top A LL: d(24.3%)/ch(16.5%). Compare B LF: d(14.8%)/y(11.3%)/s(11.2%)/p(10.7%)/qok(9.9%); B LL: ch(14.5%)/d(9.1%).
**Limitation:** (a) B_corpus ss_mean=1.164 vs B_target=1.465 (79.4% discrepancy) — target was likely derived from different corpus population or parser; the A vs B comparison is internally consistent (same parser, same filter). (b) A-dialect includes herbal and astro sections; astro has weakened grammar (F215); A values aggregate across sections. (c) The cipher calibration implication (Finding 6) is a projection, not a tested result.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key findings: (a) adj_rate is dialect-universal — the strongest evidence of a shared encoding process across A and B; (b) am_ll and y_lf diverge substantially between dialects (A at 51% and 62% of B respectively), requiring dialect-specific parameter calibration; (c) A-dialect is d-dominant at LL (24.3%) vs B ch-dominant (14.5%) — the most structurally significant LL difference; (d) ss_mean is higher in A (1.579 vs B_corpus 1.164), consistent with A having higher d/qok/ok frequencies.
**Magnitude context:** adj_rate being identical across 11,363 A words and 19,582 B words (to 4 decimal places) is the most specific cross-dialect invariant established in the project at the metric level. It suggests a process operating at the word-generation level that is dialect-independent. The am_ll divergence (3.499 vs 6.550) quantifies for the first time that the A-dialect LL slot has a fundamentally different suffix composition from B — the LL "slot" itself appears to differ in what counts as a line-closing word.

## F215: A PS FORMULA STABLE ACROSS HIGH-GRAMMAR SECTIONS (herbal-type: p=27.97×/t=5.71×/k=3.81×/f=20.34×, gal=72%; pharma: p=28.69×/t=4.28×/k=4.77×, gal=65%); A ASTRO IS EXCEPTION: t-ONLY (t=9.19×; p=k=f=0×), y=3.20× ENRICHED AT PS, gal=28% — CONSISTENT WITH F196 (astro=weakest A grammar); B FORMULA CONFIRMED IN ONE AVAILABLE SECTION (p=20.39×/t=7.35×/k=4.89×/f=10.57×, gal=69%)
**Experiment:** exp_215_ps_formula_section_stability
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H400 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED. (1) A PS formula is stable across high-grammar sections: "other" (herbal+cosmo+stars, n=115): p=27.97×/t=5.71×/k=3.81×/f=20.34×/gal=72%/y=0.00×/d=0.18×; pharma (n=23): p=28.69×/t=4.28×/k=4.77×/f=0.00×/gal=65%/y=0.69×. Both sections reproduce the total A formula (F198). (2) A astro (n=25) has DIFFERENT PS formula: t-ONLY enriched (9.19×); p=k=f=0.00×; y=3.20× ENRICHED (normally depleted 0.21-0.25×); gal=28%. Top astro PS words are all hapax. This extends F196 (astro=weakest A grammar) to PS slot specifically: A astro permits y-onset at PS and restricts gallows to t-only — the formula is present but at much reduced strictness. (3) B-dialect: only "other" section (n=98) has sufficient n — confirms standard B formula. Section-level stability for B cannot be assessed from available data. (4) Note: section classification partially broken (folio_base strips r/v, breaking regex for most folios); astro/pharma entries represent genuine sections from complex-named folios.
**Limitation:** A astro PS words are all hapax (n=1 each) — enrichments are at onset-class level, not word level. Section classification limitation means "other" combines herbal+cosmo+stars without separation. A pharma f=0.00× (no f-onset PS words in 23 pharma paragraphs) — consistent with F196's f+ch as PS-active in A herbal but absorbed into MID in B; in A pharma, f may shift toward MID. B section data insufficient.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key finding: PS formula is a grammar rule stable in high-grammar sections; A astro deviation confirms section-level grammar strength variation (not formula absence). The shared A/B PS formula (p/t/k/f enriched) is now characterized as: fully operational in high-grammar contexts; partially operational (t-reduced) in low-grammar contexts (A astro).
**Magnitude context:** The A astro exception (p=k=f=0×, y=3.20×) is the most dramatic within-dialect section difference in this project. It confirms that the same "VMS grammar system" has multiple strength levels, and the PS formula is one of the most grammar-sensitive features — relaxing dramatically in low-grammar sections. This supports the template interpretation: the formula is built into the system; how strictly it is applied varies by section/scribe.

## F214: B pos=1 ANTI-PS CONSTRAINT IS CROSS-SECTION STABLE (0/98 FOR p+t+k IN ALL B SECTIONS); t HARD-EXCLUDED FROM pos=1 IN BOTH DIALECTS (B: 0/98, A: 0/160); p HARD-EXCLUDED IN B (0/98), NEAR-EXCLUDED IN A (1/160); k HARD-EXCLUDED IN B (0/98), NEAR-EXCLUDED IN A (3/160); A pos=1 = ch(21.9%)/sh(21.2%) DOMINANT; B pos=1 = sh/qok/ch/o/d DISTRIBUTED; SHARED A/B GRAMMAR SKELETON [PS=GALLOWS] → [pos=1=ANTI-GALLOWS]
**Experiment:** exp_214_pos1_anti_ps_sections
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H405 SUPPORTED. (1) B p+t+k at pos=1=0/98 across ALL sections (other: 0/95; pharma: 0/3). Cross-section stability confirmed. (2) t is 0/98 in B and 0/160 in A — HARD EXCLUDED FROM pos=1 IN BOTH DIALECTS despite being the #2 PS class in both (B: 17.8%; A: 18.4%). (3) p: B=0/98, A=1/160 (0.6%); k: B=0/98, A=3/160 (1.9%). B exclusion is absolute; A has minimal leakage. (4) f is NOT excluded from pos=1 (B: 4.1%/2.08×; A: 1.9%/1.26×) — the anti-PS constraint is specifically p/t/k, not all gallows. (5) A pos=1 dominated by ch(21.9%,n=35)/sh(21.2%,n=34) = 43.1% combined (exactly F207's PS→shey/sheol/chor pattern). B pos=1 more distributed: sh(16.3%)/qok(15.3%)/o(13.3%)/ch(10.2%)/d(9.2%)/ol(8.2%). (6) Both A and B share the grammar skeleton [PS=gallows class] → [pos=1=anti-gallows class] — a third instance of shared A/B syntactic structure (after shared PS formula F198/F208 and qo-class anti-boundary exclusion). t=0/258 combined across both dialects at pos=1 makes t-onset the clearest empirical case of hard cross-dialect within-line positional grammar.
**Limitation:** B section classification mostly shows "other" (98/101 B paragraphs) due to folio range coverage. The constraint holds within the "other" category (0/95), making the section-level claim conservative but robust. A pharma shows 0/23 (full exclusion); A other/astro show 1-3 leakage cases from k (3) and p (1). The "grammar rule vs scribe convention" interpretation is consistent with the data but cannot definitively exclude that all sections happen to be from the same scribe.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) t-onset is universally excluded from pos=1 across both dialects and all sections (0/258 total) — the strongest cross-dialect within-line grammar constraint in the project; (b) the anti-PS slot at pos=1 is a cross-section grammar rule, not a scribe artifact; (c) A and B share the [PS=gallows → pos=1=anti-gallows] template while differing in which onset class fills pos=1 (A: ch/sh specifically; B: sh/qok/ch broadly distributed).
**Magnitude context:** t=0/258 at pos=1 (vs 17-18% at PS in both dialects) is one of the largest quantitative contrasts in the project. It surpasses the -am LL enrichment (6.8×) in raw contrast magnitude (PS→pos=1 transition for t: ~0% from ~18%, a ~∞ ratio). Combined with F213 (B pos=1 anti-PS) and F198/F208 (shared PS formula), the within-line positional grammar of VMS first lines is now fully characterized at the two-slot level for both dialects.

## F213: B FIRST-LINE pos=1 IS THE "ANTI-PS SLOT" — p/t/k (67% OF B PS) ARE STRICTLY EXCLUDED FROM pos=1 (0/98 WORDS); pos=1 DOMINATED BY sh(1.59×)/qok(2.22×)/ch(1.12×)/ol(1.66×)/d(1.13×); y+GALLOWS WORDS DIFFUSE (pos=3+ 1.38×, NOT pos=1); A-DIALECT SHOWS PARALLEL SOFTER ANTI-PS PATTERN (sh/ch dominant at pos=1; p/t near-absent)
**Experiment:** exp_213_b_pos1_y_gallows_slot
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H404 NOT SUPPORTED (y+gallows not at pos=1); NEW FINDING. B pos=1 (immediately after PS word) has ZERO words with p+t+k onset (0/98 words; expected ~65 under PS base rate; p<10⁻³⁰). These three onset classes dominate B PS (p=35.64%, t=17.82%, k=12.87%, combined 67%) but are completely excluded from pos=1. B pos=1 is instead dominated by sh(16.33%, 1.59×), qok(15.31%, 2.22×), ch(10.20%, 1.12×), ol(8.16%, 1.66×), d(9.18%, 1.13×), o(13.27%, 1.35×) — all onset classes that are near-absent from B PS. Top B pos=1 words: qokedy(4)/shedy(3)/or(3)/ytedy(2)/qokal(2)/shey(2)/chedy(2)/dar(2)/olkey(2). B first-line structure: [PS: p/t/k=67%] → [pos=1: sh/qok/ch/d/ol=anti-gallows, 0% p/t/k] → [pos=2+: variable]. A-dialect comparison: A pos=1 also shows anti-PS pattern but softer (p: 0.11×, t: 0%, k: 0.63× — not absolute exclusion); A pos=1 dominated by sh(1.46×,n=34)/ch(1.61×,n=35), consistent with F207 (PS→shey/sheol/shor). Both dialects have an anti-PS pos=1 slot; B's exclusion is complete (0/98 for p+t+k) while A's is near-complete. y+gallows words: pos=3+ enriched (1.38×, n=13); pos=1 at baseline (0.91×, n=2). H404 NOT SUPPORTED — y+gallows are diffuse in B first lines, not a pos=1 slot. f is not excluded from pos=1 (B pos=1 f=2.08×, n=4): f is the weakest PS gallows (2.97% at PS, 1.51×) and is enriched at pos=1, not excluded. The anti-PS constraint is specifically p/t/k (the three highest-PS gallows), not all gallows.
**Limitation:** n=98 at pos=1 — absolute zero for p+t+k is robust (p<10⁻³⁰ even with N=98). y+gallows at pos=3+: n=13/418 (1.38×) — directional but moderate n. A-dialect comparison: A n=160 at pos=1 — near-zero p/t (0-1 words each); k has n=3 (leakage vs B's zero); pattern is directionally consistent.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) B pos=1 has a hard exclusion of the PS onset class (p/t/k) — the three dominant PS onsets are 0/98 at pos=1; (b) B pos=1 is the "anti-PS slot" occupied by sh/qok/ch/d/ol; (c) this alternating onset pattern within B first lines is the strongest within-line positional grammar constraint established in the project; (d) A has a parallel (softer) anti-PS pattern at pos=1 (sh/ch dominant, p/t near-absent).
**Magnitude context:** The strict anti-PS exclusion at pos=1 (0/98 for p+t+k) establishes B first-line grammar as a two-slot formula: [PS: gallows class] → [pos=1: anti-gallows class]. This is the first within-line positional grammar rule with n>90 and p<10⁻³⁰ — the strongest statistical finding for within-line structure in this project. H405 generated to test section-level stability.

## F212: B FIRST-LINE BODY y-ONSET ENRICHMENT (1.88×) IS DRIVEN BY y+GALLOWS-COMPOUND WORDS (ypchedy/ypchdy/ypchey/yfchey) — NOT THE STANDARD B LF y-CLASS (ykaiin/ycheey/yshey); B PF-LL qo-CLASS EXCLUDED (0.26× COMBINED, p<0.001): qot(0.27×)/qo(0.32×)/qok(0.25×) vs WP-LL qo-CLASS (0.69× — GRADIENT EXCLUSION CONFIRMED); F206's B qo-CLASS PF-LL=0.26× EXACTLY REPRODUCED FROM INDEPENDENT PATHWAY
**Experiment:** exp_212_b_firstline_y_qot_pf_ll
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H398 SUPPORTED (UNEXPECTED); H399 CONFIRMED. (1) H398: B first-line body y-onset enrichment (1.88×, n=39) is NOT the standard B LF y-onset vocabulary (ycheey/yshey/ykaiin/yshedy/ychedy). Top first-line body y-words: ypchedy(3), ypchdy(3, fl-only: lf_rate=0), ytedy(2), yteey(2), ypchey(2, fl-only). The top 3 most-enriched y-words in B first-line body are y+gallows-compound words (y+pch: ypchedy 11.84×, ypchdy fl-only, ypchey fl-only). Also fl-only: yfcheky, yfchey, yfoldy, ylyfody, ypches. The standard B LF y-class words (ycheey, yshey, ykaiin, yteedy, ychedy) are near-absent from first-line body positions. Implication: B first-line body contains a distinct vocabulary slot for y+gallows-compound words (y-onset words with pch/fch gallows structure), separate from the y-onset LF class. This slot may immediately follow the PS word, linking the PS gallows-compound formula (pchedar, tchedy) to the first-line body via y-prefixed gallows variants. (2) H399: B PF-LL (n=94) qo-class combined = 5/94 = 5.32% (0.26× vs base 20.14%). Expected under base rate: 18.9 words; observed: 5; p<0.001. Individual onsets: qok=3/94(0.25×), qot=1/94(0.27×), qo=1/94(0.32×). B WP-LL qo-class combined = 317/2295 = 13.81% (0.69×) — less severe depletion. Gradient confirmed: para-final LL is more excluded (0.26×) than within-para LL (0.69×). F206's B qo-class PF-LL=0.26× exactly reproduced from independent pathway (exp_212 used different tier classification). B PF-LL dominant words: chedy(4)/shedy(4)/okeey(3)/okeeey(2)/chey(2)/oty(2) — confirms F207/F208. Note: cth=8.10× at PF-LL (n=2) is the same n=2 noise flagged in F205→F206 correction; still not reliable.
**Limitation:** H398: n=39 total first-line body y-words; y+gallows cluster n=8. Directional finding for vocabulary class identity. Section breakdown unreliable (most B paragraphs classified as "other" due to folio range gap in classifier — word-level findings unaffected). H399: qot and qo individual PF-LL counts are n=1 — individually unreliable; qok n=3 and combined qo-class n=5 are statistically robust (p<0.001). cth PF-LL=8.10× (n=2) remains noise as per F205/F206 correction.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) B first-line body y-onset is a DISTINCT class (y+gallows compound) from the standard B LF y-onset vocabulary — the two y-onset classes occupy different paragraph slots; (b) B qo-class gradient exclusion from paragraph boundaries confirmed (PF-LL 0.26× > WP-LL 0.69× severity); (c) F206's B PF-LL qo-class rate exactly reproduced, strengthening that finding.
**Magnitude context:** H398's finding that B first-line body y-words are predominantly y+gallows compounds (not standard LF y-words) is the first evidence that the B first-line body slot has sub-class structure. The PS formula (p/t/k/f gallows compounds) is followed not just by generic o/y/qo vocabulary but by gallows-compound y-prefix words that structurally echo the PS vocabulary. This suggests the B first-line may contain a two-step formula: [PS: gallows-compound word] → [pos=1: y+gallows-compound word] → [subsequent body: o/qo vocabulary]. H404 generated to test whether the y+gallows slot is specifically at pos=1.

## F211: POSITION-AWARE HYBRID WITH TARGET-CALIBRATED PARAMETERS (d_am=0.16, p_blind=0.40, p_lf_blind=0.22, cp=0.76, mp=0.9) ACHIEVES ALL FIVE PRIMARY VMS METRICS WITHIN 3% SIMULTANEOUSLY: am_ll=6.819 (100.1%VMS), d_ll=1.470 (100.4%VMS), y_lf=3.510 (100.1%VMS), ss_mean=1.425 (97.2%VMS), adj_rate=0.00424 (below VMS ✓); am_ll AND d_ll STABLE ACROSS p_lf_blind SWEEP (LF/LL RULES INDEPENDENT); SECONDARY: ss_mean SHOWS SMALL DOWNWARD TREND WITH INCREASING p_lf_blind (SECOND-ORDER COUPLING — MANAGEABLE AT p_lf_blind ≤ 0.25)
**Experiment:** exp_211_lf_blind_fine_sweep
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H403 SUPPORTED (CRITICAL). Fine-grained sweep p_lf_blind ∈ {0.18, 0.19, 0.20, 0.21, 0.22, 0.23, 0.24, 0.25, 0.27} with d_am=0.16, p_blind=0.40, cp=0.76, mp=0.9 fixed. N=50 sims per configuration. (1) p_lf_blind=0.22 achieves y_lf=3.510 (100.1%VMS) — essentially exact VMS target. exp_210 interpolation (0.22-0.23) was accurate. The y_lf metric is approximately linear in p_lf_blind across the tested range. (2) JOINT RESULT AT p_lf_blind=0.22: am_ll=6.819 (100.1%VMS ✓), d_ll=1.470 (100.4%VMS ✓), y_lf=3.510 (100.1%VMS ✓), ss_mean=1.425 (97.2%VMS ✓), adj_rate=0.00424 (below VMS ✓). All five primary metrics within 3% simultaneously (three of five within 1%). STRONGEST JOINT RESULT IN EXPERIMENTAL PROGRAM. (3) am_ll and d_ll are stable across the sweep (range: 6.779-6.824 and 1.460-1.492 respectively) — consistent with simulation noise; confirms LF and LL rules are independent. (4) ss_mean trend: 1.437 (p_lf=0.18) → 1.407 (p_lf=0.25) — small downward second-order coupling (blind LF y-onset words not drawn from copy buffer). At p_lf_blind=0.22, ss_mean=1.425 — within VMS range. Cross-experiment consistency: p_lf=0.20 in exp_210 (N=30) → y_lf=3.364; in exp_211 (N=50) → y_lf=3.369 (agreement within 0.005 — confirms reproducibility).
**Limitation:** (a) TARGET-AWARENESS (CRITICAL): All four calibration parameters were chosen by reference to VMS targets: cp=0.76 (ss_mean/adj_rate, exp_185), p_blind=0.40 (am_ll, exp_209), d_am=0.16 (d_ll, exp_210), p_lf_blind=0.22 (y_lf, this experiment). The sweep was explicitly designed to find p_lf_blind that matches VMS y_lf. This demonstrates JOINT ACHIEVABILITY, not independent prediction. (b) N=50 sims — mean estimates reliable but CIs remain moderate (y_lf CI=[3.219,3.754] at p_lf=0.22). (c) A-dialect metrics not tested with this architecture. (d) Quire-level VMS metric variation not tested.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key finding: at the four target-calibrated parameters, the position-aware hybrid reproduces all five primary VMS metrics to within 3% simultaneously. The architecture's discrimination status is: "precisely jointly achievable with target calibration" — the remaining discrimination gap is entirely conceptual (no first-principles derivation of the calibration parameters from Latin morphology or position-sensitivity theory).
**Magnitude context:** This is the highest-precision joint reproduction of VMS structural metrics achieved by any tested mechanism. The entire class of position-aware hybrid mechanisms (blind LL + blind LF + Timm char mod) is now fully characterized: the architecture can match any combination of {am_ll, d_ll, y_lf} simultaneously by tuning three position-specific parameters, while ss_mean and adj_rate are governed by the copy component (cp, mp) independently.

## F210: POSITION-AWARE HYBRID ACHIEVES JOINT VIABILITY ON ALL FIVE PRIMARY VMS METRICS (am_ll, d_ll, y_lf, ss_mean, adj_rate) WITH TARGET-CALIBRATED PARAMETERS; d_am=0.16 REPRODUCES d_ll=1.461 (99.8%VMS) AND am_ll=6.778 (99.5%VMS) SIMULTANEOUSLY; BLIND LF MAPPING AT p_lf_blind=0.20 CLOSES THE y_lf GAP (96%VMS); y_lf TARGET ≈ VMS AT p_lf_blind ≈ 0.22-0.24
**Experiment:** exp_210_dll_onset_recal
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H401 SUPPORTED; H402 SUPPORTED (MAJOR). (1) H401: Sweep of d_am_weight (d-onset fraction for -am word onsets in blind LL mapping) with p_blind=0.40 fixed. At d_am=0.16: am_ll=6.778 (99.5%VMS ✓) AND d_ll=1.461 (99.8%VMS ✓) simultaneously. am_ll is INDEPENDENT of d_am_weight (d_am_weight controls onset distribution of -am words but not how many LL words become -am). d_ll is linearly proportional to d_am_weight. This means am_ll and d_ll can be tuned independently — the architecture has separate controls. The LL_ONSETS[d]=0.40 miscalibration pre-existing in exp_182-186 is corrected: the correct d_am_weight is 0.16, not 0.40. (2) H402: Blind LF mapping (y-onset words with random suffixes, generated with probability p_lf_blind at all LF positions) closes the y_lf gap. At p_lf_blind=0.20: y_lf=3.364 (96.0%VMS ✓). At p_lf_blind=0.30: y_lf=4.019 (114.5%VMS — overshoots). Target y_lf=3.506 is achievable at p_lf_blind ≈ 0.22-0.24. The y_lf gap was NOT structural to the architecture — it was specific to the narrow Latin clause-initial regex (LATIN_CI_Y). A position-only LF rule can reproduce y-onset LF enrichment without morphological constraints. (3) JOINT VIABILITY: Best joint configuration (d_am=0.16, p_blind=0.40, p_lf_blind=0.20): am_ll=6.782 (99.6%VMS ✓), d_ll=1.484 (101.4%VMS ✓), y_lf=3.364 (96.0%VMS ✓), ss_mean=1.435 (98.0%VMS ✓), adj_rate=0.00410 (below VMS 0.009 ✓). FIRST CONFIGURATION to simultaneously approximate all five primary VMS structural metrics within ~4%. Previous best (exp_186): am_ll=97.1%VMS ✓ but y_lf=68% and d_ll=153%.
**Limitation:** (a) N=30 sims per configuration (wider CIs than exp_185/186 N=50). (b) TARGET-AWARENESS: All three calibration parameters were chosen by reference to VMS targets: p_blind=0.40 (produces am_ll ≈ VMS), d_am=0.16 (produces d_ll ≈ VMS), p_lf_blind=0.20 (produces y_lf ≈ VMS). This is a maximally target-calibrated design. The result demonstrates JOINT ACHIEVABILITY, not independent prediction. The probability of landing near these exact values without VMS knowledge is low. (c) Blind LF mapping uses random suffixes (SUFFIX_WEIGHTS) not constrained by Latin morphology — more target-aware than morphological LF but less constrained by source language structure. (d) Fine-tuned p_lf_blind (to precisely hit y_lf=3.506) is untested: H403 proposed for fine-grained sweep.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) d_am_weight and am_ll are independently controllable in the position-aware hybrid architecture; (b) the y_lf gap is closeable via position-only blind LF mapping (was previously labeled "structural"); (c) the position-aware hybrid architecture is now "jointly achievable" on the full five-metric primary set with appropriate target calibration. The remaining discrimination gap is conceptual: no a priori reason from Latin morphology or other external source to predict p_blind=0.40, d_am=0.16, p_lf_blind=0.20-0.24.
**Magnitude context:** This is the strongest joint approximation of VMS structural metrics by any tested mechanistic model. The architecture cannot be ruled out on structural metric grounds alone. The remaining question is whether the three calibration parameters can be derived from first principles (Latin morphology + position-sensitivity) without knowledge of VMS targets. This weakens (but does not eliminate) the cipher hypothesis relative to the intrinsic grammar hypothesis: reproducing VMS requires three separately tuned position-specific parameters, and the architecture's parameters are emergent from target calibration rather than from any structural theory of the source language.

## F209: NON-MORPHOLOGICAL LL MAPPING CAN CLOSE THE am_ll GAP (exp_186 97.1% CEILING IS NOT ARCHITECTURAL); p_blind=0.40 ACHIEVES am_ll=6.817 (100.1%VMS); LL_ONSETS[d]=0.40 OVERPRODUCES d_ll (2.25-2.30× vs VMS 1.464×) — PRE-EXISTING FLAW IN ALL EXP_182-186; INTERMEDIATE d_am WEIGHT (~16%) NEEDED TO REPRODUCE BOTH am_ll AND d_ll; ss_mean/adj_rate UNCHANGED (COPY COMPONENT INDEPENDENT)
**Experiment:** exp_209_blind_ll_mapping
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** H382 SUPPORTED. (1) The 3% am_ll gap from exp_186 is CF_rate-specific, not architectural. Morphological baseline (p_detect=1.00): am_ll=6.653 (97.7%VMS). Blind+ll_onset at p_blind=0.40: am_ll=6.817 (100.1%VMS). The position-only LL mapping exceeds the morphological ceiling. CF_rate ≈ 37% of Latin words have clause-final morphemes; at p_blind=0.40, 40% of ALL LL words map to -am — bypassing the 37% ceiling. (2) CRITICAL SECONDARY: LL_ONSETS[d]=0.40 overproduces d_ll in ALL variants: morph baseline=2.247× (153.5%VMS); blind+ll_onset at p_blind=0.40=2.303× (157.3%VMS). d_ll overproduction was untracked across exp_182-186 (d_ll not reported). Blind+random_onset (d-onset from ONSET_WEIGHTS=0.068) underproduces d_ll: 1.184× (80.9%VMS) at p_blind=0.40. VMS d_ll=1.464× lies between the two variants — requires d_am_weight ≈ 16% for -am words (vs LL_ONSETS 40% or ONSET_WEIGHTS 6.8%). Analytically: LL d-rate target = 10.6%; at p_blind=0.40, intermediate d_am ≈ 16% yields LL_d ≈ 0.40×0.16 + 0.60×0.068 = 10.5% ≈ target. (3) ss_mean=1.417-1.496 (VMS: 1.465) and adj_rate=0.00394-0.00438 (below VMS 0.009) are unchanged across all LL mapping variants — copy component is independent of LL mapping. (4) y_lf gap unchanged: 2.41-2.66× (VMS 3.506×, 68-76%) across all variants — LF mapping unchanged.
**Limitation:** N=30 sims (vs N=50 in exp_186); mean estimates stable but CIs wider. The d_ll flaw was not tracked in exp_182-186 — those experiments' am_ll/ss_mean/adj_rate results are unaffected, but d_ll was silently over-enriched throughout. No simulation of Variant C (intermediate d_am_weight ≈ 16%) — its expected am_ll+d_ll joint reproduction is analytical and untested.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) 3% am_ll gap from exp_186 is NOT architectural — position-only LL mapping closes it at p_blind=0.40; (b) LL_ONSETS[d]=0.40 is a pre-existing calibration flaw overproducing d_ll by 53%; (c) VMS d_ll=1.464× is jointly achievable with am_ll ≈ VMS using d_am_weight ≈ 16% (H401 — untested).
**Magnitude context:** The resolution of the am_ll gap is significant for theory discrimination: the position-aware hybrid architecture is NOT limited by the Latin CF_rate bottleneck. The architecture CAN reproduce VMS am_ll. The remaining open question is whether a single parameter set can jointly reproduce am_ll, d_ll, y_lf, ss_mean, and adj_rate simultaneously — the y_lf gap (H383) and d_ll calibration (H401) are the remaining discrimination targets.

(2) H396 SUPPORTED — B paragraph para-position: FIRST lines (n=712): f(6.79×)/p(3.04×)/o(2.33×)/y(1.66×)/qo(1.55×)/k(1.41×); ch(0.59×)/qok(0.54×)/l(0.43×) depleted. (4) H397 NOT SUPPORTED — A -am (base=1.979%): WP-LL=6.955%(3.51×) ≈ PF-LL=6.623%(3.35×) — no paragraph-level formula. B -am (base=2.032%): WP-LL=13.595%(6.69×) >> PF-LL=6.383%(3.14×) — -am is WP-LL dominant, DILUTED at PF-LL because B para-closing vocabulary (ok/ch/ot onset) is not -am suffix. C005 B LL enrichment (6.811×) is driven by WP-LL (6.69×); PF-LL is lower — C005 narrowed (see committed_claims.md).
**Limitation:** H395: daiin base rate manually computed (script bug: tracked onset labels not words). H396: B cth enrichments at lines 2-4 based on n=3-5 cth words per line — directional only. H396 B-last n=467 — onset enrichments reliable for common onsets (y/s/ot/ok/ch n=18-80); qot depletion (3/467=0.64% vs 3.98% base) reliable. B PS n=101 adequate. H397: A PF-LL total -am n=10 — rate reliable; individual words n=1-2, not reliable for word-level claims.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) A and B share PS formula (p/t/k/f) — the para-opening onset grammar is dialect-shared despite different suffix paradigms; (b) B 3-register model established: B middle lines are UNSTRUCTURED (near-uniform), contrasting with A middle lines (cth-enriched); (c) daiin→cth is a MIDDLE-LINE construction (3.84×), not a first-line bridge; sh→daiin is not enriched; (d) -am is a uniform line-last class in A (WP-LL ≈ PF-LL); B -am is primarily WP-LL, diluted at PF-LL by B's ok/ch para-closing vocabulary; C005 narrowed.
**Magnitude context:** The finding that A and B SHARE the PS formula (p/t/k/f) while having completely different first-line BODY vocabularies (A=sh-body vs B=o/y-body) is the clearest instance yet of shared syntactic structure with dialect-specific lexical filling. The "para-opener slot" accepts the same onset class in both dialects; what follows differs. B middle lines being near-uniform (0.99-1.03× for all onsets) means B paragraphs lack A's 3-register structure — B grammar is concentrated at para-boundaries (first and last lines) with unstructured middle content.

## F207: A PARAGRAPH = [PS: p/t/k/f (23.78×/6.04×/14.35×/3.36×)] → [FIRST-LINE BODY: sh(1.71×)/o(2.12×)/qo(1.69×); cth DEPLETED THROUGHOUT (0.17×-0.38×)] → [MIDDLE LINES: cth(1.13×)] → [LAST LINE: d-ONSET(1.67×)/daiin(1.88×,n=13)]; B PARA CLOSES WITH ok(2.48×)/ch(1.65×)/ot(1.61×); d-ONSET IS ANTITHETICAL: A=pf_ll 1.67× vs B=pf_ll 0.16×; qok DEPLETED AT PF-LL IN BOTH (A:0.12×, B:0.25×)
**Experiment:** exp_207_a_para_opening_b_pf_ll
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** (1) H390 SUPPORTED — A first-line (n=1011) onset profile vs all-A: p=4.81×, f=4.34×, sh=1.53×, o=1.86×, qo=1.67×; cth=0.27×, d=0.61×, ch=0.70×, qok=0.42×, ok=0.36×. Separating PS(pos=0) vs first-line body(pos≥1): PS is p(28.83%/23.78×)/t(18.40%/6.04×)/k(12.27%/3.36×)/f(4.91%/14.35×) formula — these 4 onset classes = 64.4% of all A PS words; sh/ch/d/cth all depleted at PS (0.19-0.58×). First-line body (pos≥1) is sh-dominant (1.71×), o-enriched (2.12×), qo-enriched (1.69×); cth strongly depleted (0.29×), d depleted (0.67×), ok depleted (0.31×), qok depleted (0.44×). Top first-line sh-words: shey(2.93×, n=19), sheol(2.26×, n=9), shor(1.94×, n=12). daiin is DEPLETED at first lines (0.54×, n=25); chol strongly depleted (0.17×, n=4). (2) H391 SUPPORTED — Position-by-position: PS(pos=0)=p/t/k/f formula. Pos=1 (immediately after PS): sh=21.2%(2.24×), o=11.2%(2.13×), qo=6.9%(2.52×), ch=21.9%(1.13×), d=2.5%(0.17×), cth=1.2%(0.34×). Pos=2-5+: sh consistently enriched (1.43-1.76×) throughout entire first line. cth depleted at ALL first-line positions (pos=1: 0.34×, pos=2: 0.36×, pos=3: 0.38×, pos=4: 0.22×, pos=5+: 0.19×). Top PS→pos=1 words: shey(5), shor(4), sheol(4). A 3-register paragraph model: [First line: p/t/k/f PS + sh/o/qo body] → [Middle lines: cth-enriched(1.13×)] → [Last line: d-onset(1.67×)/daiin dominant]. (3) H392 SUPPORTED — B pf_ll (n=94): ok=2.48×(n=16), ch=1.65×(n=24), ot=1.61×(n=10); d strongly depleted(0.16×, n=1), qok depleted(0.25×, n=3), qot depleted(0.27×). Top B pf_ll words: okeey(5.22×,n=3), oty(7.35×,n=2), shedy(2.18×,n=4), chedy(1.87×,n=4), chckhy(3.82×,n=2). A pf_ll (n=151): d-onset=1.67×(n=37), o=1.76×(n=14), ol=1.83×(n=7), ok=1.51×(n=13), ot=1.63×(n=11); sh depleted(0.42×), qok depleted(0.12×). Top A pf_ll: daiin(1.88×,n=13), am(10.65×,n=2), cthey(6.39×,n=3), dal(2.74×,n=3). The A vs B contrast: d-onset is the dominant A para-final class (1.67×) but is EXCLUDED from B para-finals (0.16×). Conversely, ok-onset closes B paragraphs (2.48×) but has no special role in A para-closing. This d/ok antithesis at pf_ll is the sharpest positional grammar split between A and B established in this project.
**Limitation:** H390: first-line onset counts reliable (n=1011); top word enrichments: shey(n=19) and shol(n=14) reliable; sheol(n=9) directional. H391: pos=1 transition n=160 (reliable); pos=4 n=120 (reliable); pos=5+ n=273 (highly reliable). cth depletion at all positions is well-established. H392: B pf_ll n=94 — reliable for onset-class level (d: n=1 is extreme but directional); A pf_ll n=151 — reliable. Top B pf_ll word enrichments based on n=2-4 are directional only. The am(10.65×, n=2) at A pf_ll is too small to claim reliably.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) A paragraph has a 3-register structure: [first-line: p/t/k/f PS + sh/o/qo body] → [middle: cth-enriched] → [last: d/daiin-dominant]; (b) cth is excluded from first paragraph lines (0.17-0.38× throughout); this is the third level of sh/cth paragraph-level segregation; (c) B paragraphs close with ok-onset/ch-onset; A paragraphs close with d-onset/daiin; d-onset at pf_ll is the clearest A vs B para-level grammar split; (d) qok-onset is depleted at pf_ll in BOTH dialects (A:0.12×, B:0.25×) — qok is not a para-final class in either dialect.
**Magnitude context:** The A 3-register paragraph model (first-line sh-body, middle-line cth-enriched, last-line d-dominant) represents a complete paragraph-level grammar characterization for A-dialect. The B counterpart: [unclear first-line formula] → [middle: qo-class dominant (20.15%)] → [last: ok/ch closing]. The two dialects have completely different paragraph architectures. The daiin(1.88×) as the single most common A para-closing word, combined with daiin→cth(2.93×) and daiin=top predecessor/successor of sh-words, establishes daiin as the CENTRAL grammatical hub of A-dialect — it bridges sh-domain (first-line) to cth-domain (middle-lines) to para-closing (last-line) within A paragraphs.

## F206: B edy-SUFFIX CLASS IS MID-DOMINANT (81.29%/1.09×), pf_ll DEPLETED (0.77×) — NOT A PARA-TERMINAL CLASS; B DEFINES 19.40% edy-SUFFIX vs A=0.45% (43× DIFFERENCE); B qo-CLASS IS 1.84× HIGHER RATE THAN A (20.15% vs 10.98%), MID-DOMINANT (1.10×), PS/PF-LL=0.25×/0.26×; qo-CLASS qo→qo/qot→qot SELF-CLUSTERING (2.09×/2.16×); A sh IS PARA-LEVEL SEGREGATED FROM cth: sh ENRICHED AT FIRST PARAGRAPH LINE (1.53×) WHILE cth IS DEPLETED (0.27×); cth IS PARAGRAPH-INTERIOR CLASS (93.80%/1.13× IN MIDDLE LINES)
**Experiment:** exp_206_b_edy_qo_grammar_sh_para
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** (1) H386 NOT SUPPORTED — B edy-suffix class (19.40% of all B words; A=0.45%, 43× difference): positional profile pf_ll=0.77× (DEPLETED), wp_ll=0.58× (DEPLETED), MID=81.29%/1.09× (dominant). edy-suffix class is NOT a para-terminal class; it is a MID content-word class. (2) H387 NOT SUPPORTED — A qo-class (combined qo+qot+qok) → sh successor: 0.75× depleted; qo→sh=0.87×, qot→sh=0.66×, qok→sh=0.74×. [sh][qo][sh] triple: 10 observed vs 9.8 expected (1.02× = baseline). sh→qo relationship is one-directional: sh introduces qo (1.49-1.90×) but qo does NOT re-introduce sh (0.75×). qo-class in A introduces ch(1.10×)/qok(1.51×)/ok(1.27×)/qot(1.42×) — self-clustering within qo-class and ch-adjacent; no sh feedback. Additional: qo-class → l is enriched (2.58×, n=13) — previously uncharacterized. (3) H388 SUPPORTED WITH MAJOR FINDING — A paragraph-line analysis: sh-onset at first paragraph line = 14.54% (base ~10%), enrichment=1.53×; cth-onset at first paragraph line = 0.99% (base ~3.68%), enrichment=0.27× (73% depleted). sh-dominant/cth-depleted at para openings; cth-dominant/sh-neutral in middle lines (cth_enr=1.13×, sh_enr=0.98×). A paragraph structure: [sh-dominant first line (1.53×)] → [cth-interior middle lines (1.13×)] → [neutral last line]. sh and cth are PARAGRAPH-LEVEL SEGREGATED in A, not just bigram-level segregated. (4) H389 SUPPORTED — B qo-class: 20.15% rate (1.84× higher than A's 10.98%). Positional: ps=0.25×/pf_ll=0.26× — qo-class never opens/closes paragraphs in B; MID=81.98%/1.10×. Sub-class self-clustering: qo→qo(2.09×), qot→qot(2.16×). qok→sh(1.20×) but qo→sh(0.87×) and qot→sh(0.78×) — sh-introduction is specific to qok-onset (not qo-class generally). B qo-class avoids cth (qo→cth: 0.68×, qok→cth: 0.35×). B qo-class vs A: B has 1.84× more qo-class; both are MID-biased; A qo-class has moderate WP-LF presence (1.20×), B qo-class does not (0.75×); B qok uniquely introduces sh, A qok depletes sh.
**Limitation:** H386: pf_ll=14/3618=0.39% based on aggregated B edy words across all sections. Section breakdown shows most B edy words are in 'other' section (3592/3618) which may include bio/stars/recipe folios not separately classified — overall positional pattern is reliable. H387: qo-class n=954 combined A bigrams — reliable; [sh][qo][sh] triple n=10 vs expected 9.8 — low power but direction (1.02×) strongly suggests no loop. H388: first paragraph line n=1011 total words; sh_n=147 (reliable for 1.53× claim); cth at first line n=10 — adequate to establish near-zero rate (0.99%), but exact enrichment (0.27×) has CI. H389: B qo-class n=3757 total — highly reliable for all claims. qo→sh n=48/570 — adequate.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) B edy-suffix is a MID content-word class (NOT para-terminal) — corrects F205's B cth pf_ll claim; the B para-terminal formula remains incompletely characterized; (b) sh and cth are PARAGRAPH-LEVEL segregated in A — sh dominates first lines, cth dominates interior lines; this establishes the macro-structure of A-dialect paragraphs; (c) qo-class in A is a one-directional receptor (receives from sh) but does not feed back to sh; (d) B qo-class is a MID-dominant self-clustering class 1.84× more concentrated than in A; qok-specific sh introduction (not qo-class generally).
**Magnitude context:** The paragraph-level sh/cth segregation (sh=1.53× at first lines, cth=0.27× at first lines) adds a THIRD level of grammatical segregation between sh and cth in A-dialect: (1) bigram level: cth depleted before/after sh (0.57×/0.71×); (2) line-level: cth is WP-LL enriched (1.55×) while sh is line-position neutral; (3) paragraph level: sh dominates first lines (1.53×), cth is absent from first lines (0.27×). This three-level segregation is a strong structural signature suggesting sh and cth serve fundamentally different grammatical roles at multiple levels of text structure in A-dialect.

## F205: sh-WORDS IN A ARE qo-INTRODUCING/ch-REPELLING CLASS (cth-NEAR-BASELINE 0.97×; ch DEPLETED AS PRED/SUCC 0.75×/0.71×; qo/qot/qok ENRICHED AFTER sh 1.90×/1.64×/1.49×); qokaiin IS A B-DOMINANT WORD (4.7× RATE IN B, MID-BIASED 83.1%, ZERO cth-SUCCESSORS IN A); B cth RATE IS 14× LOWER THAN A (0.263% vs 3.678%); B cth-WORDS ARE edy-SUFFIX CLASS; cth IS ESSENTIALLY A-SPECIFIC AS A GRAMMAR CLASS; [ch][daiin][cth][daiin] QUADRUPLE DOES NOT OCCUR (0/12 triples extended; chain terminates at cth)
**Narrowed by F206 (exp_206, 2026-04-11)**: The F205 claim "B cth-words are pf_ll=8.10× (para-terminal)" was n=2/49 sampling noise. exp_206 shows the full B edy-suffix class has pf_ll=0.77× (depleted), not enriched. B cth-words are edy-class MID-dominant content words, not para-terminal. All other F205 findings unchanged.
**Experiment:** exp_205_sh_grammar_qokaiin_cth_b
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** (1) H382 SUPPORTED — A sh-word grammar neighborhood (795 sh bigrams, 7939 total A): cth depleted as sh-predecessor (0.57×), ch depleted as sh-predecessor (0.75×). After sh-words: ch depleted (0.71×), d depleted (0.72×), cth near-baseline (0.97×). sh→sh self-attraction (pred 1.32×, succ 1.32×). sh introduces qo-class: qo(1.90×), qot(1.64×), qok(1.49×) after sh. Top predecessor word: daiin(25); top successor word: daiin(29). Individual sh-words: shol(n=104) cth=1.54×; sho(n=82) cth=0.84×; shey(n=62) cth=1.48×; sheol/shody/sheody/shodaiin all cth=0×; shaiin(n=14) cth=6.56× (but onset-class driven per H378). sh as a CLASS is not a cth-attractor (0.97×). The F201 "6th cth-construction" (sh_nonshe) is confirmed null. (2) H383 SUPPORTED — qokaiin: A-dialect n=26 (0.27%), B-dialect n=237 (1.27%) — 4.7× higher rate in B. Positional: A qokaiin MID=65.4%, WP-LF=26.9%, PS=0%; B qokaiin MID=83.1%, WP-LF=11.4%, PS=0%. A qokaiin successor: y-onset(3.58×), qok(2.37×), ok(2.11×), cth=0×. qokaiin is a B-dominant, MID-heavy, non-PS word; in A it has slightly more WP-LF presence (directional, n=26 small). (3) H384 SUPPORTED WITH MAJOR FINDING — B cth rate: 49/18649=0.263% vs A 355/9651=3.678% (A is 14× higher). B cth-words: cthedy(10), cthey(10), cthdy(6), cthy(3), cthar(3) — edy-suffix class. B cth positional profile: pf_ll=4.1%(8.10× enrichment) — B cth-words are PARA-TERMINAL. Contrast A: cth is MID(71.8%/1.11×)+WP-LL(24.5%/1.55×) — grammar function words, NOT para-terminal. B cth successors: ch(1.60×), ot(2.07×), y(2.25×); sh depleted (0.52×) — completely different successor profile from A cth. Interpretation: B "cth-words" are edy-suffix B-dialect words (cthedy=B's edy-class applied to cth-onset) functioning as para-terminal forms; they are NOT the same grammatical entity as A's cth-class. cth as a productive grammar class is essentially A-specific. (4) H385 NOT SUPPORTED — [ch][daiin][cth][daiin] quadruple: 0 observed from 12 [ch][daiin][cth] triples (expected 0.8 from independence); enrichment=0.00×. [daiin][cth][daiin] triple: 2 observed vs 3.0 expected (0.68× — below expected). Cross-line cth@LL→daiin@LF: 4/88=4.55% vs base 5.16% (0.88× — near baseline). Cross-line daiin@LL→cth@LF: 0/93 (0.00× — absent). The grammar chain terminates at cth and does not loop within or across lines.
**Limitation:** H382: sh-word individual table denominator includes all occurrences (not just those with successors); slight overcount for line-final words. shol(104) and shey(62) have adequate n; shaiin(14) directional. H383: A n=26 — all positional claims for A are directional only. H384: B cth n=49 total; pf_ll=2 instances — directional; the 14× rate difference is robust. H385: triple n=12 gives expected 0.8 quads — low statistical power; the absence is meaningful but not definitive. Cross-line n=88 cth@LL cases — adequate for testing.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) sh is NOT a cth-attractor in A (0.97×); sh introduces qo-class and self-clusters; (b) qokaiin is B-dominant (4.7× rate) and zero cth-attractor in A; (c) B cth rate is 14× lower than A — the biggest A/B asymmetry measured; B cth-words are edy-class para-terminal forms, NOT the A-dialect grammar class; (d) the grammar chain terminates at [ch→daiin→cth]; no quadruple, no cross-line chain; cth→daiin (1.50×) is moderate and does not re-trigger the chain.
**Magnitude context:** The B cth rate (0.263%) vs A cth rate (3.678%) is the starkest dialect-level quantitative asymmetry established so far. Combined with B cth-words being edy-suffix para-terminal forms, this confirms that the entire cth-grammar system (cth as a productive word class, the ch→daiin→cth chain, cth's MID/WP-LL positional role) is an A-dialect phenomenon. B-dialect's grammar is built around sh/ch-onset words and edy-suffix classes instead.

**Finding:** (1) H378 SUPPORTED WITH NUANCE — All A -aiin predecessor bigrams: n=968, cth-successor=81 (8.37%), enrichment=1.92× vs baseline (4.36%). But enrichment is NOT uniform: high-cth subset (words with cth-attracting onset classes) — shaiin=28.57%(6.56×), okaiin=15.15%(3.48×), daiin=12.76%(2.93×), chodaiin=9.52%(2.19×), otaiin=8.00%(1.84×); zero-cth subset (non-cth-attracting onsets) — aiin(n=58, 0%×), odaiin(n=26, 0%), qokaiin(n=24, 0%), saiin(n=23, 0%), ykaiin(n=15, 0%). The cth-attraction is onset-class driven, not -aiin-suffix driven. Within d-onset: daiin=2.93× >> dain=1.61× >> dal≈baseline >> dar=0.41×; dam=0%. The construction is specifically "d-onset -aiin words" (with daiin dominant), not -aiin generally. (2) H379 SUPPORTED — A cth-word successor profile (n=262): d-onset=19.08%(1.33×), cth=6.49%(1.49×), ot=6.87%(1.48×), qo=4.58%(1.64×); ch at baseline (22.14%/1.01×); sh depleted (5.73%/0.57×). Top specific successors: daiin(18), chol(10), chor(8), cthy(7), dain(6). cth→daiin enrichment=1.50× (18/262=6.87% vs daiin base 4.59%). Per cth-word: cthy→ch+d; cthol→d+ch; cthor→ch+ot. Grammar cluster confirmed: [ch-onset]→daiin→[cth-word]→daiin/d-word — a circular chain in A-dialect. sh is depleted both as cth-predecessor (1.02× within herbal A, baseline) and as cth-successor (0.57×). (3) H380 SUPPORTED — daiin→cth enrichment by section: herbal A=2.79×(n=37 cth cases, n=225 daiin), pharma A=2.15×(n=6 cth, n=89 daiin). The enrichment is consistent across A sections with adequate n — it is a dialect-level property, not herbal-only. Astro A (n=11 daiin, 0 cth) too small to test. (4) H381 SUPPORTED — A pol-prefix (n=9 tokens, 8 distinct hapax/rare words): ps=5(55.6%), wp_lf=2(22.2%), mid=2(22.2%), ll=0. B pol-prefix (n=70): ps=5(7.1%), wp_lf=56(80.0%), mid=9(12.9%). A pol-words are PARA-tier words (PS-biased=55.6%), not LINE_OPEN WP-LF openers. A pol-words (polyshy, poldchody, poldaiin) are a different lexical set from B's productive pol-words (pol, polchedy, polaiin, polshy). pol-prefix is NOT a cross-dialect grammatical class — it is B-specific as a WP-LF LINE_OPEN class. In A, pol-onset words are incidental PARA-tier vocabulary.
**Limitation:** H378: Word-level claims for small-n words (shaiin n=14, chkaiin n=5) have wide CI. The zero-cth claim for aiin(n=58), qokaiin(n=24) is reliable. H379: n=262 cth bigrams — onset-class enrichments reliable; word-level (daiin n=18) reliable direction. H380: pharma A n=6 cth cases — directional only. H381: n=9 A pol-tokens — very small, positional claims are indicative.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key findings: (a) -aiin is an onset-class-gated cth-introducer: only -aiin words with cth-attracting onset classes (d/sh/ok/ch) have cth attraction; (b) cth→daiin(1.50×) closes the grammar loop — the A-dialect chain ch→daiin→cth→daiin is confirmed; (c) sh is depleted as cth-successor (0.57×), consistent with A-dialect ch/cth vs sh grammatical segregation; (d) A pol-words are PARA-tier (PS-biased) while B pol-words are LINE_OPEN (WP-LF-biased) — completely different grammatical roles despite same morphological prefix.
**Magnitude context:** The cth-successor depletion of sh (0.57×) combined with the cth-predecessor near-baseline of sh (1.02×/1.11× within A-dialect per H372) establishes that sh and cth have a bidirectional exclusion in A: sh rarely precedes cth AND cth rarely introduces sh. This confirms sh and cth as COMPETING vocabulary classes within A-dialect's grammar — the sh/ch word cluster and the cth-word cluster are grammatically segregated even within A-dialect.

## F203: pol-PRODUCTIVE-WORDS ARE EXCLUSIVELY WP-LF (ps=0 FOR pol/polchedy/polaiin); A daiin→cth IS POSITION-INDEPENDENT (LF: 2.42×, MID: 3.05×); B daiin→cth=0% — ABSOLUTE DIALECT SPLIT (A=cth-grammar, B=sh/ch-grammar); [ch→daiin→cth] TRIPLE ENRICHED BUT INDEPENDENT (1.51×, NOT TIGHT CONSTRUCTION); pol@WP-LF UNIQUELY DEPLETES ch (0.28×) — pol IS A "ch-ISOLATOR" LINE-OPENER; A pch@PS ATTRACTS qo(3.06×)/ch(1.68×) — PARAGRAPH OPENS INTO A-DIALECT CORE VOCABULARY
**Experiment:** exp_203_pol_ps_daiin_triple_pch
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** (1) H374 SUPPORTED WITH NUANCE — pol@PS=5 (7.14%, 13.19×) from 70 total B pol tokens. But the 4 productive pol-words (pol/n=13, polchedy/n=7, polaiin/n=7, polshy/n=3) all have zero PS appearances — the 5 PS instances come from hapax/rare pol-words (including polarar=1). pch@PS=22 (12.09%, 22.32×), WP-LF=105 (57.69%), MID=50 (27.47%). pch is not PS-exclusive — it's broadly distributed across PS/WP-LF/MID. Revised picture: productive pol-words are exclusively WP-LF (LF=80%, MID=12.86%, LL=0%); productive pch-words are predominantly WP-LF+MID with moderate PS enrichment. The F200 "pol=WP-LF / pch=PS" dichotomy is directionally correct for productive words but overstated for pch. (2) H376 SUPPORTED — A daiin@LF (n=81, PS=1, WP-LF=80): successor onset cth=11.11%(2.42×); ch depleted (0.79×); sh near-baseline (0.90×). Top successors: cthor(3), qotchy(3), cthol(2). In A-dialect, daiin is a cth-attractor at BOTH line positions: LF(2.42×) and MID(3.05×). A/B dialectal split is ABSOLUTE: A daiin→cth always; B daiin@LF→sh/ch(2.15×/2.00×) and B daiin→cth=0%. This establishes daiin as a participant in the fundamental A/B grammar split: A has cth-onset vocabulary grammar; B has sh/ch-onset vocabulary grammar. daiin bridges to cth in A, to sh/ch in B. (3) H375 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED — [ch-word][daiin][cth-word] triple in A: n=12 observed vs 8 expected (independence assumption); enrichment=1.51×. This is modest (marginal significance). ch-predecessor and cth-successor affinities of daiin are largely INDEPENDENT: 22/34 (64.7%) of daiin→cth cases lack ch-predecessors. The ch-adjacency and cth-adjacency are separate grammatical properties of daiin, not parts of a tight 3-word construction. Specific recurring triple: [chol][daiin][cthy](n=2). (4) H377 SUPPORTED — B pch@PS successor: o(1.71×)/ol(1.67×)/d(1.48×); ch near-baseline (0.89×); qok depleted (0.30×). B pol@WP-LF successor: ot(2.38×)/qo(1.69×)/ol(1.74×)/sh(1.40×); ch STRONGLY DEPLETED (0.28×). pol's ch-avoidance (0.28×) is the strongest ch-depletion in any tested word class — pol functions as a "ch-isolator" that systematically avoids ch-onset successors when opening a line. A pch@PS successor: qo(3.06×)/ch(1.68×)/ot(2.11×) — A paragraphs beginning with pch open into A-dialect core vocabulary (qo-complex and ch-onset words), reflecting the A-dialect's ch/cth-grammar structure.
**Limitation:** H374: pol@PS=5 from hapax words — the claim that productive pol-words are PS=0 is based on word-level inspection (n=30 tokens for top 4 pol-words). The 5 PS hapax pol-words are exceptional rather than systematic. H375: triple enrichment 1.51× at n=12 is marginally significant; the "independent" interpretation is the most parsimonious given the weak enrichment. H376: n=81 A daiin@LF; cth-successor n=9 — adequate for direction but not precise magnitude. H377: pch@PS n=22 in B and 19 in A — small n; specific onset enrichments have wide CI.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) productive pol-words are genuinely WP-LF exclusive (PS=0) — distinguishes them from pch which is broadly distributed; (b) the A/B daiin dialectal split (A→cth; B→sh/ch) is absolute and position-independent — daiin participates fully in the A=cth-grammar vs B=sh-grammar split; (c) pol is a "ch-isolator" word class — the strongest ch-successor depletion (0.28×) of any word class tested; (d) A paragraph starts (pch@PS) open specifically into qo/ch vocabulary — A-dialect paragraph structure starts with pch and immediately enters ch/qo-onset content.
**Magnitude context:** The A/B daiin dialectal split (A: cth-successor=2.42-3.05×, ch depleted 0.79×; B: sh/ch-successor=2.00-2.15×, cth=0%) is the clearest cross-dialect grammar split established so far. It means daiin functions as a grammatical linker in both dialects, but the vocabulary it links INTO is completely different — reflecting the A-dialect's cth-dominant grammar and the B-dialect's sh/ch-dominant grammar. This is consistent with A and B having different "dominant suffix paradigms" (A: -ol/-or/-cth; B: -edy/-edy suffixes driving sh/ch words) as established in F035/F047.

## F202: pol-PREFIX AND daiin ARE FUNCTIONALLY DISTINCT LINE_OPEN WORDS (pol→ch DEPLETED 0.26×; daiin→sh/ch 2.15×/2.00×); A daiin@MID SUCCESSOR = cth(3.05×)/cthy(9)/cthol(5) — daiin→cth IS WITHIN-LINE CONSTRUCTION; cth-INTRO RANKING: ychor_stem(3.06×)>daiin(2.93×)>>d_onset(1.67×)>k_onset(1.35×)>sh_nonshe(1.11×≈baseline); F201 sh-ONSET AS "6th cth-CONSTRUCTION" REQUIRES CORRECTION (1.02× WITHIN A-HERBAL; 1.72× WAS VS CORPUS BASELINE); cosmo B shedy(13.34× PF/WP) IS PF-RESTRICTED; chedy(4.67×) IS GENERAL LL WORD NOT DEDICATED PARA-CLOSER
**Experiment:** exp_202_pol_successor_daiin_mid_cth_rank
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** (1) H370 SUPPORTED — pol@LF successor profile (n=61 pol-prefix lines in B): ch STRONGLY DEPLETED (0.26×, only 3/61=4.9% vs baseline 19.0%); ol enriched (1.84×), ot(2.20×), sh weakly enriched (1.29×). Top successors: shedy(3), sheedy(2). By section: stars prefers sh/ok/qok; cosmo prefers ol/sh/qok. Compare to daiin@LF B successors (n=87): sh=35.63%(2.15×)+ch=37.93%(2.00×)=73.6% combined. pol-prefix LINE_OPEN and daiin LINE_OPEN are FUNCTIONALLY DISTINCT: daiin opens into sh+ch vocabulary with strong enrichment; pol opens into diverse ot/ol/sh vocabulary while strongly avoiding ch. This is the first within-tier grammatical differentiation: pol and daiin are both LINE_OPEN but serve different syntactic roles. (2) H371 SUPPORTED — A daiin@MID (n=256 cases): predecessor onset — ch=23.44%(1.18×); qot=5.08%(1.67×); cth=5.47%(1.66×); compare to daiin@LL predecessor ch=32.08%(1.61×). ch-adjacency of daiin is position-general (not LL-exclusive), stronger at LL. Top predecessor words: chol(17), chor(7), cthol(5). Successor onset — cth=13.28%(3.05×) is the primary enrichment; top successor words: cthy(9), cthol(5), daiin(8). The [daiin→cth] construction (F165) is primarily a WITHIN-LINE (MID) construction: daiin precedes cth-words as a grammatical bridge within the line. sh is DEPLETED after daiin@MID (0.55×) — the B-dialect daiin→sh/ch succession (F201) is dialect-specific and position-specific. In A at MID, daiin bridges ch-vocabulary to cth-vocabulary; in B at LF, daiin opens to sh/ch vocabulary. (3) H372 SUPPORTED — Unified cth-introduction ranking (all A-dialect, baseline=4.36%): ychor_stem=3.06× (n=15, small); daiin=2.93× (n=337, robust); d_onset=1.67× (n=1001, daiin-driven — non-daiin d-onset words are near baseline); k_onset=1.35× (n=305); sh_nonshe=1.11× (n=536, NOT SIGNIFICANT); ch_onset=1.10× (baseline). CRITICAL CORRECTION to F201: sh_nonshe within A-herbal is 5.99% vs baseline 5.90% = 1.02× — not a significant cth-introducer. F201's "sh = 6th cth-introduction construction (1.72×)" was measured vs corpus-wide baseline (including B-dialect and non-herbal sections). Within A-dialect (correct control), sh_nonshe enrichment = 1.11% (all A) or 1.02% (A-herbal). sh→cth bigrams appear in A-herbal because A-herbal has ~5.9% cth base rate (vs corpus ~1.6%), not because sh specifically introduces cth. The "6th construction" claim for sh-onset is NOT SUPPORTED within A-dialect. Revised cth-introduction constructions: (1) ychor-stem class (3.06×), (2) daiin (2.93×), (3) d_onset as proxy for daiin-specific effect. k-onset (1.35×) is weak. ch_onset and sh_nonshe are at or near baseline within A. (4) H373 SUPPORTED — cosmo B shedy: PF_n=4(12.50% PF rate), WP_n=7(0.94% WP rate) → PF/WP=13.34×; shedy total_LL=11 in cosmo B, of which PF=36.4% and WP=63.6%. shedy is genuinely PF-enriched. chedy: PF_n=3(9.38%), WP_n=15(2.01%) → PF/WP=4.67×; chedy total_LL=18 in cosmo B, of which PF=16.7% and WP=83.3%. chedy appears in WP-LL positions of nearly all cosmo B paragraphs (in f75r, f76r, f76v, f77r, f77v, f78r, f79v, f80v, f83r, f84v). CORRECTION to F201: chedy is a GENERAL cosmo B LL word (appears throughout paragraphs at WP-LL), not a dedicated para-closing formula. F201 overstated chedy's para-terminal specificity. Revised picture: shedy is the para-closing formula for cosmo B (13.34×); chedy is a general LL word with mild PF elevation (4.67×) but not a closing formula.
**Limitation:** H370: n=61 pol@LF lines is adequate for onset-class conclusions but per-word successor (top successor=shedy at 3) has small n. H371: n=256 daiin@MID occurrences is large; n=34 cth-successors is adequate. H372: ychor_stem n=15 (tiny) — magnitude unreliable, but direction (strongest enrichment) is consistent. daiin n=337 (large) — very reliable. H373: n=32 cosmo B paragraphs; PF-LL n=32; WP-LL n=747. shedy's 4 PF vs 7 WP (n=11 total) is moderate; chedy's 3 PF vs 15 WP (n=18) is clear.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key corrective findings: (a) sh_nonshe is NOT a genuine cth-introduction construction within A-dialect — F201's claim requires narrowing/correction; (b) pol-prefix and daiin are functionally distinct LINE_OPEN words with opposite ch-successor profiles; (c) daiin→cth is a within-line (MID) construction, not a line-boundary construction; (d) chedy in cosmo B is a general LL word, not a dedicated para-closing formula — shedy alone has the strong para-closing enrichment.
**Magnitude context:** The daiin@MID→cth enrichment (3.05×, n=34) is the primary new structural insight: daiin functions as a within-line bridge from ch-onset vocabulary to cth-onset vocabulary in A-dialect. The construction pattern is [ch-word][daiin][cth-word] within a single line. The pol vs daiin ch-successor contrast (pol=0.26× vs daiin=2.00×) is a large, reliable difference that establishes pol-prefix and daiin as distinct grammatical entities within the LINE_OPEN tier.

## F201: pol-PREFIX = B-SPECIFIC LINE_OPEN CLASS (87.1% LF, 0% LL, n=70; stars 52.9%+cosmo 41.4%; A=9 TOKENS ONLY); daiin BIDIRECTIONAL sh/ch ADJACENCY (A@LL: ch-PREDECESSOR 1.40×/chol=10; B@LF: sh-SUCCESSOR 2.15×+ch 2.00×=73.6%); sh-ONSET = 6th cth-INTRODUCTION CONSTRUCTION (1.72×, n=27; shol+shaiin+sho+shor; 22 FOLIOS); cosmo B shedy(14.72×)/chedy(5.15×) SPREAD ACROSS 7 PARAS/6 FOLIOS — SECTION-LEVEL FORMULA (21.9% COVERAGE)
**Experiment:** exp_201_pol_daiin_sh_cth
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** (1) H366 SUPPORTED — pol-prefix words (pol, polaiin, polchedy, polshy) in B: n=70, LF=87.1%, MID=12.9%, LL=0.0% — never at LL (hard grammatical exclusion). In A: only 9 tokens (extremely rare). B section distribution: stars=52.9%, cosmo=41.4%, herbal=1.4%, other=4.3%. Top B pol-words: pol(13 tokens, 84.6% LF), polchedy(7, 71.4%), polaiin(7, 85.7%), polshy(3, 66.7%). Compared to pch-prefix (B: n=182, LF=69.8%, MID=27.5%, LL=2.7%) — pch appears at all positions and across all sections; pol is LF-exclusive and stars/cosmo-only. pol-prefix is a B-specific LINE_OPEN subclass concentrated in the two B-exclusive sections (stars+cosmo=94.3%). This confirms the mechanism behind B WP-LF p-onset flooding (F199/F200): pol-onset words are section-specific line-openers that flood B stars/cosmo WP-LF positions. (2) H367 SUPPORTED — A daiin@LL (n=106 lines): penultimate predecessor onset distribution — ch=32.08% (1.40×), qot=6.60% (2.26×), ot=6.60% (1.30×); d=0.71× (depleted), ol=0.00× (excluded). Top specific predecessors: chol(10), cthy(3), shol(3), otol(3), qotchey(2). B daiin@LF (n=87 lines): second-word successor onset distribution — sh=35.63% (2.15×), ch=37.93% (2.00×), s=2.30% (2.89×); qok=0.28×, l=0.00×, qo=0.00×, o=0.27× (depleted). Top specific successors: shey(5), chedy(4), chey(4), sheol(3), shody(3), shedy(2). Combined sh+ch = 73.6% of B daiin@LF successors. Structural interpretation: In A, daiin follows ch-onset words as a line-closer ([ch-word][daiin]@LL). In B, daiin precedes sh/ch-onset words as a line-opener (daiin[sh/ch-word]@LF). daiin maintains adjacency to sh/ch-onset vocabulary across dialects — the dialect's positional grammar reversal switches which side of daiin they appear on. (3) H368 SUPPORTED — Non-she sh-prefix → cth bigrams (n=27 total): driven by shol(5 bigrams), shor(3), shaiin(3), sho(3). cthy is the dominant cth-word recipient (8/27=30%); remaining 19 bigrams use 17 different cth-words. Section distribution: A-herbal=85.2%, A-pharma=11.1%, B-herbal=3.7%. Folio distribution: 22 distinct folios (1-3 per folio). she→cth rate=0.63% vs non-she-sh→cth rate=2.76% (4.42× more). sh-onset enrichment vs baseline=1.72×. sh-onset is established as a 6th cth-introduction construction (adding to F165's 5: ychor→cth, daiin→cth, ch-word→cth, d+ch→cth, k→cth from F191). The 22-folio spread confirms grammatical distribution, not formulaic repetition. (4) H369 SUPPORTED — cosmo B paragraphs: n=32 (29 usable PF-LL). PF-LL enrichment: shedy=14.72×, chedy=5.15×, orol=51.52×, lshedy=25.76×, qokaiin=10.30×. shedy appears in 4 distinct cosmo B paragraphs (f75r, f76v, f83r×2); chedy in 3 paragraphs (f79v, f83r, f84v). Together shedy+chedy close 7/32 (21.9%) of cosmo B paragraphs across 6 folios (f75r-f84v — full cosmo folio range). This is a genuine section-level closing formula, spread not concentrated. The remaining 78.1% use open vocabulary (consistent with F200's B PF-LL open-class finding). cosmo B para-final grammar is intermediate: partial formula (shedy/chedy) covering ~22% of paragraphs, open vocab for the rest.
**Limitation:** H366: pol-prefix detection = startswith('pol') with len≥3; this correctly captures the class. A pol-prefix (n=9) may be understated if A has very sparse stars/cosmo sections. H367: n=106 (A) and n=87 (B) are adequate for onset-class enrichments; word-level claims (chol=10) reliable. H368: n=27 total sh→cth bigrams; 1.72× enrichment at moderate n is reliable direction but magnitude has wide CI. H369: n=29 PF-LL data points; folio spread across 6 distinct folios confirms section-wide formula at high confidence.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) pol-prefix is a B-specific grammatical class (LINE_OPEN tier) exclusive to stars/cosmo sections with hard LL exclusion (0/70); (b) daiin's positional reversal between dialects is mechanistically explained by bidirectional sh/ch adjacency — the word functions as an adjacency linker to sh/ch vocabulary, not a fixed positional marker; (c) sh-onset is confirmed as a 6th cth-introduction construction (herbal A grammar, 22-folio spread); (d) cosmo B has a partial para-closing formula (shedy=14.72×, chedy=5.15×) covering 21.9% of paragraphs.
**Magnitude context:** The pol-prefix LL=0/70 (grammatical hard exclusion) is the most striking finding — this is a word class that participates in paragraph-internal grammar (LINE_OPEN) but is categorically forbidden from the line-final position. The daiin bidirectional sh/ch adjacency (73.6% of B successors are sh+ch) is the strongest evidence yet for daiin as a grammatical linker word adjacent to the sh/ch vocabulary tier, with dialect-dependent direction.
**Narrowed by:** F202 (exp_202): (a) sh-onset as "6th cth-introduction construction (1.72×)" is NOT supported within A-dialect control: sh_nonshe within A-herbal = 1.02×, within all-A = 1.11× — at noise level. The 1.72× was vs corpus-wide baseline (artifact of A-herbal's high cth density). Revised: sh-onset is not a genuine cth-introduction construction at dialect level. (b) chedy as "section-level closing formula" in cosmo B is overstated: chedy PF/WP enrichment within cosmo B = 4.67× (not 5.15×), and chedy is primarily a general LL word (WP-LL=15 vs PF-LL=3, only 16.7% para-terminal). shedy remains the true para-closing formula (PF/WP=13.34× within cosmo B).

## F200: daiin PARTICIPATES IN d-ONSET POSITIONAL SHIFT (A-LL=23.9%→B-LL=9.5%, A-LF=18.3%→B-LF=33.0%); dam UNIQUELY INVARIANT (LF=0% BOTH DIALECTS); B PF-LL: cth(6.98×)/ok(2.71×)/sh(2.66×)/ch(1.81×) — OPEN CLASS (NO WORD FORMULA); B WP-LF p-FLOODING = POL-PREFIX WORDS (pol/polaiin/polchedy), NOT pch-PARA-STARTERS; she-qo AFFINITY (qok 2.25×) IS SPECIFIC TO she-PREFIX, NOT SHARED BY NON-she sh-WORDS
**Experiment:** exp_200_cross_dialect_words
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** (1) H362 SUPPORTED — daiin does NOT show cross-dialect positional invariance. In A: LF=18.3%, LL=23.9% (n=443); in B: LF=33.0%, LL=9.5% (n=264) — daiin shifts +14.7% toward LF and -14.4% away from LL in B. daiin drives the d-onset class reversal (A: LL-biased at 28.7%; B: LF-biased at 17.5%). In contrast, dam shows LF=0% in BOTH dialects (A=LF0%/LL64.1%, n=39; B=LF0%/LL79.2%, n=24) — dam is the unique cross-dialect positional invariant. Other d-onset words (dain, dar, dal) also shift toward LF in B; dy remains LL-biased in both but weakens. dam's LL confinement is a fixed grammatical property independent of dialect. (2) H363 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED — B PF-LL onset enrichments (n=94): cth=6.98×, ok=2.71×, sh=2.66×, ch=1.81× enriched; d=0.11×, l=0.23×, r=0.00×, qot=0.30× depleted. However, B para-final closing is an OPEN vocabulary class — most PF-LL words appear only once. No single word closes >4% of all B paragraphs. Cosmo B shows most convergence: shedy(4/29=13.8%), chedy(3/29=10.3%) — these may be a partial formula. Stars, herbal B, and pharma B have no recurring closing formulas. (3) H364 SUPPORTED — B WP-LF p-onset flooding (9.6%=222/2310) is driven by POL-PREFIX words: pol(11), polaiin(6), polchedy(5) and bare p-words (paiin=4, psheody=4, pchdair=4) — these appear only at WP-LF, never at PS. PS p-onset words are pch-prefix (pchedar=3, pchedal=2 at PS). Vocabulary split: 141/174 (81%) of B p-onset words appear only at WP-LF; 24/174 (14%) appear only at PS; 9/174 (5%) are shared. Two morphologically distinct subclasses: POL-onset (p+ol compounds) = WP-LF; PCH-onset (p+ch compounds) = PS. The flooding of B WP-LF by p-onset is specifically caused by pol-prefix words, which are absent from PS. (4) H365 STRONGLY SUPPORTED — she-prefix successor enrichments (n=1438): qok=24.83% (2.34×), qo=7.02% (2.17×), qot=6.26% (1.68×); ch=9.32% (0.50×), d=4.73% (0.56×), cth=0.63% (0.39×). Non-she sh-prefix successors (n=977): cth=2.76% (1.72×), k=4.71% (1.69×), sh=13.00% (1.33×); qok=11.05% (1.04× ≈ baseline). Direct she vs non-she comparison: she/non-she qok ratio=2.25×; she/non-she cth ratio=0.23× (non-she attracts cth 4.3× more than she). Word-level: shedy→qok=36%, sheedy→qok=36%, shey→qok=26%; vs shol→sh=16%/ch=15%/d=13%, sho→ch=24%/k=14%. she-prefix is a DISTINCT GRAMMATICAL MORPHEME from non-she sh-prefix: she-prefix licenses qo-complex successors; non-she-sh licenses cth/k/sh successors.
**Limitation:** H362: shared d-words requiring n>=5 in both dialects may exclude some low-frequency words. dam's uniqueness among shared d-words is definitive given the sample. H363: cosmo B formula (shedy/chedy) is based on n=29 — moderate confidence. The high diversity of B PF-LL words may partly reflect B's longer paragraphs (more lines → more diverse last-word pool). H364: pol-prefix words WP-LF flooding claim is based on top-3 words; other pol-words not extracted may contribute more. H365: she-word n=1438, non-she sh n=977 — adequate for onset-class enrichments; word-level claims are reliable (shedy n=369).
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new findings: (a) dam is the ONLY common d-onset word with cross-dialect positional invariance — daiin, dain, and all other d-onset words participate in the B LF-shift; (b) B WP-LF p-flooding is caused by POL-prefix words (not pch-para-starters flooding into non-PS positions); (c) she-prefix is grammatically distinct from non-she sh-prefix (different successor profiles, not a single sh-onset class); (d) B para-final is onset-constrained but not word-formula-constrained, except cosmo section.
**Magnitude context:** The she-vs-non-she distinction (2.25× qok ratio, 4.3× cth ratio) is strong enough to treat she- as a separate grammatical morpheme from sh-. The pol/pch vocabulary split (81% WP-LF only / 14% PS only) confirms that p-onset flooding is not an overlap of para-starter and within-para vocabulary — it's caused by a distinct pol-onset word class that functions exclusively as WP-LF opener.

## F199: B WP-LF: p-ONSET 4.14× ENRICHED vs A (9.61% vs 2.32%), l-ONSET 4.92×; k-ONSET 0.46× DEPLETED — p-FILLS k-SLOT IN B; d+ch → sh SUCCESSOR PRIMARILY shol (2.7×, 4/12); H361 NOT TESTABLE (1-PARA-PER-FOLIO IN HERBAL A)
**Experiment:** exp_199_b_wplf_dch_sh
**Date:** 2026-04-11
**Finding:** (1) H359 SUPPORTED — B vs A within-para LF enrichment: p-onset 4.14× (B=9.61%, A=2.32%); l-onset 4.92× (B=2.86%, A=0.58%); s 1.71×; qok 1.66×. Depleted at B WP-LF: k(0.46×), o(0.40×), ch(0.48×), qot(0.41×). The p-onset flooding into B WP-LF (9.61%) explains k's paradoxically high PS enrichment in B (9.91×): in B, p occupies the within-para LF slot more than in A, pushing k out of non-PS LF positions. B WP-LF absolute composition: d=15.4%, s=11.6%, y=11.7%, qok=10.3%, p=9.6%, t=8.7%. (2) H360 PARTIALLY SUPPORTED — d+ch lines (A-dialect) are followed by sh-onset words in 12/94 cases (12.8% = 1.77×). sh-followers are diverse (8 distinct words); shol dominates (4/12=33.3%, 2.7× enriched). No single formulaic sh-word — it's a structural preference for shol as opener after d+ch lines. Top specific next words after d+ch: qor(11.0×), qotcho(9.9×), ytchy(9.9×), sol(8.2×), shol(4.7×). (3) H361 NOT TESTABLE — herbal A has 1 paragraph per folio, making folio-level gallows+ch variation untestable (n=1 data point per folio). Overall gallows+ch rates at herbal A PS: p+ch=12.6%, t+ch=8.0%, k+ch=5.7%, f+ch=4.6%.
**Limitation:** H359 B vs A ratio is corpus-level; section composition differs (B has more stars/cosmo sections which may differ from herbal A). The l-onset enrichment (4.92×) is partially explained by B having more l-onset words in general (rarer in A). H360: n=12 sh-followers is small; directional only.
**Commitment status:** Not committed. Key new finding: p-onset is 4.14× more common at B WP-LF than A WP-LF — this explains why k appears almost exclusively at B PS (it's being displaced at WP-LF by p-onset words). This reframes the A vs B k-vs-p inversion: it's not that B concentrates k at PS more strongly — it's that B uses p-onset words throughout the paragraph (including WP-LF) in a way that A does not, while k stays strictly at PS in both.
